units.la: CUm in foro causas dicentibus nefas, ut ita dixerim, videatur esse, nulla praefatione facta, iudici rem exponere, mihi Legum Atticarum interpretationem facturo multo magis inconueniens esset, origine non repetita, atque illorum manibus, protinus materiam interpretationis tractare, non quia velim verbosas facere praefationes, sed ut iij, in quorum manus nostra haec venient, libentius ad lectionem propositae materiae producantur. Omnia animantia, quae in mari, quae in terra, ne feris quidem exceptis, nascuntur, iuris peritia censentur, quod natura docuit, & auium quoque commune est: Naturalis vero ratio inter omnes homines con-stituit ius illud, quod apud omnes peraeque custoditur, quo omnes utuntur gentes: Accessit tandem id, quod quisque populus ipse sibi dixit, cum aliquid addidit, vel detraxit iuri communi, vocaturque ius ciuile, quasi ius proprium ipsius ciuitatis: Nulla autem ciuitas est, nulla gens inter eas, quae Græci sunt nominis, qua prior Atheniensium populus sibi ipse ius non constituerit: de eo quippe Aelianus ποικίλης ἱστορίας Lib. III. cap. XXXVIII. Ἄχης τι δεῖ [illegible, ~12 letters] λέγειν [?] ἐστι. E Legibus namque actiones compositae sunt, quibus inter se homines disceptarent: quas actiones ne populus, prout veller, institueret, certas solennesque esse voluerunt, appellanturque Legis actiones. Venit autem ius istud Atheniensium ciuile è Legibus & Plebiscitis: Senatusconsulta non addo, quia nisi accederet populi auctoritas, ἐπίταια [?] tantum erant, nec nisi in unum annum, quamdiu scilicet ille Quingentorum Senatus, qui decreuerat, Reipublicae praeesset, ius faciebant. Primum autem Leges latae sunt a Regibus, quarum nonnullae etiamnum hodie leguntur, & hic habes, MI LECTOR: Reges exceperunt Draco atque Solo, quorum nomina canescent seclis innumerabilibus: Draco quidem anno primo Olympiadis tricesimae nonae, cum ipse Athenis Archon esset, stadióque vicit Laco Rhipsolcus: Δεξ-χων δὲ ὁ καὶ [illegible, ~14 letters] Ὀλυμπιάδα [?] γεγονώς [illegible, ~8 letters] Εἰουσπερ Eiusque Leges proprie νόμους dixerunt, ut est apud Aelianum Variae Lib. VIII. cap. X. & apud auctorem Etymologici his verbis: νόμον γὰρ ἐκάλεσαν τὸν νόμον, καὶ ἀλφεῖοι παρὰ τοῖς πολίταις νόμοις [illegible, ~10 letters] τῷ Δεξίχντος νόμον τὸν Σόλωνος. Sed vere olim Herodicus apud Aristotelem, ὅτι οὐκ ἀνθρώπου νόμοι, ἀλλὰ Δρακόντος χαλεποὶ γράμματα. Nam noxas pene omnes capitis supplicio puniendas esse nimis seuere censuit, sanxitque: Itaque eius Leges, quoniam videbantur impendio acerbiores, non decreto iussoque, sed tacito illiteratóque Athenienfium confenfu obliteratæ funt, tandemque Solon Draconis Legibus antiquatis, B. Hieronymi verba funt in Chronico, extra eas quæ ad sanguinem pertinebant, sua iura constituit, idque anno tertio Olympiadis quadragesimæ sextæ, quo in Prætura excepit Philombrotum, designatus pacis & Legum arbiter. Soficrates apud Diogenem Laertium: ἥκμαζε μὲν οὖν Σόλων [illegible, ~20 letters] ἐκτὸς Ολυμπιάδα, ἧς τὴν τρίτην ἔτει ἤρξεν Αθηναίων, ὅτε καὶ τὰ θέσμια τοῖς νόμοις. vide Plutarchum in Solone, & Ælianum Variæ Lib. VIII. cap. X. qui scribit non forte captum fuisse Archonta, sed ab Athenienfibus electum: eoque sensu, puto, Plutarchus, καὶ τὸν Σόλωνα τῆς πολιτείας ἐξορ[?]τικὸν καὶ νομοθέτην ἀπέδειξαν. Collapsam infecutis temporibus Pisistratidarum scelere Rempublicam instauravit Clisthenes iis eiectis, Legesque suis scripsit ciuibus. Isocrates Areopagitica: τὸν δημοκρατίαν Σόλων μὲν ὁ δημοτικώτατος γενόμενος ὁμολογεῖται· Κλεισθένης δέ, ὃ τοῖς τυράννοις ἐχθαλῶν, καὶ τὸν δῆμον καταγαγὼν, πάλιν ἐξ ἀρχῆς κατέστησεν. Plutarchus in Pericle: ἐγνάφῳ Αχαείς[?]ιν Κλεισθένεις ἐτέθη, ὃς ἐξέλασε Πισιστρατίδας, καὶ καταλύσας τὴν τυραννίδα ᾠκειώσ[?] ἔθετο, ἡ πολιτεία ἄριστα κεκοσμημένη ὡς ὁμόνοια καὶ σωτηρία κατέστησεν. Post exactos vrbe Triginta Tyrannos, restituta Legibus, ἀπ' Εὐκλείδου ἄρχοντος auctoritas, multæque de nouo latæ sunt, Diocle rogante, Aristophonte, aliis: sed inter eos inferioris huius æui luce micat splendetque sua Demetrius Phalereus) qui Rempublicam constituit, & Legibus ornauit, vt est apud Plutarchum in Aristide, cum rerum Athenis potiretur: Numerat quoque Æschylum & Thaletem inter Athenienfium Legumlatores post Solonem Suidas his verbis: Νομοθέτης πρὸς Αθηναίοις ἐγένετο Δεῖκον, μὴ αὐτὸν Σόλων, καὶ μὴ τῶν Θαλῆς, καὶ μὴ τῶν Αἰσχύλος. Sed de iis, quod sciam, tantum est: alia iam expendenda occurrunt. Obseruat Aristoteles in Problematis, veteres, cum literas nescirent, Leges, quas in tabulis non habebant descriptas, cantasse, ne obliuiscerentur: περὶ ὑπομνήματα γράμματα, ἦσαν τοῖς νόμοις, ὅπως μὴ ἐπιλάθωνται ὥσπερ ἐν Αιγύπτοις ἐπὶ εἰώθασι. Verum Corybantes columnis incidere Leges docuerunt, vt Theopompus scribit ἐν τῷ πρὸς Αθηναίους· τῶν Κορυβάντων ἔστιν ὀρθμὸς ἰσάτιον λίθοις, καὶ ἐν αὐτοῖς νόμους ἀναγράφειν. Solo vero in ligneas perscripsit tabulas, quas Axonas & Kyrbes dixerunt, & in Acropoli compofuerunt: sed Ephialtes in curiam, & in forum transtulit. Anaximenes ἐν Φιλιππικῷ· τοὺς Αξονας ἐν τοῖς Κύρβεσι αὐτὴν τῆς Ακροπόλεως εἰς τὸ βουλευτήριον ἡ τῷ ἀγορᾷ μετῆσαν Εφιάλτης. Pollux. ἀπέκτεινον δὲ οἱ τε Κύρβεις ἐν οἱ Αξονες ἐν Ακροπόλει πάλαι. αὐτῆς ἡ ἵνα πᾶσιν ἔξῃ ἐκπυλιφήνη, εἰς τὸ Πρυτανεῖον καὶ τῷ ἀγορᾷ μετεκομίσθησαν. Prytaneium erat in foro, vt testatur Pausanias Atticis: πλησίον δὲ Πρυτανεῖόν ἐστιν, ἐν ᾧ νόμοι τι οἱ Σόλωνος εἰσι γεγραμμένοι. Supersfuisse autem horum fragmenta Axonum in Prytaneio etiam sua aetate testatur Plutarchus in Solone: ὁμοῦ ἢ τῆς νόμοις πᾶσιν εἰς ἑκατὸν ἐνιαυτοὺς ἔδωκε, καὶ κατεγράφησαν εἰς ξυλίνες Αξονας ἐν πλαισίοις ἀξιέχοισι ἐρεφομένοις· ὧν ἐπὶ καὶ ἡμᾶς ἐν Πρυτανείῳ λείψανα μικρὰ διεσώζετο. Polemon ἐν τοῖς περὶ Εφεσίων. Ἄξονες ἀναγεγραμμένοι ἐν τῇ Πρυτανείῳ γεγραμμένοι καὶ ἀπλυτα[?] μέρη. Quod ad cu-riam attinet intelligo Matris Deûm ædem. Suidas: καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ τόπῳ ἀναγεγραμμένον βουλευτήριον, καὶ ἀπεφέρεσθαι αὐτὸ καὶ κατέκρυψαν τῇ μητρὶ τῶν Θεῶν. Adseruari autem ibi Leges docent veteres Magistri: τοὺς νόμους ἔθεντο ἀναγεγραμμένους ἐν ᾧ Μητρῴῳ. rursum: ἐχρῶντο δὲ Ἀθηναῖοι τῇ Μητρῴῳ ἀρχείῳ καὶ νομοφυλακείῳ. Reposita quoque erant Legum antigrapha in Regia porticu. Aristoteles de Republica Atheniensium. ἀναγεγραμμένους δὲ τοὺς νόμους εἰς τοὺς κύρβεις, ἐπισθὴν δὲ τῇ στοᾷ τῇ βασιλείᾳ. Andocides Oratione de Mysteriis: εἶτ' ἀναγεγραμμένα ἐν τῇ στοᾷ τοῦτοις τῶν νόμων οἱ αὐ ἀκυμαθῶν. & in Psephismate, quod legitur ibidem, scripto post exactos Athenis Triginta Tyrannos: τοὺς ὑπὸ τοὺς Τριάκοντα τυράννους ἀναγεγραμμένον εἰς τὸν ζύγον, ἵνα ἂν πρότερον ἀναγεγράφθαι, ὥσπερ τῆς βουλῆς. Axones autem vndique scripti erant, vt in laudatis modo Polemonis verbis habes: Ἄξονες ἀναγεγραμμένοι ἐν τῇ Πρυτανείῳ γεγραμμένοι καὶ ἀπλυτα[?] μέρη. colliges quoque ex his veterum Scriptorum verbis, quibus ὃ τ' Ἀξόνων κατασκεύασμα describunt: πλινθίον μέγα ἀυσρόμηκες, ἡρμοσμένα ἐξ ξύλων τετράγωνα εἰς πλευρὰς πλατείας ἔχοντα καὶ γραμμῆς πλήρες. ἐκτέρωθεν δὲ δύναχος (alij legunt κωόνδυς) ὥστε κινεῖσθαι, καὶ ἐπιφέρεσθαι, καὶ μετατρέφεσθαι ὑπὸ τὸ γεάφοντος καὶ τὴν ἀναγνωσκόντων. Scriptura autem Axonum huiusmodi erat: primus versus scribebatur à sinistra ad dextram, secundus à dextra ad sinistram; tertius rursum à sinistra ad dextram, quartus à dextra ad sinistram, & ita deinceps eo ordine: nam βουστροφηδὸν fuisse scriptas Solonis Leges auctor est Euphorion, referente Didymo, vbi quid sit ὁ κύρβων νόμος apud Demosthenem varie interpretatur: ὅτι γὰρ ὁ ῥῆμα τῆς ἐν τοῖς Ἀξοσι γεγραφῆς βουστροφηδὸν γεγραμμένης, τὸν ἀπὸ τῶν Ἰωνῶν ἀρχόμενον νόμον, κύρβων ὀνομάζει ὁ Δημοσθένης· ὅτι γὰρ βουστροφηδὸν ἦσαν οἱ Ἄξονες καὶ οἱ Κύρβεις γεγραμμένοι διὰ λώων Εὐφοείων ἐν τῷ Ἀπολλοδώρῳ. Quot fuerint numero Axones, nullus dixero: Sextidecimi meminit Plutarchus in Solone: ἀς γὰρ ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τῶν Ἀξόνων ἐξεῖζ ἡμᾶς τῶν ἐκκειμένων ἱερέων, εἰκὼς μὲν εἶ πολλαπλασίας. Videtur quoque vicesimum primum Axonem laudare Harpocration: καὶ Σόλων ἐν εἰκοστῷ πρώτῳ τὴν νόμων. Legum vero seriem atque ordinem in iis solus ille dixerit,
units.tr: It would seem wrong, so to speak, for those pleading in the forum to set out their case before the judge without any preface. So it would be even less fitting for me, who am about to offer an interpretation of the Attic Laws, to take up the matter of interpretation at once, without first going back to its origin. I do not write this because I want to make the prefaces wordy, but so that those into whose hands this work comes may be more willing to be led to the reading of the subject proposed. All living things, those born in the sea, on the land, even the wild beasts, are said to share in a knowledge of law, which nature taught and which is common to the birds as well. Natural reason, however, established among all men that law which is observed equally by all and which all nations use. Finally there was added what each people has laid down for itself, when it has added something to, or taken something from, the common law. This is called ius ciuile, as it were the proper law of that state. There is no state, and no nation among those that bear the Greek name, in which the people of Athens did not earlier establish law for itself. On this Aelian, in his Varied History book III chapter 38, says: Ἄχης τι δεῖ [unclear] λέγειν [?] ἐστι. For the actions by which men contended with one another were framed out of the laws. The lawmakers wished these actions to be fixed and solemn, so that the people could not set them up as it pleased; and they are called appellanturque Legis actiones (the actions of the law). The ius ciuile of the Athenians came from laws and plebiscites. I do not add Senatusconsulta (decrees of the Senate), because without the authority of the people they were only ἐπίταια [?] (temporary measures), and they had the force of law only for a single year, that is, as long as that Senate of Five Hundred which had decreed them governed the state. The first laws were proposed a Regibus (by kings), some of which are still read today, and you have them here, dear reader. Among the lawgivers were Draco and Solon, whose names will grow old through countless ages. Draco, in the first year of the thirty-ninth Olympiad, while he himself was archon at Athens, saw Laco of Rhipsolis win the stadion race: Δεξ-χων δὲ ὁ καὶ [unclear] Ὀλυμπιάδα [?] γεγονώς [unclear] Εἰουσπερ. His laws they called properly νόμους (laws), as Aelian says in his Miscellaneous History book VIII chapter 10, and the author of the Etymologicum in these words: νόμον γὰρ ἐκάλεσαν τὸν νόμον, καὶ ἀλφεῖοι παρὰ τοῖς πολίταις νόμοις [unclear] τῷ Δεξίχντος νόμον, that is, the law of Solon. But Herodicus, in Aristotle, truly said of them long ago: ὅτι οὐκ ἀνθρώπου νόμοι, ἀλλὰ Δρακόντος χαλεποὶ γράμματα, that the laws were not of a man but the harsh writings of Draco. For he judged and enacted, with excessive severity, that almost all offences were to be punished by death. Therefore his laws, because they seemed far too harsh, were not repealed by decree or command, but were wiped out by the silent and unwritten consent of the Athenians. At last Solon, with Draco's laws abolished, (these are the words of St Jerome in the Chronicle) except those which concerned bloodshed, established his own laws, and he did this in the third year of the forty-sixth Olympiad, in the archonship in which he succeeded Philombrotus, appointed as arbiter of peace and of the laws. Socrates, in Diogenes Laertius: ἥκμαζε μὲν οὖν Σόλων [unclear] ἐκτὸς Ολυμπιάδα, ἧς τὴν τρίτην ἔτει ἤρξεν Αθηναίων, ὅτε καὶ τὰ θέσμια τοῖς νόμοις (Solon flourished ... in the third year of the forty-sixth Olympiad, when he held the archonship of the Athenians, and then he gave the laws their established form). See Plutarch in Solon, and Aelian in Varied History book VIII chapter 10, who writes that the archon was not chosen by lot but elected by the Athenians. In that sense, I think, Plutarch says: καὶ τὸν Σόλωνα τῆς πολιτείας ἐξορ[?]τικὸν καὶ νομοθέτην ἀπέδειξαν (they appointed Solon as the reformer and lawgiver of the state). When the state had collapsed in the following times through the crime of the Pisistratidae, Clisthenes restored it, after they had been driven out, and he wrote laws for his own citizens. Isocrates, in the Areopagiticus: τὸν δημοκρατίαν Σόλων μὲν ὁ δημοτικώτατος γενόμενος ὁμολογεῖται· Κλεισθένης δέ, ὃ τοῖς τυράννοις ἐχθαλῶν, καὶ τὸν δῆμον καταγαγὼν, πάλιν ἐξ ἀρχῆς κατέστησεν (Solon is acknowledged to have been the most popular founder of democracy, but Clisthenes, having hated the tyrants and brought back the people, re-established it from the beginning). Plutarch in Pericles: ἐγνάφῳ Αχαείς[?]ιν Κλεισθένεις ἐτέθη, ὃς ἐξέλασε Πισιστρατίδας, καὶ καταλύσας τὴν τυραννίδα ᾠκειώσ[?] ἔθετο, ἡ πολιτεία ἄριστα κεκοσμημένη ὡς ὁμόνοια καὶ σωτηρία κατέστησεν (the law of Clisthenes was set up, who drove out the Pisistratidae and, abolishing the tyranny, ... so that the state, most excellently ordered, was established in concord and safety). After the Thirty Tyrants had been driven out of the city, the authority of the laws was restored under the archon Eucleides, and many new laws were proposed, Diocles proposing, Aristophon and others. But among those of this later age, Demetrius of Phalerum shines and stands out with his own light, who set the state in order and adorned it with laws, as is said in Plutarch's Aristides, while he held power at Athens. Suidas also counts Aeschylus and Thales among the Athenian lawgivers after Solon, in these words: Νομοθέτης πρὸς Αθηναίοις ἐγένετο Δεῖκον, μὴ αὐτὸν Σόλων, καὶ μὴ τῶν Θαλῆς, καὶ μὴ τῶν Αἰσχύλος. But as far as I know that is all on these matters; other points now present themselves for consideration. Aristotle observes in the Problems that the ancients, not knowing letters, sang their laws, which they had not written down on tablets, so that they would not forget them: περὶ ὑπομνήματα γράμματα, ἦσαν τοῖς νόμοις, ὅπως μὴ ἐπιλάθωνται ὥσπερ ἐν Αιγύπτοις ἐπὶ εἰώθασι. Yet Theopompus, in his work Against the Athenians, writes that the Corybantes taught men to inscribe laws on columns: τῶν Κορυβάντων ἔστιν ὀρθμὸς ἰσάτιον λίθοις, καὶ ἐν αὐτοῖς νόμους ἀναγράφειν. Solon, however, wrote his laws on wooden tablets, which they called Axones and Kyrbes, and set them up in the Acropolis; but Ephialtes moved them into the curiam (council house) and into the forum. Anaximenes in his Philippica: τοὺς Αξονας ἐν τοῖς Κύρβεσι αὐτὴν τῆς Ακροπόλεως εἰς τὸ βουλευτήριον ἡ τῷ ἀγορᾷ μετῆσαν Εφιάλτης (Ephialtes moved the Axones and the Kyrbeis from the Acropolis to the council house or the market). Pollux: ἀπέκτεινον δὲ οἱ τε Κύρβεις ἐν οἱ Αξονες ἐν Ακροπόλει πάλαι. αὐτῆς ἡ ἵνα πᾶσιν ἔξῃ ἐκπυλιφήνη, εἰς τὸ Πρυτανεῖον καὶ τῷ ἀγορᾷ μετεκομίσθησαν (the Kyrbeis and the Axones were long ago in the Acropolis... and they were carried to the Prytaneum and to the market, so that all might have access). The Prytaneum was in the foro (forum), as Pausanias attests in his Attica: πλησίον δὲ Πρυτανεῖόν ἐστιν, ἐν ᾧ νόμοι τι οἱ Σόλωνος εἰσι γεγραμμένοι (near by is the Prytaneum, in which some of the laws of Solon are written). That fragments of these Axones were still preserved in the Prytaneum even in his own day, Plutarch also attests in his Solon: ὁμοῦ ἢ τῆς νόμοις πᾶσιν εἰς ἑκατὸν ἐνιαυτοὺς ἔδωκε, καὶ κατεγράφησαν εἰς ξυλίνες Αξονας ἐν πλαισίοις ἀξιέχοισι ἐρεφομένοις· ὧν ἐπὶ καὶ ἡμᾶς ἐν Πρυτανείῳ λείψανα μικρὰ διεσώζετο (he gave all the laws validity for a hundred years, and they were written on wooden Axones in turning frames; small remains of these were preserved in the Prytaneum even in our time). Polemon, in his work on the Ephesians: Ἄξονες ἀναγεγραμμένοι ἐν τῇ Πρυτανείῳ γεγραμμένοι καὶ ἀπλυτα[?] μέρη. As for the curia (council house), I understand it to be the temple of the Mother of the Gods. Suidas: καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ τόπῳ ἀναγεγραμμένον βουλευτήριον, καὶ ἀπεφέρεσθαι αὐτὸ καὶ κατέκρυψαν τῇ μητρὶ τῶν Θεῶν (and on that spot a council house is recorded, and it was carried off and hidden in the mother of the gods). That the laws were kept there the ancient teachers show: τοὺς νόμους ἔθεντο ἀναγεγραμμένους ἐν ᾧ Μητρῴῳ (they placed the laws written down in the Metroum). Again: ἐχρῶντο δὲ Ἀθηναῖοι τῇ Μητρῴῳ ἀρχείῳ καὶ νομοφυλακείῳ (the Athenians used the Metroum as an archive and law-office). Copies of the laws were also kept in the Royal Portico. Aristotle, in his Constitution of the Athenians: ἀναγεγραμμένους δὲ τοὺς νόμους εἰς τοὺς κύρβεις, ἐπισθὴν δὲ τῇ στοᾷ τῇ βασιλείᾳ (the laws were written on the Kyrbeis, and behind the Royal Portico). Andocides in his speech On the Mysteries: εἶτ' ἀναγεγραμμένα ἐν τῇ στοᾷ τοῦτοις τῶν νόμων οἱ αὐ ἀκυμαθῶν; and in the decree which is read in the same place, written after the Thirty Tyrants had been driven out of Athens: τοὺς ὑπὸ τοὺς Τριάκοντα τυράννους ἀναγεγραμμένον εἰς τὸν ζύγον, ἵνα ἂν πρότερον ἀναγεγράφθαι, ὥσπερ τῆς βουλῆς. The Axones were written on every side, as you have in the words of Polemon quoted just now: Ἄξονες ἀναγεγραμμένοι ἐν τῇ Πρυτανείῳ γεγραμμένοι καὶ ἀπλυτα[?] μέρη. You may also gather from the words of the ancient writers who describe the construction of the Axones: πλινθίον μέγα ἀυσρόμηκες, ἡρμοσμένα ἐξ ξύλων τετράγωνα εἰς πλευρὰς πλατείας ἔχοντα καὶ γραμμῆς πλήρες. ἐκτέρωθεν δὲ δύναχος (alij legunt κωόνδυς) ὥστε κινεῖσθαι, καὶ ἐπιφέρεσθαι, καὶ μετατρέφεσθαι ὑπὸ τὸ γεάφοντος καὶ τὴν ἀναγνωσκόντων (a large oblong tablet, made of square pieces of wood fitted together, with broad sides full of lines; on either side a pivot, so that it could be turned, lifted and rotated by the writer and by the readers). The writing of the Axones was of this kind: the first line was written from left to right, the second from right to left, the third again from left to right, the fourth from right to left, and so on in that order. For the author Euphorion, as reported by Didymus, says that Solon's laws were written βουστροφηδὸν (boustrophedon, as the ox turns in ploughing). Didymus, where he explains what the κύρβων νόμος means in Demosthenes, interprets it variously: for because Demosthenes calls the law that begins with the Ionians κύρβων (of the Kyrbeis), since the Axones and the Kyrbeis were written βουστροφηδὸν, as Euphorion says in his Apollodorus. How many Axones there were, I could not say. Plutarch in his Solon mentions the sixteenth: ἀς γὰρ ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τῶν Ἀξόνων ἐξεῖζ ἡμᾶς τῶν ἐκκειμένων ἱερέων, εἰκὼς μὲν εἶ πολλαπλασίας. Harpocration also seems to cite the twenty-first Axon: καὶ Σόλων ἐν εἰκοστῷ πρώτῳ τὴν νόμων. But the sequence and order of the laws in them, one alone could tell, as Heliodorus of ... (the rest of the sentence is unclear).

units.la: ὡς Ἡλιοδώρου τελ[?] ποδὸς ἐκ γεγυμνασμένου.
units.tr: As of Heliodorus ... [?] from the trained foot [ὡς Ἡλιοδώρου τελ[?] ποδὸς ἐκ γεγυμνασμένου].

units.la: Omne quippe ius, quodiis continetur, vel ad personas, vel ad res, vel ad actiones pertinet: Summa autem rerum diuisio in duos articulos deducitur: nam aliæ diuini iuris, aliæ humani; hæ autem vel publici, vel priuati iuris sunt: itaque optime Demosthenes in Timocratea: ἔστιν, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, δύο εἴδη ὧν εἰσὶν οἱ νόμοι καὶ πάσας τὰς πόλεις. ὧν τὸ μὲν ὅσ' ἐστὶ ἐν ᾧ χρώμεθα ἀλλήλοις, ἐν σωματοφηρίῳ, καὶ πρὸς τὴν ἰδίαν ἃ χρὴ ποιεῖν διωρισμένα, καὶ ζῶμεν ὅλως τὰ πρὸς ἡμᾶς αὐτούς· ὅ δή, ὃν ἔχειν δεῖ τῆς κοινῆς τῆς πόλεως ἵνα ἕκαστον ἡμῶν ζῆσαι, ἐν πολιτεύεσθαι βούλεται, καὶ φὴ κτᾶσθαι τῆς πόλεως. Sed hunc ordinem non sequuntur Solonis Axones: nam Leges de sacris repræsentat sextus decimus Axon. Plutarchus in Solone: ἀς γὰρ ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τῶν Ἀξόνων ἐξεῖζ ἡμᾶς τὰ ἐκκειμένων ἱερέων, εἰκὼς μὲν εἶ πολλαπλασίας. De ignominiosis est Lex octaua Axonis tertij decimi, de qua Plutarchus, ὁ δὲ τεισκαιδέκατος Ἄξων τὰ Σόλωνος τὸν ὅλον ἐξ τὸν νόμον ὕπως αὐτῆς ὀνόματι γεγραμμένον. Primus vero Axon Legem habet de exportatione fructuum: nam vbi eam retulit Plutarchus, addit: καὶ [illegible, ~8 letters] Αξων [?] ὁ τῶν [?] ... τὸν νόμον. Quare nos, cum ordinem Legum à Solone rogatarum, & in tabulas perscriptarum ignoremus, in hac nostra Syllogæ, quantum fieri potuit, Imperatoris Iustiniani vestigia in digerendo veteri iure, & componendo nouo Codice, præstimus. Consulto autem prætermisimus Leges illas, quæ in Rhetorum scriptis leguntur: Quanquam enim omnes res Athenis esse gestas prædicent, pleraque tamen fictæ sunt in argumentum Declamationum: En tibi apud Sopatrum & Marcellinum Commentariis in Hermogenem ij, qui idem virtutis poscebant præmium, ex hac Lege committuntur: [illegible, ~10 letters] Sed cras credam forte, hodie nihil: Non ignoro tamen viros insignes, & partium duces suas manu discreuisse lites è prouocatione: ita interpretor Athenæi verba Lib. IV. [illegible, ~20 letters] etiam Ombrici inter se armis lites terminabant. Nicolaus Damascenus: [illegible, ~25 letters] Sed inter Athenienses Lege sanctum fuisse, vt [illegible, ~6 letters], ij qui fortiter in bello fecissent, de præmio armis decernerent, non possum mihi persuadere: Iterum apud eundem Hermogenem, Lex peregrinum vetat in murum ascendere; si ascenderit, capital ei esto. [illegible, ~15 letters] M. Tullius eandem habet Lib. I. de Oratore Lex peregrinum vetat in murum ascendere. Verum quidem est, si quis violauerit muros, vt vsurpem verba Pomponij Lib. II. ex variis Lectionibus, capite puniri: sicuti si quis transcendet scalis admotis, vel alia qualibet ratione: nam cives Romanos alia, quam per portas, agredi non licet: cum illud hostile & abominandum sit: nam & Romuli frater Remus occisus traditur ob id, quod murum transcendere voluerit. Leg. vlt. D. de diuisione rerum: necnon & si vallum quis transcendat, aut per murum castra ingrediatur, capite punitur. Leg. III. §. XVII. D. de re militari: Nihil tamen ista ad Legem, quam de schola Rhetorum laudant Cicero & Hermogenes. Tertiam addamus è Seneca Controuers. Lib. III. Contr. III. LEX. Cum filio tricenario pater patrimonium diuidat. Non est hæc Lex pro Athenien-sium instituto, receptisque moribus, sed facit maxime ad præferendam lucem parabolæ Euangelicæ apud Lucam XV. ij 12. de luxurioso iuuene, qui vult sibi à patre patrimonium diuidi. Huiusmodi igitur Leges data opera hic non legentur digestæ: operæ fuerit pretium ceteras, quas liquido constat Athenien-sium esse, collegisse: Quanquam non dubito, nonnullas nostros fugisse oculos: & certe vix aliter fieri potuit, cum non tantum homines simus, sed etiam, dum hæc scriberemus, variis occupati curis, & mentem mortalia tangerent. Præstabunt alij, qui sequentur, feliciter; eoque maximam à nobis inibunt gratiam. Cum autem scire Leges non sit earum verba tenere, sed vim ac potestatem, Leg. XVII. De Legibus, pleraque vero in illis adeo clara non sint, vt nullus superfit disputandi locus, Legibus latis accessit siue scripto prudentium interpretatio, quam ius ciuile dixerunt Romani Iurisconsulti, quia etiam ex auctoritate prudentium venit; Leg. VII. D. de iustitia & iure: Solenne quippe est, homines, [illegible, ~12 letters] μα, si interpretatio desit, errare & labi: itaque disputatione opus esse prudentiorum, qua è diuerticulo in viam reuocentur: atque hoc docuit Pomponius Libro singulari Enchiridij, verbis, quæ corrupte leguntur in hunc modum: Hs Legibus latis, cœpit, ut naturaliter evenire solet, ut interpretatio desideraret prudentium auctoritate necessariam esse disputationem fori: Leg. II. §. V. D. de origine iuris: Emendo: cœpit, ut naturaliter evenire solet, ut interpretatio desit, errare, & prudentium auctoritate necessariam esse disputationem fori. Prudentes istos, qui de iure responderent, Εξηγηταὶ dixerunt nostri Athenienses, quorum, ut alia aliorum atque adeo ipsius Demosthenis prætermittam loca, & παῖς τῷ Εὐέργου καὶ Μνησιδούλου ψευδομαρτυρεῖν[?] meminit Demosthenes, & festiuissime Terentius Phormione deridendos propinat, cum ita de iure refpondentes dicentesque inducit,
units.tr: All law that is contained in any body of law concerns either persons, or things, or actions. The main division of things is made in two parts: some belong to divine law and others to human law, and human law is either public or private. So Demosthenes rightly says in the Against Timocrates: "There are, men of Athens, two kinds of laws, by which all states are governed. One kind is what we observe in our dealings with one another, in the commercial and contractual sphere, and which defines what each of us must do in his own affairs, and how we live with respect to ourselves in general. The other kind is what the state wishes each of us to observe in order to live as a citizen, and what we must obey in our public life [ἔστιν, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, δύο εἴδη ὧν εἰσὶν οἱ νόμοι καὶ πάσας τὰς πόλεις. ὧν τὸ μὲν ὅσ' ἐστὶ ἐν ᾧ χρώμεθα ἀλλήλοις, ἐν σωματοφηρίῳ, καὶ πρὸς τὴν ἰδίαν ἃ χρὴ ποιεῖν διωρισμένα, καὶ ζῶμεν ὅλως τὰ πρὸς ἡμᾶς αὐτούς· ὅ δή, ὃν ἔχειν δεῖ τῆς κοινῆς τῆς πόλεως ἵνα ἕκαστον ἡμῶν ζῆσαι, ἐν πολιτεύεσθαι βούλεται, καὶ φὴ κτᾶσθαι τῆς πόλεως]. But Solon's Axones do not follow this order: the sixteenth Axon contains the laws concerning sacred matters, as Plutarch says in his Life of Solon, where he mentions the laws on sacrifices in the assembly of the Axones [ἀς γὰρ ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τῶν Ἀξόνων ἐξεῖζ ἡμᾶς τὰ ἐκκειμένων ἱερέων, εἰκὼς μὲν εἶ πολλαπλασίας]. The law on the disfranchised is the eighth law of the thirteenth Axon, of which Plutarch says: "The thirteenth Axon contains the whole law of Solon, written under its own name" [ὁ δὲ τεισκαιδέκατος Ἄξων τὰ Σόλωνος τὸν ὅλον ἐξ τὸν νόμον ὕπως αὐτῆς ὀνόματι γεγραμμένον]. The first Axon contains a law on the export of produce: when Plutarch cites it he adds: "and [illegible] Axon ... the law" [καὶ [illegible] Αξων [?] ὁ τῶν [?] ... τὸν νόμον]. Therefore, since we do not know the order in which Solon's laws were proposed and written on the tablets, in this our collection we have followed, as far as possible, the footsteps of the Emperor Justinian in arranging the old law and composing the new Code. We have deliberately omitted those laws which are read in the writings of the rhetoricians. Although they claim that all these things were done at Athens, most of them were invented as material for declamations. Look, in the commentaries of Sopater and Marcellinus on Hermogenes, two men who claimed the same prize of virtue are brought to court under this law: [illegible] But perhaps I believe tomorrow, not today. Nevertheless, I am not unaware that distinguished men and leaders of factions settled their disputes by a challenge to hand-to-hand combat; so I interpret the words of Athenaeus in Book IV: [illegible] also the Umbrians settled their quarrels among themselves by arms. Nicolaus of Damascus: [illegible] But I cannot persuade myself that it was sanctioned by law among the Athenians that [illegible], those who had fought bravely in war should decide the prize by arms. Again, in the same Hermogenes, a law forbids a foreigner to climb the wall; if he climbs, let him be put to death. [illegible] Marcus Tullius has the same law in Book I of On the Orator: a law forbids a foreigner to climb the wall. It is true that, to borrow the words of Pomponius in Book II of the Various Readings, if anyone has violated the walls, he is punished by death; likewise if anyone climbs over them by ladders brought up, or by any other means: for it is not lawful for Roman citizens to approach except through the gates, since that is hostile and abominable; for Remus, the brother of Romulus, is said to have been killed for this reason, that he wished to leap over the wall. Law last, Digest, On the Division of Things: and also if anyone crosses a rampart, or enters a camp through a wall, he is punished by death. Law III, section 17, Digest, On Military Affairs. Yet these have nothing to do with the law which Cicero and Hermogenes cite from the school of the rhetoricians. Let us add a third from Seneca, Controversies, Book III, Controversy III, LAW: a father divides his patrimony with his son who is thirty years old. This law is not in accordance with the practice and accepted customs of the Athenians, but it serves chiefly to bring out the light of the Gospel parable in Luke 15:12, about the profligate youth who wants his father to divide his patrimony for him. Such laws, therefore, will not be deliberately arranged here; it would have been worth the effort to collect the others, which are clearly known to be Athenian. Nevertheless, I do not doubt that some have escaped my eyes, and indeed this could hardly have been otherwise, since we are not only human, but also, while writing these things, occupied with various cares, and mortal affairs touched our minds. Those who follow will do better, and will win the greatest gratitude from us for it. Since, however, "to know the laws is not to hold their words but their force and power" (Law 17, On the Laws), and since most of them are not so clear that no room for dispute remains, an interpretation by the learned has been added in writing to the enacted laws, which the Roman jurists called civil law, because it also comes from the authority of the learned (Law 7, Digest, On Justice and Law). For it is customary for men, if interpretation is lacking, to err and stumble, and so there is need of disputation among the more learned, by which they may be called back from a byway to the road. Pomponius taught this in his single book of the Enchiridion, in words that are corruptly read in this way: after the laws had been proposed, it began, as usually happens naturally, that interpretation was lacking, and the authority of the learned made a disputation of the forum necessary. Law II, section 5, Digest, On the Origin of Law: I say: it began, as naturally happens, that interpretation was lacking, and the authority of the learned made a disputation of the forum necessary. Those learned men who gave answers on law our Athenians called Exegetes [Ἐξηγηταί]. Of these, to pass over other passages of others, and of Demosthenes himself, Demosthenes mentions & the boy of Euergus and Mnesidoulos (bearing false witness) [παῖς τῷ Εὐέργου καὶ Μνησιδούλου ψευδομαρτυρεῖν[?]], and Terence very wittily brings them forward to be mocked in the Phormio, when he introduces men answering and speaking about the law in this way:

units.la: CRA. Ego quæ in rem tuam sint, ea velim facias. mihi Sic hoc videtur. quod te absente hic filius Egit, restitui in integrum æquum est, & bonum: Et id impetrabis. dixi. DE. Dic nunc Hegio.
units.tr: CRA. I'd like you to do what is in your own interest. For me, this is how it looks: since your son acted in your absence, it is right and good that he be restored to the original position, and you will obtain it. I have spoken. DE. Now speak, Hegio.

units.la: HE. Ego sedulo hunc dixisse credo: verum ita est, Quot homines, tot sententiæ: suus cuique mos. Mihi non videtur quod sit factum, Legibus Rescindi posse: & turpe inceptum est. DE. Dic Crito.
units.tr: HE. I believe he has spoken carefully; but it is true: as many men, so many opinions; each has his own way. It does not seem to me that what has been done can be rescinded by law, and the undertaking is shameful. DE. Now speak, Crito.

units.la: CRI. Ego amplius deliberandum censeo. Res magna est.
units.tr: CRI. I think we should deliberate further. The matter is important.

units.la: Quemadmodum autem olim Romæ interpretandi scientia apud collegium Pontificum erat, Leg. II. §. VI. D. de origine iuris, ita etiam Atheniensium instituto, quod auctorem habuit Theseum, fuit apud Εὐπατρίδας. Plutarchus in Theseo: Εὐπατρίδας μὲν γινώσκειν τὰ ἱερά[?], ἡ πρὸς ἡγείσθαι Ἀρχοντας ἀποδείξεις[?] καὶ νόμων διδασκάλους εἶναι[?], ὁσίων καὶ ἱερῶν Ἐξηγητάς. Horum Εὐπατριδῶν, quibus natalium gentisque iure inferiores non sumus, sed censu atque peritia, exemplum secuti, Legum, quas in hac Sylloge descripsimus, non tantum verba tenere, sed etiam vim ac potestatem interpretari conati sumus in hoc scripto:
units.tr: Just as at Rome the knowledge of interpreting the law was among the college of Pontiffs (Law II, section 6, Digest, On the Origin of Law), so also at Athens, by the custom whose author was Theseus, it belonged to the Eupatrids. Plutarch in the Life of Theseus: "The Eupatrids were to know the sacred things, to appoint the magistrates, and to be teachers of the laws, and interpreters of the holy and sacred things" [Εὐπατρίδας μὲν γινώσκειν τὰ ἱερά[?], ἡ πρὸς ἡγείσθαι Ἀρχοντας ἀποδείξεις[?] καὶ νόμων διδασκάλους εἶναι[?], ὁσίων καὶ ἱερῶν Ἐξηγητάς]. Following the example of these Eupatrids, whom we do not rank below in the rights of birth and lineage, but in wealth and skill, we have tried in this writing not only to keep to the words of the laws we have described in this collection, but also to interpret their force and power:

units.la: Scitum fuit Heraclitì, πάντα ῥεῖ ψυχῶν εἶ[?] καὶ δαιμόνων πλήρη[?], vt loquitur Diogenes Laërtius, & est apud Aristotelem in Metaphysicis: unde, cum aliquando frigus esset, & Heraclitus ad furni ignem accessisset vt calesceret, hospites, qui conuentum volebat, fidenti animo introire iussit, quia & illic Dij erant: narrat Aristoteles περὶ ζῴων μορίων Lib. I. cap. V. his verbis, ὁ Ἡράκλειτος λέγει τοὺς ξένους εἰπεῖν[?], τοῖς βουλομένοις αὐτῷ συντυχεῖν[?], οἱ δ' ἐπεσθ[?]ιόντες εἰσὶν αὐτὸν ἀρμόσμενον[?] πρὸς τὰ ἴπνα[?], ἔφησεν· ἐκέλευσε γὰρ αὐτοὺς εἰσιέναι θαρροῦντας[?]· εἶ γὰρ καὶ ἐνταῦθα θεοί[?]. quod allusit A. Gellius in Præfatione, quæ ἐπιστολῇ[?] extremis Noctibus Atticis legitur, restatus nullum fuisse tam malum librum, e quo aliquid, quod in suum verteret commodum, non excerpserit, cum illud, inquit, Heracliti Ephesij viri summe nobilis verbum cordi habe-rem, quod profecto ita est, Introite, nam & hic Dij sunt. Idem tibi dictum a me puta, MI LECTOR, sed & interea per Musas ipsas,
units.tr: Heraclitus's saying is well known: "All things flow, and the soul and the daemons are full" [πάντα ῥεῖ ψυχῶν εἶ[?] καὶ δαιμόνων πλήρη[?]], as Diogenes Laertius reports, and it is found in Aristotle's Metaphysics. Hence, when it was once cold and Heraclitus had approached the oven's fire to warm himself, he bade the strangers who wished to meet him to enter boldly, because the gods were there too. Aristotle relates this in On the Parts of Animals, Book I, chapter 5, in these words: "Heraclitus is said to have told the strangers who wished to meet him, who found him warming himself at the oven, to come in with confidence; for even here the gods are present" [ὁ Ἡράκλειτος λέγει τοὺς ξένους εἰπεῖν[?], τοῖς βουλομένοις αὐτῷ συντυχεῖν[?], οἱ δ' ἐπεσθ[?]ιόντες εἰσὶν αὐτὸν ἀρμόσμενον[?] πρὸς τὰ ἴπνα[?], ἔφησεν· ἐκέλευσε γὰρ αὐτοὺς εἰσιέναι θαρροῦντας[?]· εἶ γὰρ καὶ ἐνταῦθα θεοί[?]]. Aulus Gellius alluded to this in the Preface, which is read as a letter at the end of the Attic Nights, where he says that there is no book so bad that one cannot excerpt from it something to turn to one's own advantage, since, he says, he kept in his heart that saying of Heraclitus of Ephesus, a man of the highest nobility: "Come in, for here too are gods." The same, dear reader, let me say to you as well; and meanwhile, by the Muses themselves,

units.la: Musarumque novem communia sacra rogatus, προοίμια[?], quæ nobis exciderunt, condona, affectu siquidem in te, in literas propenso meremur. Voto finiam, quo Legum istarum opus cum in scripta referret Solo, auspicatus est,
units.tr: Musarumque novem communia sacra rogatus, (asked to share the rites common to the nine Muses), the preludes [προοίμια] that have slipped from us, pardon them; for by our affection toward you, inclined as it is toward letters, we deserve it. I will end with the prayer with which Solon began when he set down the work of these laws in writing:

units.la: Εὐχόμεθα Διὶ Κεχνίδῃ [?] βασιλῆι [?]
units.tr: We pray to Zeus Kechnides, the king [Εὐχόμεθα Διὶ Κεχνίδῃ βασιλῆι].

units.la: Θεσμοῖς [?] τοῖσδε [?] πόλιν ἀγαθὴν καὶ κῶδας ὁπάσαι [?].
units.tr: that by these statutes [Θεσμοῖς τοῖσδε] he would bestow on this city good laws and tablets [πόλιν ἀγαθὴν καὶ κῶδας ὁπάσαι].

units.la: Admonendus est Lector, in hac Legum Sylloge, illas, quæ in Commentario uncialibus literis scribuntur, asterisco notari: Si qua autem irrepserunt sphalmata, iis offendi ne velit, rogatur.
units.tr: The reader should be reminded that in this collection of laws, those passages written in capital letters in the commentary are marked with an asterisk. If any errors have crept in, he is asked not to take offence at them.

units.la: SUMMA PRIVILEGII.
units.tr: SUMMARY OF THE PRIVILEGE.

units.la: CAUTUM est authoritate Regia ne quis in regno Franciæ, librum cui titulus est, Leges Atticæ, Samuel Petitus collegit, digessit, & commentario illustrauit, absque Caroli Morelli Typographi Regij & Bibliopolæ Parisiensis permissu intra septennium imprimat aut diuendat: publicationis siquis se-cus fecerit, mulcta mille librarum vindicabitur, prout in ipso diplomate continetur, Dato Lutetiæ Parisiorum die trigesimo primo Decembris, anno M. DC. XXXIV.
units.tr: By royal authority it is decreed that no one in the kingdom of France may print or sell, within seven years, the book entitled Attic Laws, which Samuel Petit has collected, arranged and illustrated with a commentary, without the permission of Charles Morel, royal printer and bookseller of Paris. If anyone publishes it otherwise, he shall be fined one thousand pounds, as is set out in the decree itself. Given at Paris, on the thirty-first day of December, in the year 1634.

units.la: VIRO ILLVSTRISSIMO FRANCISCO AVGVSTO THVANO IACOBI AVGVSTI FILIO, CONSISTORIANO COMITI, ET LIBELLORVM SVPPLICVM IN REGIA MAGISTRO,
units.tr: TO THE MOST ILLUSTRIOUS MAN FRANCIS AUGUSTUS THUANUS, SON OF JAMES AUGUSTUS, COUNSELLOR OF THE CONSISTORY, AND MASTER OF REQUESTS IN THE KING'S COUNCIL,

units.la: SAMVEL PETITVS.
units.tr: SAMUEL PETITUS.

units.la: CVM animo mecum reputo ingentes illas, FRANCISCE AVGVSTE THVANE, VIR ILLVSTRISSIME, quasi in te, quasi hereditario iure collatas miramur, virtutes; cùm dignitatem amplissimam, te hac [illegible, ~9 letters] cōpellare, tenuitatis meae mihi probe conscius, & operae leuidensis, vix audeo: Eductus quippe atque educatus inter ipsos poene dixerim literarum hostes, non est quod sperem quicquam à me, quod aetatem ferat, in publicum edi posse: neque adeo me ipse amo, vt tibi probari hoc quicquid est libelli, quod nomini tuo, si pateris, VIR ILLVSTRISSIME, eo consecratum, confidam: [illegible, ~20 letters]. Verum animos mihi addidit, vt auderem, veneranda LEGVM, quarum syllogen do, & interpretationem facio, maiestas, & eorum, plerorumque certe, qui has condidere LEGES, sancti atque ad virtutem facti mores, & inclyta famâ gloria: maxime cum vnicè optarent domum tuam, tot tuorum imaginibus maiorum claram, adire, & ad te de suis referre LEGIBVS, quo maiori, imo certa cum spe earum ferendarum, tuae beati praeiudicio sententiae, illas promulgent, ac literatum populum rogent: Atque hic quidem merito illis sensus est, fuit quippe domus tua aliquot ab hinc retro seculis Themidis sacrarium, Vosque ex illa inter principes Iustitiæ Sacerdotes, de quibus verè dixerim quicquid Græcia mendax audet in historiis de suo Solone, Thalete, Æschylo, Demetrio Phalereo, aliis, quibus Rempublicam suam optimis ornatam LEGIBVS, atque constitutam Atheniensis imputat populus: Sed vt & tibi, VIR ILLVSTRISSIME, eos in ædes tuas admittendi sit animus, cùm nullo possim meo merito, precè à te expeto, & enixè rogo: ita faxit Deus Opt. Max. sic voueo, sic spero, vt, qui sanctissimum tuum parentem, qui maiores tuos, viros supra omnem laudem, iam virtutibus æquasti, cumulatis honoribus longe superes. Vale
units.tr: When I reflect within myself on those great virtues, Francis Augustus Thuanus, most illustrious sir, which we admire as though they were handed down to you by hereditary right, and when I consider your most ample dignity, I scarcely dare to address you, being well aware of my own slightness and of the trifling nature of this work. Brought up, indeed, and educated, I might almost say, among the enemies of letters, I have no reason to hope that anything from me, of whatever quality, can be published that will endure the age. Nor do I love myself so much as to trust that this little book, whatever it is, will please you, though I have dedicated it to your name, if you permit it, most illustrious sir. [illegible, ~20 letters]. Yet what gave me the courage to dare was the venerable majesty of the LAWS, whose collection I give and whose interpretation I offer, and the holy and virtuous conduct, and the renowned glory, of their authors, or at least of most of those who framed these laws. Especially since they most earnestly wished to approach your house, so renowned for the portraits of so many of your ancestors, and to bring their laws before you, so that, with your blessed judgment as a guarantee, or rather with a sure hope of their enactment, they might promulgate them and ask the literate public to receive them. And indeed they had good reason for this, for your house was for several centuries past a sanctuary of Themis, and from it came you, priests of justice among the chief men, of whom one may truly say whatever lying Greece dares to claim in its histories about their Solon, Thales, Aeschylus, Demetrius of Phalerum, and the others, by whom the Athenian people credit their commonwealth as having been adorned and established with the best laws. But so that you, most illustrious sir, may have the inclination to admit them into your house, since I can make this request of you by no merit of my own, I ask you humbly and earnestly: may God, the best and greatest, grant it. Thus I pray, thus I vow, thus I hope, that you, who have already equalled in virtue your most revered father and your ancestors, men beyond all praise, may far surpass them in heaped-up honours. Farewell.

units.la: VIR ILLVSRISSIME. Scripsimus Lutetiæ Parisiorum
units.tr: MOST ILLUSTRIOUS SIR. Written at Paris.

units.la: A. D. VIII. kal. Ianuarias anni Dionysiani MDXXXV.
units.tr: On the eighth day before the Kalends of January, in the year of Dionysius 1635.

units.la: LEGES A SAMVEL COLLEGIT E LIBER P
units.tr: THE LAWS OF ATTICA COLLECTED BY SAMUEL PETIT, FROM THE BOOK P, ARRANGED AND COMMENTED UPON

units.la: DE DEORVM CVLTV DIEBVS FESTIS TITVLVS
units.tr: ON THE DAYS OF FESTIVALS IN THE WORSHIP OF THE GODS TITLE

units.la: α'. ΘΕΟΥΣ καρπῶις ἀχάλ-λειν.
units.tr: 1. The gods are to be honoured with the fruits of the season [ΘΕΟΥΣ καρποῖς ἀχαλλεῖν].

units.la: β'. * Θεσμὸς αἰώνιος τῆς Ἀθηνᾶς νεμοιῶμοις κύριος † ἀπόυτε χρόνον, Θεοῖς ἡμᾶν καὶ Ἡρωας ἐγχωρίους ἐν χώρᾳ, ἐμποιήμοις νόμοις παν-τεῖοις, ἰδίας, κ' δωάμιν στῶ θύφημία, ὁ Ἀρχῆς καρπῶν πιλαφόροις ἐπετηίους.
units.tr: 2. An eternal ordinance of Athena: the gods and the local heroes in the land are to be honoured according to the ancestral laws, with the first fruits of each season offered as the law prescribes, in the manner and to the extent that the magistrates have established [Θεσμὸς αἰώνιος τῆς Ἀθηνᾶς … Ἡρωας ἐγχωρίους ἐν χώρᾳ, ἐμποιήμοις νόμοις παντείοις].

units.la: γ'. Γεῦσατον καὶ δραχμιλῶ, πι' ἀὸπ μεδίμνου.
units.tr: 3. Let a drachma be given from each medimnus [Γεῦσατον καὶ δραχμιλῶ, πι' ἀπὸ μεδίμνου].

units.la: δ'. * Τὰ ἔκχρηστα ἱερσα.
units.tr: 4. The sacred things set apart for use [Τὰ ἔκχρηστα ἱερά].

units.la: ε'. Τοῖς ἐκ Ουσίας ἰσιζας, φέρειν ἐξ αὐτῆς ουσίας τῆς οἰκείοις.
units.tr: 5. For those who belong to the estate, let them bring from the estate itself to their own [Τοῖς ἐκ οὐσίας ἰσιζας, φέρειν ἐξ αὐτῆς οὐσίας τῆς οἰκείοις].

units.la: ς'. Τὰ ὑπολειπόμενα τῆς ουσίας τοῖς ἱερεὺς λαμβάνειν.
units.tr: 6. The remainders of the estate are for the priests to receive [Τὰ ὑπολειπόμενα τῆς οὐσίας τοῖς ἱερεὺς λαμβάνειν].

units.la: ζ'. Τὸ ἀλλότρια [?] ἐν ταῖς [?] τῷ Ἀπόλλωνος ἐκωτὸν ἀπιάσθαι, καὶ [?].
units.tr: 7. The … of Apollo, that which belongs to others among the … is to be taken for oneself, and … [Obscura; Τὸ ἀλλότρια … τῷ Ἀπόλλωνος ἐκωτὸν ἀπιάσθαι, καὶ].

units.la: η'. Τοῖς ξένοις, καὶ τῆς δούλοις ἐλθῶν ἔξεσθαι εἰς τὰ ἱερὰ τὰ δημοτελῆ, ἐ ζαοσα-μένοις καὶ ἰκετυσσιοῖς εἰσιέναι.
units.tr: 8. For strangers and slaves who come to enter the public sacred rites, let them enter only after they have been purified and have made their suppliant offerings [Τοῖς ξένοις, καὶ τῆς δούλοις ἐλθῶν ἔξεσθαι εἰς τὰ ἱερὰ τὰ δημοτελῆ, ἐ ζαοσαμένοις καὶ ἰκετυσσιοῖς εἰσιέναι].

units.la: θ'. Τοῖς ἀσυπερπάτμοις μὴ ἐξεῖναι εἰσι-έναι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν Σεμνῶν [?].
units.tr: 9. For those who are unpurified, it is not permitted to enter the temple of the Semnai [Τοῖς ἀσυπερπάτμοις μὴ ἐξεῖναι εἰσιέναι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν Σεμνῶν].

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters]ATTICÆ, [illegible, ~3 letters]PETITVS [illegible, ~4 letters] T DIGESSIT. [illegible, ~2 letters]RIMVS.
units.tr: LEGES ATTICAE: Sam Petit has collected and arranged them. BOOK FIRST.

units.la: [illegible, ~3 letters], SACRIS ÆDIBVS, [illegible, ~3 letters]S, ET LVDIS.
units.tr: [illegible], ON SACRED BUILDINGS, [illegible], AND GAMES.

units.la: PRIMVS.
units.tr: FIRST.

units.la: DEOS frugibus venerantor.
units.tr: Let them honour the gods with the fruits of the earth.

units.la: Lex esto antiquissima, æternæque auctoritatis in Attica, Venerandos esse Deos, atq; Heroas patrios & indigenas publicè secundum patrias sanctiones, priuatim verò bonis verbis, frugumq; primitiis, libis annuis, pro facultatum modulo.
units.tr: Let this be the most ancient law, of eternal authority in Attica: that the gods and the native and ancestral heroes are to be venerated, publicly according to the ancestral ordinances, and privately with good words, with first-fruits of the crops and yearly cakes, according to each person's means.

units.la: Drachmain [?] ouem, octodecim in medimnum.
units.tr: A drachma for each sheep; eighteen [drachmas] per medimnus.

units.la: Eximiæ hostiæ.
units.tr: Choice victims.

units.la: Qui sacra fecerunt, aliud è victimis domum referunto.
units.tr: Those who have performed the sacred rites shall carry home another portion of the victims.

units.la: Reliqua ex sacris victimis cedunto Sacerdotibus.
units.tr: The remaining parts of the sacred victims shall go to the priests.

units.la: Qui in æde Apollinis ventrem exonerauerit, seipsum in iudicio deserto, eique capital esto.
units.tr: Whoever defecates in the temple of Apollo shall be deprived of his standing in court, and it shall be a capital offence for him.

units.la: Peregrinis seruisq; fas esto publica Atheniensis populi Templa adire, vel videndi causa, ibidemque supplicibus sedere.
units.tr: It is lawful for foreigners and slaves to enter the public temples of the Athenian people, whether to look on, and to sit there as suppliants.

units.la: Redeuntibus postliminio ab hostibus, fas non esto sacellum Eumenidum adire.
units.tr: Those returning from the enemy by postliminium may not enter the shrine of the Eumenides.

units.la: Supplices Sacrosancti sunto.
units.tr: Suppliants shall be inviolable.

units.la: Die populo Atheniensium festo ne cuiquam, sive privatim, sive publice iniuria fiat, neve habetor concio de aliis rebus, quam iis quæ ad festorum religionem pertinent.
units.tr: On the festival day of the Athenian people, no one shall be wronged, either privately or publicly, and no assembly shall be held on any business other than that which pertains to the religious observance of the festivals.

units.la: Nefas esto in veste tincta Panathenæorum pompam ludosque spectare.
units.tr: It is forbidden to watch the procession and the games of the Panathenaea in a dyed garment.

units.la: Panathenæis maioribus Rapsodi Homeri carmina recitanto.
units.tr: At the greater Panathenaea, rhapsodes shall recite the songs of Homer.

units.la: Inquilini in pompa ligones ferunto: Eorumque filiæ hydrias & umbellas.
units.tr: Resident aliens shall carry mattocks in the procession, and their daughters the water-jars and parasols.

units.la: Peregrinum Mysteriis ne initiaro.
units.tr: Do not initiate a foreigner into the Mysteries.

units.la: Qui Mysteria vulgarit, ei capital esto.
units.tr: Whoever divulges the Mysteries, let it be a capital offence for him.

units.la: Initiati, qua tunc essent amicti veste, Deabus, consecranto.
units.tr: Initiates shall consecrate themselves to the goddesses, dressed in whatever garments they then wear.

units.la: Fœmina bigis ad sacra Eleusinia ne vehitor: siqua secus faxit, multa drachmarum sex mille irrogator.
units.tr: A woman shall not be conveyed to the Eleusinian rites in a two-horse chariot; if anyone does otherwise, a fine of six thousand drachmas shall be imposed.

units.la: Libellum supplicem Mysteriorum diebus ne offerto.
units.tr: Do not present a suppliant petition on the days of the Mysteries.

units.la: Nemini Mysteriorum diebus manum iniiciro.
units.tr: No one shall lay hands on another on the days of the Mysteries.

units.la: Postridie Mysteriorum Senatus in Eleusinio habetor.
units.tr: On the day after the Mysteries the Senate shall meet in the Eleusinion.

units.la: Quotannis Thesmophoria celebrantor.
units.tr: The Thesmophoria shall be celebrated every year.

units.la: Thesmophoriis nexi vinculis solu-untor.
units.tr: At the Thesmophoria, those held in bonds shall be loosed from their chains.

units.la: Cum pompe Libero ducitur in Piræo, agunt Comœdi & Tragœdi, item Lenæa pompa, & agentibus Tragœdis atque Comœdis: Astycorum quoque Liberalium pompa, saltante puerorum choro, dum fit Comus, aguntque Comœdi & Tragœdi: Thargelorum item pompa & certamine: neque quidquam alterius capito, neque pœnam pro mora exigito ab eo, qui iudicatum non soluerit:
units.tr: When the procession of Dionysus (Liber) is led to the Piraeus, comic and tragic actors shall perform, likewise the Lenaean procession, with tragic and comic actors performing; also the procession of the Astic Liberalia, with a chorus of boys dancing while the revel (comus) is held, and comic and tragic actors performing; likewise the procession and contest of the Thargelia. Nor shall anyone seize anything from another, nor exact a penalty for delay from one who has not paid a judgment.

units.la: ι'. Τοὺς ἱκέτας [?] ἀσφαλῆς.
units.tr: Suppliants [are] secure. [Τοὺς ἱκέτας ἀσφαλῆς]

units.la: ια'. Ἀποψιτῶν τῆς Ἀθηναίων ἀγόντων ἐ-σμυλωίας μήτ' ἰδίᾳ, μήτε κοινῇ μηδὲν δι-λήλους ἀδικεῖν ἐν τούτῳ τῷ χρείῳ, μηδὲ χρηματίζειν, ὃ, τι αὖ μὴ τοῖς ἑορ-τῆς ἡ[?].
units.tr: Of the resident foreigners, who are leading the Athenian ... festival: neither privately nor in common shall anyone wrong another during this time, nor conduct public business, except what pertains to the festival. [Ἀποψιτῶν τῆς Ἀθηναίων ἀγόντων ... μήτ' ἰδίᾳ, μήτε κοινῇ μηδὲν ἀδικεῖν ἐν τούτῳ τῷ χρόνῳ, μηδὲ χρηματίζειν ...]

units.la: ιβ'. Ἐν τοῖς τῆς Παναθηναίων ἀγῶνι μὴ ἐξξῆναι τοῖς βαπτὸν ἔχοντι ἱμάτιον θεά-σθαι.
units.tr: At the contest of the Panathenaea, it shall not be permitted for one wearing a dyed cloak to watch. [Ἐν τοῖς τῆς Παναθηναίων ἀγῶνι μὴ ἐξεῖναι τοῖς βαπτὸν ἔχοντι ἱμάτιον θεᾶσθαι.]

units.la: ιγ'. Καθ' ἑκάστῳ πενταετηρίδα Παναθηναίων τὰ τῶ Ὁμήρου ἐπὶ ῥαψῳδεῖ-σθαι.
units.tr: Every fifth year at the Panathenaea, the works of Homer are to be recited rhapsodically. [Καθ' ἑκάστην πενταετηρίδα Παναθηναίων τὰ τοῦ Ὁμήρου ἐπὶ ῥαψῳδεῖσθαι.]

units.la: ιδ'. Τοὺς μυρίκους ἐν ταῖς πομπαῖς αὐτοῖς μὴ σκάφας φέρειν· ἐς δὲ ζυγατίσας αὐτῶν ὕδρῳα, καὶ σκιάδα.
units.tr: The myrtle-bearers in the processions shall not carry bowls; but [they shall carry] yoked ... of them, and a sunshade. [Τοὺς μυρίκους ἐν ταῖς πομπαῖς αὐτοῖς μὴ σκάφας φέρειν· ἐς δὲ ζυγατίσας αὐτῶν ὕδρῳα, καὶ σκιάδα.]

units.la: ιε'. Μηδεὶς ξένον μύῳ[?].
units.tr: Let no one ... a foreigner ... the Mysteries. [Μηδεὶς ξένον μύῳ ...]

units.la: ιϛ'. Τὸν ἐξεπίτροπα τὰ Μυστήρια, πε-[?].
units.tr: The one entrusted with the Mysteries ... [Τὸν ἐξεπίτροπα τὰ Μυστήρια ...]

units.la: ιζ'. Ἐν οἷς ἂν ἱματίοις μοιχεῖν, εἰς τὴν ἡμέραν ταῦτα διαλλαγὴν[?].
units.tr: In whatever garments one commits adultery, on that day these ... are to be exchanged. [Ἐν οἷς ἂν ἱματίοις μοιχεῖν, εἰς τὴν ἡμέραν ταῦτα διαλλαγὴν ...]

units.la: ιη'. Ἐπὶ ζητήσεις μὴ ἀπιέναι γυναῖκα Ἐλευσινάδε· εἰ δὲ ἂς φωραθείη, ἀπὸ τῆς δραχμὰς ἑξακισχιλίας.
units.tr: A woman shall not go to the Eleusinian rites to seek ...; if she is caught, [the penalty is] six thousand drachmas. [Ἐπὶ ζητήσεις μὴ ἀπιέναι γυναῖκα Ἐλευσινάδε· εἰ δὲ ἂς φωραθείη, ἀπὸ τῆς δραχμὰς ἑξακισχιλίας.]

units.la: ιθ'. Μὴ ὑβρίζειν ἱκετείαν τῆς Μυστ-ηρίοις.
units.tr: Not to outrage the suppliant rite at the Mysteries. [Μὴ ὑβρίζειν ἱκετείαν τῆς Μυστηρίοις.]

units.la: κ'. Μηδενὸς τοῖς Μυστηρίοις ἐπιλαμβά-νεσθαι.
units.tr: No one shall be seized during the Mysteries. [Μηδενὸς τοῖς Μυστηρίοις ἐπιλαμβάνεσθαι.]

units.la: κα'. Τῷ βουλῷ τῆ ὑστεραίᾳ τῶν Μυ-στηρίων ἔδραν ποιεῖν τὸ τῶν Ἐλευσινίῳ.
units.tr: On the day after the Mysteries the Council shall hold its session at the Eleusinion. [Τῇ βουλῇ τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ τῶν Μυστηρίων ἕδραν ποιεῖν τὸ τῶν Ἐλευσινίῳ.]

units.la: κϛ'. Κατ' ἔτος πάλιν τὰ Θεσμοφό-ρια.
units.tr: Again, every year, the Thesmophoria. [Κατ' ἔτος πάλιν τὰ Θεσμοφόρια.]

units.la: κγ'. Ἐν τῆς Θεσμοφορίοις λύεσθαι τὰς δισμωτάς.
units.tr: At the Thesmophoria the prisoners shall be released. [Ἐν τοῖς Θεσμοφορίοις λύεσθαι τὰς δεσμώτας.]

units.la: κδ'. * Εὐήγγελος εἶπεν ὅταν ἡ πομ-πὴ ἡ τοῦ Διονύσου ἐς Πειραιεῖ, καὶ οἱ Κω-μῳδοὶ καὶ οἱ Τραγῳδοί, καὶ ὅτι Λιωαῖς Γομπὴ, καὶ οἱ Τραγῳδοί, καὶ οἱ Κω-μῳδοί, καὶ τῆς ἐν ἄστει Διονυσίοις ἢ Γομ-πὴ, καὶ οἱ παῖδες, καὶ ὁ Κάλμος, καὶ οἱ Κωμῳδοί, καὶ οἱ Τραγῳδοί, καὶ Θαρ-γηλίων τῇ Γομπῇ, καὶ τῶν ἀγῶνι μήτε ἕξειν, μήτε ἐπεχεῖσθαι, μηδὲ λαμβά-νειν ἕτερον ἑτέρου, μηδὲ τῶν ἐξημέ-ρων ἐν τοῖς ἑώρταις ἐμέρεις· ἐὰν δέ τι πύτῶν τὶς ἀσεβαίη, ὑπόδικος ἔσω τῷ παιδοτ[?], καὶ παθοόλαι κατ' αὐτὸ ἐσω-σθν ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησία τῇ ἐν Διονύσου, ὡς ἀδικοῦντας καὶ ἀ ταῖς τῶν ἄλλων ἀδικουμένων γέγονασι[?].
units.tr: Euangelos said that when the procession of Dionysus goes to the Piraeus, and the comic and tragic poets, and the Lenaean procession, and the tragic and comic poets, and at the city Dionysia the procession, and the boys, and the Kalmos, and the comic and tragic poets, and the Thargelian procession, and in the contest neither to have nor to hold back, nor to take one thing from another, nor ... on the festival days; and if anyone of them acts impiously, he shall be liable ... and let him be ... in the assembly at the sanctuary of Dionysus, as having wronged, and ... as the others have been wronged. [Εὐήγγελος εἶπεν ὅταν ἡ πομπὴ ἡ τοῦ Διονύσου ἐς Πειραιεῖ, καὶ οἱ Κωμῳδοὶ καὶ οἱ Τραγῳδοί, καὶ ὅτι Λιωαῖς Γομπὴ, καὶ οἱ Τραγῳδοί, καὶ οἱ Κωμῳδοί, καὶ τῆς ἐν ἄστει Διονυσίοις ἢ Γομπὴ, καὶ οἱ παῖδες, καὶ ὁ Κάλμος, καὶ οἱ Κωμῳδοί, καὶ οἱ Τραγῳδοί, καὶ Θαργηλίων τῇ Γομπῇ, καὶ τῶν ἀγῶνι μήτε ἕξειν, μήτε ἐπεχεῖσθαι, μηδὲ λαμβάνειν ἕτερον ἑτέρου, μηδὲ τῶν ἐξημέρων ἐν τοῖς ἑώρταις ἐμέρεις· ἐὰν δέ τι πύτῶν τὶς ἀσεβαίη, ὑπόδικος ἔσω τῷ παιδοτ..., καὶ παθοόλαι κατ' αὐτὸ ἐσωσθν ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησία τῇ ἐν Διονύσου, ὡς ἀδικοῦντας καὶ ἀ ταῖς τῶν ἄλλων ἀδικουμένων γέγονασι.]

units.la: κε'. * Τοῖς Πρυτάνεσι ποιῆν ἐκκλησίαν ἐν Διονύσου τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ ἐν Γαμδίοις, ἐν δὲ ταύτῃ χειροτονεῖν ποῆσαι μὴ ταῖς ἱεραῖς, ἔπειτα καὶ ταῖς παθόλαις παραδιδόσ-θω καὶ γαλλιμίας ἕνεκα τῆς πομπῆς, ἢ τῶν ἀγώνων τῶν ἐν ταῖς Διονυσίοις, ἐσαν δὲ μὴ ἐκπεπληρωμέναι ὦσιν.
units.tr: To the Prytanes: let them hold an assembly in the sanctuary of Dionysus on the day after, in the Gamelion; and in this assembly they shall not elect for the sacred ..., then also let [matters] be handed over ... for the sake of the procession, or of the contests at the Dionysia, if they have not been completed. [Τοῖς Πρυτάνεσι ποιεῖν ἐκκλησίαν ἐν Διονύσου τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ ἐν Γαμηλίοις, ἐν δὲ ταύτῃ χειροτονεῖν ... ἔπειτα καὶ ταῖς παθόλαις παραδιδόσθω ... τῆς πομπῆς, ἢ τῶν ἀγώνων τῶν ἐν ταῖς Διονυσίοις, ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἐκπεπληρωμέναι ὦσιν.]

units.la: κς'. Μυδείου τῆς Διονυσίοις ἐπιλαμβ-ἀνεσθαι.
units.tr: Not to seize anyone at the Dionysia. [Μηδένα τῆς Διονυσίοις ἐπιλαμβάνεσθαι.]

units.la: κζ'. Δημοσίᾳ μηδένα ἀποκτιννύσθαι πρὶν ἂν εἰς Δῆλον ἀφίκηται ὁ πλοῖον, καὶ πάλιν δδῖσ[?].
units.tr: No one shall be put to death publicly before the sacred ship has arrived at Delos, and again ... [Δημοσίᾳ μηδένα ἀποκτιννύσθαι πρὶν ἂν εἰς Δῆλον ἀφίκηται ὁ πλοῖον, καὶ πάλιν ...]

units.la: κη'. Ἀλωσις ἱερὰ μὴ ἐχεῖν.
units.tr: Not to hold a sacred capture. [Ἁλωσις ἱερὰ μὴ ἔχειν.]

units.la: κθ'. Τῷ Ὀλυμπία νικήσαντι δραχμὰς πεντακοσίας δίδοσθαι.
units.tr: To the victor at Olympia, five hundred drachmas shall be given. [Τῷ Ὀλυμπίᾳ νικήσαντι δραχμὰς πεντακοσίας δίδοσθαι.]

units.la: λ'. Τῷ Ἰσθμια νικήσαντι δραχμὰς ἑκατὸν δίδοσθαι.
units.tr: To the victor at the Isthmus, one hundred drachmas shall be given. [Τῷ Ἰσθμίᾳ νικήσαντι δραχμὰς ἑκατὸν δίδοσθαι.]

units.la: λα'. Τὸν Τραγικὸν Χορὸν στεφανίσαι ἐκ πεντεκαιδεκα.
units.tr: The tragic chorus shall be crowned from fifteen [persons]. [Τὸν Τραγικὸν Χορὸν στεφανίσαι ἐκ πεντεκαίδεκα.]

units.la: λβ'. Τὰς Τραγῳδίας τῆς ποιητῆς, Αἰσχύλου, Σοφοκλέους, Εὐριπίδου, τῶν Γραμματικῶν τῆς πόλεως ἀποδιαχινώσκειν πῶς ὑποκριτομένοις οὐκ ἀξίως αὐτὰς ὑποκρίνεσθαι.
units.tr: The tragedies of the poets Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides shall be examined by the city's grammarians, so that those who act them do not perform them unworthily. [Τὰς Τραγῳδίας τῶν ποιητῶν, Αἰσχύλου, Σοφοκλέους, Εὐριπίδου, τῶν Γραμματικῶν τῆς πόλεως ἀποδιακινώσκειν ...]

units.la: λγ'. Τὸν ἐπὶ τῆς Κωμῳδῶν ἀγῶνα πῶς ζῶσις ὑπέπλεξιν ἐφάμιλλον ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, καὶ τὸν νικήσαντα εἰς ἄγυ καταλέγεσθαι.
units.tr: The comic contest: that the choregoi (producers) be ... in the day, and the victor be enrolled in the ... [Τὸν ἐπὶ τῆς Κωμῳδῶν ἀγῶνα ... ἐφάμιλλον ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, καὶ τὸν νικήσαντα εἰς ἄγυ καταλέγεσθαι.]

units.la: λδ'. Μὴ εἰσπλέειν ἕνα εἰπεῖν, μὴ πω διαχωρίζειν ἐπὶ γεγονότα.
units.tr: Not to sail in to speak, not to separate ... [Μὴ εἰσπλέειν ἕνα εἰπεῖν, μὴ πω διαχωρίζειν ἐπὶ γεγονότα.]

units.la: Τὸν Ἀρχοντα μὴ Φαυερὰς κωμῳδεῖν.
units.tr: The Archon shall not openly mock in comedy. [Τὸν Ἄρχοντα μὴ Φανερὰς κωμῳδεῖν.]

units.la: λς'. Μὴ κωμῳδεῖν ἐξ ὀνόματος.
units.tr: Not to mock by name in comedy. [Μὴ κωμῳδεῖν ἐξ ὀνόματος.]

units.la: λζ'. Τῷ Μοισικῷ κατ' εἴδη ἑαυτῆς διαιρεῖσθαι, καὶ οὐκ ἐξεῖναι ἄλλῳ εἰς ἄλλο καταχρῆσθαι μέλοις εἴδος.
units.tr: Music shall be divided according to its own kinds, and it shall not be permitted for one kind of music to be misused for another. [Τῷ Μουσικῷ κατ' εἴδη ἑαυτῆς διαιρεῖσθαι, καὶ οὐκ ἐξεῖναι ἄλλῳ εἰς ἄλλο καταχρῆσθαι μέλοις εἶδος.]

units.la: λη'. Εὐκοσμίαν ἔχειν τὸ τῆς θεάτρου ἄρχοντα τῆς ὑπηρεσίας ἐξ[illegible, ~6 letters] τὸν Qui secus faxit, accusator à læso & parabolæ aduersus eum dantor apud populum, pro concione in Bacchi, sirempse Lege, qui aduersus alios, qui festi religionem temerarint.
units.tr: The Archon of the theatre shall maintain good order in the theatre ... [Εὐκοσμίαν ἔχειν τὸ τῆς θεάτρου ἄρχοντα τῆς ὑπηρεσίας ...] Whoever acts otherwise, the accuser from the injured party shall be given a summons before the people, in the assembly at the Bacchus [theatre], according to the law, against those who violated the religion of the festival.

units.la: Prytaneis concionem in Bacchi cogunto, Pandiis, postridie Dionysiorum, & de sacris primum referunto, Probolæ deinde dantor de iniuriis illatis, pompæ vel Ludorum Dionysiacorum caussa, de quibus transactum non fuerit.
units.tr: The Prytanes shall convene an assembly in the theatre of Bacchus on the Pandia, the day after the Dionysia, and shall first report on the sacred matters; then a preliminary hearing shall be granted concerning the injuries inflicted, on account of the procession or the Dionysiac games, concerning which nothing has been settled.

units.la: Nemini diebus Liberalium festis manum iniicito.
units.tr: On the festival days of the Liberalia, no one shall be laid hands on.

units.la: Deliorum festos dies, dum Delum itur, reditur, Damnatorum suppliciis ne funestato.
units.tr: On the festival days of Delos, while the journey to Delos is made and returned from, do not pollute them with the executions of condemned persons.

units.la: Alois victimam ne mactato.
units.tr: Do not slaughter a victim on the threshing-floors.

units.la: Olympionicis quingentæ de publico drachmæ dantor.
units.tr: To Olympic victors, five hundred drachmas shall be given from the public treasury.

units.la: Isthmionicis centum de publico drachmæ dantor.
units.tr: To Isthmian victors, one hundred drachmas shall be given from the public treasury.

units.la: Tragicorum Chorus è quindecim personis constituitor.
units.tr: The tragic chorus shall be constituted of fifteen persons.

units.la: Æschyli, Sophoclis & Euripidis Tragœdias, vrbis Scriba publicè prælegito. Histriones eas ne agunto.
units.tr: The public clerk of the city shall read aloud publicly the tragedies of Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides. Actors shall not perform them.

units.la: Comœdi Anthesteriis fabulas docento atque cömittunto in Theatro. Victorem Ciuitate donato.
units.tr: Comic poets shall teach their plays at the Anthesteria and shall compete in the theatre. The victor shall be honoured by the city.

units.la: Histrio fabulam ne agito annorū triginta minor.
units.tr: An actor under thirty years of age shall not perform a play.

units.la: Magistratui in comœdia conuiciū palam ne facito.
units.tr: Do not openly revile a magistrate in comedy.

units.la: Nemini in comœdia expresso nomine conuicium facito.
units.tr: No one shall be reviled by name in comedy.

units.la: Musica in sua genera distribuitor, eaque ne inuicem permutantor.
units.tr: Music shall be divided into its own kinds, and these shall not be exchanged with one another.

units.la: Spectatores sine rixa in Theatro sedento. qui secus fecerit, Archontis iussu ab apparitoribus submouetor , ni paret, multator.
units.tr: Spectators shall sit in the theatre without brawling. Whoever acts otherwise shall be removed by the attendants at the order of the Archon, and if he does not obey, shall be fined.

units.la: Neptuno ludi celebrantor in Pyræo choris tribus ad minimum ἐγκωμίοις[?] saltantibus. Decem minæ victori præmium esto. Octo ei, qui secundas. Sex vero ei qui tertias obtinuerit.
units.tr: Games shall be celebrated for Neptune at the Piraeus, with at least three choruses dancing. Ten minae shall be the prize for the victor, eight for the one who comes second, and six for the one who obtains third place.

units.la: Galli gallinacei publicè committuntor in Theatro , uno quotannis die.
units.tr: Cock-fights shall be held publicly in the theatre, on one day each year.

units.la: Mensium Kalendis sacra facito.
units.tr: Perform sacrifice on the Kalends of each month.

units.la: De Sacrorun[?]
units.tr: On the Sacred Rites

units.la: TITVLVS S[?]
units.tr: TITLE S[?]

units.la: Rex è Novemviris unus, ut Parasitos constituant, & è singulis secundum Leges eligant populis curato. Parasiti singuli sine dolo malo seponunto hecteum hordei è parte quisque sua. Athenienses epulo in templo excipiunto secundum patrium morem. Acharnensium Parasiti ex illo, quod collegerunt, hordei hecteū Apollini in apothecis reponunto.
units.tr: The king, one of the Nine Archons, shall take care to appoint Parasites and choose them from each of the tribes according to the laws. Each Parasite shall without fraud set aside a hekteus of barley from his own share. The Athenians shall receive them at a feast in the temple according to ancestral custom. The Parasites of the Acharnians shall deposit in the storehouses for Apollo the hekteus of barley which they have collected.

units.la: Parasiti Acharnensium Sacra Apollini faciunto.
units.tr: The Parasites of the Acharnians shall perform the sacred rites to Apollo.

units.la: Rex, quisquis is erit, cum Parasitis, quos è singulis antea elegerint populis, cum senibus item, atque fœminis univiris, curato.
units.tr: Whoever the king is, he shall take care of these matters together with the Parasites whom they have previously chosen from each tribe, and likewise with the elders and the women married once only.

units.la: Sacerdos cum Parasitis menstrua sacra facito. Parasiti de Nothis, aut Nothorum liberis unum eligunto secundum morem patrium: si Parasitari detrectat in ius vocanto.
units.tr: The priest shall perform the monthly sacred rites with the Parasites. The Parasites shall choose one man from the bastards, or from the children of bastards, according to ancestral custom; if he refuses to act as Parasite, summon him to court.

units.la: Duo Ceryces sunto è genere Cerycum Mysticorum, ijdemque annum, in Delio Templo Parasiti sunto.
units.tr: There shall be two Ceryces from the family of the Mystic Ceryces, and these same men shall be Parasites for the year in the temple at Delos.

units.la: Duorum boum præcidaneorum eximiorum tertia pars in certamen: reliquarum duarum una sacerdoti: altera Parasitis cedunto.
units.tr: A third part of two choice first-fruit oxen shall go to the contest; one of the remaining two shall go to the priest, and the other to the Parasites.

units.la: Ad sarta tecta Templi, Apothecæ, [illegible, ~3 letters]ν, ἐπιβολῶ ἐπιβάλλειν.
units.tr: For the roofing and repair of the temple, the storehouses, ... to impose (?) [ἐπιβολῶ, ἐπιβάλλειν].

units.la: λϑ′. Τοῦ Ποσειδῶνος ἀγῶνα παῖδι ἐν Γειγειῇ, κυκλίων χορῶν οὐχ ἔλαττον [?]τειῶν. Διδόσθαι [?]ἀπὸ τῆς νικῶσιν οὐχ ἔλαττον δίκης [?]μνᾶς. τῆς δὲ δωδεκάτης, ὀκτὼ. ἐξ δὲ τῆς πεντάκις χρηζῶν.
units.tr: 39. Of the contest of Poseidon for boys at Geigeis, of cyclic choruses not fewer than ... To the winners shall be given not less than one mina ..., and in the twelfth (year) eight ..., and from the five times ... [λϑ′. Τοῦ Ποσειδῶνος ἀγῶνα παῖδι ἐν Γειγειῇ, κυκλίων χορῶν οὐχ ἔλαττον ... Διδόσθαι ... ἀπὸ τῆς νικῶσιν οὐχ ἔλαττον δίκης ... μνᾶς. τῆς δὲ δωδεκάτης, ὀκτὼ. ἐξ δὲ τῆς πεντάκις].

units.la: μ′. Ἀλεκτρυόνας ἀγωνίζεσθαι δημοσίᾳ [?]ἐν τῷ πατρῷ μιᾶς ἡμέρας τῆς ἔτους.
units.tr: 40. Cocks shall compete publicly in the ancestral place on one day of the year [μ′. Ἀλεκτρυόνας ἀγωνίζεσθαι δημοσίᾳ ... ἐν τῷ πατρῷ μιᾶς ἡμέρας τῆς ἔτους].

units.la: μα′. Ταῖς Νομιλωίαις ζῆν.
units.tr: 41. To the Nomilōiai, to live [μα′. Ταῖς Νομιλωίαις ζῆν].

units.la: [?]ἐν Ministris. SECVNDVS.
units.tr: ... among the Ministers. Second.

units.la: α′. * Ἐπιμελεῖσθαι δὲ τὸν Βασιλέωντα τῆ τε ἡγεχόντων, ὅπως ἀὐ καθιαζῶνται καὶ τοὺς Γαςσοῖτες ἐν τῇ δήμων αἱρῶνται, ἡ τὰ γαμαμέμνα· τοὺς δ᾽ Γαςσοῖτες ἐκ τῆς βουλεύλιας ἐκλέγῃ ἐκ τῇ μέσῃς τῆς ἑαυτῶν ἕκαστον ἐκ τῆς χρῆσων δαμινάς τοὺς ὅτας Αθηναίους ἐν τῷ ἱερᾷ καὶ τὰ πάτρια· τὸν δ᾽ ἐκτὸς πρέχειν εἰς τὰ ἡγεχεῖα τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος τοῖς Ἀχαρνέων Γαςσοῖτες ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκλογῆς τῶν χρῶν.
units.tr: 1. The king shall take care, together with the leaders, that the sacred rites are duly performed; and they shall choose the Gasmoitai from the tribes, or ... from the council by lot, each from the tribes, to sacrifice for the Athenians in the temple and according to ancestral custom; and the one from outside shall serve at the sacred rites of Apollo for the Acharnian Gasmoitai, chosen from the lot of the ... [α′. Ἐπιμελεῖσθαι δὲ τὸν Βασιλέωντα τῆ τε ἡγεχόντων, ὅπως ... τοὺς Γαςσοῖτες ἐν τῇ δήμων αἱρῶνται ... Αθηναίους ἐν τῷ ἱερᾷ καὶ τὰ πάτρια ... τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος τοῖς Ἀχαρνέων Γαςσοῖτες ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκλογῆς τῶν χρῶν].

units.la: β′. * Θύειν τῷ Ἀπόλλωνι τοὺς Ἀχαρνέων Γαςσοῖτες.
units.tr: 2. The Acharnian Gasmoitai shall sacrifice to Apollo [β′. Θύειν τῷ Ἀπόλλωνι τοὺς Ἀχαρνέων Γαςσοῖτες].

units.la: γ′. * Ἐπιμελεῖσθαι δ᾽ ἡ Βασιλέα τὸν αἰεὶ βασιλεύοντα ἡ τοὺς Γαςσοῖτες, οὓς ἀὐ ἐκ τῆς δήμων ἀποσαίρονται, καὶ τοὺς γεγενῆσθαι, ἡ τὰς γυναῖκας τοῦ ἀφ᾽ ἱεροποιοῖς.
units.tr: 3. The king who always reigns shall take care of the Gasmoitai whom they select from the tribes, and of those who have been born, and of the wives of those from the sacred ... [γ′. Ἐπιμελεῖσθαι δ᾽ ἡ Βασιλέα τὸν αἰεὶ βασιλεύοντα ἡ τοὺς Γαςσοῖτες, οὓς ... καὶ τοὺς γεγενῆσθαι, ἡ τὰς γυναῖκας τοῦ ... ἱεροποιοῖς].

units.la: δ′. * Τὰ δ᾽ ἐπιμελῶνα ζυῖτω ὁ ἱερεύς, μετὰ τῶν Γαςσοῖτων. Οἱ δ᾽ Γαςσοῖτοι εἶα τῆς ἐκ τῶν λόγων ἡ τῶν τυτῶν παιδῶν καὶ πάτρεια, ὃς δ᾽ ἀὐ μὴ θέλῃ ἀποδοκιμῆν, εἰσαγέτω ἡ ἐκ τυτῶν εἰς ὃ δικαστήριον.
units.tr: 4. The priest shall direct these cares together with the Gasmoitai. The Gasmoitai shall ... from the speeches (?) and the (?) of the boys and the ancestral custom; whoever refuses to accept, let him bring him before the court [δ′. Τὰ δ᾽ ἐπιμελῶνα ζυῖτω ὁ ἱερεύς, μετὰ τῶν Γαςσοῖτων. Οἱ δ᾽ Γαςσοῖτοι ... τῆς ἐκ τῶν λόγων ... ὃς δ᾽ ἀὐ μὴ θέλῃ ἀποδοκιμῆν, εἰσαγέτω ... εἰς ... δικαστήριον].

units.la: ε′. * Καὶ τὸ Κήρυκα ἐκ τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς Κηρύκων τῆς Μυσηλιῶνιδος, πύτις δὲ ἀποδοκιμῆν ἐν τῷ Δηλίῳ ἑαυτόν.
units.tr: 5. And the herald, from the day of the Heralds of Mysteliōn, ... let him reject himself at Delos [ε′. Καὶ τὸ Κήρυκα ἐκ τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς Κηρύκων τῆς Μυσηλιῶνιδος, ... ἀποδοκιμῆν ἐν τῷ Δηλίῳ ἑαυτόν].

units.la: ς′. * Τοῖς δὲ βοοῖς τοῖς ἡγεμόνοιν τῆς ἐξαγεμένοιν, ὃ ἀφ᾽ τείπον μέρος εἰς τὸν ἀγῶνα, τὰ δ᾽ δύο μέρη, ὃ ἀφ᾽ ἔπεσιν τῷ ἱερῷ, ὃ ᾗ, πῶς Γαςσοῖτες.
units.tr: 6. For the oxen, the leaders of the sacrifices, one third part goes to the contest and the two parts ... to the sacred (rites), whoever ... the Gasmoitai [ς′. Τοῖς δὲ βοοῖς τοῖς ἡγεμόνοιν τῆς ἐξαγεμένοιν, ὃ ἀφ᾽ τείπον μέρος εἰς τὸν ἀγῶνα, τὰ δ᾽ δύο μέρη ... τῷ ἱερῷ ... Γαςσοῖτες].

units.la: ζ′. * Εἰς τὸν ἀποκοδώ τῷ νεῷ τῷ Ἀρχείου, καὶ τῆ Γαργασίπου, καὶ τῆς οἰκίας τῆς ἱερᾶς διδόναι ὃ ἄργύριον, ὁπόσου δὲ οἱ τῶν ἱερέων ἀποκλᾶσαι μισθώσειν.
units.tr: 7. For the repair of the temple of Archeion and of Gargasipos, and of the sacred house, silver is to be given, at whatever price the priests shall let it out for hire [ζ′. Εἰς τὸν ἀποκοδώ τῷ νεῷ τῷ Ἀρχείου, καὶ τῆ Γαργασίπου, καὶ τῆς οἰκίας τῆς ἱερᾶς διδόναι ὃ ἄργύριον, ὁπόσου δὲ οἱ τῶν ἱερέων ἀποκλᾶσαι μισθώσειν].

units.la: κʹ[?]. Θαλλοφόρεις τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ τοὺς καλοὺς ἐκλέξασθαι.
units.tr: 20. Let them choose the beautiful ones to carry branches for Athena [κʹ. Θαλλοφόρεις τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ τοὺς καλοὺς ἐκλέξασθαι].

units.la: Τὴν γυναῖκα τῆς Βασιλέως ἀξιῶ ἔχ[?], καὶ μὴ ὑπομεμιγμένῳ ἑτέρῳ αἵματι, ἀλλὰ πάρθενον γαμεῖν.
units.tr: I require the king's wife to be ... and not mixed with other blood, but to marry a virgin [Τὴν γυναῖκα τῆς Βασιλέως ἀξιῶ ἔχ[?], καὶ μὴ ὑπομεμιγμένῳ ἑτέρῳ αἵματι, ἀλλὰ πάρθενον γαμεῖν].

units.la: ιʹ. Τοὺς ἱερᾶς καὶ τὰς ἱερείας ἐπαρξώ[?]νεις ἔ[?], οὐ μόνον ἰδία, ἀλλὰ κοινῇ τὰ ἱερά.
units.tr: 10. The priests and priestesses ... not only privately but the sacred rites in common [ιʹ. Τοὺς ἱερᾶς καὶ τὰς ἱερείας ... οὐ μόνον ἰδία, ἀλλὰ κοινῇ τὰ ἱερά].

units.la: ιαʹ. Μηδὲ ἱεροποιῶν ἄγαπος Θεῷ κληρούσθω, ἐὰν ὅτι καθαρεύει ὁ σῶμα.
units.tr: 11. Let no one of the sacrificers be chosen by lot for God, unless the body is clean [ιαʹ. Μηδὲ ἱεροποιῶν ἄγαπος Θεῷ κληρούσθω, ἐὰν ὅτι καθαρεύει ὁ σῶμα].

units.la: ιϛʹ. * Ἐπειδὴ ἀγρίων ἡ θυσία ἔστι τῷ λεῷ.
units.tr: 16. Since the sacrifice is of the wild (?) to the people [ιϛʹ. Ἐπειδὴ ἀγρίων ἡ θυσία ἔστι τῷ λεῷ].

units.la: LIBER De Le[illegible, ~6 letters]
units.tr: BOOK. On Le[illegible, ~6 letters]

units.la: TITVLVS ΕΠΙΧΕΙΡΟΤΟΝΙΑ ΝΟΜΩΝ.
units.tr: TITLE: ON THE EPICHEIROTONIA OF THE LAWS.

units.la: Ἐπειδὴ τῷ ἐφόρῳ Πρυτανείας τῇ ἐπιδικάτῃ, ὡς ταὶ δήμῳ, ἐπειδαν δὲ ξῃ, ὁ κῆρυξ ὑπαγορεύειν ποιῆν τῷ νόμων, ὅταν μὲν ἡ τῷ βουλευτικῷ. Δὲ πρὸ τῆ χειροτονίᾳ εἶπε τῷ χειρίῳ, ὁ χειρότης ἐπὶ ταῖς ἐπὶ ἐπιχειροῦσι, καὶ ἑτέρου ἀρχῶν. Ἠ δὲ ἐπιχειροτονία ἔσῳ ἡ ἀρχὴ ὅταν δοκῇ ἀρχὴ οἱ νόμοι οἱ βουλευτικοί, ἦ ὕστερα ὅταν μὴ δοκῇ, εἶπε τῷ χειρῷ ἐκ ταῦτα. Τῷ δὲ ἐπιχειροτονίαν ἐᾶν τῶν νόμων καὶ τὰς νόμους τὰς χειμένους. ἐαν δὲ ὧν λύῃ τῶν νόμων τῶν χειμένων ἀπαχειροτονηθῶσι, τὰς Πρυτανείας ἐφ' ὧν δὴ ἡ ἐπιχειροτονία ἡ ἔνῃ, ποιεῖ καὶ τῶν ἀπαχειροτονηθέντων τ' πλε[?]ταῖς ὅτ πεισῶν ἐκκλησίαν. Τοὺς δὲ πρεσβύτας οἷον τὰ χωσὶ προσεδρεύοντες ἐπ' ταύτῃ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ χρηματίζειν ἐπὶ ὠφέλιας ἐκ τῶν ἱερῶν καὶ ποιεῖ τῶν Νομοφυλάκων, καὶ ἐπὶ ἐκκλησίαν καθελ[?]ῶ[?]νται καὶ ποιεῖ τῷ ἀργυρίῳ ἀπὸ τῶν πόλιν τῆς Νομοφυλάκας ἔσας. Τοὺς δὲ Νομοφύλακας εἶ[?] genti dator, quanto faciendum opus locauerint Sacerdotes, quibus id commissum est.
units.tr: When the presiding officer of the Prytaneum puts the question to the people (as is done in the assembly), and the herald has been ordered to make the proclamation of the laws: when the matter belongs to the Council, the herald, before the vote by show of hands, says, "Whoever wishes to propose a law, let him come forward," and so on. The epicheirotonia is held when the magistrates think a law is beneficial, but not when they think otherwise, and the herald then says this, in these words. The laws and the established statutes are to be left alone for the epicheirotonia. If any laws are rejected by vote, the presiding officers put the matter before the assembly on the day on which the epicheirotonia took place, and also the laws that were rejected, by the vote of the people. The elders, who sit in attendance as the Council does, are to deal with this assembly concerning the advantages drawn from the sacred revenues, and also the Guardians of the Laws, and they are to be summoned to the assembly and are to see to the money from the city's treasury of the Guardians of the Laws. Concerning the Guardians of the Laws ... [the remainder is corrupt, and the Latin fragment reads:] ... of the people, as much as the priests to whom the matter has been committed have contracted to have done.

units.la: Senes Minervae oleae ramum Panathenaeis gestantes, forma florenti eligunter.
units.tr: Old men carrying the olive branch of Minerva at the Panathenaea are to be chosen for their flourishing appearance.

units.la: Rex in vxorem ciuem Atticam virginem ducito.
units.tr: The king shall take as his wife an Athenian citizen, a virgin.

units.la: Sacerdotes priuatim singuli, totaeque gentes & familiae, sacerdotij sui rationem reddunto.
units.tr: Each priest privately, and whole clans and families, are to render an account of their priesthood.

units.la: Nullius Deorum Sacerdos sorte legitor, qui caltus non sit.
units.tr: The priest of no god is to be chosen by lot who is not of noble birth.

units.la: Cum apud Agnusios sacrificium ab ijs fiat.
units.tr: Since among the Agnusii the sacrifice is performed by them.

units.la: PRIMVS.
units.tr: FIRST.

units.la: PRIMVS.
units.tr: FIRST.

units.la: LEGVM RECENSIO.
units.tr: REVIEW OF THE LAWS.

units.la: Vndecimo primae Prytaneias die, pro concione, post vota voce praeconis peracta, Leges ordine recensentor, primum eae quae sunt de Senatu: deinde de Republica: tum de Nouemuiris: demum de reliquis Magistratibus. Primumque fciscitor, an satis sit Legum de Senatu: deinde, an non sit satis: atque ita deinceps, de Legibus quae Rempublicam spectant. Concio habetor secundum leges, quae obtinent, ad recensendas leges. Siquae autem leges, quae obtinent, improbantur, Prytaneis, qui huic legum recensioni praesunt, vltima trium concionum habento de improbatis legibus. Proëdris[?], quibus concioni huic praesse fortito contigerit, omnino referuto, post relationem primam, quae est de rebus sacris, de Nomothetis, de quibus scilicet legibus sententiam sint laturi, & vnde stips illis suppetet. Nomothetae autem de ijs sunto, qui Heliasticum iusiurandum iurarunt.
units.tr: On the eleventh day of the first Prytany, after the prayers have been offered at the sermon in the voice of the herald, the laws are reviewed in order: first those concerning the Senate, then those concerning the Commonwealth, then those concerning the Nine Archons, and last those concerning the remaining magistrates. And first they ask whether the laws concerning the Senate are sufficient, then whether they are not sufficient; and so on in turn for the laws that concern the Commonwealth. The assembly is held according to the laws now in force, for the purpose of reviewing the laws. If any of the laws now in force are disapproved, the Prytanes who preside over this review shall hold the last of three assemblies on the disapproved laws. The Proedri, to whom it has fallen by lot to preside over this assembly, must in any case bring forward, after the first business, which concerns sacred matters, the matter of the Nomothetae: namely, on which laws they are to pass judgement, and from where the funds for them are to come. The Nomothetae are to be those who have sworn the Heliastic oath.

units.la: Si vero Prytaneis concione non habeant, aut proëdri non referant, secundum has leges, Prytanú quisque mille drachmis Mineruæ sacris, Proëdrorum vero singuli quadraginta drachmis, Mineruæ item sacris, mulctátor. Eorum nomina apud Thesmothetas deferuntor, quæadmodum eorú, quia ærarii cum sint, tamen Magistratum gerunt. Si vero Thesmothetæ delatos in iudicium non rapiant, ex hac Lege, in Senatu Areopagiticum ne cooptantor, vt qui Legú Emendationem peruerterint. Ante concione quisquis Athenienfium Legem ferre voluerit, proponat scriptis ad Eponymorú statuas, Leges, quas rogaturus est, vt pro numero propositarú Legum, populus decernat de tempore, quod Nomothetis erit præscribendum. Qui vero nouam Legem fert, in albú describito, & proponito quotidie ad Eponymorú statuas, donec concio habeatur. Eliúgtor autè ex vniuerso Atheniensiú populo, die Hecatombæonis vndecimo, viri quinque, qui Patrothetis[?] abrogandæ erunt.
units.tr: But if the Prytanes do not hold the assembly, or the Proedri do not bring forward the business, then under these laws each Prytanis is to be fined a thousand drachmas for the sacred funds of Minerva, and each of the Proedri forty drachmas, likewise for the sacred funds of Minerva. Their names are to be laid before the Thesmothetae, in the same way as those of the treasury officials, who, although they are of the treasury, nonetheless hold a magistracy. If the Thesmothetae do not bring the accused to trial, then by this law they are not to be co-opted into the Areopagus Council, since they have subverted the amendment of the laws. Before the assembly, whoever of the Athenians wishes to propose a law shall publish in writing, at the statues of the Eponymous Heroes, the laws he intends to propose, so that the people may decide, according to the number of laws posted, the time to be prescribed for the Nomothetae. Whoever proposes a new law shall write it on a tablet and post it daily at the statues of the Eponymous Heroes until the assembly is held. Five men are to be chosen from the whole Athenian people, on the eleventh day of Hecatombaeon, who are to repeal the laws...

units.la: DECRETVM.
units.tr: DECREE.

units.la: Populus sciuit. Tisamenus scripsit. Atheniéses Rempublicam secúdum patria instituta gerunto. Legibus autem Solonis, & mensuris, & ponderibus vtuntor, vt & Draconis sanctionibus, quibus etiam olim vsi sumus. Si quibus vero opus fuerit legibus, eas electi à Senatu Nomothetæ in tabella describunto, & ad Eponymorum statuas proponunto, vt à quouis legi possint: Eodemque hoc mense Magistratibus in manus danto: datas prius Senatus Quingentorum, & Nomothetæ quos populares elegerint, iurati approbanto. Cui vis priuato Senatum adire liceto, & quod sibi bonum videtur de illis Legibus consulere. Ἐὰν δ' οἱ Γρυτοπώλεις μὴ παισὶ χῇ γεγεγραμμένα τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἢ οἱ παιδεύσεσι μὴ χρηματίσωσι, χῇ τὰ γεγεγραμμένα ὀφείλειν τῷ μ[?] Γρυτοπωλέων ἕκαστον χιλίας δραχμὰς ἱερὰς τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ, τῷ δὲ Γεσέδρων ἕκαστος ὀφειλέτω τὰ παραρρύεντα δραχμὰς ἱερὰς τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ, καὶ ἐνδεῖξις αὐτῶ ἔτω τοῖς τοῖς Θεσμοθέταις, καὶ ἐὰν μὴ ἐσφάλλων τὰ δημόσια. Οἱ δὲ Θεσμοθέται τὰς εἰσαγγέλτας εἰσαγόντων εἰς τὸ δεσμωτήριον χῇ τὸν νόμον, ἢ μὴ αἰσιοῦντων εἰς Ἄρειον πάγον ὡς καταλύοντες τὸ ἐπωμορφωσιν τῷ νόμῳ. Γρεῖ δὲ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ὁ βουλόμενος Ἀθηναίων νομοθετεῖν, ἐκλιπέτω ἐπωμορφωσιν τῷ ἐπωνύμῳ γράψας τοὺς νόμους, οἷς ἂν ᾖ, ὅπως δὲ πρὸς τὸ πλῆθος τῶν ἐκπεπτωκότων νόμων ψηφίσηται ὁ δῆμος ἐπὶ τὸ χρέους τῆς Νομοθέτας. Ὁ ᾗ ἀλλης τὸν χρόνον νόμον αἰσαγγεῖλας εἰς λήθωμα ἐκλιπέτω ἐπωνύμῳ ὀσημέσθαι, ἕως ἂν ἐκκλησία ᾖ. ἀιρεῖσθαι ᾗ ἐν τοῖς σεωσπολη-γησομένους τῇ δήμων τῆς νόμοις οἱ ἀὐ ἐν τοῖς νομοθέταις λύωσι· πέντε ἄνδρες ὃς Ἀθηναίων ἀποδώτων τῇ ἐνδικαίτῃ τῆς ἐκπεμπομένος μίλιως.
