Dominicum itaque diem ita semper honorabilem decernimus & venerandum, vt à cunctis executionibus excusetur: nulla quemque vrgeat admonitio, nulla fidefussionis flagitetur exactio, taceat apparitio, aduocatio delitescat, sit ille dies à cognitionibus alienus, praeconis horrida vox silescat, reffurent à controuersiis litigantes, & habeant fœderis interuallum, adse simul veniant aduersarij non timentes, subeat animos vicaria paenitudo, pacta conferant, transactiones loquantur. Dat. Id. Decembr. Constantinop. Zenone & Marciano Coss.[?] Idemque Iudaeis indultum est diebus Sabbatis aut festis ab Imperatoribus Honorio & Theodosio, vt constat è Lib. III. Cod. Theod. cod. Impp. Honorius & Theodosius AA. Ioanni PF. P. Post alia. Die Sabbati ac reliquis, sub tempore quo Iudaei cultus sui reuerentiam feruant, neminem aut facere aliquid, aut villa ex parte conueniri debere praecipimus, cum Fiscalibus commodis, & litigys priuatorum conflat reliquos dies posse sufficere, &c. Dat. VII. Kalend. Aug. Rauennae DD. NN. Honorio VIII. & Theodosio III. Coss. Habes Leg. XIII. C. de Iudaeis & Caelicolis, non ad Ioannem, sed ad Iouium PP. datam VIII. Kal. Aug. Rauennae DD. NN. Honorio VIII. & Theod. Aug. III. Conf. Vide etiam Legem II. C. eod. quae legitur in Nomocanone Photii Tit. VII. cap. IV. εἴρηται ἡ βιβλίου α'. πτ. θ. [?] idque iam olim ab Augusto institutum, cuius Rescriptum extat apud Iosephum Lib. XVI. cap. X. [?] [?] Σαλαμίνα [?] idque iam olim ab Augusto institutum, cuius Rescriptum extat apud Iosephum Lib. XVI. cap. X.
units.tr: Demosthenes mentions this law in the speech against Meidias [ἐν τῷ κατὰ Μειδίου]: "I said that the man who (...) in the market-place of the city, on the (day) of the mysteries, committed a wrong; when Euandrus had accused him, the people (...) of the acquittal and of Menippus." Ulpian: "Perhaps, regarding the offence against the festival and its security as something grave, he seizes (...)." The Christian emperors also wished this same reverence to be shown to the principal festivals of the Christians. The emperors Valentinian, Theodosius and Arcadius: "On the fifteen days of Easter the compulsion of the annona service and the exaction of all public and private debts is to be deferred. Given on the 2nd day before the Ides of August at Rome, in the consulship of Timasius and Promotus. See Law VII, Cod. De feriis." Constantine the Great ordered that on the day called the Lord's day, and likewise on Friday, all causes and suits and other business should rest. This law is praised by Sozomen, Ecclesiastical History, Book I, chapter VIII: [τῷ ἡ Κυριακῷ καλουμένῳ ἡμέραν τῶν Ἑλλήνων ἐφ' ἑαυτῶν ἐδόμασιν, Ἑλλῆνες ἡ ἡλίου ἀπαθείας, καὶ ἡ τῶν ἐδόμης σωματείας δικαστῶν καὶ τῶν ἄλλων πραγμάτων σχολῇ ἀγὼν πάντας, καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ λιτῆς ὁ ἡμέρα ἀγαπῶν] Some of this law is read in Cod. Theod. Law I, in these words: "The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Helpidius. As it seemed most unworthy that the day of the Sun, which is celebrated for our veneration, should be occupied by quarrelling disputes and harmful contentions of parties, so it is pleasing and agreeable that on that day the things most desired be accomplished. Therefore, on the festal day, all may have licence to emancipate and manumit, and they are not to be prevented from doing so in these matters. Given 5 days before the Nones of June, at Caralis, in the consulship of Crispus II and Constantine II." You also have the constitution of Leo and Anthemius, Law X, Cod. ibid.: "The Emperors Leo and Anthemius Augusti to Armasius, praetorian prefect. We therefore decree that the Lord's day be always so honoured and venerated, that it be excused from all executions: let no one be pressed by summons, let no demand for surety be made, let the attendant be silent, let advocacy lie hidden, let that day be free from hearings, let the harsh voice of the herald fall silent; let litigants rest from disputes and have a respite of truce, let adversaries come together without fear, let a remorse for the time be stirred in their minds, let them make agreements and let settlements speak. Given on the Ides of December at Constantinople, in the consulship of Zeno and Marcian." The same indulgence was granted to the Jews on Sabbaths or festivals by the Emperors Honorius and Theodosius, as is clear from Book III of the Cod. Theod.: "The Emperors Honorius and Theodosius Augusti to John, praetorian prefect. Among other things: On the Sabbath and the other days, at the time when the Jews keep the reverence of their worship, we direct that no one be made to do anything or be summoned in any way; since it is agreed that the remaining days are sufficient for fiscal business and the suits of private persons, etc. Given 7 days before the Kalends of August at Ravenna, in the consulship of our lords Honorius VIII and Theodosius III." You have Law XIII, Cod. On Jews and Heavenly worshippers, given not to John but to Jovius, praetorian prefect, 8 days before the Kalends of August at Ravenna, in the consulship of our lords Honorius VIII and Theodosius Augustus III. See also Law II of the same title, which is read in the Nomocanon of Photius, title VII, chapter IV: [εἴρηται ἡ βιβλίου α'. πτ. θ. [?]] and this was already long ago instituted by Augustus, whose rescript survives in Josephus, Book XVI, chapter X. [Σαλαμίνα] and this was already long ago instituted by Augustus, whose rescript survives in Josephus, Book XVI, chapter X.

units.la: Cum fieri vix quiret, vt omnia rite atque ordine peragerentur, Lege cautum, vt postridie Mysteriorum Senatus in Eleusinio haberetur.
units.tr: Since it could hardly be that everything was carried out rightly and in order, the law provided that the Senate should sit at Eleusis on the day after the Mysteries.

units.la: Τὼ βουλεύ[?] τῇ ὑπηρεσίᾳ [?] μυστηρίων ἐξόδῳ [?] Postridie Mysteriorum Senatus in πιλὸς ἐν τοῦ Ἐλευσῖνι[?]. Eleusinio habetur.
units.tr: [Τὼ βουλεύ[?] τῇ ὑπηρεσίᾳ [?] μυστηρίων ἐξόδῳ [?]] The Senate sits on the day after the Mysteries [πιλὸς ἐν τοῦ Ἐλευσῖνι[?]] at Eleusis.

units.la: Solonis Lex haec est, ex qua postridie Mysteriorum, Rege referente, Senatus in Eleusinio habebatur, cogniturus de iis qui in Mysteria aut diei festi religionem commisissent, Andocides ἐν τοῖς ὁπλίτας [?] Ἐλευσῖνι[?] [?] ... [?] Eleusinio habebatur.
units.tr: This is Solon's law, by which, on the day after the Mysteries, the Senate was held at Eleusis on the report of the king, to hear cases against those who had committed offences in the Mysteries or against the religious observance of the festival day. Andocides [ἐν τοῖς ὁπλίτας [?] Ἐλευσῖνι[?]] ... was held at Eleusis.

units.la: Cereri quoque Eleusiniae Thesmophoria agitabantur, idque quotannis ex Lege:
units.tr: At Eleusis the Thesmophoria, the festival of Ceres, were also celebrated, and this every year by law:

units.la: Κατ' ἔτος πλὴν τὰ Θεσμοφόρια. Quotannis Thesmophoria celebrantor.
units.tr: [Κατ' ἔτος πλὴν τὰ Θεσμοφόρια.] Every year the Thesmophoria are celebrated.

units.la: Meminit huius Legis Graecus Theocriti Interpres ad Idyllium IV. docetque festum istud procuratum fuisse à matronis, sed quae, vt aliunde constat, essent in casto: [?] Ἀλωαῖος, κατ' ἔτος πλὴν τὰ Θεσμοφόρια, καὶ [?] ... [?] Quam in rem sumtus facere tenebatur maritus, siquidem vxorem duxisset, cui dos esset tria talenta. Ἴφικυς ὁ τῆς ἀπὸ τῆς Πυῤῥου ϰλήρου. καὶ ἐν τε τῷ δήμῳ κεκτημένης [?] πεντακοσίων ταλάντων [?] ἐπὶ [?] εἰ τὸ οἶκον, εἰ ὧν γεγαμηκὼς, ὠνᾶτο δὲ [?] τῆς γαμετῆς γυναικὸς ἡ Θεσμοφόρια, καὶ τἆλλα, ὅσα προσῆκε, ἀφυπηρέτει [?] τὴν δήμῳ τῆς γυναικὸς, ἀπὸ γε οὐσίας τιλι-κύτης.
units.tr: The Greek interpreter of Theocritus, on Idyll IV, mentions this law and teaches that this festival was conducted by matrons, who, as is known from elsewhere, were in a state of chastity. [[?] Ἀλωαῖος, κατ' ἔτος πλὴν τὰ Θεσμοφόρια, καὶ [?]] ... [?] For this purpose the husband was bound to make the expense, if he had married a wife who had a dowry of three talents. [Ἴφικυς ὁ τῆς ἀπὸ τῆς Πυῤῥου ϰλήρου. καὶ ἐν τε τῷ δήμῳ κεκτημένης [?] πεντακοσίων ταλάντων [?] ἐπὶ [?] εἰ τὸ οἶκον, εἰ ὧν γεγαμηκὼς, ὠνᾶτο δὲ [?] τῆς γαμετῆς γυναικὸς ἡ Θεσμοφόρια, καὶ τἆλλα, ὅσα προσῆκε, ἀφυπηρέτει [?] τὴν δήμῳ τῆς γυναικὸς, ἀπὸ γε οὐσίας τιλι-κύτης.] Iphicus, of the lot of Pyrrhus ... and in the deme possessing (...) five hundred talents (...) if he was married, he bought the Thesmophoria from his wife's (property), and the other things which were fitting, from the wife's (dowry), from a modest estate.

units.la: His autem festis Thesmophoriorum diebus nexi vinculis soluebantur, itaque Lege cautum erat:
units.tr: During these days of the Thesmophoria, those in bonds were released from their chains, and so the law provided:

units.la: Ἐν τοῖς Θεσμοφορίοις λύεσθαι τοῖς δεσμώταις.
units.tr: [Ἐν τοῖς Θεσμοφορίοις λύεσθαι τοῖς δεσμώταις.] During the Thesmophoria the prisoners are to be released.

units.la: Descripsimus hanc Legem è Marcellino atque Sopatro, quia nobis ex Vlpiano constat id etiam aliis nonnullis festis obseruatum fuisse: nam eccè de Panathenaeis Vlpianus in Timocratcam; ἐν τῷ [?] ἡ ἡμέρα τῇ Παναθηναίᾳ. τὸ δὲ ἐξὸν ἀφεῖσθαι τοὺς δεσμοὺς τοῖς δεσμώταις ἐν τῇ πόλει [?]. Item Liberalibus: idem Vlpianus in Androtianam. ἔτος γὰρ ὡς αἰτεῖσθαι τὸ τῆς Διονυσίων ἑορτῆς, εἶτα ἐμβάλλεσθαι. Laudat itaque Legem hanc Marcellinus in Hermogenem. νόμως ἐν τοῖς Θεσμοφορίοις λύεσθαι τοὺς δεσμώτας. Sopater de Diuisione Quaestionis. νόμος τοῖς δεσμώταις ἐν τοῖς Θεσμοφορίοις λύεσθαι, ἐπαναστάσας τὴς ὅτι τῇ ἐαυτῆς γυναικὶ, τὸν οἰκίτην ἐλάσει, ἡ δήσας, ἀπεδήμησεν. Ὑπὸ τῶν τῆς Θεσμοφορίων ἐλυσε τὸν οἰκίτην ἡ γυνή. Ὑπὸ τῶν τῆς Θεσμοφορίων, cum inchoarentur. E captiuis autem illi tantum liberabantur, qui sacris poterant interesse, at quibus ob piaculum, aut alia de causa interdicebatur, illi vinculis non eximebantur. Sopater ibidem: ἐξαίρεσιν δεσμωτείου ἀδικῶν, οἱ μετὰ ἱερᾶν, ἡ ἀσυνδέτων, διαγῆς, οὐ τοῖς ἀκαθαρσίαις, ἡ σιαγῆς, ἡ τῶν πεφυρμένων ἀπελαυνομένους. Idem indulgere consueuerant Imperatores Christiani diebus festis Paschatis, idque quotannis Rescripto caucbant: in hanc rem leguntur nonnulla Imperatorum Rescripta Cod. Theod. de Indulgentiis criminum: primúmque habetur Leg. III. in haec verba: Impp. Valentinianus, Valens, & Gratianus AAA. ad Vienensium P.V. Ob diem Paschae, quem intimo corde celebramus, omnibus, quos reatus adstringit, carcer inclusit, claustra diffoluimus. Adtamen sacrilegus, in maiestate reus, in mortuos veneficus, siue maleficus, adulter, raptor, homicida, communione istius muneris separentur. Dat. III. Non. Maij, Rom. Lupicino & Iouino Coss.
units.tr: We have taken this law from Marcellinus and Sopater, because it is clear to us from Ulpian that this was also observed on some other festivals. Ulpian, against Timocrates, on the Panathenaea: [ἐν τῷ [?] ἡ ἡμέρα τῇ Παναθηναίᾳ. τὸ δὲ ἐξὸν ἀφεῖσθαι τοὺς δεσμοὺς τοῖς δεσμώταις ἐν τῇ πόλει] the day of the Panathenaea; and it was permitted to loose the bonds of the prisoners in the city. Likewise for the Liberalia: Ulpian, against Androtion: [ἔτος γὰρ ὡς αἰτεῖσθαι τὸ τῆς Διονυσίων ἑορτῆς, εἶτα ἐμβάλλεσθαι] for it was the custom to ask for (release) at the time of the festival of the Dionysia, and then to be thrown in. Marcellinus therefore cites this law in his work against Hermogenes: [νόμως ἐν τοῖς Θεσμοφορίοις λύεσθαι τοὺς δεσμώτας] that by law the prisoners are loosed at the Thesmophoria. Sopater, On the Division of the Question: [νόμος τοῖς δεσμώταις ἐν τοῖς Θεσμοφορίοις λύεσθαι, ἐπαναστάσας τὴς ὅτι τῇ ἐαυτῆς γυναικὶ, τὸν οἰκίτην ἐλάσει, ἡ δήσας, ἀπεδήμησεν] a law that prisoners are loosed at the Thesmophoria, since a man who had risen up against his own wife, or who had bound (her), had gone abroad. [Ὑπὸ τῶν τῆς Θεσμοφορίων ἐλυσε τὸν οἰκίτην ἡ γυνή.] By the (festival of) the Thesmophoria the wife loosed the husband (?). [Ὑπὸ τῶν τῆς Θεσμοφορίων, cum inchoarentur.] At the beginning of the Thesmophoria. Yet only those prisoners were released who could take part in the sacred rites; those who were forbidden to do so on account of an impurity or for some other reason were not freed from their bonds. Sopater in the same place: [ἐξαίρεσιν δεσμωτείου ἀδικῶν, οἱ μετὰ ἱερᾶν, ἡ ἀσυνδέτων, διαγῆς, οὐ τοῖς ἀκαθαρσίαις, ἡ σιαγῆς, ἡ τῶν πεφυρμένων ἀπελαυνομένους] the exemption of those in prison who had wronged, those who were with the sacred things, or unbound, ... not for uncleanness, or the jaw (?), or of those who were driven away as defiled. The Christian emperors were accustomed to grant the same indulgence on the festival days of Easter, and secured it every year by rescript. Several rescripts of the emperors concerning the indulgence of crimes are read in the Cod. Theod., under De indulgentiis criminum; the first is Law III, in these words: "The Emperors Valentinian, Valens and Gratian Augusti to the prefect of Vienne. On account of the day of Easter, which we celebrate with our inmost heart, we have opened the prison and unbarred the gates for all whom guilt has bound. Yet the sacrilegious, the accused of treason, the poisoner of the dead or evil-doer, the adulterer, the abductor and the murderer shall be separated from communion in this favour. Given 3 days before the Nones of May at Rome, in the consulship of Lupicinus and Jovinus."

units.la: Titulus huius Legis praefert nomen Gratiani, tanquam Augusti, sed falso, nondum enim erat Augustus Gratianus, leuatus enim est a patre Augustus nono Kal. Septembr. his Coss. Lupicino & Iouino, vt videre est apud Socratem & Idatium. Secundo quod datum dicitur hoc Rescriptum Rom. id est, Romae, verum non est: Est quippe hoc Rescriptum Valentiniani, qui tunc temporis non erat Romae, sed in Galliis: nam anno praecedenti, qui Consules habuit Gratianum NB. P. & Dagalaïphum, VIII. Id. Octobr. erat Remis. vide Legem XI. Cod. Theod. de Poenis. Dat. VIII. Id. Octob. Remis Gratiano A. I. & Dagalaifo Coss. item quintodecimo Kalendas Decembreis Leg. VIII. Cod. Theod. de Accusationibus & Inscriptionibus, ad Maximinum Correctorem Tuscia. Dat. XV. Kalend. Decemb. Remis, Acc. Florentia, Gratiano Nob. Caes & Dagaelcifo Coss. & septimo earundem Kalendarum Leg. IX. Cod. Theod. cod. ad Valerianum P.V. Dat. VII. Kal. Decemb. Remis, Gratiano NB. P. & Dagaëlcifo Coss. At octauo Idus Decembreis Veronae statuit subscriptio Legis IX. Cod. Theod. de Veteranis ad Dagalaifum Magistrum Militum, Dat. VIII. Id. Decemb. Veronae, Gratiano NB. P. & Dagalaipho Coss. Sed Verona scriptam esse mihi non possum persuadere, nam toto eo tempore fuit in illo Lugdunensis aut Belgicae Galliae tractu: Quare rescribendum puto Virodani. Haec vrbs distabat Durocortoro Remorum triginta nouem millibus passuum. Itinerarium Antonini:
units.tr: The title of this law gives the name of Gratian as Augustus, but falsely. Gratian was not yet Augustus, for his father raised him to that rank on the ninth day before the Kalends of September in the consulship of Lupicinus and Iovinus, as can be seen in Socrates and Idatius. Second, it is said that this rescript was given at Rome, that is, Romae, but this is not true. The rescript is Valentinian's, and at that time he was not at Rome but in Gaul. In the previous year, when Gratian N.B.P. and Dagalaiphus were consuls, he was at Rheims on the eighth day before the Ides of October; see Law XI, Cod. Theod. de Poenis: Given on the eighth day before the Ides of October at Rheims, in the consulship of Gratian A. I. and Dagalaiphus. Likewise on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of December, Law VIII, Cod. Theod. de Accusationibus et Inscriptionibus: to Maximinus, corrector of Tuscia. Given on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of December at Rheims; received at Florence; in the consulship of Gratian the most noble Caesar and Dagalaiphus. And on the seventh day before the same Kalends, Law IX, Cod. Theod. in the same place: to Valerianus, P.V. Given on the seventh day before the Kalends of December at Rheims, in the consulship of Gratian N.B.P. and Dagalaiphus. But the subscription of Law IX, Cod. Theod. de Veteranis places a rescript on the eighth day before the Ides of December: to Dagalaiphus, Master of Soldiers. Given on the eighth day before the Ides of December at Verona, in the consulship of Gratian N.B.P. and Dagalaiphus. I cannot persuade myself, however, that it was written at Verona, for during all that time he was in that district of Lugdunensis or Belgic Gaul. Wherefore I think Virodani should be read. This city was thirty-nine miles distant from Durocortorum of the Remi. The Itinerary of Antoninus:

units.la: ITER A DVROCORTORO DIVODV- RVM VSQVE. M. P. LXII.
units.tr: THE ROAD FROM DUROCORTORUM AS FAR AS DIVODURUM, 62 MILES.

units.la: Sic Basilia | M. P. X. Axuenam | M. P. XII. Virodunum | M. P. XVII.
units.tr: Thus: Basilia, 10 miles; Axuena, 12 miles; Virodunum, 17 miles.

units.la: Anno sequenti, Lupicino atque Iouino Coss. quarto Kalendas Februarias erat Remis. Leg. IX. Cod. Theod. de Re militari, ad Iouinum Magistrum Equitum, Dat. IV. Kalendas Feb. Remis, Lupicino & Iouino Conss. Vnde fit vt putem corrigendam esse subscriptionem Legis IV. Cod. Theod. de Metallis & Metallarijs, quae II. est Cod. eod. itemque Legis XIII. Cod. Theod. de Susceptoribus, praepositis, & arcariis, quae est V. C. eod. vtraque est ad Germanianum Com. S. L. Dat. VI. Id. Ian. Rom. Lupicino & Iouino Coss. itaque ἀντὶ τῆς Romae [?], rescribo Remis, quibus item in locis, vt iam vidimus, morabatur quarto Kalendas Februarias huius anni: ibidemque etiam fuit sextodecimo Kalendas Martias, Leg. X. Cod. Theod. de Re militari, ad Iouinum Magistrum Militum, Dat. XVI. Kal. Mart. Remis, Lupicino & Iouino Conss. Fuit quoque quarto Kalendas Maij, Leg. III. Cod. Theod. de praediis Nauiculariorum, ad Dracontium Vic. Afric. Dat. IV. Kal. Maij, Remis, Lupicino & Iouino Coss. Non igitur Romae fuit tertio Nonas Maij huius anni: quare ἀντὶ τῆς Rom. [?] Leg. illa III. Cod. Theod. de Indulgentiis criminum, reponendum est Remis: quibus in sedibus tunc erat, vt & quartodecimo Kalendas Iunias, Leg. IV. Cod. Theod. de Aduocato Fisci, ad Rufinum PF. P. Dat. XIV. Kal. Iun. Remis, Lupicino & Iouino Coss. Denique Legem hanc tertiam Cod. Theod. de Indulgentiis criminum, datam non credo tertio Nonas Maij: nam quid fieri velint iis, quos ob reatum carcer includebat; cauent Imperatores ob diem Paschae, nempe claustra illis dissolui. Atqui frustra id cauerent, celebritas enim Paschae iam erat peracta: erat quippe hic annus, qui Consules habuit Lupicinum atque Iouinum, Christi Dionysianus tercentesimus sexagesimus septimus, Cyclo Solis duodecimo, Lunae septimo, litera Dominicali G. Terminus Paschalis tertio Kalendas Aprileis, feria sexta: Pascha celebratum est Kalendis Aprilibus: Nec est, quod quisnam obiiciat, ista cauteri ab Imperatore in sequentem annum: nam & quotannis hac de re rescribebant ad Praefectos atque Magistratus, vt iam ante diximus, & praeterea, quod caput est, habes Rescriptum anni sequentis Leg. IV. Cod. Theod. eod. Imppp. Valentinianus, Valens, & Gratianus AAA. ad Olybrium P.V. Paschae celebritas postulat, vt quoscumque nunc aegra expectatio quaestionis, poenaque formido sollicitat, absoluamus: decretis tamen veterum mos gerendus est, ne temere homicidij crimen, adulterij foeditatem, maiestatis iniuriam, maleficiorum scelus, insidias venenorum, raptusque violentiam sinamus euadere. Lecta VIII. Id. Iun. Valentiniano & Valente II. AA. Coss. Rescribendum itaq; nullus dubito ad Legem tertiam. Dat. III. Non. Mart. Remis, Lupicino & Iovino Coss. Mirari autem satis non possum Legem quartam lectam fuisse tantum octauo Idus Iunias. atqui annus erat Christi Dionysianus tercentesimus sexagesimus octauus, Cyclo Solis tertiodecimo, Lunae octauo, litera Dominicali FE, Terminus Paschalis quartodecimo Kalendas Maias, feria sexta, Pascha duodecimo Kalendas Maias, Valentiniano & Valente II. AA. Coss. Sed multo magis stupendum est, quod subscribitur Legi VI. Cod. Theod. eod. Imppp. Gratianus, Valentinianus, & Theodosius AAA. ad Antidium V. C. Vicarium. Paschalis laetitiae dies ne illa quidem tenere finit ingenia, qua flagitia fecerunt: pateat insuetis horridus carcer aliquando luminibus. Alienum autem censemus ab indulgentia, qui nefariam criminum conscientiam in maiestatem superbe animauerit, qui parricidali furore raptus, sanguine proprio manum tinxit, qui cuiusque praeterea hominis caede maculatus est, qui genialis tori ac lectuli fuit inuasor alieni, qui verecundiae virginalis raptor extitit, qui venerandum cognati sanguinis vinculum profano caecus violauit incestu, vel qui noxiis quaesita graminibus & diris immurmurata secretis, mentis & corporis venena composuit: aut qui sacri oris imitator & diuinorum vultuum adpetitor, venerabiles formas sacrilegio eruditus impressit. His ergo tali quoque sub absolutione damnatis, indultum nostrae Serenitatis eo praecepti fine concludimus, ut remissionem veniae crimina, nisi semel commissa, non habeant; ne in eos liberalitatis Augustae referatur humanitas, qui impunitatem veteris admissi non emendationi potius, quam consuetudini deputarunt: Recitatae XII. Kal. Aug. Rom. Syagrio & Eucherio Coss. Annus hic erat Christi Dionysianus tercentesimus octagesimus primus, Cyclo Solis vicesimo sexto, Lunae secundo, litera Dominicali C, Terminus Paschalis octauo Kalendas Aprileis, feria quinta, Pascha quinto Kalendas eadem. Sequitur Lex VII. Cod. Theod. eod. Imppp. Gratianus, Valentinianus, & Theodosius AAA. ad Marcianum Vic. Religio aniuersariae obseruationis hortatur, vt omnes omnino periculo carceris, metuque poenarum eximi tuberemus, qui leuiore crimine rei sunt postulati. Vnde apparet, eos excepi, quos atrox cupiditas in scelera compulit: saeuiora, in quibus est primum crimen, & maxime maiestatis, deinde homicidij, veneficiique, ac maleficiorum, stupri atque adulterij, parique immanitate sacrilegij, sepulchrique violatio, raptus, monetaque adulterata figuratio. Dat. XI. Kal. April. Med. Richomere & Clearcho Coss. Hi Consules fuerunt anno Christi Dionysiano tercentesimo quarto, Cyclo Solis primo, Lunae quinto, litera Dominicali GF, Terminus Paschalis vndecimo Kalendas Aprileis, feria sexta, Pascha nono Kalendas eadem. Scripta haec Lex in ipso Paschali Termino, hoc est, vndecimo Kalendas Aprileis die, ad Marcianum Vicarium, vt puto, Italiae, qui Mediolani quoque erat, vt & Imperator. Vltimum huius argumenti Rescriptum, quo Iudices vult Imperator, non expectato alio Rescripto Principis, cum saepius Rescripta haec, vt exemplis praecedentibus potest comprobari, tardius, adeoque post Paschae celebritatem, deferrentur, exequi quod consueuerant Imperatores, habetur Leg. VIII. Cod. Theod. eod. Imppp. Gratianus, Valentinianus, & Theodosius AAA. ad Neotherium PP. Nemo deinceps tardiores fortassis affatus nostrae perennitatis expectet : exequantur iudices, quod indulgere consuevimus. Vbi primum dies Paschalis exiterit, nullum teneat carcer inclusum, omnium vincla soluantur. Sed ab his secernimus eos, quibus contaminari potius gaudia laetitiamque communem, si dimittantur, aduertimus. Quis enim sacrilego diebus sanctis indulgeat? quis adultero, vel incesti reo tempore castitatis ignoscat? quis non raptorem in summa quiete & gaudio communi persequatur instantius? Nullam accipiat requiem vinculorum, qui quiescere respultos quadam sceleris immanitate non sinit: patiatur tormenta veneficus, maleficus, adulteratorque moneta: homicida quod fecit, semper expectet: reus etiam maiestatis, de domino aduersum quem talia molitus est, veniam sperare non debet: Dat. V. Kal. Mar. Med. Arcadio I. & Bautone Coss. Eadem haec Lex habetur Leg.III. C.de Episcopali audientia: sed finis; ab his verbis, His ergo tali sub adstrictione damnatis, &c. petitur e Leg. VI. Cod. Theod. de Indulgentiis criminum: subscriptio vero haec, Dat. Kal. Maij, Arcadio A. & Bautone V.C. Conss. emendanda est e Codice Theodosiano, Dat. V. Kal. Mart. Annus erat Christi Dionysianus tercentesimus octagesimus quintus, Cyclo Solis secundo, Lunae sexto, litera Dominicali E, Terminus Paschalis fuit quarto Idus Aprileis, feria quinta, Pascha Idibus Aprilibus. Quinetiam moribus Romanis abolitio publice fit ob diem insignem, Leg. VIII. D. ad Senatusconsultum Turpillianum. Quinetiam Honorius iussit, ut singulis Dominicis diebus rei de carcere educerentur, quo posset victualis substantia illis ministrari, & ut ad balneum praedictis diebus sub fida custodia ducerentur. Leg. vlt. C.Theod. de Custodia Reorum.
units.tr: In the following year, in the consulship of Lupicinus and Iovinus, on the fourth day before the Kalends of February he was at Rheims. Law IX, Cod. Theod. de Re militari: to Iovinus, Master of the Horse, given on the fourth day before the Kalends of February at Rheims, in the consulship of Lupicinus and Iovinus. Hence I think that the subscription of Law IV, Cod. Theod. de Metallis et Metallariis, which is the second of that title, and likewise that of Law XIII, Cod. Theod. de Susceptoribus, praepositis et arcariis, which is the fifth of that title, should be corrected; both read to Germanianus, Count of the Sacred Largesses. Given on the sixth day before the Ides of January at Rome, in the consulship of Lupicinus and Iovinus. So I rescribe Remis in place of instead of Romae [?] [ἀντὶ τῆς Romae], since, as we have seen, he was staying there on the fourth day before the Kalends of February of this year. He was also there on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of March, Law X, Cod. Theod. de Re militari: to Iovinus, Master of Soldiers. Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of March at Rheims, in the consulship of Lupicinus and Iovinus. He was also there on the fourth day before the Kalends of May, Law III, Cod. Theod. de praediis Nauiculariorum: to Dracontius, Vicar of Africa. Given on the fourth day before the Kalends of May, at Rheims, in the consulship of Lupicinus and Iovinus. Therefore he was not at Rome on the third day before the Nones of May of this year, and so instead of Rom. [?] in that Law III, Cod. Theod. de Indulgentiis criminum, must be restored to Remis, the seat where he then was, as also on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of June, Law IV, Cod. Theod. de Aduocato Fisci: to Rufinus, P.P. Given on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of June at Rheims, in the consulship of Lupicinus and Iovinus. Finally, I do not believe that this third Law of the title de Indulgentiis criminum was given on the third day before the Nones of May. For what the Emperors wish done for those whom prison held on account of their crime, they provide for because of the day of Easter, namely that their chains be loosed. But they would take such care in vain, since the celebration of Easter had already passed. This year, the one whose consuls were Lupicinus and Iovinus, was the 367th year of the Christian era of Dionysius, with the solar cycle 12, lunar cycle 7, and dominical letter G. The Paschal term was the third day before the Kalends of April, a Friday, and Easter was celebrated on the Kalends of April. Nor can anyone object that this caution was given by the Emperor for the following year. For they used to rescribe on this matter every year to the Prefects and Magistrates, as we said before. Moreover, and this is the main point, you have the rescript of the following year, Law IV, Cod. Theod. in the same title: The Emperors Valentinian, Valens and Gratian AAA. to Olybrius, P.V. The celebration of Easter requires that we absolve those whom anxious expectation of trial and dread of punishment now trouble. Yet the custom of the old decrees must be observed, lest we allow the crime of homicide, the foulness of adultery, the injury to majesty, the wickedness of poisonings, the plots of venom, and the violence of rape to escape rashly. Read on the eighth day before the Ides of June, in the consulship of Valentinian and Valens AA. for the second time. Therefore I have no doubt that the third Law must be rescribed. Given on the third day before the Nones of March at Rheims, in the consulship of Lupicinus and Iovinus. But I cannot sufficiently wonder that the fourth Law was read only on the eighth day before the Ides of June. Yet that year was the 368th year of the Christian era of Dionysius, with solar cycle 13, lunar cycle 8, dominical letter FE, the Paschal term the fourth day before the Kalends of May, a Friday, and Easter on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May, in the consulship of Valentinian and Valens AA. But it is far more astonishing that the following is subscribed to Law VI, Cod. Theod. in the same title: The Emperors Gratian, Valentinian and Theodosius AAA. to Antidius, V.C., Vicar. Not even the day of joyful Easter lets men's minds relax from the crimes they have committed: let the grim prison be open at last to eyes unused to light. We judge, however, that indulgence is not to be extended to one who has proudly stirred up a wicked consciousness of crime against majesty, who, carried away by parricidal fury, has stained his hands with his own blood, who is defiled by the slaughter of any man, who has been an invader of another's marriage bed, who has been a ravisher of virginal modesty, who blindly violated the venerable bond of kinship by profane incest, or who has compounded poisons of body and mind, having sought the means of harm and muttered dire secrets; or who, an imitator of the sacred countenance and a seeker of divine images, has impressed venerable forms by sacrilege. Therefore, since such men are condemned even to this kind of absolution, we conclude that the indulgence of Our Serenity is granted on this condition: that the remission of pardon should not hold for crimes committed more than once, lest the kindness of Augustan liberality be extended to those who have reckoned the impunity of a former offence as a matter for habit rather than for amendment. Read on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August at Rome, in the consulship of Syagrius and Eucherius. This year was the 381st year of the Christian era of Dionysius, with solar cycle 26, lunar cycle 2, dominical letter C, the Paschal term the eighth day before the Kalends of April, a Thursday, and Easter the fifth day before the Kalends of the same month. Next follows Law VII, Cod. Theod. in the same place: The Emperors Gratian, Valentinian and Theodosius AAA. to Marcianus, Vicar. Religious observance urges that we free from the danger of prison and the fear of punishment all who are accused of lesser crimes. From this it is clear which offences were excepted, those which fierce desire drove men to commit: the more savage ones, among which the first is the crime against majesty, then homicide, poisoning and sorcery, illicit sex and adultery, sacrilege of equal savagery, violation of a tomb, rape, and the counterfeiting of coin. Given on the eleventh day before the Kalends of April, in the consulship of Merobaudes and Richomeres and Clearchus. These consuls held office in the year 394 of the Christian era of Dionysius, with solar cycle 1, lunar cycle 5, dominical letters GF, the Paschal term the eleventh day before the Kalends of April, a Friday, and Easter the ninth day before the Kalends of the same month. This Law was written on the very Paschal term, that is on the eleventh day before the Kalends of April, to Marcianus, I think Vicar of Italy, who was also at Milan, as was the Emperor. The last rescript of this matter, by which the Emperor wills that the judges act without waiting for another rescript of the Prince, since these rescripts were more often delivered late, and so after the celebration of Easter, as earlier examples can show, is found in Law VIII, Cod. Theod. in the same place: The Emperors Gratian, Valentinian and Theodosius AAA. to Neoterius, P.P. Let no one henceforth expect our eternal favour, which may come too late: let the judges carry out what we are accustomed to grant. As soon as the day of Easter arrives, let no prison hold anyone shut in; let the chains of all be loosed. But we separate from this those whom we observe would be defiled, if released, in the joy and common happiness. For who would show indulgence to a sacrilegious man on holy days? Who would pardon an adulterer, or one accused of incest, in a time of chastity? Who would not pursue a ravisher more urgently in the great quiet and common joy? Let not him who does not allow the restless to rest because of a certain monstrous wickedness receive any relief from his chains. Let the poisoner, the sorcerer and the adulterator of coin suffer torments. Let the murderer always await what he has done. Nor should one accused of majesty, who has plotted such things against the lord he opposes, hope for pardon. Given on the fifth day before the Kalends of March at Milan, in the consulship of Arcadius I and Bauto. This same Law is found as Law III, Cod. de Episcopali audientia, but its ending, from the words His ergo tali sub adstrictione damnatis onwards, is taken from Law VI, Cod. Theod. de Indulgentiis criminum. The subscription, Given on the kalends of May, in the consulship of Arcadius Augustus and Bauto V.C., must be emended from the Theodosian Code to Given on the fifth day before the Kalends of March. The year was the 385th of the Christian era of Dionysius, with solar cycle 2, lunar cycle 6, dominical letter E. The Paschal term fell on the fourth day before the Ides of April, a Thursday, and Easter on the Ides of April. Moreover, by Roman custom an abolition is proclaimed publicly on a notable day, Law VIII, Dig. ad Senatusconsultum Turpillianum. Moreover Honorius ordered that the accused be brought out of prison on each Sunday, so that a supply of food could be provided to them, and that on the said days they be led to the bath under trustworthy guard: Law last, Cod. Theod. de Custodia Reorum.

units.la: Inter sacra, quae maxime coluerunt Athenienses, non infimum locum obtinent Dionysia, itaque & ut ea rite fierent, & celebrantibus bene esset, qua potuerunt ratione cauerunt suis Legibus.
units.tr: Among the sacred rites that the Athenians cultivated most diligently, the Dionysia hold no small place. So, both that they might be performed properly and that those who celebrated them might fare well, they took what precautions they could by their laws.

units.la: ΕΥΗΓΟΡΟΣ[?] ΕΙΠΕΝ ΟΤΑΝ Η ΠΟΜΠΗ Η ΤΩΙ ΔΙΟΝΥΣΩΙ ΕΝ ΠΕΙΡΑΙΕΙ, ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΚΩΜΩΙΔΟΙ ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΤΡΑΓΩΙΔΟΙ ΚΑΙ ΕΠΙ ΛΗΝΑΙΩΙ ΠΟΜΠΗ ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΤΡΑΓΩΙΔΟΙ ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΚΩΜΩΙΔΟΙ ΚΑΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΝ ΑΣΤΕΙ ΔΙΟΝΥΣΙΟΙΣ Η ΠΟΜΠΗ ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΠΑΙΔΕΣ, ΚΑΙ Ο ΚΩΜΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΚΩΜΩΙΔΟΙ, ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΤΡΑΓΩΙΔΟΙ, ΚΑΙ ΘΑΡΓΗΛΙΩΝ ΤΗΙ ΠΟΜΠΗΙ ΚΑΙ ΤΩΙ ΑΓΩΝΙ ΜΗΤΕ ΕΞΕΙΝΑΙ, ΜΗΤΕ ΕΝΕΧΥΡΑΣΑΙ, ΜΗΤΕ ΛΑΜΒΑΝΕΙΝ ΕΤΕΡΟΝ ΕΤΕΡΟΥ, ΜΗΔΕ ΤΩΝ ΥΠΕΡΗΜΕΡΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΑΥΤΑΙΣ ΤΑΙΣ ΗΜΕΡΑΙΣ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΤΙ ΤΟΥΤΩΝ ΤΙΣ ΠΑΡΑΒΑΙΝΗΙ, ΥΠΟΔΙΚΟΣ ΕΣΤΩ ΤΩΙ ΠΑΘΟΝΤΙ, ΚΑΙ ΠΡΟΒΟΛΑΙ ΚΑΤ' ΑΥΤΟΥ ΕΣΤΩΣΑΝ ΕΝ ΤΗΙ ΕΚΚΛΗ-
units.tr: Eugorus [?] said: "When the procession for Dionysus goes in Piraeus, and the comedians, the tragedians, and the procession at the Lenaea, and the tragedians and comedians, and the procession of the city Dionysia, and the boys, and the revel [komos] and the comic actors, and the tragic actors, and the procession and contest of the Thargelia, let no one be arrested, nor seize another's goods, nor take a pledge from another, nor exact a fine for delay during these days. If anyone transgresses any of these, let him be liable to the penalty, and let public notices be posted against him in the Assembly" [Εὐηγόρος(?) εἶπεν ὅταν ἡ πομπὴ ἡ τῷ Διονύσῳ ἐν Πειραιεῖ, καὶ οἱ κωμῳδοὶ καὶ οἱ τραγῳδοὶ καὶ ἐπὶ Ληναίῳ πομπὴ καὶ οἱ τραγῳδοὶ καὶ οἱ κωμῳδοὶ καὶ τοῖς ἐν ἄστει Διονυσίοις ἡ πομπὴ καὶ οἱ παῖδες, καὶ ὁ κῶμος καὶ οἱ κωμῳδοί, καὶ οἱ τραγῳδοί, καὶ Θαργηλίων τῇ πομπῇ καὶ τῷ ἀγῶνι μήτε ἐξεῖναι, μήτε ἐνεχυρασαι, μήτε λαμβάνειν ἕτερον ἑτέρου, μηδὲ τῶν ὑπερημέρων ἐν ταύταις ταῖς ἡμέραις. ἐὰν δέ τι τούτων τις παραβαίνῃ, ὑπόδικος ἔστω τῷ παθόντι, καὶ προβολαὶ κατ' αὐτοῦ ἔστωσαν ἐν τῇ ἐκκλη-].

units.la: Cum pompa Libero ducitur in Piraeo, agunt Comoedi, & Tragoedi, item Lenaea pompa, & agentibus Tragoedis atque Comoedis: Astycorum quoque Liberalium pompa, saltante puerorum Choro, dum fit Comus, aguntque Comoedi, & Tragoedi: Thargeliorum item pompa ac certamine: neque pignus, neque quicquam alterius capito, neue poenam pro mora exigito ab eo, qui iudicatum non soluerit: Qui secus faxit, accusator a laeso, & parabolae aduersus eum dantor apud populum
units.tr: When the procession for Liber is led in Piraeus, the comedians and tragedians act, likewise the Lenaean procession, with the tragedians and comedians acting; also the procession of the Astycan Liberalia, with a chorus of boys dancing, while the comus is performed and the comedians and tragedians act; likewise the procession and contest of the Thargelia. Let no one seize a pledge, nor take anything belonging to another, nor exact a penalty for delay from one who has not paid a judgment. Whoever acts otherwise, let him be liable to the accusation of the injured party, and let proclamations be issued against him before the people.

units.la: ΣΙΑΙ ΤΗΙ ΕΝ ΔΙΟΝΥΣΟΥ ΩΣ ΑΔΙΚΟΥΝΤΟΣ ΚΑΘ' Α ΠΕΡΙ ΤΩΝ ΑΔΙΚΟΥΝΤΩΝ ΓΕΓΡΑΠΤΑΙ.
units.tr: Law of the Dionysia, as it is written concerning wrongdoers, against those who do wrong.

units.la: pro concione in Bacchi, firempfe Lege, qua aduerfus alios, qui religionem temerarint.
units.tr: In the speech on behalf of Bacchus [...] the law against others who have violated religion.

units.la: Lex extat apud Demosthenem in Midiana: Ea autem vt commode intelligatur, sciendum est trina fuisse apud Athenienses Dionysia, nempe τὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς, quae mense Posideone, τὰ Ἀνθεστήρια, quae Anthesterione, τὰ δ' ἄστυ, ἢ κατ' ἄστυ quae Elaphebolione mense celebrabantur, neque de his quisquam disputat: At vero quod τὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς Dionysia eadem sint, quae Λήναια etiam dicuntur, negat vir summus, & contendit Lenaea Dionysia illa esse, quae mense Anthesterione peragebantur: auctoremque laudat Hesychium: qui expressissime de nomine, ad hanc rem, Lenaeorum: Λήναια, ὅτι Ληναῖος [?] Dionysia fuit, Dionysia ... [illegible, ~12 letters] Dionysia fuit. Idem Hesychius: Λήναιων μὲν, Ὀσθηνᾶ τῷ μὲν Βοιωτοὶ οὕτω [?] ... Τὰς ἐπιφάνειας [?] Βουκολικὸν [?], ὃ ἔλεγεν Ἐπιμηλίου, ὡς μὲν τὴν Βουκολικὴν ἑστι. ἔστι δὲ ἡ Ἀνθεστηρίων ἑορτὴ [?] ... Quin & ipse Hesychius Anthesterionem ipsum Lenaeonem appellat: Διονύσια, ἑορτὴ Ἀνθεστηρίων Διονύσου ἡμέρα, τὰ λήνα, τὰ ἀγρὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς μύθους Ποσειδῶνος. τὰ δὲ κατ' ἄστυ μύθους Ληναίους, τὰ δ' ἐπὶ ἀγρὸς ἐξ ἀγορᾶς Λήναιον [?]. Vocem nihil [?] varie emendant, alij enim subfituunt πάλαι, alij, inter quos est vir summus, Ληναῖα, vel ἀγών, atque ita triplicia Dionysia fuis figillatim menfibus pulchre ab Hesychio ordinata: Quare ita intelligedus Aristophanes in Acharnensibus: Ἐγὼ δὲ πολλῷ γὰρ ἐκ πολὺς λέγω Αξῶ τὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς εἶναι Διονύσια.
units.tr: The law is found in Demosthenes' speech Against Midias. To understand it properly, one must know that there were three Dionysia among the Athenians: the rural Dionysia (τὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς), celebrated in the month Posideon; the Anthesteria (τὰ Ἀνθεστήρια), celebrated in Anthesterion; and the city Dionysia (τὰ δ' ἄστυ, or κατ' ἄστυ), celebrated in Elaphebolion. No one disputes this. But that the rural Dionysia are the same as those also called the Lenaea, a distinguished man denies, and he contends that the Lenaea were those Dionysia celebrated in the month Anthesterion. He cites Hesychius as authority, who speaks most plainly about the name in this connection: "Lenaia: because Lenaios was a Dionysia [...]" Hesychius again: "Of the Lenaion [...]" Some editors vary the text in various ways; some insert palai, others, including this distinguished man, insert Lenaia or agon. Thus Hesychius neatly lists the three Dionysia, each in its own month. Accordingly Aristophanes in the Acharnians should be understood thus: "I say that the rural Dionysia are the Lenaea" [...].

units.la: De Lenaeo male interpretari Scholiastem pugnat vir eruditissimus: Posideonis facra esse nemo non videt. Sed de ijs verba ibi fiunt à persona Acharnensi, quae grauioribus soluta curis, rus se conferre destinat: & tempus, in quo loquitur, ad inducias, de quibusibi mentio, spectat. Neque melius idem putat intelligi ab Graeco Interprete, quae in eadem Comoedia hisce verbis traduntur Αὔτη γὰρ ἐσμὲν, ὁ ὅτι Λήναια τ' ἀγών Κοῦσι ξένοι ταχέως φίλοι γὰρ [?] Ἡκοιεν δ' ἐπὶ ἐκ τῆς πόλεως συμμαχίας.
units.tr: A most learned man argues that the Scholiast misinterprets the Lenaeum: no one fails to see that Posideon is sacred to them. But the words there are spoken by the Acharnian character, who, freed from heavier cares, resolves to go to the country, and the time he speaks of relates to the truce mentioned there. Nor does this man think the Greek interpreter understands it better, where in the same comedy these words are rendered: "For we are the ones who say the Lenaea is a contest. Strangers come quickly, for they are friends [...] and they came from the city's alliance."

units.la: O ὅτι Λήναια ἀγὼν ipsissima Anthesteria fuit, seu Liberalia, quae in Limnis agebantur, id est, Lenaea, quibus scilicet Comoedia illa, Acharnenses, docebatur Euthymene Archonte. Lenaeon enim erat in vrbe, non rure, locus in quo certamina celebrabant Athenienses ante Theatrum extructum. Ibi etiam Bacchi Lenaei fanum, adeoq; à Limnis locus hic non diuersus. Hesychius: Ὅτι Ληναῖα, ἀγὼν ἔστι ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ Λήναιον πελάζοντα [?] ... ἐν ᾧ ἐπιτάττω Λήναιον, ... Ληναῖα οἰκοδομήσιμα [?]. Verum nō possumus discedere à sententia, quae vulgo recepta est: neq; dubitamus asserere Lenaea Liberalia esse τὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς Dionysia mitto auctoritatem Graeci Aristophanis Scholiastae, quam cleuat vir magnus, at non est, quod respondeat Thrasyllo apud Diogenem Laertium in Platone: Tragoedi, inquit, τίνα ἀφ' ἀν[?] ἴγκα, Διονυσίοις, Λήναιοις, Πάνα Σταυράίοις, Χύτροις. Retenentur hic festa, per quae fabulas suas committebant Tragici, nempe Dionysia, Lenaea, Panathenaea, & Chytri: Sed non negat Vir magnus Dionysia hic esse [illegible, ~12 letters] Panathenaea sunt verè in his [illegible, ~14 letters] superfunt igitur Lenæa, atque Chytri, quibus Dionysia [illegible, ~8 letters] κατ' ἀγροὺς[?], Anthesteriaque designari nullum est dubium; & quidem Chytri pars sunt Liberalium Anthesteriorum. Scholiastes Aristophanis ad Acharnenses, Φησὶ δὲ Ἀπολλόδωρος [illegible, ~20 letters] Ἀνθεστηρίοις [?] καλεῖσθαι γυναῖκες ἅλλῳ τὴν ἑορτὴν Διονύσου ἀγόμεναι [?]. τρεῖς μὲν δὲ, Πιθοίγια, Χόες, Χύτροι. Pithœgia celebrabantur die undecimo mensis Anthesterionis, Choës, duodecimo; Chytri tertiodecimo. Plutarchus Symposiac. Lib. III. Quæst. VII. [illegible, ~30 letters] Harpocration: Χόες, Διονύσια [?] τῆς [?] τὰ ὀνόματα. ἑορτὴ τῆς παρ' Ἀθηναίοις, ἀγομένη Ἀνθεστηριῶνος δωδεκάτῃ, quo die celebrari scribit Thucydides Lib. II. Dionysia in Limnis, siue Anthesteria: ὃ δὲ [illegible, ~40 letters] ἀγαθὴν [?] τὴν ἐξ [illegible, ~20 letters] ὁ Ζεὺς [?]. Ἐπὶ τοῦ [illegible, ~30 letters] Ἀπόλλων Διονυσιακοῖς [?] τὰ Διονύσια.
units.tr: That the Lenaea is a contest is the very Anthesteria, or the Liberalia, which were performed in the Limnae, that is, the Lenaea, at which that comedy, the Acharnians, was produced under the archon Euthymenes. For the Lenaion was in the city, not in the country, the place where the Athenians held contests before the theatre was built. There also was the shrine of Bacchus Lenaeus, so this place is not different from the Limnae. Hesychius: "Lenaia is a contest in the agora; Lenaion lying near [...] in which I command the Lenaion [...]." But we cannot depart from the opinion that is generally accepted, and we do not hesitate to assert that the Lenaea Liberalia are the rural Dionysia. I set aside the authority of the Greek Aristophanes' Scholiast, which this great man praises, but there is no reason to answer Thrasyllus in Diogenes Laertius in his life of Plato: "Tragedians," he says, "[...] for the Dionysia, the Lenaea, the Panathenaea, and the Chytri." Here are named the festivals at which the tragic poets presented their plays: the Dionysia, the Lenaea, the Panathenaea, and the Chytri. But that great man does not deny that the Dionysia are meant here [...] the Panathenaea are truly in these [...]. So the Lenaea and the Chytri remain, and there is no doubt that by these the rural Dionysia and the Anthesteria are designated; and indeed the Chytri are a part of the Liberal Anthesteria. The Scholiast of Aristophanes on the Acharnians says: "Apollodorus says [...] the women are called Anthesteria, leading the festival of Dionysus. There are three days: Pithoigia, Choes, Chytroi." The Pithoigia were celebrated on the eleventh day of the month Anthesterion, the Choes on the twelfth, the Chytri on the thirteenth. Plutarch, Symposiacs, book III, question VII [...]. Harpocration: "Choes, a Dionysia, a festival among the Athenians, celebrated on the twelfth of Anthesterion" [...] on which day Thucydides, book II, writes that the Dionysia in the Limnae, or Anthesteria, were celebrated [...] "Apollo at the Dionysiaca [...] the Dionysia."

units.la: De Chytris Harpocration. ἐστι δὲ ἡ Ἀθηναίων ἑορτὴ Χύτροις, ἥς μνημονεύει Δείναρχος ἐν τῷ κατὰ Γνήσιον. ἤγαγε δὲ ἡ ἑορτὴ Ἀθηναίοις [illegible, ~24 letters] τῇ ἑκτῇ δίκης, ὡς φησὶ Φιλόχορος ἐν τῷ περὶ ἑορτῶν.
units.tr: On the Chytri, Harpocration: "The Chytri is an Athenian festival, which Dinarchus mentions in his speech Against Gnesion. The festival was held by the Athenians on the [...] day, as Philochorus says in his work On Festivals."

units.la: Quanquam Aristophanis Scholiastes Choum & Chytrorum eundem esse diem statuit. ἐν μιᾷ ἡμέρᾳ ἄγοντο οἱ τε Χύτροι καὶ οἱ Χόες Ἀθηναῖοι. Quare dicendum est Chytrorum nomine intelligi Dionysia Anthesteria in Limnis, vt qui essent huius festi pars, & quidem illa, in qua Tragœdiæ docebantur. Restat igitur, vt apud Thrasyllum Lenæorum nomine intelligantur Dionysia τὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς, quæ alioquin prætermitterentur, cum tamen certum sit Dionysiis his ταῖς κατ' ἀγροὺς dramata committi solita fuisse. Prætera Limnæ erant in vrbe meridiem versus, vt habes in laudatis Thucydidis verbis, cuius Interpres Græcus hæc notat: Λίμναι, τόπος ἐν τῇ ἀκροπόλει τῶν Ἀθηναίων. Lenæum vero erat extra vrbem. Stephanus: Λήναιον ἀγὼν Διονύσου ἐν ἀγροῖς, ἔστι τις λήναιον, Ἀπολλόδωρος ἐν τείτῳ Χρηστῶν. ἡ Λήναιος, ἡ Λήναια. ἔστι δὲ ἡ δῆμος. Quare non est existimandus Hesychius his aduersari, itaque referibo illius verba: Ἔστι Λήναιον ἀγών. ἐπὶ δὲ τοῦ ἀγροῦ. Λήναιον πεῖδολον ἔχον μίαν, ἡ δὲ αὐτὴ Λήναιον Διονυσιακῶν, ἐν ᾧ ἐπιπλωῶν οἱ ἀγῶνες Ἀθηναῖοι, περὶ δὲ Ἡλίου εἰκῆ ἀμφιδιασμένων.
units.tr: Although the Scholiast of Aristophanes holds that the Choes and the Chytri are the same day: "On one day the Athenians celebrated both the Chytroi and the Choes." Hence it must be said that by the name Chytri are understood the Dionysia Anthesteria in the Limnae, as they were part of this festival, and indeed that part in which the tragedies were presented. It remains, then, that in Thrasyllus the name Lenaea is understood as the rural Dionysia, which otherwise would be passed over, although it is certain that plays were customarily presented at these rural Dionysia. Moreover the Limnae were in the city, toward the south, as you have in the words of Thucydides cited above, whose Greek interpreter notes: "Limnae, a place on the Athenian acropolis." But the Lenaeum was outside the city. Stephanus: "Lenaeum, a contest of Dionysus in the fields; there is a certain Lenaeum; Apollodorus in the third book of Chrestoi. The Lenaeus, the Lenaea. It is also a deme." Hence Hesychius should not be thought to contradict these, and I will repeat his words: "There is a Lenaeum, a contest. It refers to the field. The Lenaeum has one [...], and the same is the Lenaeum of the Dionysiaca, in which the contests of the Athenians were held, and concerning which they are idly disputing."

units.la: Non dicit Hesychius Lenæum esse intra vrbem: sed hoc tantum: Commentabatur ille hæc Aristophanis verba:
units.tr: Hesychius does not say that the Lenaeum is within the city, but only this, when he comments on these words of Aristophanes:

units.la: [illegible, ~18 letters]

Notat itaque præter hunc ἔστι Λήναια ἀγῶνα, alterum etiam fuisse, scilicet Liberalium τῶν κατ' ἄστυ, quæ mense Elaphebolione celebrabantur: Deinde quid sit Λήναιον, docet. Meminit autem Dionysiorum Lenæorum siue κατ' ἀγροὺς, & τῶν κατ' ἄστυ tantum, quia ea tempestate, qua fabulam Acharnenses docebat Aristophanes, nondum Dionysiis Anthesteriis, siue Chytris committebantur & producebantur in scenam Comicorum dramata: idque primum institutum Callia μετ' Ἀντιφῶν Athenis Prætore, vt suo loco dicemus, Deo dante, anno tertio Olympiadis nonagesimæ tertiæ, quo anno commisit Comicus drama, cui titulum fecit Ranæ. Atqui Acharnenses docuit Aristophanes Euthydemo Archonte, anno tertio Olympiadis octagesimæ octauæ. Vnde sequitur optime Aristophanis Scholiasten Lenæa interpretari τὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς Dionysia, neque alia intelligere potuit Aristophanes hoc versu:
units.tr: Thus he notes that, besides this Lenaea contest, there was another, namely the Liberalia of the city (τῶν κατ' ἄστυ), which were celebrated in the month Elaphebolion. Then he explains what the Lenaeum is. Now he mentions the Lenaea of the Dionysia, that is, the rural ones, and the city ones alone, because at the time when Aristophanes was presenting the Acharnians, the plays of the comic poets were not yet committed to the Anthesteria Dionysia, or Chytri, nor produced on the stage; and this was first instituted by Callias, with Antiphon as praetor at Athens, as we shall say in its place, God willing, in the third year of the ninety-third Olympiad, in which year the comic poet produced the play he titled Frogs. Yet Aristophanes produced the Acharnians under the archon Euthydemus, in the third year of the eighty-eighth Olympiad. From this it follows that the Scholiast of Aristophanes rightly interprets the Lenaea as the rural Dionysia, and Aristophanes could understand nothing else by this verse:

units.la: Αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐσμὲν, ὁ ὑπὸ Λωναίῳ τ' ἀγρῷ. [?]
units.tr: For we are the ones under the Lonaean field. [Αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐσμὲν, ὁ ὑπὸ Λωναίῳ τ' ἀγρῷ.]

units.la: Nam Dionysia τὰ κατ' ἄγρους non sunt, at multo minus Anthesteria, quia his Dionysiis nondum Comici docebant fabulas: Restat ergo ut de Dionysiis τοῖς κατ' ἀγροῖς interpretemur: atque ob id ipsum meminit tantum Hesychius duorum Liberalium, eorum quæ κατ' ἀγροὺς Posideone, & illorum quæ κατ' ἄστυ Elaphebolione mense peragebantur commissione Comœdiarum: Hesychii autem verba ita sunt legenda: Διονύσια, ἑορτὴ Ἀθήναιν, ἡ Διονύσου ἥγετο, τὰ μὲν κατ' ἀγροὺς μηνὸς Ποσειδεῶνος, τὰ δὲ χέα μηνὸς Ληναιῶνος, τὰ δὲ ἐν ἄστει Ἐλαφηβολιῶνος. Dicit Hesychius Dionysia κατ' ἀγροὺς celebrari mense Posideone, τὰ δὲ χέα μηνὸς Ληναιῶνος, sed nomen famamque fortiri & accipere à mense Lenæone, qui proculdubio idem apud Athenienses cum Posideone, & certe id verum est: nam hæc Dionysia κατ' ἀγροὺς maxime celebrantur Lenæorum nomine. Non sunt igitur Lenæa Dionysia eadem cum Anthesteriis, neque Lenæa celebrabantur in Limnis, sed κατ' ἄστυ: itaque rescribo apud Hesychium, Λίμναι ἐν Ἀθήναις τόπος ἀφιερωμένος Διονύσῳ, ᾧ παρὰ τὰ Λιναῖα ἥγετο. Limnæ locus est intra Athenarum urbem Baccho consecratus, in cuius honorem Lenæa alibi peragebantur: Neque item mensis Lenæon idem est cum Anthesterione, neque id dicit Hesychius, sed hoc unum, Lenæa eo mense peragi solita, quem alii cum Bucatio, alii cum Hermæo comparabant: Λιναιῶν μὲν, ὃ ὁ Πλούταρχος βουκάτιον καλεῖ [?], εἰκάζει δὲ ὁ Πλούταρχος Βουκάτιον, ᾧ γὰρ ψυχῆς ὅσιν. ἕνιοι δὲ τὴν Ἑρμαῖον, ὃς μὴ τὸν βουκάτιόν ἐστιν. καὶ γὰρ Ἀθηναῖοι τῷ τῇ Ληναιῶν ἑορτῇ ὁμοίως ἀπαρτίζουσιν. [?]
units.tr: For the Dionysia "in the country" [τὰ κατ' ἄγρους] are not the Anthesteria, and still less are the Anthesteria them, because at these Dionysia the comic poets did not yet produce plays. It remains, then, that we interpret the Dionysia "in the country" [τοῖς κατ' ἀγροῖς]. For this very reason Hesychius mentions only two festivals of Liber: those held in the country, in the month Posideon, and those held in the city, in the month Elaphebolion, at which comedies were performed. The words of Hesychius should be read thus: "Dionysia, a festival of the Athenians, which was celebrated in honour of Dionysus: those in the country in the month of Poseideon, those in the open in the month of Lenaion, and those in the city in the month of Elaphebolion." [Διονύσια, ἑορτὴ Ἀθήναιν, ἡ Διονύσου ἥγετο, τὰ μὲν κατ' ἀγροὺς μηνὸς Ποσειδεῶνος, τὰ δὲ χέα μηνὸς Ληναιῶνος, τὰ δὲ ἐν ἄστει Ἐλαφηβολιῶνος.] Hesychius says that the Dionysia in the country are celebrated in the month Posideon, but the ones "in the open" [τὰ δὲ χέα] take their name and fame from the month Lenaeon, which without doubt among the Athenians was the same as Poseideon. And this is certainly true: for these Dionysia in the country are celebrated chiefly under the name of the Lenaea. The Lenaea are therefore not the same Dionysia as the Anthesteria, and the Lenaea were not celebrated in the Limnae but in the city. So I would correct the text of Hesychius: "Limnae, a place in Athens consecrated to Dionysus, where it was celebrated beside the Linaea." [Λίμναι ἐν Ἀθήναις τόπος ἀφιερωμένος Διονύσῳ, ᾧ παρὰ τὰ Λιναῖα ἥγετο.] The Limnae is a place within the city of Athens consecrated to Bacchus, in whose honour the Lenaea were celebrated elsewhere. Nor is the month Lenaeon the same as the Anthesterion, nor does Hesychius say so; he says only this, that the Lenaea were customarily celebrated in that month, which some compared with the Boukatios and others with the Hermaios. "Linaion, which Plutarch calls Boukation [?], but Plutarch conjectures Boukation, for it is of the soul…; some (say) Hermaion, which is not the Boukation. For the Athenians also celebrate it in the same way as the festival of the Lenaea." [Λιναιῶν μὲν, ὃ ὁ Πλούταρχος βουκάτιον καλεῖ [?], εἰκάζει δὲ ὁ Πλούταρχος Βουκάτιον, ᾧ γὰρ ψυχῆς ὅσιν. ἕνιοι δὲ τὴν Ἑρμαῖον, ὃς μὴ τὸν βουκάτιόν ἐστιν. καὶ γὰρ Ἀθηναῖοι τῷ τῇ Ληναιῶν ἑορτῇ ὁμοίως ἀπαρτίζουσιν. [?]]

units.la: Optime certe Plutarchus comparat cum Bucatio suorum Bœotorum mensem Lenæonem, unde sequitur Lenæonem eundem esse cum Posideone, quo mense τὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς Dionysia celebrabantur: id liquido constabit ex ipso Plutarcho, cuius hæc verba sunt in Aristide ubi agit de Plataensi pugna: Τῶν τῆς μάχης ἐμαχέσαντο τῇ πεπάλῃ τῆς Βοιωτοῖς, ἔνθα Βοιωτοὶ κεκηρυγμένοι ἱσταμένου κατ' Ἀθηναίους, τῆς δὲ Βοιωτοῖς, πεπάλῃ τῆς Παναμου φύλοιτος. Dies vicesimus septimus Panemi Bœotorum est quartus politice, id est, tertius vere Boëdromionis Athenienstium: Ergo cepit Panemus die septimo Metagitnionis anni Lunaris Athenienses: itaque optime idem Plutarchus Panemum hunc confert cum Metagitnione in Camillo: αἰάπα λιν δὲ ὁ Μεταγεΐτνιῶν (οἱ Βοιωτοὶ Παναμου καλοῦσιν) Ἑλλην σὺν ἀμφίς γέγονε. Τοῦτον δὲ τῆς μηνὸς ἐξόδιμη ᾗ τῷ ἐν Καρίαν μάχῳ πηδήσαντες, &c. Eratque dies hic septimus Metagitnionis Athenienstum dies primus Panemi Bœotorum. Atque hinc emendandus est, ut hoc obiter addam, Plutarchus ibidem in his, quæ paullo ante leguntur: Βοιωτοῖς, ἱπποδρομίου μηνὸς, ὡς δὴ Ἀθηναῖοι καλοῦσιν, Ἐκατομβαιῶνος ἱσταμένου πέμπτῃ, δύο λαβὼν σὺν ἑκὸν νίκας ἐπιφάνειᾶς, τῷ τε τῷ Λέυκτρα, ᾗ τῷ ὑπὸ Γεγαμένῳ. Quæ de Panemo diximus faciunt, ut possimus pronunciare de Hippodromio, quem fruftra putant viri magni septimum esse, imo octauus est, cepitque à vero die septimo Hecatombæonis, qui politice octauus numeratur, occupatque ex hinc Hecatombæonis ceteros dies, eiusque dies vltimus (nam cauus est hic Bœotorum mensis) cadit in sextum Metagitnionis, à die vero septimo Metagitnionis incipit Panemus, vt iam diximus, eiusque vicesimus septimus dies cadit in diem tertium, politice quar-
units.tr: Plutarch certainly compares well with the Boukation the Lenaeon of his Boeotians, from which it follows that the Lenaeon is the same as Posideon, in which month the Dionysia in the country were celebrated. This will be clear beyond doubt from Plutarch himself, whose words in the Life of Aristides, where he treats of the battle of Plataea, are these: "Of the battle, they fought on the day of the... (Boeotian month) in which the Boeotians... was held against the Athenians..." [Τῶν τῆς μάχης ἐμαχέσαντο τῇ πεπάλῃ τῆς Βοιωτοῖς, ἔνθα Βοιωτοὶ κεκηρυγμένοι ἱσταμένου κατ' Ἀθηναίους, τῆς δὲ Βοιωτοῖς, πεπάλῃ τῆς Παναμου φύλοιτος.] The twenty-seventh day of the Boeotian Panemus is the fourth by the civil reckoning, that is, truly the third of the Athenian Boedromion. Therefore Panemus began on the seventh day of the lunar month Metageitnion at Athens. So Plutarch himself rightly compares this Panemus with the Metageitnion in his Life of Camillus: "The Metageitnion (which the Boeotians call Panemus) happened to fall… And at the end of this month, at the battle in Caria, they leapt…" [αἰάπα λιν δὲ ὁ Μεταγεΐτνιῶν (οἱ Βοιωτοὶ Παναμου καλοῦσιν) Ἑλλην σὺν ἀμφίς γέγονε. Τοῦτον δὲ τῆς μηνὸς ἐξόδιμη ᾗ τῷ ἐν Καρίαν μάχῳ πηδήσαντες, &c.] This seventh day of the Athenian Metageitnion was the first day of the Boeotian Panemus. And from this, as I add in passing, Plutarch must be emended in the passage read a little before: "Of the Boeotians, the month of the horse-race, as the Athenians call it, on the fifth day after the beginning of Hecatombaeon, having won two victories…" [Βοιωτοῖς, ἱπποδρομίου μηνὸς, ὡς δὴ Ἀθηναῖοι καλοῦσιν, Ἐκατομβαιῶνος ἱσταμένου πέμπτῃ, δύο λαβὼν σὺν ἑκὸν νίκας ἐπιφάνειᾶς, τῷ τε τῷ Λέυκτρα, ᾗ τῷ ὑπὸ Γεγαμένῳ.] What we have said about Panemus enables us to say something about the Hippodromios, whom great men have vainly thought to be the seventh month; indeed it is the eighth, and it began on the true seventh day of Hecatombaeon, which by civil reckoning is counted the eighth, and it fills the remaining days of Hecatombaeon; its last day (for this Boeotian month is hollow) falls on the sixth of Metageitnion. From the true seventh day of Metageitnion Panemus begins, as we have said, and its twenty-seventh day falls on the third day, by civil reckoning the fourth, of Boedromion. This observation will lead us to the investigation of the truth. It is clear that Plutarch here means the beginning of the Hippodromios, as the illustrious man also notes, who is not to be heard in what he denies, that Plutarch added [illegible] to the Hippodromion. For I do not doubt that Plutarch must be read thus: [illegible].

units.la: [?] Greek text in the scan is faint and partly blurred; readings marked [?] are doubtful. tum, Boedromionis, quæ obseruatio nos deducet ad inuestigationem veri: Manifestum autem est hic à Plutarcho Ιπποδρομίῳ ἱσταμένῳ intelligi, quod etiá monet vir Illustris, qui non est audiendus in eo, quod negat Plutarchum apposuisse [illegible, ~12 letters] τῆ Ιπποδρομίῳ. Nam nullus dubito ita rescribendum esse apud Plutarchum: [illegible, ~45 letters]. Excideràt litera numeralis ι, quia ab ea incipiebat sequens dictio: est autem Ἑκατομβαιῶνος δεκάτῃ, dies vere decimus Hecatombæonis, qui politice vndecimus numerabatur, nam hic mensis erat cauus, vt alibi probauimus: Erat autem dies [illegible, ~20 letters] dies quintus politice Hippodromij, reuera autem quartus, qui incidit in diem decimum Hecatombæonis. Incipit namque Hippodromius à die septimo Hecatombæonis: Atque ex his repetendum est initium mensis Bucatij. Hinc nempe patet cepisse die septimo mensis Posideonis: Quare optime Plutarchus apud Hesychium comparat cum Lenæone, qui Posideon est, optimeq; conuenit cum iis, quæ de tempestate anni refert idem Plutarch in Pelopida:
units.tr: [Greek text in the scan is faint and partly blurred; readings marked [?] are doubtful.] …by civil reckoning the fourth, of Boedromion, which observation will lead us to the investigation of the truth. It is clear here that Plutarch means the Hippodromios beginning, as the illustrious man also notes, who is not to be heard in what he denies, that Plutarch added [illegible] to the Hippodromios. For I do not doubt that Plutarch must be read thus: [illegible]. The numeral letter ι had dropped out, because the following word began with it: it is the tenth day of Hecatombaeon [Ἑκατομβαιῶνος δεκάτῃ], which by civil reckoning was counted the eleventh, for this month was hollow, as we have proved elsewhere. The day was [illegible], the fifth day by civil reckoning of the Hippodromios, but in truth the fourth, which falls on the tenth day of Hecatombaeon. For the Hippodromios begins on the seventh day of Hecatombaeon. From this the beginning of the month Bukation must be recovered. From this it plainly appears that it began on the seventh day of the month of Poseideon. Wherefore Plutarch rightly compares it in Hesychius with the Lenaeon, which is Poseideon, and it agrees very well with what the same Plutarch reports of the season of the year in his Life of Pelopidas:

units.la: [illegible, ~120 letters]
units.tr: [illegible]

units.la: & paulò post: [illegible, ~60 letters]. Atque ex his facile posset, si quidem rem tanti faceremus, pro ea, quæ est inter hos Bœotorum mensesque atque Atticos, comparatione, Periodum siue Octaeteridem, siue, quod potius puto, dum tempora Pelopidæ spectò, Enneadecaeteridem extruere, atque caput illius deprehendere. Atque hæc de Lenæis siue Dionysiis [illegible, ~6 letters] satis, si addidero, videri diesfestos non fuisse ab omnibus otiosè transactos: nam in palliata Terentij Heautontimorumeno, dies, quo erant Dionysia [illegible, ~6 letters], Menedemo, qui in illo ipso populo, Lenæo, apud quem agitabantur hæc Dionysia, degebat, fuit [illegible, ~8 letters]: ecce namque tibi Menedemum occantem; huic quippe rei rastros præ manibus habebat: & proculdubio Menander hanc fabulam docuerat Liberalibus [illegible, ~4 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters]. De Liberalibus habes Scena I.
units.tr: And a little after: [illegible]. From these things one could easily, if we thought the matter of such importance, construct, for the comparison between these Boeotian months and the Attic ones, a Period or Octaeteris, or, what I think better while I look to the times of Pelopidas, an Enneadecaeteris, and so discover its head. And let this suffice concerning the Lenaea or Dionysia [illegible], if I add that the festival days were not spent idly by everyone. For in the palliata of Terence, the Heautontimorumenos, the day on which the Dionysia [illegible] were held was [illegible] for Menedemus, who lived in that very people, the Lenaeon, where these Dionysia were celebrated. For behold, Menedemus is there digging, for he had rakes in hand for this business; and no doubt Menander had produced this play at the Liberalia [illegible]. You have the Liberalia in Scene 1:

units.la: Dionysia hic sunt: hodie apud me sis volo.
units.tr: The Dionysia are here today; I want you to be with me.

units.la: Liberalia verò [illegible, ~6 letters] intelligi, accipies ex eadem Scena: nam [illegible, ~8 letters] Chremetem ædes habuisse suas probat, quod Menedemi ager in proximo:
units.tr: That the Liberalia [illegible] is to be understood, you will learn from the same scene, for [illegible] shows that Chremes had his own house, because Menedemus's field is next door:

units.la: Inde adeo quod agrum in proxime hic mercatus es.
units.tr: Since you have bought the field here nearby.

units.la: Idque pro ædibus Chremetis, vnde dicebat,
units.tr: And this refers to Chremes' house, whence he said:

units.la: Nunquam tam mane egredior, neque tam vesperi / Domum reuertor, quin te in fundo conspicer / Fodere aut arare.
units.tr: I never go out so early, nor come home so late in the evening, but I see you in your field digging or ploughing.

units.la: Atque ex his, vt & ex istis eiusdem Scenæ:
units.tr: And from these, as also from those of the same scene:

units.la: --Istos rastros interea tamen
units.tr: —Meanwhile put down those rakes

units.la: Adpone, ne labora.
units.tr: so that you don't tire yourself.

units.la: Tempus Liberalium [illegible, ~8 letters] designari certum est, nam & fodit fossas, quo pluuia aqua delabatur, & arat, & occat, quæ omnia incidunt in illam anni tempestatem, quæ ab autumnali æquinoctio ad brumam intercedit, cùm iam claufa funt maria, itaque tributa Athenas non importabant locij tunc temporis, & foli fuum Lenæorum fiue Dionyfiorum ἦν κατ' ἄστυ festum agitabant Athenienses: Aristophanes verbis iam sæpe laudatis: Αὐτὴ γὰρ ἐσμὲν, ὁ ὑπὲρ Αἰωαίας τ' ἀγών. Κύπρου ξένοι πρῶτον, ὅτι τὸ φῶς. Ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐν τῷ πόλεως οἱ ξυμμαχοί.
units.tr: The time of the Liberalia [illegible] is certainly indicated, for men dig trenches through which rainwater may run off, and plough, and harrow, all of which fall in that season of the year which lies between the autumn equinox and the winter solstice, when the seas are now closed, so that tributes were not then being brought into Athens, and the Athenians celebrated the Lenaea or Dionysia "in the city" [ἦν κατ' ἄστυ] alone. Aristophanes, in the words already often cited: "For we are the ones under the Aiakai contest. Strangers first of Cyprus, because of the light. But we, in the city, the allies." [Αὐτὴ γὰρ ἐσμὲν, ὁ ὑπὲρ Αἰωαίας τ' ἀγών. Κύπρου ξένοι πρῶτον, ὅτι τὸ φῶς. Ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐν τῷ πόλεως οἱ ξυμμαχοί.] The Scholiast: "The contest of the Dionysia was arranged for the year… that the Athenians… tribute… of the Aiakai, so called, that strangers… the third, Athenians…" [ὁ τῆ Διονυσίων ἀγὼν ἐπλαίσθη εἰς τὸ ἔτος. ὅτι οἱ φόρου Ἀθηναῖοι τῶν.]

units.la: Scholiastes: ὁ τῆ Διονυσίων ἀγὼν ἐπλαίσθη εἰς τὸ ἔτος. ὅτι οἱ φόρου Ἀθηναῖοι τῶν. ὅτι τῶν Αἰωαίας λεγόμενος ὅτι ξένοι ἡ τρίτῳ Ἀθηναῖοι· ἀλλὰ ἴδιον. Hunc locum descripsimus,quia ea confirmant maximè, de quibus in superioribus disputauimus, cùm de constituendis aliquot Hefychij locis ageremus: scilicet tunc duo tantum Dionysia,& τὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς, & τὰ κατ' ἄστυ, celebrabantur commissione Comœdiarum: ex hypothesi hac itaque dicunt duo tantum fuisse Dionysiorum festa, non quod Anthefleria non celebrarentur, sed quia Comici iis nondum sua producebant dramata. Verùm quod diximus tributa non fuisse Athenas importata quando celebrabantur Lenæa, videtur aduersari titulo Orationis cuiusdam Antiphontis, cuius meminit Harpocration: Ἀμφίτης Ἀθηναῖος τῆς Λιωαίας φόρου, πολὺς αὐτῶν τῆς Θράκης. Scd hic, meo iudicio, agitur de tributo, quod pendebant Atheniensibus Lenæi Elidis populi, quorum è Phlegonte meminit Stephanus: Λιωαῖοι, χώρα τῆς Πισαίων. ὁ πολίτης Λιωαίας· Φλέγων παραγεγραπται ἔδει Ολυμπιάδ. Hoc vnum commune Lenæis & Anthefleriis Liberalibus, quod vtrifque præerat Rex: de Lenæis habes apud Pollucem, de Anthefleriis colligere licet è Demosthenis Oratione in Neæram. Sed nimium multa fortasse, quæ tamen, spero, certè opto, ingrata non eruntingenuis & liberalibus adolescentibus. Nunc porro restat expendenda Lex, qua cauetur ne quis Liberalibus, aut Thargelijs pignus, aut quicquam alterius ἐκ χρῆς ἡμῶν capiat, neve pœnam à quoquam, quod iudicatum non soluerit, pro mora exigat: qui secus fecisset,poterat apud populum iniuriarum in scli religionem postulari: Legem hanc ὡλλά ξεῖ descripsit Demosthenes in Midiana: sed in illa quædam non satis emendatè legunrur: ΕΥΗΓΟΡΟΣ ΕΙΠΕΝ ΟΤΑΝ Η ΓΩΜΡΗ Η, ΤΩΙ ΔΙΟΝΥΣΩΙ ΕΝ ΓΕΙΡΑΙΕΙ ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΚΩΜΩΙΔΟΙ ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΤΡΑΓΩΙΔΟΙ. Triplicia illa Liberalia recensentur hæc Lege,quorum in superioribus meminimus: nam en tibi Dionysia quæ dicit esse ἐν ΠΕΙΡΑΙΕΙ. Sequitur ΕΠΙ ΑΗΝΑΙΩΙ ΓΩΜΡΗ, id est,Dionysia κατ' ἄστυ. Denique ΤΟΙΣ ΕΝ ΑΣΤΕΙ ΔΙΟΝΥΣΙΟΙΣ Η ΠΟΜΡΗ, Dionysia, quæ mense Elaphebolione celebrabantur. Sunt igitur prima illa Dionysia ΕΝ ΠΕΙΡΑΙΕΙ, antiquissima, quæ in Limnis mense Anthefleriorne peragebantur. Quomodo igitur dicentur in Piræo? Sanè non potest, nam si in Piræo celebrabantur, non igitur in Limnis, nam Limnæ intra vrbem: Αἰωαῖ, τῆς δὲ τῆ ἀκρόπολι ΑΣΤΩΙ, inquit Thucydides Scholiastes: Atqui certum est, atque indubitatum est in Limnis fuisse celebrata Anthefleria ista Dionysia: Est igitur medium in his ΕΝ ΠΕΙΡΑΙΕΙ. Quare rescribendum putamus: ΟΤΑΝ Η ΓΩΜΡΗ Η, ΤΩΙ ΔΙΟΝΥΣΩΙ ΗΝ ΠΕΡ ΑΙΕΙ ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΚΩΜΩΙΔΟΙ
units.tr: I have transcribed this passage because it strongly confirms what we argued earlier, when we were settling some passages of Hesychius: namely, that only two Dionysia were celebrated with the performance of comedies, the one "in the country" [τὰ κατ' ἀγροὺς] and the one "in the city" [τὰ κατ' ἄστυ]. On this hypothesis they say there were only two festivals of Dionysia, not because the Anthesteria were not celebrated, but because the comic poets did not yet produce their plays at them. But what we said, that tribute was not brought into Athens when the Lenaea were celebrated, seems to conflict with the title of a certain oration of Antiphon, which Harpocration mentions: "Amphitês, an Athenian, of the tribute of the Aiakai, much of it from Thrace." [Ἀμφίτης Ἀθηναῖος τῆς Λιωαίας φόρου, πολὺς αὐτῶν τῆς Θράκης.] But this, in my judgement, concerns the tribute which the Lenaeans of the people of Elis paid to the Athenians, of whom Stephanus mentions from Phlegon: "Lenaioi, a region of the Pisaeans; the citizen of Lenaia; Phlegon is cited in the Olympiads." [Λιωαῖοι, χώρα τῆς Πισαίων. ὁ πολίτης Λιωαίας· Φλέγων παραγεγραπται ἔδει Ολυμπιάδ.] The one thing the Lenaea and the Liberalia of the Anthesteria share is that both were presided over by a king: about the Lenaea you have it in Pollux, and about the Anthesteria one may gather it from Demosthenes' oration against Neaera. But perhaps I have said too much; yet I hope, and earnestly wish, that it will not be unwelcome to freeborn and liberal young men. Now it remains to examine the law by which it is provided that no one shall take a pledge during the Liberalia or the Thargelia, nor anything else "from anyone" [ἐκ χρῆς ἡμῶν], nor exact a penalty from anyone for delay in paying what has been adjudged; whoever did otherwise could be prosecuted before the people for an injury against the sacred rites. Demosthenes wrote out this law in his speech against Midias, but some things in it are not read quite correctly: "Eyēgoros said: whenever the…, at the Dionysia in the Peiraieus, and the comedies, and the tragedies." [ΕΥΗΓΟΡΟΣ ΕΙΠΕΝ ΟΤΑΝ Η ΓΩΜΡΗ Η, ΤΩΙ ΔΙΟΝΥΣΩΙ ΕΝ ΓΕΙΡΑΙΕΙ ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΚΩΜΩΙΔΟΙ ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΤΡΑΓΩΙΔΟΙ.] This law lists three kinds of Liberalia, of which we have spoken above: for here are the Dionysia which it says were "in the Peiraieus." Then follows "at the Asteian (city) comedy," that is, the Dionysia "in the city." Finally "at the Dionysia in the city, the comedy," the Dionysia celebrated in the month Elaphebolion. The first Dionysia, therefore, "in the Peiraieus," the most ancient, which were celebrated in the Limnae in the month Anthesterion, are the ones in question. How then can they be said to be in the Peiraieus? Certainly they cannot, for if they were celebrated in the Peiraieus they were not in the Limnae, since the Limnae lie within the city: "Aiakai, the tribute of the Acropolis, in the city," says the Scholiast on Thucydides. Yet it is certain and beyond doubt that these Anthesteria Dionysia were celebrated in the Limnae. The middle term, then, is "in the Peiraieus." Wherefore we think it should be read: "Whenever the…, at the Dionysia [in the Peiraieus?] and the comedies…"

units.la: ΚΑΙ ΟΙ ΤΡΑΓΩΙΔΟΙ. Ratio emendationis nostrae haec est: Ante annum tertium Olympiadis nonagesimae tertiae in scenam productam non sunt Comicorum dramata Anthesteriis Liberalibus: hoc primum anno, cuius Fastos signauit Praetor Athenis Callias [illegible, ~12 letters], institutum est, ut scribit Aristoteles, Anthesteria Dionysia celebrati commissione Comoediarum: sed id diu non obtinuit, nam Cinesias Aristophanis aequalis, & Poetis Comicis, à quibus vexabatur, parum aequus, hanc Legem abrogari curauit, & demum Lycurgus Rhetor Legem tulit, quia Comoedias docere Anthesteriis, cauebatur: Cum igitur Euegorus huius Legis auctor videret rem adeo firmam non esse, ut mutari nequiret, & paululum ante Lycurgus Legem hanc, de Comoediarum commissione Liberalibus Anthesteriis, tulisset, optime Euegorus in hac sua Lege dixit, [illegible, ~14 letters] Comoedis. Atque ex his circumscribere licet tempus latae huius Legis, nam lata est post illam Lycurgi, qui in Republica eadem tempestate cum Demosthene floruit, eius vero meminit Demosthenes in Midiana, quam scripsit anno quarto Olympiadis centesimae septimae, Callimacho Athenis Praetore: Ergo ante hunc annum quartum Olympiadis centesimae septimae scripta est haec Lex ab Euegoro, sed non longe ante, siquidem post latam alteram illam à Lycurgo de Comoediis docendis Liberalibus Anthesteriis scripta est. Hac igitur Lege non licebat quicquam alterius, vel pignori capere [illegible, ~10 letters], ac ne quidem [illegible, ~12 letters]. Ulpianus: [illegible, ~20 letters]. Demosthenes paulo post: [illegible, ~30 letters]. De Liberalibus autem non tantum agitur, verumetiam de Thargelijs, quae in honorem Apollinis atque Dianae celebrabantur: Sed non possumus satis mirari virum eruditissimum ad hanc Legem referre illa ex Andocidis [illegible, ~5 letters] Oratione: [illegible, ~40 letters]. Nam ista ante Thargelia facta sunt, non ipsis Thargelijs, nempe statim ac Choragus renunciatus est: & certe Theodotus puer, periit die vicesimo septimo Munychionis, elatus est die vicesimo nono: en tibi eadem Oratione elatum esse die tertio à morte: [illegible, ~30 letters]. incidisse autem hunc diem in vicesimum nonum Munychionis ex his constat, quae eadem Oratione leguntur: [illegible, ~30 letters]. Die tricesimo mensis, [illegible, ~5 letters] reos erat peracturus Aristonem & Philinum, pridie cum accusauit caedis Philocrates, quo die puer elatus erat: ergo elatus est die vicesimonono mensis, qui Munychion est: quod hinc patet. Philocrates cum suis deferunt hunc Choragum, cui Orationem scripsit Antiphon, apud Regem die ultimo mensis, quo noster hic Choragus causam agebat apud iudices aduersus Aristonem, aut aliud ex iis, quos accusaverat: [illegible, ~60 letters] Rex negat posse per Leges illum [illegible, ~12 letters] habes in sequentibus: [illegible, ~70 letters] Nam futurus erat adhuc in Magistratu duos tantum menses, Thargelionem & Scirrhophorionem, quatuor autem opus erat: [illegible, ~45 letters] Dicuntur igitur illa à Rege die tricesimo mensis Munychionis, cum superesset duo menses Thargelion atque Scirrophorion anno perficiendo. Longè autem ante quam illa accidissent, dicit se neque ullum multasse, neque pignus cepisse, scilicet, cum Chorum legeret, qui saltare debebat Thargeliis, ipse optimus interpres his verbis: [illegible, ~50 letters] Non igitur cum Thargeliorum festum celebraretur: ac proinde neque ad hanc Legem attendit, adde quod non negat his verbis, siquidem illa capio, se potuisse multare, aut pignus capere, sed ex eo quod non fecerit, suam probat [illegible, ~10 letters]. Denique, etiamsi ista omnia contigissent Thargeliis, non potuisset animum advertere ad hanc Legem, siquidem nondum erat scripta: nam Antiphon longè antequam ferretur suum obiverat diem. Atque haec quidem satis, sed non possum, quia tam commoda se offert occasio, praetermittere quaedam ex eadem Antiphontis Oratione, quin emendem & illustrem. Docet igitur in sequentibus è Choragi persona Antiphon, quando scripta fuerit apud Regem, qui anno sequenti Magistratu iniit, dicat: [illegible, ~110 letters] Verum non optime convenit his numeris cum calculo, quia in sequentibus docet se fuisse unum è Quingentorum Senatu, cui absolvendae suae Tribus Prytaneiae duo tantum dies supererant. Tribus autem eius primam sortita erat Prytaneiam, quando nomen apud Regem delatum est: [illegible, ~80 letters] Erat autem Prytancia numerus dierum triginta quinque. Harpocration: [illegible, ~30 letters] Ergo Choragi nostri nomen delatum est apud Regem [illegible, ~40 letters], die tricesimo quarto Prytaneias, qui erat quintus Metagitnionis; nam Hecatombaeon cavus est: itaque neque vicesimo Metagitnionis die, delatus est, neque Rex ab adito suo Magistratu dies quinquaginta praefuerat. Referibo igitur: Ἀλλὰ πρῶτον τῆς Ἰούνου τῆς μιᾶς ἢ εἰ κ' ἔσται, ἡμέρας. Aduenerant, inquit, Metagitnionis mensis dies quinque, si quidem, sunt. Optime certè, vt subductis rationibus demonstratur. Hecatombaeoni viginti nouem dies sunt imputandi, adde quinque dies Metagitnionis, fiunt triginta quatuor, tricesimo autem quarto die Prytaneias delatus est apud Regem, itaque vix quintus dies aduenerat. Ex his quoque constat in sequentibus legendum esse: ὥστε αἱ συμπάσαι ἡμέραι ἡμέραι ἕξ ἡμέρα ὠφέλιμοι εἴκοσι ὀκτὼ, πλέον ἢ πεντεκαίδεκα τοῦ ἑκάστου τῆς Βασιλέως. Facilis lapsus in literis numeralibus, ita vt litera ν scribatur αὐτῆ λ'.
units.tr: καὶ οἱ τραγῳδοί [and the tragic poets]. The reason for our emendation is this. Before the third year of the ninety-third Olympiad, comedies were not staged at the Anthesteriis Liberalia. In that year, whose Athenian archon was the praetor Callias [illegible], it was instituted, as Aristotle writes, that comedies be performed at the Anthesteria, the Dionysia. But this did not last long. Cinesias, a contemporary of Aristophanes and not very fair to the comic poets, by whom he was attacked, had the law repealed. Finally the orator Lycurgus proposed a law forbidding comedies to be produced at the Anthesteriis. Since Euegorus, the author of this law, saw that the matter was not so settled that it could not be changed, and since Lycurgus had a little earlier proposed his law on the staging of comedies at the Liberalia, the Anthesteriis, Euegorus rightly said in his own law [illegible] for Comoedis. From this we can fix the date of this law. It was passed after that of Lycurgus, who flourished in public affairs at the same time as Demosthenes. Demosthenes mentions it in the Midiana, which he wrote in the fourth year of the hundred and seventh Olympiad, when Callimachus was praetor at Athens. So this law was written by Euegorus before that fourth year of the hundred and seventh Olympiad, but not long before, since it was written after that other law of Lycurgus on staging comedies at the Liberalia, the Anthesteriis. By this law it was not allowed to take anything of another's, or to seize a pledge [illegible], nor even [illegible]. Ulpian: [illegible]. Demosthenes shortly after: [illegible]. The law deals not only with the Liberalia but also with the Thargelijs, which were celebrated in honour of Apollo and Diana. But we cannot sufficiently wonder that so learned a man refers to this law those words from the speech of Andocides [illegible]: [illegible]. For those things were done before the Thargelia, not during the Thargelijs themselves, namely as soon as the choregus was proclaimed. And certainly the boy Theodotus died on the twenty-seventh day of Munychion and was buried on the twenty-ninth day. Look, in the same speech he is said to have been buried on the third day after death [illegible]. That this day fell on the twenty-ninth of Munychion is clear from what is read in the same speech: [illegible]. On the thirtieth day of the month, [illegible], Philocrates was about to pursue the accused Ariston and Philinus; he had charged them with murder the day before, the day on which the boy was buried. So the boy was buried on the twenty-ninth day of the month, which is Munychion, as is clear from this. Philocrates and his people denounce this choregus, for whom Antiphon wrote a speech, before the king on the last day of the month, the day on which our choregus was pleading his case before the judges against Ariston or one of those whom he had accused [illegible]. The king denies that by the laws he can [illegible]. You will have the following: [illegible]. For he was to remain in office only two more months, Thargelion and Scirrhophorion, whereas four were needed [illegible]. Therefore those things were brought before the king on the thirtieth day of Munychion, when two months, Thargelion and Scirrhophorion, were left to complete the year.
