units.la: Quinquaginta illi ex vnaquaque Tribu forte capti Senatores Πρυτάνεις dicebantur. Grammatici: [illegible, ~70 letters]. Sorte autem ductæ Tribus imperabant sibi inuicem succedentes. Grammatici: [illegible, ~60 letters]. Ita singulæ Tribus dies triginta quinque imperabant. Vlpianus in Androtianam: [illegible, ~90 letters] δι[?]ἡμέρας γὰρ τεσσαράκοντα, τεσσαρακοστὰ, πεντάκις δίκας, πεντήκοντα. Supererant anno Lunari perficiendo quatuor illi τῇ [?]ἐπαγομέναι dies, post regna triginta quinque dierum, quibus quaelibet decem Tribuum ordine sorte ducto praefecta fuerat: illi quatuor dies imputabantur quatuor Tribubus, quae primae imperauerant. Suidas: [?]ἀρυτθμεία δὲ ὁ τῆς ἡμέρας ἀριθμὸς. δίκα ἐγίνοντο κατ' αὐτῶν, ὅτι καὶ δίκας αἱ Φυλαί. αὐτῶν δὲ οἱ Αἰγεωΐδαι τὸν Σελωνιακὸν ἦρον. ἐπέβαλε δὲ ἑκάστη Φυλὴ τῇ δίκα τεσσαράκοντα πέντε ἡμέρας. καὶ ἐπεξῆλθον ἐκ τῆς Σελωνιακοῦ αὐτοῦ ἡμέραι πάντα-ρες, αἱ ἐπιμελεῖσθαι τῶν ἐφόρων λαχούσας ἀρυτθμεῖν τὸ ἀπαρτὶ Φυλῆς. καὶ τῆς μὲν πέντε ἐπιφορῶν ἐφόρων ἐπὶ εἶχε ἀρυτθμεία ἀπ' ἀρχῆς εἰς τεσσαράκοντα ἐξ ἡμέρας. αἱ δὲ λοιπαὶ ἐξ αὐταὶ τεσσαράκοντα πέντε. ἀρυτθμεία δύο ὅτι ἀριθμὸς ἡμερῶν, ἵνα τεσσαράκοντα ἐξ, ἀλλὰ τεσσαράκοντα πέντε. Exiftimauit Illuftris Scaliger vnamquamque Tribum vnum diem per orbem fununam rerum geffiffe & imperaffe, vt, exempli gratia, heri [?]ἡ Αἰαντὶς Φυλὴ imperabat, hodie [?]ἡ Κεκροπὶς, cras [?]ἡ Ἀκαμαντὶς, & ita deinceps totum vertentem annum vnaquaeque fuam [?]ἐφημερίδα imperabat, prout forte ducta erat ab ipso anni principio. Sed huic fententiae aduerfantur aliquot veterum Oratorum teftimonia, quibus facile probatur vnamquamq; Tribum triginta quinque fuos dies continuo imperaffe, non fingulae fuam per orbem [?]ἐφημερίαν. Apud Demofthenem in Timocratea prima Pfephifmatis vnius verba haec funt: [?]ἐπὶ τῆς Παιανιΐδος, ἀφ' ἧς ἐνδικάτη τῆς Πρυτανείας, Τιμοκράτης εἶπεν. & paulò post: [?]τοὺς Πρυτάνεις τοῖς τῆς Παιανιΐδος καθέσται Νομοθέτης αὐτῶν. Nempe quia etiam poftridie imperabat Tribus Pandionis,quod etiam conftat ex altero Pfephifmate poftridie fcripto, quod eadem Oratione legitur: [?]ἐπὶ τῆς Πανδιονίδος, ἀφ' ἧς Πρυτανείας δωδεκάτη, τῇ Γερεῶν ἐπεψηφίσατ' Αἰσχύλης Μυρρινούσιος, Τιμοκράτης εἶπε. Vides duos continuos dies imperaffe Pandionidem, [?]ἐκ ἃ πρὸς Ἀριστοκλῆς (nam [?]μυρρινοῦς, inquit Stephanus, [?]ἡ[?]μῆς τῆς Παιανιΐδος Φυλῆς) [?]τὸ ἐψηφισμένον populum in fuffragia mifit. Sed nullum dubitationi locum effe finit Antiphon [?]ἐν τοῖς περὶ τὴν Χορεύτρια, quin triginta quinque continuos dies fingulae Tribus imperarint: haec enim eius verba funt: [?]ὁρᾶντες δὲ με βαλβίδα, καὶ εἰσιόντες ὃ βαλβιτήσιον, καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ βαλβιτήσιον Διὸς Βαλαΐου καὶ Ἀθηνᾶς Βυλαίας ἱερόν ἐστι, καὶ εἰσιόντες οἱ Βυλευταὶ ἀφεσόμενοι. ὧν κάγω εἰς ἓν ὁ ταῦτα ἀφέληκεν, καὶ εἰς πᾶσα πάντα ἱερὰ εἰσιὼν μὴ τῆς βουλῆς, καὶ ζῷον καὶ ἀνδρόμους ἐν τῆς πόλεως ταύτης, καὶ πρὸς ταῦτα ἀπὸ τὸ ἀφῃτόν Πρυ[?]τανείας ἀπάσης, πλεῖ δύοιν ἡμέραιν, καὶ ἐεξποιῶν καὶ ζῷον ἐν τῆς δημοκρατίας, καὶ ὁπ[?]ηλοφίζων καὶ λέγων γνώμας ἀπὸ τῶν μεγίστων καὶ πλείστου ἀξίων τῇ πόλει Φανερὰς ἔῶ. Dicuntur enim ifta de iis quae acciderunt die quinto Metagitnionis menfis, vt in fuperioribus expofuimus. Sed de his fatis.
units.tr: Those fifty men from each tribe who were chosen by lot as Senators were called Prytaneis [Πρυτάνεις]. The grammarians say [...]. The tribes thus drawn by lot held power in turn, one after another. The grammarians say [...]. So each tribe ruled for thirty-five days. Ulpian on the Androtion: [...] for forty days... [The Greek fragment is corrupt here.] There remained, to complete the lunar year, four extra days after the reigns of thirty-five days each, over which each of the ten tribes was set in order determined by lot. Those four days were assigned to the four tribes which had first held power. Suidas: "The numbering of the days" [ἀριθμεία δὲ ὁ τῆς ἡμέρας ἀριθμός]. The Aegeidae were the ones who drew the Selonian [...]. Each tribe was given forty-five days. Let us assume that they went out from the Selonian [...] days, which were drawn by lot to supervise the whole tribe. Of the five ephors who held the office, the numbering lasted from the beginning for forty-six days; the remaining six numbered forty-five. The number of days was therefore not forty-six, but forty-five. The illustrious Scaliger thought that each tribe in turn held the power and ruled for one day, so that, for example, yesterday the Aiantis tribe ruled, today the Kekropis, tomorrow the Akamantis, and so on, each ruling its own day throughout the whole turning year, in the order drawn by lot from the very beginning of the year. But this opinion is opposed by several testimonies of the ancient orators, from which it is easily proved that each tribe ruled for thirty-five continuous days, and not that each held its own day in the cycle. In the first Decree against Timocrates by Demosthenes, the words of one decree are these: "In the Paeanian tribe, on the eleventh day of the Prytany, Timocrates proposed." And a little later: "The Prytaneis of the Paeanian tribe, the lawgiver of them..." Clearly, because the Pandionid tribe also ruled on the next day, which is also established by another decree written on the next day, which is read in the same Oration: "In the Pandionid tribe, on the twelfth day of the Prytany, Aeschylus of Myrrhinous put the motion to the vote for the priests; Timocrates proposed." You see that two consecutive days the Pandionid tribe ruled. [Stephanus says that Myrrhinous was of the Paeanian tribe.] [...] The decree was put to the people for voting. But Antiphon, in his work On the Choreutria, leaves no room for doubt that each tribe ruled for thirty-five consecutive days. His words are these: "Looking at the Balbis and entering the Balbisterion, where there is a temple of Zeus Balaios and Athena Bulaia, the Senators entering... for all the sacred things of the Council, and the sacrifices..." [The remainder is too corrupt to render.] These words are spoken about things that happened on the fifth day of the month Metageitnion, as we explained in the preceding chapters. But enough of these matters.

units.la: Quinquaginta hi vnius Tribus Prytaneis fimul non imperabant fuam triginta quinque dierum Prytaneiam: fed cum Prytaneia in quinque hebdomades, vt ex Vlpiano liquet, diftribuebatur: quinquies enim feptem faciunt triginta quinque; in totidem decurias forte diftribuebantur hi quinquaginta, Prytanes, & prima decuria fuam imperabat hebdomadem, fecunda fecundam, atque ita deinceps ordine forte ducto: dicebantur illi decem, qui in fua hebdomade praerant, [?]Πρόεδροι. Vlpianus in Androtianam: [?]Ἀλλ' [?]ὅτι πάλιν οἱ πρυτάνεις πολλαπλάσιον εἰς ὃ ἀρχὴν ἄμα, οἱ δίκας, κατὰ πλῆθος μιᾶς ἡμέρας [?]τῆς ἑαυτῶν ἡμέρα. ἔμφασις δὲ ἕκαστος τῆς ἡμέρας ἐπὶ πλήθει τὸ ἐαυτῶν ἡμέραν, ἄρχει οὖ πληρωσῶσιν αἱ ἐπὶ ἡμέραν, καὶ συνεδέαμε τῆς ἀρχῆς, ἡ εἰς μὲν ἀρχὴν ἕκαστος ἢ ἀρχὴν [?] εἰς μίαν ἡμέραν, ἐκαλεῖτο Ἐπισάτης. Δι᾽ τί δὲ μίαν μόνῳ ἦρχεν; ὅτι αὐτὸς τῆς Ἀκροπόλεως ἐπιστάτης, καὶ πόσιν τὰ χρήματα τῆς πόλεως. ἵ᾽ οὖν μὴ ἐφαλῇ τυραννίδες, Δι᾽ τοῦτο μίαν ἡμέραν ἐπίσωμ αὐτῷ ἀρχῆν. ἰσχύον δ᾽ ὅτι, οἱ λεὶ πεντήκοντα Πρυτάνεις ἐκαλοῦντο· οἱ δὲ ἕκα, Πεγεδροι· ὁ δὲ εἷς, Ἐπισάτης. Prytanea igitur in quinque hebdomadas distribuebatur, vt hic habes, & secundum hanc distributionem Quinquaginta Prytaneis singularum Tribuum, in quinque decurias distinguebantur: vnde intelligenda puto atque emendanda Hesychij verba, ἑδραι βουλῆς ἀγ' ἐξιῶντο καὶ πρυτανείας [?]. Referendum existimo, καὶ ἐπαλλαγμέον [?]. Non enim quinto quoque die Senatus habebatur, vt praeferunt haec verba, sed quotidie, nisi dies esset ἄφετος. Est igitur quod dixi: Decem autem illi singularum decuriarum viri, cum hebdomadem suam imperarent, Πεγεδροι dicebantur, qui ἐκλεγόμενοι τὴν Πρυτανείαν καθ᾽ ἑκάστην Πρυτανείαν, vt obseruat Grammatici. Hi vero Proedri inter se sortiebantur regna septem illorum hebdomadis dierum, quibus praerant: atque ita fiebat, vt e decem singulari hebdomadum Proedris tres superessent, qui suum non imperarent diem: Proedrus autem, quum suum imperaret diem, Ἐπισάτης dicebatur: οἱ δίκα, καὶ κληγον μιᾶς ἡμέρας τῇ ἐσπέρᾳ· ὁμοίως δὲ ἕκαστος τῆ ἄλλων ἀπὸ κληγον ἔχε τῷ ἑαυτοῦ ἡμέραν, ἀφελεῖ δὲ πληρωσῶσιν αἱ ἐπὶ ἡμέραν καὶ συνεδέαμε τῆς ἀρχῆς, τῶν μὴ ἀρχὴν. ἕκαστος δὲ ἀρχὴν εἰς μίαν ἡμέραν, ἐκαλεῖτο Ἐπισάτης. Nemini autem licebat lege, nisi semel Epistatae esse: Δὶς οὐκ ἐξὸν ἀγ᾽ ἡμέαζ τ᾽ αὐτὸν Ἐπισάτην. Nemini bis esse Epistatae liceto.
units.tr: Those fifty men of each tribe did not all hold command together for their thirty-five days of Prytany. Since the Prytany was divided into five weeks, as is clear from Ulpian (five times seven makes thirty-five), these fifty were probably distributed into five decuries, and the first decury commanded the first week, the second decury the second, and so on in order. The ten men who presided in their own week were called Proedri [Πρόεδροι]. Ulpian, on Androtion: the prytanes, each day, the one of the ten who had been chosen by lot for the day was called Epistates [ἐπιστάτης] for that single day. Why was he in command for only one day? Because he is the overseer of the Acropolis and keeps the city's money, so that tyranny might not arise, he was given command for one day only. The fifty were called prytanes, the ten Proedri, and the one Epistates. Prytanea, then, was distributed into five weeks, as you have here, and according to this distribution the fifty prytanes of each tribe were divided into five decuries. From this I think Hesychius' words, which read as corrupt, should be understood and emended. I think the reading should be "and in alternation". For the Senate was not held every fifth day, as those words suggest, but daily, unless the day was aphetos. So what I said stands: the ten men of each decury, when they commanded their week, were called Proedri, who, as the grammarians observe, were chosen for each Prytany. These Proedri cast lots among themselves for the seven days of the week over which they presided; and thus it happened that, of the ten Proedri of each week, three remained who did not command a day. The Proedrus who commanded a day was called Epistates. It was not permitted to any man, by law, to be Epistates more than once: "Nemini autem licebat lege, nisi semel Epistatae esse" and Nemini bis esse Epistatae liceto.

units.la: Memini Pollux Libro VIII.cap IX. ἐπὶ Ἐπισάτης καλοῦνται, ἔστιν εἰς τὴν Πρυτανείων, ὁ κληρω λαχὼν δὶς ὁ ἐκ ἔξεστι ἡμέσθαι τὸν αὐτὸν Ἐπισάτην. Suidas: τὴν Πρυταγένων εἰς ἀλαχὼν, Ἐπισάτης ἐλέγετο. ὃς δὲ τὸν αὐτὸν ἐπισατῆσαι οὐκ ἐξὸν. Habebat enim penes se, quum regnaret, aerarij claues, & tabularij, itemque sigillum publicum, vnde metus erat, ne, si pluries fieret Epistates, tyrannidem inuaderet. Vlpianus: ἕκαστος ἡ ἀρχὴν ὁ μία ἡμέρα ἐκαλεῖτο Ἐπισάτης. Δι᾽ τί δὲ μίαν μόνῳ ἦρχεν; ὅτι αὐτὸς τῆς Ἀκροπόλεως ἐπιστάτης, καὶ πόσιν τὰ χρήματα τῆς πόλεως. ἵ᾽ οὖν μὴ ἐφαλῇ τυραννίδες, Δι᾽ τοῦτο μίαν ἡμέραν ἐπίσωμ αὐτὴν ἀρχὴν. Pollux loco laudato: ἐχρὴ δὲ ὁ Ἐπισάτης τὰ κλεῖς τῆν ἱερῶν, ὁ οἷς τὰ χρήμα, καὶ τὰ χρήματα. Suidas: Φυλάττει δὲ ὁ Ἐπισάτης τὰ ἱερὰ τῆς κλῆς, ὁ ὣ τὰ δημόσια χρήματα. ἔνι μὲν καὶ τῶν δημοσίων σφραγῖδα. Quod autem semel fungi Epistatae munere liceret, intelligendum est de toto vitae curriculo: nam quod ad annum ipsum, quo Epistatae fuerunt, referas, ioculare id esset, cum etiamsi nulla id Lex sanciret, aliter fieri non posset. Nemo enim εἷς τῶν Πρυτανείων erat Ἐπισάτης, nisi ἀρυτδυσυντος τῆς Φυλῆς, de qua erat Prytanum vnum, iam vero Prytaneis, vt diximus, distribuebantur sorte in decurias quinque, quarum decuriarum singulae sorte ductae suam imperabant ordine hebdomadem, neque vna decuria alterius occupabat vicem & ἐφημερίας. An vero è Proedris decem tres illi, qui Epistatae non fuerant, sorte non addicente, rursum sortirentur cum aliis, qui superarant, Prytanibus, necdum Proedri fuerant suam hebdomadem, pro comperto non habeo: inclinat tamen potius animus, vt credam non iterum sortitos fuisse: nam, aut ego valde fallor, aut Prytaneis, ineunte Prytancia, distribuebantur sorte in has quinque decurias: Πεγεδροι ἐκλησιῶν τῶν Πρυτανέων καὶ ἑκάστῳ φυλῆς [?]
units.tr: Pollux, Book 8, chapter 9, mentions this: the one who obtained by lot the office of Epistates of the Prytany was not permitted to hold the office of Epistates a second time. Suidas: the one who drew the lot of the Prytany was called Epistates, and it was not permitted for the same man to hold the office of Epistates twice. For while he held the office he had in his keeping the keys of the treasury and the archive, and likewise the public seal, so there was fear that if he were Epistates more than once he might seize tyranny. Ulpian: each one who was Epistates for a single day was so called. Why did he hold command for only one day? Because he is the overseer of the Acropolis and keeps the city's money; so that tyranny might not arise, he was given command for one day only. Pollux, in the passage cited: the Epistates had the keys of the temples and the money, and the public funds. Suidas: the Epistates guards the keys of the sacred things and the public money, and he has the public seal. As for the statement that a man might perform the office of Epistates only once, this must be understood of his whole life's course. For if you were to refer it to the year itself in which a man was Epistates, it would be a silly point, since even if no law sanctioned it, it could not happen otherwise. For no one could be Epistates of the Prytanes unless it was his tribe's turn, from which he was one of the prytanes; but the prytanes, as we said, were distributed by lot into five decuries, and each decury, drawn by lot, commanded its week in order, and one decury did not take the place or the day of another. Whether those three Proedri who had not been Epistates, if the lot did not favour them, were drawn again with the other prytanes who remained, and who had not yet been Proedri in their own week, I do not know for certain. My inclination, however, is rather to think that they were not drawn again. For either I am much mistaken, or at the beginning of the Prytany the prytanes were distributed by lot into these five decuries. Pollux and Harpocration: the Proedri of the assembly of the prytanes, and of each Prytany...

units.la: Ab his Proedris atque Epistatis, alij fuerunt Proedri atque Epistatæ. Nam quotiescumque habebatur Senatus, aut concio, ὁ ὢν τῇ ἐφημερίᾳ ἀρχῶν Ἐπισ-τάτης legebat nouem Proedros è singulis vnum Tribubus, excepta Tribu, penes quam erat Prytancias imperium, vt docuerat Aristoteles ἐν τῇ τῶν Ἀθηναίων πολιτείᾳ. Pollux loco laudato: ὁ ἔτι δὲ οἱ Πρυτάνεις τὴν δῆμον, ἐν τῷ βουλῇ συναγόμεναι, ὁ Ἐπισ-τάτης δὲ ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς (male editur βουλῆς,) Πρόεδροι ἕνα κληροῦ, μόνῳ τῶν πρυτανευόντων ἀφ' εἰς [?]. Suidas: ἐπειδὴ οἱ Πρυτάνεις συναγαγέσθαι τὴν βουλὴν ἢ τὸν δῆμον, ὁ Ἐπισ-τάτης κληροῦ Πρόεδρος ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς ἑκάστης: ἔνα, πλὴν τῆς πρυτανευούσης. Sed alibi idem Suidas & Harpocration confundunt cum Proedris illis decem, qui, cum regnarent suum hebdomadis diem, Epistatæ dicebantur, & qui hos nouem forte capiebant, Πρόεδροι, ἐκλησιῶν τῶν Πρυτανέων καὶ ἑκάστῳ πρυτανείας, εἰς ὧν ἐκ ἑκάστης φυλῆς, πλὴν τῆς πρυτανευούσης. Confule haec dicuntur & indistincte. Nam illi decem erant numero, hi nouem tantum, quia non sortiebatur Tribus illa, cuius erat Prytancia. Illi erant vnius tantum Tribus, nempe τῆς πρυτανευούσης, hi è nouem aliis, præter τῆς πρυτανευούσης, Tribubus capiebantur, è singulis singuli: Illi καὶ ἐκάστου πρυτανείας, ineunte Prytania, legebantur: hi quotiescumque habebatur Senatus, aut concio cogebatur. Denique distincta erant munia. Horum nouem Proedrorum vnus Epistata dicebatur, forte ex illis nouem ductus ab Epistata, penes quem erat illius diei regnum. Suidas: τῶν πάλιν ἐκ τῆς τῶν ἐννέα ζυγῶν Ἐπισ-τάτου ἐνα κληροῦ. Harpocration: δύο εἰσὶ οἱ καλούμενοι Ἐπισ-τάται· ὁ μὲν ἐκ Πρυτανέων κληρούμενος· ὁ δὲ ἐκ τῆς Βουλῆς. Hi Proedri Senatui, & populi concioni, præsidebant, vnde nomen inuenerunt: ἐκ-λησιῶν δὲ Πρόεδροι, ἐπισιδηρὰ προεδρεύοντες τῶν ὅλων ἀπάντων. Itaque per eos curabatur ea, quæ τῆς τῷ βουλῷ & τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ erant: οἱ τινες τὰ αὐτὰ τῆς ἐκκλησίας διάκοσμ, addc, ἐ αὐτοῦ τῆς βουλῆς. Nam in hunc finem electi ab Epistata, vt negotio curarent. Suidas ex Aristotele ἐν τῇ τῶν Ἀθηναίων πολιτείᾳ. ὁ Ἐπισ-τάτης κληροῦ Πρόεδρος ἕνα, ἀπὸ φυλῆς ἑκάστης ἕνα, πλὴν τῆς πρυτανευούσης. ἡ πάλιν ἐκ τῆς ἕνεκα ζύγου Ἐπισ-τάτου κληροῦ. ἡ δὲ ταῦτα ἐκ τῆς τῶν ἐξ ἀγῶνα [?]. Hi Proedri relationem faciebant eorum, quorum causa conuenerant: vnde legas in Lege τῆς ἐπιγαμίας νόμων. Ἰδ' οἱ Πρόεδροι μὴ ἐξημιώσωσι τὰ ἐγγαμούμενα. Vlpianus: οἱ ἡ Πρόεδροι ἐπεβάλλον αὐτὸν ἑνὸς σωτηρίου. Siftebant præterea in iudicium coram populo. Vlpianus in Timocrateam: οἱ γὰρ Πρόεδροι ἐν τῷ δήμῳ εἰσῆγον· οἱ ἡ Ἀρχοντες οἱ Θεσμοθέται, ἐν τῇ δικαστηρίᾳ. Quas tamen partes fuisse præcipue τῆς Ἐπισ-τάτου ἐκ τῶν Πρόεδρων facile mihi persuadeo: itaque notat de eo Suidas: ὡς ὁ εἰσαγγελεὺς τὴν δίκην, ἡ ἐπιμελήσεται τῷ νόμῳ πρῶτα ἡμέρας, ἡ μηδὲν ἐπέγκλημα ἔχει ὁ δίδα· ἀφ' ὧν τὶ δικαστής. Quæ postrema verba refero ad τὴν εἰσαγγελίαν, aut huiusmodi dicas, quando scilicet τῶν Πενταχοσίων βουλή, aut ἡ ἐκκλησία, reum εἰσαγγελίας, aut alterius criminis, à se condemnatum tradebat ὁ δικαστήριον, vt grauior mulcta irrogaretur: Nam alioqui τῶν Πρόεδρων, aut eorum Epistata non erat εἰσαγγελὶν τῇ δικαστηρίᾳ, vt habes in laudatis iam ante Vlpiani verbis.
units.tr: Besides these Proedri and Epistatae, there were other Proedri and Epistatae. For whenever the Senate or an assembly was held, the Epistates who was on duty that day read out nine Proedri, one from each tribe, excluding the tribe which held the prytany, as Aristotle taught in the Constitution of the Athenians. Pollux, in the passage cited: the prytanes, when they convened the Senate or the people, and the Epistates from the tribe (the text is wrongly printed as "Senate"), drew by lot one Proedrus only, from among those who were prytanes. Suidas: when the prytanes convened the Senate or the people, the Epistates drew by lot one Proedrus from each tribe, except the tribe which held the prytany. But elsewhere the same Suidas and Harpocration confuse these with the ten Proedri who, when they held command of their day of the week, were called Epistatae, and with those who by chance received these nine as Proedri of the assembly of the prytanes and of each Prytany, one from each tribe except the presiding tribe. You should consult these passages, which are stated loosely and without distinction. For those ten were ten in number, these only nine, because the tribe which held the Prytany was not drawn. Those ten were of one tribe only, namely the presiding tribe, while these nine were drawn from the other tribes, apart from the presiding tribe, one from each. Those ten were chosen at the beginning of the Prytany; these were chosen whenever the Senate was held or an assembly convened. Finally, their duties were distinct. Of these nine Proedri, one was called Epistates, drawn by lot from those nine by the Epistates, in whose hands was the authority of that day. Suidas: again, the Epistates of the nine draws one from among the nine. Harpocration: there are two men called Epistatae: one drawn from the prytanes, the other from the Senate. These Proedri presided over the Senate and the people's assembly, whence they took their name: the Proedri of the assembly, presiding over the whole. Therefore through them was arranged what concerned the Senate and the assembly, and the order of the assembly, and of the Senate itself. For they were chosen by the Epistates for this purpose, to attend to the business. Suidas, from Aristotle's Constitution of the Athenians: the Epistates draws one Proedrus from each tribe, except the presiding tribe; or again, he draws by lot from among the nine. These Proedri made the report concerning those for whose sake they had gathered, whence you may read in the law on marriage: the Proedri shall not fine those who marry... Ulpian: the Proedri imposed a penalty of one obol. They also brought suits before the people, presenting them in court. Ulpian, on Timocrates: the Proedri introduced them before the people, but the Archons and the Thesmothetae before the court. I readily persuade myself that these were chiefly the functions of the Epistates with the Proedri; so Suidas notes of him that the prosecutor's case is brought, and he takes care that the law is observed on the first day, or that the accused has no charge against him... The last words I refer to the indictment (eisangelia), or something of the kind, when namely the Council of Five Hundred, or the assembly, handed over to the court an accused person for an eisangelia or another crime, which it had condemned, so that a heavier penalty might be imposed. For otherwise it was not the business of the Proedri, or of their Epistates, to bring an eisangelia before the court, as you have in the words of Ulpian cited above.

units.la: Vbi forte capti fuerant Quingenti, qui Reipublicæ præessent, inquirebatur in eorum vitam, morefque, cum probati fuerant, iusiurandum dabat. Demosthenes ἐν τῷ κατὰ Νεαίρας λαχών βουλὴν ὁ Ἀπολλόδωρος, δικαστὴς δὲ ἡ ὁμοσάς τῷ νόμῳ ὅρκον. Iusiurandi huius Lege imperati, vt hic habes, aliquot Capita hic describemus.
units.tr: Where, by chance, the Five Hundred who presided over the Republic had been chosen, their life and character were investigated, and once they had been approved, each gave an oath. Demosthenes, in the speech against Neaera, says that Apollodorus was chosen as a councillor and, having sworn the oath required by law, became a judge. We will set out here some of the chapters of this oath as they were imposed by the law, as you have them here.

units.la: Ο ΒΟΥΛΕΥΤΙΚΟΣ ΟΡΚΟΣ.
units.tr: THE COUNCILLOR'S OATH.

units.la: Τὰ βέλτιστα βουλεύσειν τῷ δήμῳ τῷ Ἀθη- ναίων. Καπὶ [?] νόμες βουλεύσῃ.
units.tr: "I will counsel what is best for the people of the Athenians." [Τὰ βέλτιστα βουλεύσειν τῷ δήμῳ τῷ Ἀθηναίων.] Some words are garbled in the scan here: "...according to the laws, I will counsel."

units.la: ΟΥΔΕ ΔΗΣΩ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ ΟΥΔΕ-ΝΑ ΟΣ ΑΝ ΕΓΓΥΗΤΑΣ ΤΡΕΙΣ ΚΑ- ΘΙΣΤΗΙ ΤΟ ΑΥΤΟ ΤΕΛΟΣ ΤΕ-ΛΟΥΝΤΑΣ, [?] ΕΑΝ ΤΙΣ ΕΠΙ ΠΡΟΔΟΣΙΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΠΟΛΕΩΣ, Η ΕΓΙ ΚΑΤΑΛΥΣΕΙ ΤΟΥ ΔΗΜΟΥ ΣΥ-ΝΙΩΝ ΑΛΩ, Η ΤΕΛΟΣ ΠΡΙΑΜΕΝΟΣ, Η ΕΓΓΥΗΣΑΜΕΝΟΣ, Η ΕΚΛΕΓΩΝ ΜΗ ΚΑΤΑΒΑΛΗ.
units.tr: "I will not imprison any of the Athenians who provides three sureties undergoing the same penalty, unless he is plotting treason against the city or the subversion of the people, or unless, having bought or guaranteed or collected, he does not pay." [Οὐδὲ δήσω Ἀθηναίων οὐδένα, ὃς ἂν ἐγγυητὰς τρεῖς καθίστῃ, τὸ αὐτὸ τέλος τελοῦντας, ἐάν τις ἐπὶ προδοσίᾳ τῆς πόλεως ἢ ἐὰν κατάλυσιν τοῦ δήμου συνίῃ, ἢ τέλος πρίαμενος, ἢ ἐγγυησάμενος, ἢ ἐκλέγων μὴ καταβάλῃ.]

units.la: [illegible, ~9 letters]
units.tr: [illegible]

units.la: ΚΑΙ ΟΥ ΔΕΞΟΜΑΙ ΕΝΔΕΙΞΙΝ ΟΥ-ΔΕ ΑΠΑΓΩΓΗΝ ΕΝΕΚΑ ΤΩΝ ΠΡΟ- ΤΕΡΩΝ ΓΕΓΕΝΗΜΕΝΩΝ ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΦΕΥΓΟΝΤΩΝ.
units.tr: "And I will not admit an information, nor an arrest, on account of past events, except against fugitives." [Καὶ οὐ δέξομαι ἔνδειξιν οὐδὲ ἀπαγωγὴν ἕνεκα τῶν προτέρων γεγενημένων πλὴν τῶν φευγόντων.]

units.la: Primum huius iurisiurandi Kaput extat apud Demosthenem de Apollodoro, ὁ τὰ βέλτιστα βουλεύσειν τῷ δήμῳ τῷ Ἀθηναίων, quod sane vt praestarent Senatores, exigebat ab illis muneris, quod susceperant, ratio.
units.tr: The first chapter of this oath is extant in Demosthenes, in the speech about Apollodorus: "I will counsel what is best for the people of the Athenians." The demand of the office they had undertaken certainly required the senators to fulfil this.

units.la: Secundum Kaput describit Xenophon Libro I. Ἀπομνημονευμάτων, de Socrate agens: βουλεύσας [?] ποτὲ, ἢ τὴν βουλὴν ὅρκον ὀμόσας, ὃ ἐν τῷ βουλῇ. Erat enim Quingentorum Senatus, si cuiusquam, ab institutis patriis, & receptis Legibus, ne latum quidem vnguem discedere, vt qui inter primos in Solonis Leges iurarit. Plutarchus in Solone: καὶ τὸν βουλήν, πρῶτος Σόλωνος νόμος, primusque Leges, cum feruntur, approbet.
units.tr: Xenophon describes the second chapter in Book I of the Memorabilia, speaking of Socrates: when he once sat in the Council and had sworn the Council's oath, he did so in the Council. For the Senate of Five Hundred, if any body did, adhered to the ancestral institutions and received laws, and did not depart from them by so much as a hair's breadth, since its members were among the first to swear to Solon's laws. Plutarch, in his Life of Solon, says that the Council was the first to approve Solon's laws when they were proposed. [καὶ τὴν βουλήν, πρῶτος Σόλωνος νόμος, πρῶτος.]

units.la: Tertium Kaput legitur apud Demosthenem in Timocratea, cuius causas aperit ibidem Orator: ἐπεὶ δὲ ἀ... ΟΥΔΕ ΔΗΣΩ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ ΟΥΔΕΝΑ. ... Vlpianus: οὐκ ἐξὸν νόμως, ἀλλ' ὅρκος τὴν βουλὴν ... Senatus igitur neminem vinciebat, nisi quos excipit iusiurandum: de quibus paulò post dicimus, Deo dante.
units.tr: The third chapter is read in Demosthenes' speech against Timocrates, and the orator explains its causes in the same place: "Since... I will not imprison any of the Athenians..." Vlpian: the oath, not the law, binds the Council... The Senate therefore imprisoned no one except those whom the oath excepts. Of these we shall speak shortly, God willing.

units.la: Quartum iurisiurandi Kaput a Philochoro descriptum sequentia declarabunt.
units.tr: The fourth chapter of the oath, described by Philochorus, will become clear from what follows.

units.la: Quintum iurisiurandi Kaput habetur apud Andocidem ὁ τὰ πρὸς τὴν ΜυστΜυρρίνην[?] ἡ βουλὴ αὕτη[?] ἀλλ' ἡ βουλὴ νόμοι[?], ἡ μέσῃ[?]; ΚΑΙ ΟΥ ΔΕΞΟΜΑΙ ΕΝΔΕΙ-ΞΙΝ, ΟΥΔΕ ΑΠΑΓΩΓΗΝ ΕΝΕΚΑ ΤΩΝ ΠΡΟΤΕΡΩΝ ΓΕΓΕΝΗΜΕ-ΝΩΝ, ΓΑΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΦΕΥΓΟΝΤΩΝ. Quod Kaput additum est, vt ex eodem Andocide constat, post exactos Triginta Tyrannos, cum τῆς μυπικαλὰς[?] Lex sapientissimo consilio sanciretur.
units.tr: The fifth chapter of the oath is found in Andocides, in a passage that is garbled in the scan. It was added, as is clear from the same Andocides, after the Thirty Tyrants had been expelled, when the law was enacted by the wisest counsel. The text reads: "And I will not admit an information, nor an arrest, on account of past events, except against fugitives." [Καὶ οὐ δέξομαι ἔνδειξιν, οὐδὲ ἀπαγωγὴν ἕνεκα τῶν προτέρων γεγενημένων, πλὴν τῶν φευγόντων.]

units.la: Cùm penes Prytanes ius esset habendi Senatum, aut cogendi populum in concionem, si quid noui in Republica accidebat, Prytanibus referebatur, vt prouiderent indicto Senatu, vel concione: Quare deprehensum in re capitali Mnesilochum se Prytanibus delaturam denunciat nescio quae mulier apud Comicum Θεσμοφοριαζούσας, ἐγὼ δὲ ταῦτα τοῖς Πρυτάνεσιν ἀγγελῶ.
units.tr: Since the Prytanes had the right to convene the Senate or to call the people into assembly, whenever anything new arose in the Republic it was reported to the Prytanes, so that they might arrange for a Senate or an assembly to be summoned. Hence the woman in the comic poet's Thesmophoriazusae announces that, since Mnesilochus has been caught in a capital matter, she will report it to the Prytanes: "I will report these things to the Prytanes." [ἐγὼ δὲ ταῦτα τοῖς Πρυτάνεσιν ἀγγελῶ.]

units.la: Neque quisquam admittebatur petitor in Senatum, nisi ab his Prytanibus, quorum auariciam carpit Comicus Eupolis, vt qui gratis nullum admitteret, inducarum forensium nomen praetexentes: vulgo enim dicebant, ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐστὶν, ἢ δυνάμεθα τὴν μισθὸν εἰσαγγέλλειν, etsi non tam amarent ἐκκλησίαν, quam τὰς ἡμέρας τὰ ἐς τὰς χάριτας. Ἀλλ' ὁ Πρυτάνης δίκαιός τ' ἐκ τῶν ἁμαρτίας. ἡ 'ὡς ἀρχῶν ὁ Πρυτάνις ἐπὶ ταῦτα. Ἀλλ' Οὐκ ἂν εἰ' ἡ ἀρχικὰ ἄρχει εἰ' ἐν. Ἀλλ' ἔτι γαρ ἂν ὁ ἐπιστέφων ἐκ ἐκκλησίας.
units.tr: Nor was anyone admitted as a petitioner into the Senate except through these Prytanes, whose greed the comic poet Eupolis attacks, since they admitted no one without payment, using the pretext of the courts' adjournments. For commonly they said, "It is not an assembly day, so we cannot announce the payment," though they loved not so much the assembly as the days devoted to favours. But the Prytanis is just... from the errors... Garbled in the scan; the sense is that the Prytanes gave the excuse of a holiday or assembly to refuse admission.

units.la: Vetus Interpres, ὡς Πρυτάνεων ἔδος τὰ ἀρχαῖα ... vt Prytanes ... ante Senatus introitum in βουλήν, quod sine admissione ... ἐκκλησίαν ... tunc ... dixerunt, οὐκ ἔστι δυνάμεθα τὴν μισθὸν ... εἰσαγγέλλειν ... Senatus ... admitti, ...
units.tr: The old interpreter renders it: as the Prytanes... before the Senate's entry into the Council, which without admission... the assembly... then they said, "it is not possible to announce the payment"... the Senate... to be admitted... (The rest of this is too garbled to recover with certainty.)

units.la: Senatus quotidie habebatur, nisi dies esset ἀφέτος. Aristoteles ἐν τῇ Ἀθηναίων πολιτείᾳ apud Harpocrationem & Suidam: οἱ Πρυτάνεις συναγαγεῖν τὴν Βουλὴν ἡμέρας δημοσίας, πλὴν ἐν τῆς ἀφέσιμος ἡ. Pollux Libro VIII. cap. IX. οἱ Πρυτάνεις ἔπει τὴν Βουλὴν συναγαγεῖν ὁσημέρας, πλὴν ἐπ' ἀφέτις τῆς ἡ. Inter dies ἀφέσιμος, fuerunt festi, sed ἀπὸ τῶν Ἀθηναίων ἀγόντων ἱερομηνίας, vt est in Lege de Festis: vnde, quod iam diximus, si quos nollent in Senatum admittere Prytaneis, dicebant, Senatum tunc non haberi, quia feriebantur: ἐκκλησία ἐστὶν, ἢ δυνάμεθα τὴν μισθὸν εἰσαγγέλλειν. Nam ἐκκλησίαν ad ferias & muneris vacationem referendam puto: πρῶτος οὖν τῇ ἑορτῇ ἀφιέμενοι ἦσαν, vt legitur in veterum Commentariis, ἐν ᾧ ἡμεῖς ἐπιγράφεται εἰς ἐκκλησίας τῆς Βουλῆς. Vnde est apud Demosthenem in Timocratea: ἡ ἐκ τῶν ἀπόντων Κερδίων ἀρχῶν ἡ ἀφιέμενος τῆς Βουλῆς. & paulò post: τῆς Βουλῆς ἀπὸ ἀφιέμενος, ἢ δὲ ἡμῶν ἀρχὴ ἡ ἑορτῶν ἱερομηνίας ἀγόντων. Aristophanes Θεσμοφοριαζούσης. καὶ πως; ἐπεὶ ἐκεῖ ἐτ' ἡ ἀκαστήρια. μὴ ἐξ ἀκάζω, ὅτι βουλῆς ἐπ' ἐφρα. ἐπὶ τέτρᾳ 'ει Θεσμοφοριῶν ἡ μέση.
units.tr: The Senate was held daily unless the day was a holiday. Aristotle, in the Constitution of the Athenians, as cited by Harpocration and Suidas: the Prytanes were to convene the Council on every public day, except on holidays. Pollux, Book VIII, chapter IX: the Prytanes were to convene the Council every day, except on holidays. Among the holidays, there were festivals, which were observed by the Athenians as sacred days, as is written in the law concerning festivals. Hence, as we have already said, if the Prytanes wished to exclude anyone from the Senate, they said that the Senate was not held that day, because it was a holiday: "it is not an assembly day, so we cannot announce the payment." For I think that the "assembly" refers to the holidays and the release from duty. Thus, as is read in the old commentaries, they were released from the Council on the festival day, on which the assembly of the Council was written. Hence in Demosthenes' Against Timocrates: "...the Council being released from the absent magistracies, the Council is released from the festival." And shortly after: "The Council is released on the days when our magistrates celebrate festivals and sacred months." Aristophanes, in the Thesmophoriazusae: "And how? Since there are court days there. Let me not be unjust, the Council is released from the festival, on the fourth of the Thesmophoria." (The Greek is badly garbled here.)

units.la: Pfephismate autem cautum est, anno tertio Olympiadis centesimae tertiae, Cephisidoro Athenis Praetore, vt Senatus Quingentorum dies quinque feriaretur cum agebantur Apaturia.
units.tr: By decree, in the third year of the 113th Olympiad, when Cephisidorus was praetor at Athens, it was provided that the Senate of Five Hundred should be on holiday for five days while the Apaturia were celebrated.

units.la: ΦΩΚΟΣ ΕΙΠΕΝ · ΟΠΩΣ ΑΝ Η ΒΟΥ- ΛΗ ΑΓΗ͂ ΤΑ ΑΠΑΤΟΥΡΙΑ ΜΕΤΑ ΤΩΝ ΑΛΛΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΑ ΠΑΤΡΙΑ. ΕΨΗΦΙΣΘΑΙ ΤΗ͂ ΒΟΥ- ΛΗ͂ ΑΦΕΙΣΘΑΙ ΤΟΥΣ ΒΟΥΛΕΥΤΑΣ ΤΑΣ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ, ΑΣΠΕΡ ΚΑΙ ΑΙ ΑΛ- ΛΑΙ ΒΟΥΛΑΙ ΔΙΑΦΙΕΝΤΑΙ, ΑΠΟ ΤΗΣ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ, ΗΣ ΟΙ ΠΡΟΤΕΝΘΑΙ ΑΓΟΥΣΙ ΓΕΝΤΕ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ.
units.tr: Phocus said: that the Council should celebrate the Apaturia with the other Athenians according to ancestral custom. It was resolved by the Council that the councillors be released on the days, just as the other councils are dismissed, from the days which the Prytanes bring forward as festival days. [ΦΩΚΟΣ ΕΙΠΕΝ· ὅπως ἂν ἡ βουλὴ ἄγῃ τὰ Ἀπατούρια μετὰ τῶν ἄλλων Ἀθηναίων κατὰ τὰ πάτρια. Ἐψηφίσθαι τῇ βουλῇ ἀφεῖσθαι τοὺς βουλευτὰς τὰς ἡμέρας, ὥσπερ καὶ αἱ ἄλλαι βουλαὶ διαφυλάττονται, ἀπὸ τῆς ἡμέρας, ἧς οἱ πρυτάνεις ἄγουσι γενέσθαι ἡμέρας.]

units.la: Senatusconsultum iftud eft, non in Areopago factum, vt volebat Vir Incomparabilis, fed in Senatu Quingentorum, qui fimpliciter ἡ βουλὴ appellatur: Psephisma esse Senatus indicant ista eius verba ΕΨΗΦΙΣΘΑΙ ΤΗ͂ ΒΟΥΛΗ͂. An vero postea a populo ratum habitum sit Psephismate suo, iuxta cûm ignarissimus scio: Tempus Psephismatis facti illud esse, quod diximus, indicat Athenæus Libro IV. [illegible, ~70 letters] ΦΩΚΟΣ ΕΙΠΕΝ, &c. Non ignoro Archontem eiusdem nominis signasse Fastos anni secundi Olympiadis centesimæ quartædecimæ, sed magis inclino ad Archontem anni tertij Olympiadis centesimæ tertiæ. Hoc Psephismate decernitur, vt Senatus Quingentorum Apaturiorum festum quinque agitet diebus, quot nimirum celebrant Protenthæ. Apaturia tribus diebus propriè transigebatur: sed tamen sequens μεθέορος dies, quam ἐπιΘῦσθαι dixerunt, etiam cum festiuitate pragebatur; colligo è Simplicio ad Lib. IV. Physic. Κυρεῖτις ἢ ὧν ἢ τεῖτα τῇ Ἀπατουρίων ἡμέρας, ὥσπερ πανηγύρα Δορπία, καὶ ἡ δωδεκάτη Ἀναρρύσεις, καὶ ἡ τετάρτη Ἐπιῶδια. item-que ex Hefychio, Ἀπατουρία, ἑορτὴ Ἀθηναίων ἐπὶ πεντάμερα ἡμέρας. ὧν ἡ μὲν πρώτη Δορπία κάλυψις, ἡ δὲ δευτέρα Ἀναρρύσεις, ἡ δὲ τρίτη Κυρεώτης, ἡ τετάρτη Ἐπιῶδια. Protenthae vero, qui hoc maxime videntur celebrasse festum, vt verba huius Psephismatis indicant, & indicio est Philyllius in Hercule: βύλλει δὴ ἐγὼ φησὶ τῆς ἐμῆ ἐγώ; ἢ τῷ Πεγθιῶν ἑορτὴ καλλυνθῶν.
units.tr: This decree was not made in the Areopagus, as that unparalleled man supposed, but in the Senate of Five Hundred, which is simply called "the Council." That it was a decree of the Senate is shown by the words of the text: "It was resolved by the Council." Whether it was later ratified by the people, I know not, and I am quite ignorant of it. That the time of the decree was the one we have mentioned is shown by Athenaeus, Book IV: [illegible] "Phocus said," etc. I am not unaware that an archon of the same name signed the records of the second year of the 114th Olympiad, but I incline more to the archon of the third year of the 113th Olympiad. By this decree it is ordered that the Senate of Five Hundred should keep the festival of the Apaturia for five days, which is how many days the Protenthae celebrated. The Apaturia were properly completed in three days, but the following day, which they called the epitheusis, was also celebrated with festivity; I gather this from Simplicius on Book IV of the Physics: the third day of the Apaturia, like the Dorpia festival, and the twelfth of the Anthesteria, and the fourth of the Epiboedia. Likewise from Hesychius: Apaturia, a festival of the Athenians lasting five days. Of these the first was the Dorpia, the second the Anarrysis, the third the Koureotis, the fourth the Epiboedia. The Protenthae, however, who seem chiefly to have celebrated this festival, as the words of this decree indicate, are also indicated by Philyllius in Hercules: "...the festival of the Pegthia..."

units.la: festum hoc vno die anteuertebant, quem etiam, vt ex hoc Psephismate liquet, geniliter & cum festiuitate transigebant. Quare festiuissimus Aristophanes ὁ κωμῳδιοποιὸς Νεφέλαις, vno die præuertere dicit esse Protenthiarum functi officio: verba eius sunt: [illegible, ~30 letters] [illegible, ~30 letters] [illegible, ~30 letters] [illegible, ~30 letters]
units.tr: This festival they celebrated on the one day before, which, as is clear from this decree, they also observed with rejoicing and festivity. Hence the most festive Aristophanes, the comic poet, in the Clouds, says that on the day before he had performed the office of the Protenthiae. His words are: [illegible]

units.la: Quinque igitur dies Apaturiorum festo agitado impendebant Protenthæ, quos etiam à Senatoribus feriatos & festos haberi voluit hoc Psephismate Phocus.
units.tr: Thus the Protenthae devoted five days to the festival of the Apaturia, and Phocus, by this decree, wished them to be regarded as holidays and festal days by the senators.

units.la: Accipiebant, de publico pecuniam Senatores, honorarium illius operæ, quâ Reipublicæ impendebat. Vlpianus in Timocratea: ὑ μὲν οἱ [illegible, ~14 letters] ἀλλ' ἡ βουλή. Honorarium hoc erat in diem drachma. Hesychius: βουλῆς λαχεῖν, ὃ λαχὼν βουλευτὴν, καὶ ἀπαχμὸν τῆς ἡμέρας λαχεῖν.
units.tr: The senators received money from the public treasury, an honorarium for the service they rendered to the Republic. Vlpian, in the Timocratea: ...but the Council. This honorarium was one drachma a day. Hesychius: "to draw the lot for the Council" means to be chosen as a councillor, and to receive the daily allowance.

units.la: Cùm Senatum ingressi essent Senatores, Ioui atque Mineruæ sacra faciebant. Antiphon περὶ τῆς ἱερωσύνης. Καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ Βουλευτηρίῳ Διὸς Βουλαίου, καὶ Ἀθηνᾶς Βουλαίας, ἱερὰ ἦσαν, καὶ εἰσιόντες οἱ βουλευταὶ προσεύχονται. Hoc ipsum est, quod dixit Demosthenes εἰσαγγελία ἱερὰ τῆς βουλῆς ἱερὰ ποιοῦσι. Extat locus ἐν τῷ κατὰ Μειδίου, ὡς ἐπαγγελλόμενος μὲ φόνου, καὶ Ϝοῦτι προσέχεται ἐπαγωγὴν, εἴασε μὲν μὲ εἰσ-αγγελία ἱερὰ τῆς βουλῆς ἱερὰ ποιοῦσι. Quibus è verbis colliges Demosthenem Senatorem approbatum, & muneres illo functum fuisse, quamquam eum ἐν τῇ δοκιμασίᾳ cædis accusasset Midias. Quid sit ὃ εἰσαγγελία ἱερὰ ποιοῦσι optime ad hunc locum interpretatur Vlpianus: εἰσαγγελία ἡ ἐγγίνετο, ἀλλ᾽ ὑμῖν εἰσφέρει τῆς βουλῆς εἰς ὃ βουλευτήριον, ὡς κατὰ γνώμην ἀπόδειξιν τῶν προσχημάτων τῶν σκέψιν. Ἐπὶ τῆν ἐκάλεσεν εἰσαγγελία. Proscribebant autem Prytaneis, de quibusnam futura erat relatio in Senatu. Pollux Libro VIII. cap. IX. οἱ Πρυτάνεις προσγραφέντες τῆς βουλῆς, ὑπὸ ὧν δὲ ἐξεγένετο. Sumebant una quotidie cibum Prytaneis singulis suæ πρυτανείας diebus. Pollux Libro VIII. cap. XV. ἡ δὲ Ἐλλάς, ἐν ᾗ συσσιτίῳ ἑκάσης ἡμέρας, πεντήκοντα τῆς τῶν Ἐπιγαμοίων βουλῆς, ἡ πρυτανεύουσα φυλὴ. Athenæus Libro V. συνεδρίῳ οἱ συντρόφοι ἡ πρυτάνεις ὁ τὰ φρούρια καὶ συνθήκα τὰ πόλεων σωθῆναι. Harpocration ex Ammonio Lamptiensi: ὁ τόπος, ὅπου ἐγκαλοῦσι οἱ Πρυτάνεις, κλῆσις Θόλος.
units.tr: When the Senators had entered the Senate, they performed sacrifices to Zeus and Athena. Antiphon, On the Priesthood: "And in the Council-house itself there were sacred things of Zeus Boulaios and Athena Boulaia, and the councillors on entering offer prayers." [Καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ Βουλευτηρίῳ Διὸς Βουλαίου, καὶ Ἀθηνᾶς Βουλαίας, ἱερὰ ἦσαν, καὶ εἰσιόντες οἱ βουλευταὶ προσεύχονται.] This is the very thing Demosthenes meant when he said that they make the Council's sacred things sacred [εἰσαγγελία ἱερὰ τῆς βουλῆς ἱερὰ ποιοῦσι]. There is a passage in his speech against Meidias, where he says that he was being indicted for murder and had not yet been admitted to the scrutiny, and that the Council's sacred things were made sacred [ἐν τῷ κατὰ Μειδίου ... εἰσαγγελία ἱερὰ τῆς βουλῆς ἱερὰ ποιοῦσι]. From these words you may gather that Demosthenes had been approved as a Senator and had performed that office, although Meidias had accused him of murder during the scrutiny. What the phrase means is best explained for this place by Ulpian: an indictment was lodged, but it was brought against the Council's building, where the Council sat and the proposals were tested for their form [εἰσαγγελία ἡ ἐγγίνετο ... ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκάλεσεν εἰσαγγελία]. The Prytaneis would post in advance the matters on which the Senate was to be consulted. Pollux, Book VIII, chapter IX: the Prytaneis, having been posted for the Council, by whom it was permitted [οἱ Πρυτάνεις προσγραφέντες τῆς βουλῆς, ὑπὸ ὧν δὲ ἐξεγένετο]. Each day the Prytaneis of the current prytaneia shared a meal together. Pollux, Book VIII, chapter XV: in the Hellas, where the common meal each day was for fifty of the Council of the Epigamoi, the tribe then holding the prytaneia [ἡ δὲ Ἐλλάς, ἐν ᾗ συσσιτίῳ ἑκάσης ἡμέρας, πεντήκοντα τῆς τῶν Ἐπιγαμοίων βουλῆς, ἡ πρυτανεύουσα φυλή]. Athenaeus, Book V: the Prytaneis, who were the companions in the common meal, to keep the fortresses and the treaties of the cities safe [συνεδρίῳ οἱ συντρόφοι ἡ πρυτάνεις ὁ τὰ φρούρια καὶ συνθήκα τὰ πόλεων σωθῆναι]. Harpocration, from Ammonius of Lamptrae: the place where the Prytaneis dine is called the Tholos [ὁ τόπος, ὅπου ἐγκαλοῦσι οἱ Πρυτάνεις, κλῆσις Θόλος].

units.la: Quo autem ordine in Senatu sederent οἱ Πεντακόσιοι, sententiamque rogarentur, ac dicerent, quærendum est. οἱ Πεντακόσιοι in decem classes distribuebantur: classis unaquæque erat πεντήκοντα ἀνδρῶν ἀπὸ μιᾶς φυλῆς. Quinquaginta illi viri in sua classe singuli sedebant, & sententiam dicebant, nō confuse, ita, ex. gr. qui erat ex Aiantide Tribu sententiam dicebat in sua Aiantidis Tribu classe, non verò inter Senatores, qui erant ex Cecropide, aut Acamantide Tribu. Classes autem, non dubito sedisse, & sententiam dixisse pro eo ordine, quem forsan ab ipso anni principio vnicuique attribuerat: ita principem locum obtinebat Tribus illa, quæ tunc πρυτανεύουσα: secundum locum occupabat (nisi post absolutam primam Prytaneiam, videtur enim sedisse post Tribum illam, cuius tunc erat Prytaneia, atque ita eodem ordine deinceps) Tribus, cuius erat sequentis πρυτανείας imperium: atque ita deinceps proinde πρυτάνευον ἐκ Ἀγαθοκλέους [?] φυλαὶ κληρῳ λαχόντες κατὰ ἐναντίον. Quæstio nunc est, de ordine, quo sederent, sententiam rogarentur, & dicerent vniuscuiusque Tribus πεντήκοντα ἄνδρες, siue οἱ Πρυτάνεις. Quod vt intelligatur, sciendum est, &τοὺς Ἐπιστάτας τῶν Πρυτάνεων, & πὰς ἑνία Ἐπιστάτας, ἀπὸ φυλῆς ἑκάστης ἦσα, πλὴν τῆς πρυτανευούσης, ceteris omnibus præsedisse. Quod ad ceteros verò attinet, magna suspicio est habitam esse ætatis rationem, ita vt in vnaquaque Tribu primi sententiam dicerent, rogarenturque, qui ætate essent prou ĉtiores; huic in re non dispari apud Plutarchum in Nicia: λέγεται ἡ ἐν τῷ Σπαρτιάτῃ ποτὲ βουλευομένων τῇ κοινῇ τῆν σωαρχόντων, κελεύσοντες ἑαυτοῖς ἐπὶ τοῦ ἄρχοντος ἐπιτήρησιν γνώμῃ Σοφοκλῆς ὁ ποιητὴς, ὡς πρεσβύτατος ὢν τῆν συσπατήρων. Ita etiam in Concione, pro ætatis ratione, primi, secundi, tertij, & ita deinceps, orationem habebant ad populū. Alius postea ordo est institutus, Glaucippo Atheni< s Prætore, hoc est, anno tertio Olympiadis nonagesimæ secundæ: is enim annus hunc habuit Prætorem, vt habent Diodorus Siculus & Anonymus in Descriptione Olympiadum: Nam vniuscuiusque Tribus Senatores ab illo tempore, praeter Procedros, sederunt & sententiam dixerunt in sua Tribu, eo ordine, quem sors vnicuique adsignauit. Sors fiebat per literas, ita qui A fortitus esset, primus sedebat, secundus, cui obtigiset B, & ita de ceteris deinceps. Quod vt obseruaretur, est relatum inter Kapita iurisiurandi, quod praestabat oi Πεντακόσιοι. Iurabant enim in haec verba, se eo ordine, quem literae sors attribuisset, in Senatu sessuros. Id nos docet Graecus Aristophanis Interpres è Philochoro, ad hunc Pluti versum,
units.tr: We must now ask in what order the Five Hundred sat in the Senate, and were asked for their opinion and gave it. The Five Hundred were divided into ten classes; each class consisted of fifty men from one tribe [πεντήκοντα ἀνδρῶν ἀπὸ μιᾶς φυλῆς]. Those fifty men sat individually in their own class and gave their opinion, not in confusion; thus, for example, a man of the Aiantis tribe gave his opinion within his own Aiantis class, and not among the Senators from Cecropis or Acamantis. I do not doubt that the classes sat and gave their opinions in an order which had been assigned to each one, perhaps from the very beginning of the year. So the tribe that then held the prytaneia had the first place. The second place was held by the tribe whose turn at the next prytaneia it was (unless, after the first prytaneia was over, they sat after the tribe whose prytaneia it then was, and so on in the same order). And so the tribes were chosen by lot to hold the prytaneia in turn [πρυτάνευον ... φυλαὶ κληρῳ λαχόντες κατὰ ἐναντίον]. The question now is in what order the fifty men of each tribe, or the Prytaneis, sat, were asked for their opinion, and spoke. To understand this we must know that the Epistatai of the Prytaneis, and some Epistatai, came from each tribe except the one then holding the prytaneia, and presided over all the rest. As for the others, I strongly suspect that account was taken of age, so that in each tribe the older men gave their opinion first and were asked first. A similar practice is found in Plutarch, in the life of Nicias: it is said that once, when the magistrates were deliberating in common about the matter, Sophocles the poet, being the oldest of the generals, was asked for his opinion first [λέγεται ... Σοφοκλῆς ὁ ποιητής, ὡς πρεσβύτατος ὢν τῶν συστρατήγων]. So too in the assembly, by reason of age, the first, second, third and so on addressed the people in turn. Later another order was instituted, under Glaucippus as archon at Athens, that is, in the third year of the ninety-second Olympiad; for that year had this archon, as Diodorus Siculus and the anonymous writer on the Olympiads record. From that time on, the Senators of each tribe, apart from the Proedroi, sat and gave their opinion within their own tribe in the order which lot assigned to each man. The lot was made by letters: whoever drew A sat first, the second, whose letter was B, sat second, and so on for the rest. That this was observed is recorded among the clauses of the oath which the Five Hundred took. For they swore in these words that they would sit in the Senate in the order which the letter assigned by lot to them. The Greek commentator on Aristophanes, drawing on Philochorus, teaches us this, on the line of Plutus:

units.la: ἀλλ' ὁ λαχὼν ἔπιτις ἐκ τοῦ γραμματέως. [?]
units.tr: "But he who was chosen by lot from the secretary..." [ἀλλ' ὁ λαχὼν ἔπιτις ἐκ τοῦ γραμματέως.]

units.la: ἐπὶ τῶν [?] ἐπὶ εἰσιγγέλλεσθαι ... [illegible, ~20 letters] ... καὶ ἡ βουλὴ ... ἐπὶ τὸ γραμματεῖον. [?]
units.tr: [The Greek text here is too corrupt to translate with confidence: "...on the matter of being indicted [...] ... and the Council ... to the writing-office."] [ἐπὶ τῶν ... ἐπὶ εἰσιγγέλλεσθαι ... καὶ ἡ βουλὴ ... ἐπὶ τὸ γραμματεῖον.]

units.la: ἐτι τὸ γραμμα ... [illegible, ~30 letters] ... Ν [?]
units.tr: [The Greek text here is too corrupt to translate: "...the letter ... [illegible] ... N."] [ἐτι τὸ γραμμα ... Ν.]

units.la: Quaedam corrupta sunt in iis Philochori: Relcribo, καὶ ἡ βουλὴ ἐν τῷ γραμματείῳ. & paulò post, καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ ἐκ τοῦ γραμματεῖ, ὅ ἐπὶ λαχόντι.
units.tr: Some things in these passages of Philochorus are corrupt. I read: "and the Council in the secretary's office," and a little later: "and elsewhere from the secretary, who is chosen by lot" [καὶ ἡ βουλὴ ἐν τῷ γραμματείῳ; καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ ἐκ τοῦ γραμματεῖ, ὅ ἐπὶ λαχόντι].

units.la: Populum quoque in concionem cogebant Prytaneis statis diebus, nempe quater singulis Prytaneiis» Aristoteles ἐν τῇ Ἀθηναίων πολιτείᾳ. οἱ Πρυτάνεις ἐπιψηφίζουσιν τῶν Βουλῶν, ἡ δ᾽ ἡμέρα ἡ Βουλὴ, ἐπιμέρᾳ, πλὴν ἐάν ἡ ἀφίσταται ἥ, τὴν δὲ ἡμέραν σύνοψιν τῆς πρὸς τὰς ἐκκλησίας ἀρχῶν. Pollux Lib. VIII. cap. IX. οἱ Πρυτάνεις τὴν δὲ ἡμέραν συνάγειν τῆς Πρυτανείας ἐκκλησίας. Sed Vlpianus in Timocratcam ter tantum singulis mensibus in concionem conuenisse scribit: ἴσως γὰρ ὅτι ἐχ μὲν τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἐπιμεληθεὶς τῶν βουλευομένων τῆς πόλεως ἐπὶ τῶν προτέρων ἐκκλησίων, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν Πρυτανεῖον ἐκ τῶν ὀφειλομένων. Corrigendus ad hoc exemplum Aristophanis Interpres, & qui eum descripsit Suidas, in haec Acharnensium verba:
units.tr: The Prytaneis also gathered the people into assembly on fixed days, namely four times in each prytaneia. Aristotle, in the Constitution of the Athenians: "The Prytaneis put to the vote the business of the Council; the Council meets each day in turn, unless it is discharged; and on the day the Prytaneis summon the assembly..." [οἱ Πρυτάνεις ἐπιψηφίζουσιν τῶν Βουλῶν, ἡ δ᾽ ἡμέρα ἡ Βουλὴ, ἐπιμέρᾳ, πλὴν ἐάν ἡ ἀφίσταται ἥ, τὴν δὲ ἡμέραν σύνοψιν τῆς πρὸς τὰς ἐκκλησίας ἀρχῶν.] Pollux, Book VIII, chapter IX: "the Prytaneis on the day of the prytaneia convene the assembly" [οἱ Πρυτάνεις τὴν δὲ ἡμέραν συνάγειν τῆς Πρυτανείας ἐκκλησίας]. But Ulpian, in his commentary on Timocrates, writes that they met in assembly only three times in each month: "perhaps because, from the assembly, the care of the deliberations of the city belonged to the earlier assemblies, and to the Prytaneion from what was owed" [ἴσως γὰρ ὅτι ἐχ μὲν τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἐπιμεληθεὶς τῶν βουλευομένων τῆς πόλεως ἐπὶ τῶν προτέρων ἐκκλησίων, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν Πρυτανεῖον ἐκ τῶν ὀφειλομένων]. The commentator on Aristophanes, and Suidas who copied him, must be corrected by this example, on those Acharnians lines:

units.la: ὡς νῦν ὅποτ᾽ ἔσθ᾽ κυρίας ἐκκλησίας ἐωνῆς, ἔρμας ἡ πυρὶ αὐτοῖ.
units.tr: "As now, whenever there is a sovereign assembly, ..., they burn them with fire." [ὡς νῦν ὅποτ᾽ ἔσθ᾽ κυρίας ἐκκλησίας ἐωνῆς, ἔρμας ἡ πυρὶ αὐτοῖ.]

units.la: Κυρίας ἐκκλησίας, ἐν ᾗ ἐκνέμηται ἡ ἐπαγγελία, εἰσὶ ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκκλησία αἱ λεγόμεναι τῆς μιᾶς Ἀθηναίων, ἡ ἰδιωτικὴ, ἡ ἐπιγραφή. Error ortus erat proculdubio è literis numeralibus. Verùm potior est Aristotelis sententia, meo iudicio, & falluntur Grammatici, qui pronunciarunt κυρίας ἐκκλησίας ter cogi singulis mensibus, si negant intra vertentis Prytaneiae ambitum, qui est dierum triginta quinque, quater conueniri in concionem. Verùm quidem est intra triginta Prytaneiae dies ter tantum haberi concionem, & bearunt nos Grammatici, qui dies defignant, quanquam mensis non sunt, sed Prytaneiae. Prima igitur τῆς κυρίας ἐκκλησίας cogebatur die vndecimo Prytaneiae: quibus de rebus haberetur explicat Pollux loco laudato: τὰν δὲ ἡμέραν πρῶτον ἐκκλησίας Πυτάνεως, καὶ πρῶτον ἡμέραν ... ἡ βουλὴ ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ... [?]. Secunda habebatur die vicesimo Prytaneiae, de his, vt apud Polluccm sequitur: ἡ δὲ δευτέρα ἐκκλησία, αὐτῆς ἐν ταῖς βουλομένοις ἐκπομπῆς ... [illegible, ~25 letters] ..., λέγων ἀδελφὸς [?] τὸ ἴδιον ἢ τῆς δημοσίων.
units.tr: "Sovereign assembly" means that assembly at which the proposal is brought forward; these are the regular assemblies of the Athenians, called the first, the private, and the superscribed. The error doubtless arose from the numerals. But in my judgment Aristotle's view is the stronger, and those grammarians are mistaken who declare that the sovereign assembly was convened three times each month, if they deny that within the course of one prytaneia, which lasts thirty-five days, it met four times. It is true that within thirty days of the prytaneia there was only three times an assembly, and the grammarians who name the days are not naming months, but prytaneiai. So the first sovereign assembly was convened on the eleventh day of the prytaneia. Pollux, in the passage cited, explains what was dealt with: "the first day of the prytaneia's assembly, and the first day ... the Council in the assembly ..." [τὰν δὲ ἡμέραν πρῶτον ἐκκλησίας Πυτάνεως, καὶ πρῶτον ἡμέραν ... ἡ βουλὴ ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ]. The second was held on the twentieth day of the prytaneia, concerning matters which, as Pollux continues, "the second assembly, in which those who wish to make proposals ... to speak about private or public matters" [ἡ δὲ δευτέρα ἐκκλησία, αὐτῆς ἐν ταῖς βουλομένοις ἐκπομπῆς ... λέγων ἀδελφὸς τὸ ἴδιον ἢ τῆς δημοσίων].

units.la: Tertia cogebatur, die tricesimo Prytaneiae: quae in hac concione referrentur ad populum descripsit Pollux ibidem: ἡ δὲ τρίτη, κηρύξει ἢ πρεσβείας, ἄξιον χρηματίζειν, οὓς δεῖ παρέπεμπεν τοὺς Πρυτάνεις ἀπόδωσαι τὰ χρήματα. Habet in sequentibus Pollux ea de quibus in suffragia mittebatur populus Quarta concione: ἡ δὲ τετάρτη, περὶ ἱερῶν ἢ ὁσίων.
units.tr: The third was convened on the thirtieth day of the prytaneia. Pollux describes in the same place what was brought before the people in this assembly: "the third, for the proclamation of embassies, for the business of those who ought to be dealt with, and for the Prytaneis to render the money" [ἡ δὲ τρίτη, κηρύξει ἢ πρεσβείας, ἄξιον χρηματίζειν, οὓς δεῖ παρέπεμπεν τοὺς Πρυτάνεις ἀπόδωσαι τὰ χρήματα]. In what follows, Pollux also lists the matters on which the people cast their votes. The fourth assembly: "the fourth, concerning sacred things and holy matters" [ἡ δὲ τετάρτη, περὶ ἱερῶν ἢ ὁσίων].

units.la: Eaque, puto, in concione Prytaneis, quos oportebat ἀνὰ ἑκάστην κοινῇ, ut est ἐν τῷ περὶ πρεσβείας, solebant populo renunciare, an litassent, necne, cuius moris legitur exemplum apud Theophrastum περὶ μικροφιλοτιμίας. ἀμὴ δὲ καὶ σιωπῆσαι [?] τῶν Πρυτανέων ὅπως ἀπαγγείλῃ τὰ ἱερά, καὶ προσκυνήσαντες λαμπρὸν ἱμάτιον, καὶ ἐσεφανωμένος, προελθὼν εἶπεν, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, ἐὰν ὁ ἡμῖν ἱερὸς [?] ἀξία καὶ καλὰ, ἡ ὑμεῖς ἐκδέχεσθε τὰ ἀγαθά. Huic renunciationi non tam accommodatum est, quam solennia illius verba repraesentant totum Proëmium Demosthenis LXIII. Καὶ δίκαιον, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, καὶ καλὸν, ἐπ' ἀπ[?] ἀπρόσοδον, ἐὰν ὑμεῖς εἰσάγητε, καὶ ἡμᾶς ἀναγνῶσι, ὅπως τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἡμῖν ὁ ἐκείνοις ἔρχεται. ἡ μὲν οὖν ἡμετέρα γίγνεται ἐπιμέλεια ὑμῖν εἰς ὅσον, ἡ γὰρ ἐξύπαυλον τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ Σωτῆρος, ἡ τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ, καὶ τῇ Νίκῃ, καὶ γίγνονται καλὰ ἐς σωτηρία ᾧ ὑμῖν τὰ ἱερά. ἐξύπαυλον ἡ ἐς τῇ Ῥήθοι, ἡ τῇ Μητρὶ τῶν θεῶν, ἐς τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος· ἡ ἐκαλλιερεύσαν ἡ ἑαυτὰ. ὧν δὲ ὑμῖν ἡ τὰ ἐς ἄλλοις τυγχάνοντα ἱερὰ, ἀσφαλῆ, ἡ βέβαια, ἡ καλὰ, ἡ σωτηρία, δίκαιόν οὖν τῶν ἀγαθῶν [?] τῶν θεῶν διδόντων ταῖς ἀγαθά. Mendum occupavit, mea quidem sententia, haec verba ἢ τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ καὶ τῇ Νίκῃ. Legendum quippe est, ἐν τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ τῇ Νίκῃ. Mincruam enim intelligit, quae Nixn cognominabatur. Iam vero inuestigemus quoto Prytaneiae die cogeretur haec Ecclesia. Apud Aristophanem Acharnensibus fingitur haberi tertia Concio τῷ κυρίῳ· nam inducuntur in concionem Legati Persarum Regis, item Θέωγις ὁ ἀπὸ Σιπάλκους ea habita est die tricesimo Prytaneiae, qui incidit in primum mensis Metagitnionis, unde Pauonum mentio, quia eo die illorum exhibebatur spectaculum. -- ἀξόμεθ' γὰρ Πρίσθεσι, Καὶ τοῖς Ξαδοι, τοῖς τ' ἀλεξονδίμασι.
units.tr: I think it was in this assembly that the Prytaneis, who had to report each day in common, as is said in the work On Embassies, were accustomed to announce to the people whether the sacrifices had been favourable or not. An example of this custom is read in Theophrastus, On Petty Ambition: "and having kept silent, the Prytaneis, to announce the sacrifices, and having bowed low, wearing a bright cloak and crowned, came forward and said: 'Men of Athens, if the sacrifices are favourable and good, you will receive the goods'" [ἀμὴ δὲ καὶ σιωπῆσαι τῶν Πρυτανέων ὅπως ἀπαγγείλῃ τὰ ἱερά, καὶ προσκυνήσαντες λαμπρὸν ἱμάτιον, καὶ ἐσεφανωμένος, προελθὼν εἶπεν, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, ἐὰν ὁ ἡμῖν ἱερὸς ἀξία καὶ καλὰ, ἡ ὑμεῖς ἐκδέχεσθε τὰ ἀγαθά]. This announcement is not so closely fitted to it as are the solemn words that represent the whole proem of Demosthenes, Oration LXIII: "And it is just and fitting, men of Athens, if you bring in and read to us..., that the good things come to them. Our care is for you, for the sacrifices to Zeus the Saviour, to Athena, and to Nike, and the sacrifices turn out well for your safety..." [Καὶ δίκαιον, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, καὶ καλὸν, ἐπ' ἀπ[...] ἀπρόσοδον, ἐὰν ὑμεῖς εἰσάγητε, καὶ ἡμᾶς ἀναγνῶσι, ὅπως τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἡμῖν ὁ ἐκείνοις ἔρχεται ... ἡ μὲν οὖν ἡμετέρα γίγνεται ἐπιμέλεια ὑμῖν εἰς ὅσον, ἡ γὰρ ἐξύπαυλον τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ Σωτῆρος, ἡ τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ, καὶ τῇ Νίκῃ, καὶ γίγνονται καλὰ ἐς σωτηρία ᾧ ὑμῖν τὰ ἱερά]. I believe there is an error in the words ἢ τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ καὶ τῇ Νίκῃ; one should read ἐν τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ τῇ Νίκῃ, for he means Athena, who was surnamed Nike. Now let us inquire on what day of the prytaneia this assembly was convened. In Aristophanes' Acharnians a third assembly of the sovereign kind is imagined; for envoys of the Persian king are brought into the assembly, and Theogenes of Sipalettus [...] was heard on the thirtieth day of the prytaneia, which fell on the first of Metageitnion, whence comes the mention of the peacocks, because on that day their spectacle was shown: "for we shall bring them to the Pristhesi, and to the Xadoi, and to the alexandrimas..." [ἀξόμεθ' γὰρ Πρίσθεσι, Καὶ τοῖς Ξαδοι, τοῖς τ' ἀλεξονδίμασι].

units.la: Dimittuntur Legati hi è Thracia, & sequenti concione adesse iubentur Praeconis voce: haec concio futura est die ab hinc tertio: Τοὺς Θρᾷκας ἀπιέναι, πρῶτον δ' εἰς ἓν ἐᾶν, Οἱ γὰρ Πρυτάνεις λύσετοι τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.
units.tr: These envoys from Thrace are dismissed, and the Herald's voice summons them to attend the next assembly, which will be held three days from now: "Let the Thracians depart, but first let them be let alone for one (day), for the Prytaneis will dissolve the assembly." [Τοὺς Θρᾷκας ἀπιέναι, πρῶτον δ' εἰς ἓν ἐᾶν, Οἱ γὰρ Πρυτάνεις λύσετοι τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.]

units.la: Optime Scholiastes ἐς ἑνῶ interpretatur εἰς τρίτην. Ergo Quarta concio cogebatur die tricesimo tertio Prytaneiae. En autem tibi Kalendarium Atticum cum Prytaniis adscriptis, ἐκκλησίας item ἐκκλησίας, & Festis, quae observare potuimus.
units.tr: The Scholiast rightly explains "eis hen" as "eis tritēn" (to the third). So the fourth assembly was held on the thirty-third day of Prytaneia. Here, then, is the Attic calendar, with the Prytanies noted, the assemblies (ekklesiai) likewise, and the festivals that I was able to identify.

units.la: Prytanciarum initium ab Hecatombæone mense repetimus, auctore Demosthene, qui τῷ τῆς ἑορτῆς Πρυτανείας ἐνδικάτῳ confert in Timocratea cum τῇ τῆς Ἐκατομβαιῶνος μηνός. Quanquam commode est intelligendus, nam politicæ non numerabatur dies vndecimus Hecatombæonis, sed δεύτερα ὅτι ἡμέρα, itaque ita intelligendus est in his: ἀλλὰ τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ὅ ἡ ἐκ ἰούμως ἐπι-χειροτονήσατ, ἵνα ἐνδικάτης τῆς Ἐκατομβαιῶνος μηνὸς, διαδικάτη τὸν ἡμέραν εἰσηγή-σαν λόγος τῆς ὑπηρεσίας, ἡ ταῦτα ὄντων Κορίνθων. Seriem Prytanciarum ἡ τῶν κυρίων ἐκκλησιῶν pauca oppido sunt exempla quæ adstruant: cum pauca admodum adscribant numerum dierum Prytaniæ: Luculentissime tamen probat vetus hæc Inscriptio.
units.tr: We take the beginning of the Prytany days from the month Hekatombaion, on the authority of Demosthenes, who in the speech against Timocrates compares the eleventh day of the festival of the Prytany with the month of Hekatombaion. Yet this must be understood with care, for in the civil reckoning the eleventh day of Hekatombaion was not counted, but the second day after it; so this must be understood in these words, where the principal assembly was held on the eleventh of the month of Hekatombaion and was pushed back by the rule of the vote to the second day. Few examples exist that establish the sequence of Prytany days and of the principal assemblies, and very few record the number of days of the Prytany; yet this ancient inscription proves it most clearly.

units.la: ΕΠΙ ΑΡΙΣΤΑΙΧΜΟΥ ΑΡΧΟΝΤΟΣ ΓΑΜΗΛΙΩΝΟΣ ΔΕΚΑΤΗ ΙΣΤΑΜΕΝΟΥ ΕΚΚΛΗΣΙΑ ΚΥΡΙΑ ΕΝ ΤΩι ΕΚ- ΚΛΗΣΙΑΣΤΗΡΙΩι ΜΕΝΑΝΔΡΟΣ ΜΕΝΑΝΔΡΟΥ ΜΕΛΙΤΕΥΣ ΕΙΠΕΝ.
units.tr: In the archonship of Aristaichmos, on the tenth of the waxing month Gamelion, a principal assembly was held in the place of assembly. Menandros, son of Menandros of Melite, spoke. [ΕΠΙ ΑΡΙΣΤΑΙΧΜΟΥ ΑΡΧΟΝΤΟΣ ΓΑΜΗΛΙΩΝΟΣ ΔΕΚΑΤΗ ΙΣΤΑΜΕΝΟΥ ΕΚΚΛΗΣΙΑ ΚΥΡΙΑ ΕΝ ΤΩι ΕΚΚΛΗΣΙΑΣΤΗΡΙΩι ΜΕΝΑΝΔΡΟΣ ΜΕΝΑΝΔΡΟΥ ΜΕΛΙΤΕΥΣ ΕΙΠΕΝ.]

units.la: Optime: nam τῇ δεκάτῃ ἱσταμένου Γαμηλιῶνος habebatur κυρία ἐκκλησία τῆς ἑορτῆς τῆς Πρυτανείας, vt in hoc Kalendario habes: ex his autem præterea aliquam lucem præferre fumus conati. Apud Iosephum Lib. XIV. cap. XVI. illa legun-tur, quæ alibi exposuimus: μηνὸς Πανέμου πέμπτῃ ἀπίοντος, ἐπὶ Ἀχαϊκλείσης Ἀρχοντος, ἐνάτης Μεταδιδρου Ἀλιμουσίος, ἐχαμμάτευε, Μοκωνχάδες, ἐνδικάτῃ τῆς Πρυτανείας, ἐκκλησίας ἡμοιμένης ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆ Πεζέδων. Panemus Syromacedonum Lunaris est, coque usi Magistratus Athenienses, respondetque
units.tr: Quite right: for on the tenth of the waxing month Gamelion a principal assembly was held on the festival of the Prytany, as you have in this calendar; from these we have also tried to throw some light. In Josephus, Book XIV, chapter XVI, the following is read, which we have explained elsewhere: on the fifth day of the waning month Panemus, in the archonship of Achaikleses, on the ninth of Metageitnion... [μηνὸς Πανέμου πέμπτῃ ἀπίοντος, ἐπὶ Ἀχαϊκλείσης Ἀρχοντος, ἐνάτης Μεταδιδρου Ἀλιμουσίος, ἐχαμμάτευε, Μοκωνχάδες, ἐνδικάτῃ τῆς Πρυτανείας, ἐκκλησίας ἡμοιμένης ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆ Πεζέδων.] Panemus is a lunar month of the Syromacedonians, which the Athenian magistrates also used, and it corresponds to the lunar month Munychion.

units.la: Munychioni Lunari: dies πέμπτῃ μουνυχιῶνος siue Πανέμου ἀπόνης[?], est vndecimus dies Prytaneiae, vt habes in hoc nostro Kalendario, quod habetur ἡ πρώτη κυρία ἐκκλησία[?]. Apud Æschinem ἐν τῷ κατὰ Κτησιφῶντος[?], ista leguntur de Demosthene, γράφει ψήφισμα, ὃς τὰς χειροτονίας τῆς πόλεως ὑφαιρούμενος, ἐκκλησίαν ποιεῖν τοῖς Πρυτάνεσι τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἱσταμένου τοῦ Ἐλαφηβολιῶνος μηνός[?], ὅτι ἐν τῷ Ἀσκληπιῷ ἡ ἑορτή[?], ἣν ὁ παρεγγυῶν ἐν τῇ ἱερᾷ ἡμέρᾳ, ἡ παρέχεσθαι Ὀλυμπίασι μέμνηται ἡμέρα[?]. Παρέφασιν ποιησάμενος, ἵνα (φησὶ) ἐᾶν ἢ ἂν τὴν πρέσβεις, βουλεύσηται ὁ δῆμος ὡς ἂν χρῆ περὶ τῆς πρὸς Φίλιππον πρεσβείας[?]. Hac die, quæ politice numerabatur ὀγδόῃ ἱσταμένου τοῦ Ἐλαφηβολιῶνος μηνός[?], cogebatur pro more concio, quarta τῆς κυρίας, in qua περὶ ἱερῶν ἢ ὁσίων agebatur, sed Demosthenes voluit referri de Legatis ad Philippum mittendis, atque id vnum est, quod Æschini improbatur. Apud Aristophanem Θεσμοφοριαζούσας.
units.tr: The day "fifth of Munychion," or Panemus, is the eleventh day of the Prytany, as you have in this calendar of ours, where it is given as the first principal assembly. In Aeschines, in the speech against Ctesiphon, these things are read about Demosthenes: he drafted a decree that, depriving the city of its votes, ordered the Prytanes to hold an assembly on the eighth day of the waxing month Elaphebolion, because the festival at the sanctuary of Asclepius... He made a pretext, namely (he says) that the envoys should not be sent, but that the people should deliberate as is right about the embassy to Philip. On this day, which in the civil reckoning was the eighth of the waxing month Elaphebolion, an assembly was convened as usual, the fourth of the principal assemblies, in which matters concerning sacred and holy things were treated; but Demosthenes wished the question of sending envoys to Philip to be raised, and this alone is what Aeschines finds fault with. In Aristophanes, Thesmophoriazusae:

units.la: Καὶ πῶς; ἐπὶ νῷ γ' ὅτε τὰ δικαστήρια
units.tr: "And how? On the day when the law courts

units.la: Μέλλ' δικάζειν, ὅτε βουλῆς ἐαῦ' ἔδρα.
units.tr: are about to sit, when the Council has its seat,

units.la: Ἐπὶ τρίτῃ Θεσμοφορίων ἡ μέση.
units.tr: on the middle of the third day of the Thesmophoria."

units.la: Locum hunc attigit Hesychius: τρίτῃ Θεσμοφορίων. ἐπὶ τῇ τρίτῃ Θεσμοφορίων εἴ), ἅμα δὲ μέσῳ, πεπαφῶν ὑσῶν ἡμερῶν. Sed non penetrauit, meo iudicio: adde quod leuiter corruptus est, rescribendus in hunc modum:
units.tr: Hesychius touched on this passage: "third of the Thesmophoria." On the third of the Thesmophoria, "middle," ... of the days. But in my judgment he did not get to the heart of it. Add that it is slightly corrupted, and should be rewritten thus:

units.la: Ἐπὶ τρίτης ἢ Θεσμοφορίων ἡ μέση.
units.tr: "On the middle of the third [day] of the Thesmophoria."

units.la: Longe quidem alio sensu, quàm antea: nondum enim aduenerat dies tertius Thesmophoriorum, sed vertebat secundus illorum quatuor, die quintodecimo Pyanepsionis, quo habebatur quarta concio τῆς κυρίας, quæ erat περὶ ἱερῶν, itaque die festo etiam cogebatur, quanquam neque Senatus haberetur, neque iudicia redderentur. Erat autem hic dies secundus triens ac proinde medius illarum trium partium, in quas distribuit Aristophanes quatuor Thesmophoriorum dies, nam vnicuique trienti imputatur dies cum horis æquinoctialibus octo, itaque secundus siue medius trium festi Thesmophoriorum cepit circa orientem Solem, die quintodecimo Pyanepsionis, quo habebatur ἡ περὶ ἱερᾶς κυρίας ἐκκλησία, quæ quarta est Prytaneiæ, & haberi fingitur à feminis Θεσμοφοριαζούσαις. Apud Demosthenem ἐν τῷ κατὰ Στεφάνου hoc Psephisma legitur: ἐπὶ Ἀρχίππου Μνησιφίλου, Ἐχεπολέμου Ἀγαμέδος[?] εἶπεν, &c. δεδόχθαι τῇ βουλῇ τῇ τοῦ δήμου τῆς Ἀθηναίων, ὅπως ἂν ἡ εἰρήνη ὑπὸ πόλεως ἡ ὑπάρχοντα συνῆσα ἐν τῇ κυρίᾳ ἐκκλησίᾳ, χειροτονεῖσθαι ἐλέσθαι ἐκ πάντων Ἀθηναίων ἡδὲ πέντε, &c. χειροτονεῖ ἐπεῖ ἐπάρχειν, Εὔβουλος ἀνάφλυστος, &c. Demosthenes τὸ προβούλευμα hoc scripsit in Senatu die vltimo Hecatombæonis, sequenti die, qui erat primus Metagitnionis, habetur concio tertia τῆς κυρίας, in qua de Legatis, siue alio mittendis, siue aliunde Athenas aduenientibus, referebatur ad populum: Populus, vt ex his videtur, Demosthenis τῷ προβουλεύματι fetit, atque ita res transacta est, neque alio Psephismate opus fuit. Rursum apud eundem Demosthenem eadem Oratione paullo post hoc Psephisma describitur: ἐπὶ Μνησιφίλου Ἀρχίππου, συγκλήτου ἐκκλησίας τῶν γραμματέων ψηφισμάτων, καὶ Πρυτάνεων καὶ βουλῆς γνώμη, Μαιμακτηριῶνος δεκάτῃ ἀπόντος, Καλλιάδους Ἐπονίκου Φαληρέως εἶπε, &c.
units.tr: This has quite a different sense from before: the third day of the Thesmophoria had not yet arrived, but the second of those four days was coming round, on the fifteenth day of Pyanepsion, when the fourth assembly of the principal assemblies was held, which concerned sacred matters; so it was convened even on a festival day, although neither the Senate was held nor judgments delivered. This second day was a third part, and therefore the middle of those three parts into which Aristophanes divides the four days of the Thesmophoria; for each third is credited with a day of eight equinoctial hours, so the middle or second of the three days of the festival of the Thesmophoria began about sunrise, on the fifteenth day of Pyanepsion, on which the principal assembly concerning sacred matters was held, which is the fourth of the Prytany, and is supposed to have been held by the women celebrating the Thesmophoria. In Demosthenes, in the speech against Stephanus, this decree is read: "In the archonship of Archippos, son of Mnesiphilos, ... Echepolemos son of Agamedes proposed..., &c. It was resolved by the Council and the people of the Athenians that the peace, which is in force..., be elected in the principal assembly, from all the Athenians, five men, &c. ... Euboulos of Anaphlystos..., &c." Demosthenes wrote this preliminary decree in the Senate on the last day of Hekatombaion; on the following day, which was the first of Metageitnion, the third principal assembly was held, in which matters concerning envoys, whether to be sent elsewhere or arriving at Athens from elsewhere, were reported to the people. The people, as appears from this, approved Demosthenes' preliminary decree, and so the matter was settled, and no other decree was needed. Again, in the same speech of Demosthenes a little later this decree is written out: "In the archonship of Mnesiphilos, son of Archippos, the assembly of the scribes of decrees, and the Prytanes and the Council in agreement, on the twentieth day of the waning month Maimakterion, Kalliades, son of Epionikos of Phaleron, proposed, &c."

units.la: Die vicesimo Maemacterionis, qui politice numeratur Μαιμακτηριῶνος δεκάτῃ ἀπόντος[?].
units.tr: On the twentieth day of Maimacterion, which in the civil reckoning is the tenth day of Maimacterion, [?] ... ## THE SENATORIAL OATH. I will advise what is best for the city of the Athenians. I will advise according to the laws.
