units.tr: If any orator speaks in the Council or in the Assembly about the matters brought forward, either not separately concerning each matter, or twice about the same matter before the same men, or if he reviles someone, or abuses someone, or speaks improperly in a way that gives offence, or if he speaks about matters not on the agenda, or is urged on... [ΤΩΝ ΡΗΤΟΡΩΝ ΕΑΝ ΤΙΣ ΛΕΓΗ ΕΝ ΒΟΥΛΗ Η ΕΝ ΔΗΜΩΙ ΠΕΡΙ ΤΩΝ ΕΙΣΦΕΡΟΜΕΝΩΝ]

units.la: Si quis Oratorum in Senatu, aut in populo, vel non seorsim de re proposita, vel bis de eadem re apud eosdem dixerit, siue conuiciatus fuerit, siue maledixerit alicui, siue pede supploferit[?], vel inter decernendum importune locutus fuerit de rebus
units.tr: If any of the orators in the Senate or before the people speaks, either not separately about the matter proposed, or twice on the same matter before the same people, or if he has reviled anyone, or has insulted someone, or has stamped his foot, or has spoken unseasonably during the voting on matters

units.la: ΕΛΚΗΙ ΤΟΝ ΕΠΙΣΤΑΤΗΝ ΑΦΕΙΜΕΝΗΣ ΤΗΣ ΕΚΚΛΗΣΙΑΣ Η ΤΗΣ ΒΟΥΛΗΣ, ΚΥΡΙΕΥΕΤΩΣΑΝ ΟΙ ΠΡΟΕΔΡΟΙ ΜΕΧΡΙ ΠΕΝΤΗΚΟΝΤΑ ΔΡΑΧΜΩΝ ΕΙΘ' ΕΚΑΣΤΟΝ ΑΔΙΚΗΜΑ ΕΠΙΓΡΑΦΕΙΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΓΡΑΚΤΟΡΣΙΝ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΓΑΕΟΝΟΣ ΑΞΙΟΣ ΕΣΤΙ ΖΗΜΙΑΣ ΕΠΙΒΑΛΛΟΝΤΕΣ ΜΕΧΡΙ ΠΕΝΤΗΚΟΝΤΑ ΔΡΑΧΜΩΝ ΕΙΣΦΕΡΕΤΩΣΑΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΗΝ ΒΟΥΛΗΝ, Η ΕΙΣ ΤΗΝ ΠΡΩΤΗΝ ΕΚΚΛΗΣΙΑΝ ΕΝ ΤΩι ΒΟΥΛΕΥΤΗΡΙΩι, ΟΤΑΝ ΔΙΕΞΙΩΣΙ ΚΛΗΣΕΙΣ ΚΡΙΝΑΤΩΣΑΝ. ΚΑΙ ΕΑΝ ΚΑΤΑΓΝΩΣΘΗι ΑΥΤΟΥ ΚΡΥΒΔΗΝ ΥΗΦΙΖΟΝΤΩΝ ΤΩΝ ΒΟΥΛΕΥΤΩΝ, ΕΓΓΡΑΨΑΤΩΣΑΝ ΟΙ ΠΡΟΕΔΡΟΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΓΡΑΚΤΟΡΣΙ ΤΩΝ ΠΑΡΑΝΟΜΩΝ.
units.tr: ...and who is not concerned with the matters before the Assembly or the Council, the presidents shall have power to impose a fine of up to fifty drachmas on each offence and shall enter it for the collectors. If the offence seems worthy of a heavier penalty, the presidents shall impose a fine of up to fifty drachmas and bring the case before the Council, or before the first assembly in the Pnyx when the nine... have decided. And if he is condemned, when the councillors have voted in secret, the presidents shall enter the fine for the unlawful acts for the collectors.

units.la: alienis ab his, de quibus referebant Proedri, vel aliquem concitarit, vel Epistolam traxerit, dimissa concione, aut Senatu, eius multandi potestas esto penes Proedros ad quinquaginta drachmas vsque: quinquaginta hae drachmae exigendae inscribitor exactoribus hoc nomine: Quod si grauiorem meruisse poenam videbitur, irrogata multa ad quinquaginta drachmas vsque, deferunto ad Senatum, aut concionem, quae prima habebitur Vbi in ius vocatus fuerit, in Senatu indicanto. Quod si damnatus fuerit, clam suffragia ferentibus Senatoribus, Proedri multam exactoribus exigendam Legum violatarum nomine inscribunto.
units.tr: ...are not concerned with those matters about which the presidents report, or if he stirs up anyone, or draws up a letter, once the assembly or Senate has been dismissed; the power to fine him shall rest with the presidents, up to fifty drachmas. These fifty drachmas are to be collected and entered under this heading for the collectors. If the offence seems to deserve a heavier penalty, the fine imposed, up to fifty drachmas, shall be referred to the Senate or to the assembly which is held first. When he has been summoned to court, he shall be indicted in the Senate. If he is condemned, with the senators giving their votes in secret, the presidents shall enter the fine for the collectors to exact under the heading of violated laws.

units.la: Legem hanc descripsit. Æschines: ἐκ τῶν κατὰ Τιμάρχου. ἀναγνώσεται οὖν ὑμῖν τοὺς νόμους τοὺς [?] τῆς ἐκκλησίας [?] χειροτονίας [?] τῶν ῥητόρων. NOMOI ΤΩΝ ΡΗΤΟΡΩΝ, ΕΑΝ ΤΙΣ ΛΕΓΗι ΕΝ ΒΟΥΛΗι Η ΕΝ ΔΗΜΩι, &c. Observandum autem est, vbi nos scripsimus: KAI EAN KATAGNOSOHi AYTOY KPYBDHN YHΦIZONTΩN TΩN BOYΛEYTΩN legi, ΥΗΦΙΖΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΩΝ ΒΟΥΛΕΥΤΩΝ. Sed reponendum est, ΚΡΥΒΔΗΝ ΥΗΦΙΖΟΝΤΩΝ ΕΝ. (id est πέντε ἢ πεντήκοντα) ΤΩΝ ΒΟΥΛΕΥΤΩΝ. clam suffragia ferentibus quinquaginta quinque Senatoribus, vbi numerum definit, quot minimum clam suffragia ferre debebant Senatores, nempe quinquaginta quinque: At in concionibus numerus non definitur eorum, qui suffragia clam ferre debent, sed permittitur vniuscuiusque, qui concioni interest, arbitrio, vnde passim legas, ὑηφισαμένων μὴ ἐλάττων ἐξακισχιλίων, οἷς ἂν δόξῃ, χρύσεον ὑηφιζομένοις.
units.tr: Aeschines cites this law from his speech against Timarchus: "Therefore I will read to you the laws concerning the election of orators by the assembly. LAWS CONCERNING ORATORS: If anyone speaks in the Council or in the Assembly, etc." It must be noted that where we have written, "and if he is condemned, when the councillors vote in secret," the text reads "when the councillors vote in secret." But it should be restored as "when five or fifty of the councillors vote in secret," that is, secretly voting fifty-five senators, which fixes the minimum number of senators who had to vote in secret, namely fifty-five. In the assemblies, however, the number of those who had to vote in secret was not fixed. It was left to the discretion of each person attending the assembly, whence you read everywhere that not fewer than six thousand voted, as they wished, voting in secret.

units.la: DE MVNERIBVS ET HONORIBVS.
units.tr: ON PUBLIC SERVICES AND OFFICES.

units.la: TITVLVS QVARTVS.
units.tr: TITLE FOUR.

units.la: NON ignoro τοὺς [?] λειτουργοῦντας [?] Magistratibus non posse accenseri, si rem ad viuum reseces, quin tamen aliquam ἐχχῆς [?] speciem prae se ferant, non sinit nos dubitare Demosthenes in Midiana, nam de numero τῶν ἰδιωτῶν [?] eximit, vt adscribat iis, qui in aliqua dignitate sunt positi, eos namque his designat verbis: εἰς δὲ ἡ πόλις ὑπὸ ἀλλήλων, ὃ ἀποφυγοφείειν [?], ἢ τινά [?] τιμῶν δέ. optime Vlpianus ad hunc locum: ἐχρῆ γὰρ [?] ὁ Χορηγὸς ἀδύνατον [?] ἀφιέναι τῆς χρατείας [?] τὸν χορὸν, ἢ εἰσάγειν, ὅτι βλάπτει. Excusabant Choragi a militia eos, qui sibi in pompa ministrabant & saltabant, vt suo loco, Deo dante, dicemus, ἢ εἰσάγειν, ὅτι βλάπτει, quibus verbis, vt puto, significat Vlpianus, Choragum habuisse, si liberet, [illegible, ~12 letters], si qua inter Chori, quem dabat, saltatores lis oriretur. Munera autem ista altero quoque anno obibant, ex hac Lege:
units.tr: I am aware that those who performed the public liturgies (λειτουργοῦντες) cannot be counted among the magistrates, if the matter is cut down to the quick. Yet they still show some outward likeness of office. Demosthenes in the Midianea leaves no room for doubt on this point. He removes them from the number of private citizens and assigns them to those who hold some dignity, for he marks them out in these words: "but the city, from one another, [...] or some honours." The best commentary on this passage is Ulpian: the choragus had to excuse the chorus from military service, or from bringing it on stage, because it was harmful. Choragi excused from military service those who attended them in the procession and danced, as we shall say in its place, God willing. By these words, as I think, Ulpian means that the choragus had [illegible] if any dispute arose among the dancers of the chorus he provided. These public services they also performed every other year, by this law:

units.la: Ἐπιαυτὸν διαλιπόντα ἕκαστον λειτουργεῖν. Altero quoque anno munera obeunto.
units.tr: "Performing the services at intervals of a year." Performing public services every other year.

units.la: Huius Legis meminit Demosthenes in Leptinea: ἐκ τῶν νῦν ἀρχόντων νόμων ἐκ παλαιῶν χειρῶν, οὓς οὐδεὶς αὐτὸς ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἐπὶ μὴ ἡ χειρὶ καλῶς ἔχειν, ἐπιαυτὸν διαλιπόντα ἕκαστον λειτουργεῖν. Quanquam multi volentes singulis quibusque annis munia ista publica adibant: constat vel exemplo illius, cui scripsit Lysias [Greek title, illegible, ~8 letters] in ea enim ista leguntur: quae, quanuis plusc ula sint, adscribemus. ἐγὼ γὰρ ἰδιχιμάσθαι μὲν ὅτι Θεοπόμπου Ἀρχοντος, κατὰ δὲ Χορηγὸς Τεχνωδῆς, ἀναλῶσαι τεσσαράκοντα μνᾶς. ἡ τέτρα μὲν Θαργηλίοις νικήσας αὐδρίχῳ χορῷ, διαλίας δραχμάς· ὅτι ὁ Γλαυκίππου Ἀρχοντος, εἰς Πυρρίχισας Πανα-θηναίοις τῆς μεγάλης ὀκταχοσίας. ἐπὶ δὲ αἰδρῶν χορηγῶν εἰς Διονύσια ὅτι τῷ αὐτῷ Ἀρχοντος, σίκησε, καὶ ἀνάλωσε σὺν τῇ τῶν πεποδὸς ἀναλίσκῃ πεντακισχιλίας δραχμάς· καὶ ὅτι Διοκλέους Πανα-θηναίοις τοῖς μικροῖς κυκλικῷ χορῷ τεσσάρων. τὸν δὲ μεταξὺ χρόνον ἐτειμησάμην ἑαυτὸν ἐτῶν, καὶ ἐξ Ἀλαντα ἀνήλωσα, ὅμως εἰσφορὰν, τῷ μὲν, τεσσαράκοντα μνᾶς, τῷ δὲ πεντακισχιλίας δραχμάς, εἰσιτωσα. ὅτι δ' ὁ κατὰ πλοῦτος ὅτι Ἀλεξίου Ἀρχοντος, ἀὐτὸς ἐγυμνασιάρχων εἰς Πεγαμῆα, ἓ σίκων, ἀναλώσας δώδεκα μνᾶς. ἡ ὕστερον κατὰ τὴν Χορηγὸς παιδικῷ χορῷ, καὶ ἀνήλωσα πλέον ἢ πεντακισχιλίας μνᾶς. ὅτι ὁ Εὐχλείδου Ἀρχοντος Κωμωδὸς χορηγῶν Κηφισοδότῳ, σίκων, καὶ ἀνήλωσα σὺν τῇ τῆς σκηνῆς ἀλαῖσι ἐκχρήσεως μνᾶς. καὶ Πανα-θηναίοις τῆς μικρῆς ἐχορήγησεν Πυρρίχισας ἀγωνίοις, καὶ ἀνήλωσα ἑαυτὸν μνᾶς. νενίκηκα ὁ τέτρᾳ μὲν ἀ-μιλλώμενος ὅτι Σοωνίῳ, ἀναλώσας πεντεκαίδεκα μνᾶς. καὶ τούτων ἂν κατέλιξα, εἰ ἐβουλόμην κατὰ τὰ γεγραμμένα ἐν τῷ νόμῳ λειτουργεῖν, ὁ[?] δὲ ἀ ὃ τέταρτον μέρος ἀνήλωσα. Habes in his nobile exemplum hominis singulis paene annis semel atque iterum munera ista obeuntis, quod facilius constabit appositis Fastis Archontum Athenien-sium.
units.tr: Demosthenes recalls this law in the Leptinea: "from the laws of the present magistrates, from the old ones, which no one has ever been able to fulfil properly from the beginning, [the law of] performing services at intervals of a year." Yet many who were willing undertook these public duties every single year. This is clear from the example of the man for whom Lysias wrote his speech. In it the following is read, which I shall set down even though it is rather long. "For I was enrolled, when Theopompus was archon, as a choragus for the tragic contest, and I spent forty minas. In the Thargelia, I won with a men's chorus, spending two thousand drachmas. In the archonship of Glaucippus, I was choragus for the Pyrrhic dance at the Greater Panathenaea, at a cost of eight hundred. Then for the men's choruses at the Dionysia, in the same archon's year, I won, and spent five thousand drachmas, together with the cost of the ... ; and in the archonship of Diocles, for the cyclic chorus at the Lesser Panathenaea, I spent four. In the meantime I was assessed for [...] and I spent a talent, and I paid the levy, forty minas to one and five thousand drachmas to another. And in the archonship of Alexias, I was gymnasiarch for the Peganea, and I spent twelve minas. Later, I was choragus for the boys' chorus, and spent more than five thousand minas. In the archonship of Euclides, as comic choragus, I equipped Cephisodotus, and spent, together with the hire of the stage properties, [...] minas. And at the Lesser Panathenaea I provided the Pyrrhic dancers, and spent [...] minas. I won the contest against Sosias with a pyrrhic [...] and spent fifteen minas. And I would have enrolled all these, if I had wished to perform services according to what is written in the law, but I spent a fourth part [more]." In these words you have a notable example of a man who undertook these services nearly every year, once or even twice, a fact that will be clearer from the list of Athenian archons set out below.

units.la: OLYMPIAS XCII.
units.tr: OLYMPIAD 92.

units.la: ANNI OLYMP. | ARCHONTES. II. | THEOPOMPVS. Is, cui Orationem hanc scripsit Lysias, tutela exit in viros transcriptus. Anthesteriis Choragus fit, itémq; Thargeliis. III. | GLAVCIPPVS. Choragus est Panathenæis Maioribus, & Dionysiis τοῖς κατ' ἄγρ. itémque Trierarchus. IV. | DIOCLES. Choragus Panathenæis Minoribus.
units.tr: Year of the Olympiad | Archons. II. | THEOPOMPUS. This is the man for whom Lysias wrote the speech. He was released from guardianship and enrolled among the men. He became choragus at the Anthesteria, and likewise at the Thargelia. III. | GLAUCIPPUS. He was choragus at the Greater Panathenaea, and at the Dionysia [...], and likewise trierarch. IV. | DIOCLES. Choragus at the Lesser Panathenaea.

units.la: In annum secundum Olympiadis nonagesimæ quintæ coniicimus Præturam Euclidis, non autem in secundum Olympiadis nonagesimæ quartæ, tum auctore Eusebio in Latino B. Hieronymi Chronico, tum quia è Legibus constat Euclidem Ἄρχοντα ᾑρέθη μετ' ὀλίγον χρόνον τὴν Τελευτὴν [?]. Neque potest eius Magistratus adscribi anno tertio Olympiadis nonagesimæ quintæ, quod à nobis olim factum est, sed fallebamur: Nam Euclide Archonte Panathenæa minora celebrata sunt, vt ex his Lysiæ liquet: Ergo Euclides Archon non fuit anno tertio Olympiadis nonagesimæ quintæ: Anno quippe tertio Olympiadis Panathenæa Maiora celebrabantur, non autem Minora. Itaque apud Suidam referibendum est, Τοῖς δὲ Βαβυλωνίοις ἐδίδαξε ἐπὶ Καλλιστράτου Ἀ-θηναίους ἐπὶ τῆς Εὐχαρίδου καὶ. ἐν ᾧ δὲ Εὐχαρίδου. & apud Apollonium eodem exemplo. Sed ad Lysiam, siue potius eum, cui Lysias Orationem scripsit, redeamus: ἐγὼ δέ, inquit, ἐδιδάχθην μὲν ὅτι Θεοπόμπου Ἄρχοντος [?], id est, in viros transcriptus sum Theopompo Archonte, anno scilicet secundo Olympiadis nonagesimæ secundæ. Addit deinde eo anno Choragum fuisse, itémque anno sequenti, qui Prætorem habuit Glaucippum, nec non etiam, Prætore Diocle, qui signauit Faštos anni quarti Olympiadis nonagesimæ secundæ: ὅτι Διοκλέους Γλαυκίππου ... τὴν Τειναρχίαν [?]. Quodnam sit intermedium tempus, quod inter Prætuam Theopompi & Dioclis intercessit, facile quiuis videt, scilicet Prætuam Glaucippi: Eo igitur anno Trierarchus fuit: atqui dixit, τῶν δ' μεταξὺ χρόνον ἐπειναφέρχων ἐπὶ ἑτῶν, ἡ ἐξ Ταλάντα ἀπὸλωσα [?] quasi armorum spatio septem ad Dioclis vsque Prætuam Trierarchus fuerit, quod omnino verum non est: Nam ante Theopompum Archontem Trierarchus esse non potuit, vt qui nondum sui esset iuris, Theopompo demum Archonte tutela exiit, & in viros transcriptus publica obire cepit munia, & anno sequenti, Glaucippo Prætore Trierarchus triremem instruxit suo sumptu, quem fecit in hanc rem talentorum septem, maiorem certe, quam sex talentorum. Atque hoc est, quod dixit Orator, sed eius verba in mendo cubant: nos mendo liberamus & rescribimus: τὸν δ' μεταξὺ χρόνον ἐπειναφέρχων, ἐπὶ ἑτῶν, ἐπὶ ἢ τὴν ἐξ Ταλάντα ἀπώλωσα. Sed hæc obiter. Altero, vt iam diximus, quoque anno Athenienses ex Lege publica obibant munera, quare alia pacis sunt τείς εἰρήνης, alia belli, τείς πολέμου, vt ἰωquitur Vlpianus ad Leptineam: Pacis quidem hæc sunt, Χορηγία, Ἐσθαρμ, ἡ Γυμναστραρχία. Belli vero, Εἰσφο-ρά, ἡ Τειναρχία.
units.tr: We assign the archonship of Euclides to the second year of the ninety-fifth Olympiad, not to the second year of the ninety-fourth. We do so both on the authority of Eusebius in the Latin Chronicle of St Jerome, and because it is clear from the Laws that Euclides was chosen archon shortly before the [...] . Nor can his magistracy be assigned to the third year of the ninety-fifth Olympiad, as we once did, but we were mistaken. For in the archonship of Euclides the Lesser Panathenaea were celebrated, as is clear from these words of Lysias. Therefore Euclides was not archon in the third year of the ninety-fifth Olympiad, since in the third year of the Olympiad the Greater Panathenaea were celebrated, not the Lesser. Hence the passage in Suidas must be corrected: "to the Babylonians he taught in the archonship of Callistratus, the Athenians in the archonship of Eucharides", and in the case of Eucharides. The same correction applies to Apollonius in the same example. But let us return to Lysias, or rather to the man for whom Lysias wrote the speech. "I," he says, "was enrolled when Theopompus was archon," that is, I was released from guardianship and enrolled among the men in the archonship of Theopompus, in the second year, that is, of the ninety-second Olympiad. He then adds that he was choragus in that year, and likewise in the following year, when Glaucippus was the presiding magistrate, and also when Diocles was the presiding magistrate, who marked the Fasti of the fourth year of the ninety-second Olympiad: "for in the archonships of Diocles and Glaucippus ... the trierarchy." It is easy for anyone to see what intervening time lay between the archonship of Theopompus and that of Diocles, namely the archonship of Glaucippus. So in that year he was trierarch. Yet he said, "in the intervening time, for some years, I spent a talent," as if he had been trierarch for about seven years up to the archonship of Diocles. This is by no means true. For he could not have been trierarch before the archon Theopompus, since he was not yet his own master. Only under Theopompus did he leave guardianship, become enrolled among the men, and begin to perform public services. Then in the following year, under Glaucippus as presiding magistrate, he equipped a trireme at his own expense, spending seven talents on it, certainly more than six talents. This is what the orator meant, but his words lie in a corrupt state. We free them from the corruption and restore them as follows: "in the intervening time, for some years, I spent a talent." But this is a digression. As we have already said, in the other year too the Athenians undertook public services by public law. Hence some are for peace, others for war. As Ulpian says on the Leptinea: the peacetime services are the choregia, the gymnasiarchy, and the [...]; the wartime services are the levy and the trierarchy.

units.la: Choragus est, qui sumptus præbebat ad Ludos, τὴν ἐλ̓ν, id est, choragium, quo instruebatur Theatrum & Chorus. Vlpianus ad Leptineam: Χορηγὸς, ὁ τῆς Διονυσίοις ἐν τῆς Γμαλιλιώταις τοῦ Χορῷ ἐφ' ὧ πρέσχων, καὶ στέφανος, ἢ κόσμον, ἢ ὅσα αὐτὶ τῆς Διονυσίῳ πωλήνυειν. Sed longe fallitur Grammaticus, si his tantum Ludis constitutos fuisse Choragos putat: nam fuerunt & aliis, vt ex iis, quæ iam ante è Lysia descripsimus, liquet. Hos Choragos designabant & constituebant vnaquæque Tribus suos: Libanius in Argumento Midianæ: Καθίσασθαι ὑπὸ τῆς Χορηγικῆς φυλῆς, Χορηγὸς ὁ ὧ ἐκάστης φυλῆς τὰ αἰαλωμάτα πρέχων τὰ αὐτὶ τῆς Χορῷ. Anonymus in Argumento eiusdem: ἐκείνη ἐπὶ τῆς Χορηγὸς ἐφ' ἑκάστης φυλῆς ἐπὶ ὃ πέφυκεν Χορῷ παίδων τε ἢ αὐλῷ. Choragi constituti sortiebantur pro concione tibicines, præsidente Archonte, ex hac Lege:
units.tr: A choragus was the man who provided the money for the games, the choregia, by which the theatre and the chorus were equipped. Ulpian on the Leptinea: a choragus is the man who at the Dionysia, in the contest of the choruses, undertakes the expense of the chorus, and the garland or adornment, or whatever else is spent on the Dionysia. But the grammarian is greatly mistaken if he thinks that choragi were appointed only for these games. There were others as well, as is clear from what we have already quoted from Lysias. Each tribe appointed and designated its own choragi. Libanius in the Argument to the Midianea: "the tribe of each choragus was seated by the choragic tribe, the choragus being the man who furnished the expenses of the chorus for each tribe." The anonymous author in the Argument to the same speech: "then the choragus for each tribe for the chorus of boys or of the flute, as the case required." The appointed choragi drew lots in the assembly for the flute-players, with the archon presiding, by this law:

units.la: Ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ τὴν Ἀρχοντα ἐπικληρῶν τὰς Χορὸς τοὺς Αὐλητάς.
units.tr: In the assembly, the Archon allots the flute-players to the choregi by lot [Ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ τὴν Ἀρχοντα ἐπικληρῶν τὰς Χορὸς τοὺς Αὐλητάς].

units.la: Choragus pro sortis ordine tibicinem eligebat, quem vellet maxime. Legem laudat Demosthenes in Midiana: Προύσης ὁ τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ὅτι ἢ Ἀρχοντα ἐπικληρῶν ὁ νόμος τὰς Χορῆς τοὺς Αὐλητὰς κελεύει, προελθὼν ἐπὶ ἐμὲ ἐγὼ χορηγὸν ἐπελαστής. ἡ κληρουμένων, ὧσπερ αἰρέσεως ἡ Αὐλητῶν ἔλαχον. Sortiebantur igitur Choragi, præsidente Archonte, atque is cui prima fors obtigerat, primus eligebat tibicinem, quem vellet, cui secunda fors obuenerat, secundus eligebat, atque ita deinceps pro fortis ordine. Fiebat autem ista fortitio mense integro, antequam darentur Ludi, in quos instruebantur Chori. Anonymus in Argumento Midianæ: ἐΐρος ὁ ὧ ἐπὶ μέγιστος ἡ ἑορτῆς ἡ Ἀρχοντα σὺν ἀἡ τοῖς Χορηγὸς ἐκάστης φυλῆς εἰς ὃ ἀγῶνα ἐπὶ τὴν αὐλητήν. Ita etiam apud Archontem Choragi solebant δωρεὰς χορῶν Poetis: eratque Archontis videre, vt id fieret recte, & ad celebrandos maiori cum voluptate atque dignitate Ludos: qua de re insignis est Hesychij locus, qui corrupte legitur in hæc verba. πυρ ἀφέλης. Κεφαλὴς ἀπὸ Διυρεμένου ἐν Βουκόλοις ἀρξάμενος, ὅτε χορὸν οὐκ ἔλαβεν, ἐπὶ τὴ Ἀρχοντος ἐστὶν ὃ πτήρξ. Non ignoro Virum Incomparabilem in Animaduersionibus ad Athenæum locum hunc attigisse: & optime quidem ille obseruauit Cratinum in Prologo Bubulcorum grauiter coquestum fuisse de Choragi cuiusdam consumelia, qui alij nescio cui Comico potius quàm ipsi Chorum dederat, quo referenda sunt ea, quæ ex hac Comœdia leguntur apud Athenæum Lib.XIV. Ος οὐχ ἑδωκ' αἰτωῦτ' Σοφοκλεῖ χορὸν, Τῷ Κλεομάχῳ δ' ἢ οὐχ αὐ ἠξίουν ἐγώ Ἐμοὶ διδάσκειν οὐδ' αὖ εἰς Ἀδωνια.
units.tr: Each choregus, in the order of the lot, chose whichever flute-player he most wanted. Demosthenes cites the law in the Midiana: "Proceeding to me, the Archon's assistant said that the law orders the Archon to allot the flute-players to the choregi by lot, and I, as choregus, came forward and took the first lot, and drew the flute-players" [Προύσης ὁ τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ὅτι ἢ Ἀρχοντα ἐπικληρῶν ὁ νόμος τὰς Χορῆς τοὺς Αὐλητὰς κελεύει, προελθὼν ἐπὶ ἐμὲ ἐγὼ χορηγὸν ἐπελαστής. ἡ κληρουμένων, ὧσπερ αἰρέσεως ἡ Αὐλητῶν ἔλαχον]. The choregi were therefore chosen by lot, with the Archon presiding, and the one who drew first place chose first the flute-player he wanted, the one with the second lot chose second, and so on in the order of the lots. This drawing was made a whole month before the Games were given, for which the choruses were trained. The Anonymus, in the Argument to the Midiana, says: the festival's great contest, at which the Archon together with the choregi of each tribe chose the flute-players for the contest. So too the choregi used to give the choruses to the poets at the Archon's office; and it was the Archon's business to see that this was done properly and that the Games were celebrated with greater pleasure and dignity. A notable passage of Hesychius concerns this, which is read corruptly in these words: "Fire, you have taken away. Cephalus, beginning from Diyremenus in the Bucolics, when he did not get a chorus, is for the Archon's [office]." I am aware that the incomparable man in his Animadversions on Athenaeus touched on this passage, and he rightly observed that Cratinus in the Prologue to the Bubulcorum complained bitterly about the insult of a certain choregus, who had given the chorus to some other comic poet rather than to Cratinus himself. To this belong the lines of this comedy read in Athenaeus, Book XIV: "He who did not give me a chorus, but gave it to Sophocles, and to Cleomachus, and would not allow me to produce, nor again to Adonis."

units.la: Sed emendationem verborum Hesychij, quam adfert Vir incomparabilis, probare non possumus: Ea hæc est: πῦρ, πῦρ, εἶχά. Κεφαλὴς ἀπὸ Διυρεμένου ἀρξάμενος, ὅτε χορὸν οὐκ ἔλαβε, πρὸς Ἀρχοντος, πρ' ἡ πτήνης. Mitto, quod nimium recedit ab edita Hesychij lectione; satis namq; est ad improbandam eius coniecturam, quod hic confundat Archontem cum Choragō, quasi scilicet, qui eo anno Archon fuit, fuerit quoq; Choragus. Atqui Archontes suæ anno Præturæ excusationem habebant horum munerum. Referibo igitur: πῦρ πρὸς ὧ, χεῖ. Κεφαλὴς ἀπὸ Διυρεμένου ἐν Βυκόλοις ἀρξάμενος, ὅτε χορὸν οὐκ ἔλαβεν, ἐπὶ τὴ Ἀρχοντος ἐστὶν, ἢ ἢ τυρξ. De Archonte ista dicuntur, quem comparat cū reprobo nummo, cui impressa littera X oftendit mittendum esse in ignem & cōflandum: Quanquam enim Archon non daret Chorū, vt qui Choragus non esset, tamen cum Choragi eo præsidente darent, partes illius erant obseruare, vt meliores quique Poetæ coëmerētur, quo Ludi magnificentius instaurarentur.
units.tr: But I cannot approve the emendation of Hesychius's words that the incomparable man offers. It reads: "Fire, fire, alas. Cephalus, beginning from Diyremenus, when he did not get a chorus, [went] to the Archon, for the [office]." I pass over the fact that it departs too far from the printed reading of Hesychius; it is enough to refute the conjecture that it confuses the Archon with the choregus, as if the man who was Archon that year had also been choregus. Yet the Archons, during their year of office, had an exemption from these duties. I therefore write: "Fire, to him, alas. Cephalus, beginning from Diyremenus in the Bucolics, when he did not get a chorus, is for the Archon's [office], or for the [...]." This is said of the Archon, whom he compares with a worthless coin marked with the letter X, which shows that it must be sent into the fire and melted down. For although the Archon did not give the chorus, since he was not the choregus, nevertheless, when the choregi gave them under his presidency, it was his part to see that the best poets were secured, so that the Games might be celebrated more splendidly.

units.la: Lege autem erat cautum, ne quis peregrinus in Choro saltaret: si Choragus in hanc Legem commisisset, multabatur drachmis mille.
units.tr: By law it was forbidden for any foreigner to dance in the chorus; if a choregus broke this law, he was fined a thousand drachmas.

units.la: Μὴ χορεύειν ξένον, ἢ χιλίας ἀποτίνειν τὸν Χορηγόν.
units.tr: "A foreigner may not dance in the chorus, or the choregus shall pay a thousand [drachmas]" [Μὴ χορεύειν ξένον, ἢ χιλίας ἀποτίνειν τὸν Χορηγόν].

units.la: Hospes in Choro ne saltato, si secus fecerit, Choragus mille drachmis multator.
units.tr: "Let no guest dance in the chorus; if he does otherwise, the choregus shall be fined a thousand drachmas."

units.la: Plutarchus in Phocione Legis meminit: νόμου γὰρ ὄντος Ἀθήνησι τότε, μὴ χορεύειν ξένον, ἢ χιλίας ἀποτίνειν τὸν Χορηγὸν, ἀπάγειν εἰσαγαγὼν ξένους τοῖς χοροῦσι, ἕκαστον ὀρχεῖσθαι, ἅμα καὶ τῇ ζημίᾳ αὐτὰ χιλίας ἐκάστῳ, εἰσῆγεν εἰς τὸ θέατρον. Meminit quoque Demosthenes in Midiana: καὶ μὲν δὴ ταῦτα, ὅτι βαλλόμενοι μηδένα ἀγωνίζεσθαι ξένον. Vlpianus: δύο γάρ εἰσι νόμοι, ἀλλ' οὐχ ὁμοίως ἐμφέρονται· μὴ ἐξεῖναι ξένον ἀγωνίζεσθαι. Idque religiose obseruatum est Dionysiis τοῖς κατ' ἄστυ, at non item Lenæis τοῖς κατ' ἀγροὺς, quibus non tantum peregrini poterant in Choro saltare, sed etiam inquilini ipsi erant Choragi & præbitores. Interpres Comici ad Plutum. οὐκ ἐξέλῳ δὲ ξένον χορεύειν ἐν τῷ Ἀσχῷ Χορῷ. ἐν δὲ τῷ Λιναίῳ ἐξέλῳ, ἐπεὶ ἡ Μέτοικοι ἐχρήσαντο.
units.tr: Plutarch, in the Life of Phocion, mentions the law: "For there was then at Athens a law that a foreigner must not dance in the chorus, or the choregus must pay a thousand [drachmas]; when the choregus brought in foreigners to dance with the choruses, each of them was introduced into the theatre, and along with the penalty, a thousand [drachmas] for each." Demosthenes also mentions it in the Midiana: "And these things, since it was forbidden for any foreigner to contend." Ulpian: "For there are two laws, but they are not worded alike: that a foreigner may not contend." This was strictly observed at the City Dionysia, but not at the Lenaea in the country, where not only foreigners could dance in the chorus, but resident aliens themselves were choregi and providers. The scholiast of the comic poet on the Plutus: "I do not allow a foreigner to dance in the chorus at the Ascian [festival], but at the Linaean I allow it, since the resident aliens used it."

units.la: Quinetiam antequam Ludi peragerentur licebat Lege peregrinum in ius vocare apud Prætorem, ne saltaret.
units.tr: Moreover, before the Games were held, the law allowed a foreigner to be summoned to court before the Praetor, so that he might not dance.

units.la: Ξένον οὐκ ἔτι εἰσιέναι εἰς τὸ θέατρον ἐξεῖναι παρεσκευάσατο ἐπὶ τῇ Ἀρχοντι.
units.tr: "The law has provided that a foreigner may not enter the theatre, before the Archon."

units.la: Peregrinum, antequam Ludis ipsis saltet, in ius apud Archontem vocare fas esto.
units.tr: A foreigner may be summoned before the Archon to court before he dances in the Games themselves; let this be lawful.

units.la: Laudat Legem hanc Vlpianus in Midianam. λέγει γὰρ τὸν ἐπιεικῆ νόμον τὸν χαλεπὸν, ξένον μὴ ἀγωνίζεσθαι, καὶ εὐρήσεις ἢ εἶπεν. ἡ γὰρ ἀπείρητο πωλεῖσθαι. ἀλλὰ εἰσιέναι ἀπαξ εἰς τὸ θέατρον, οὐκ ἐπὶ ἐχθρῷ παρεσκευάσατο. ἐγὼ ἢ ἐξέλῳ. Rursum: ἡ γὰρ ἐξέλῳ ἀλλως τὸν ξένον ἐξάγειν, ἀλλὰ παρεσκευάσασθαι τῷ ἀρχῷ. Andocides: ὁ τῆς Ἀλκιβιάδου χαλεπὸν ἢ τὸ νόμου, τὴν χορεύσεως ἐξάγειν ὅτι ἀδικῶς βουλήσεται ξένον ἀγωνίζομαι, οὐκ ἐξὸν ἐπιχωρῆσαι χωλύειν.
units.tr: Ulpian cites this law in the Midiana. "For he says that the severe law forbids a foreigner to contend, and you will find what he said: for it was forbidden to sell [him]. But to enter the theatre once was not forbidden him, but was prepared for an enemy. I am not able [to say]." Again: "For it is not forbidden otherwise to lead the foreigner out, but it has been prepared for the magistrate." Andocides: "The harsh law of Alcibiades, to lead out of the dance one who unjustly wishes to contend as a foreigner, is not permitted, [and it is] forbidden to let it go."

units.la: Quod si quis Choragus, cum dabantur Ludi, peregrinum saltantem in Choro raperet in ius ad Archontem, multabatur quinquaginta drachmis, mille vero, si è scena exturbaret, & suo moueret loco.
units.tr: But if any choregus, when the Games were given, dragged a foreigner who was dancing in the chorus before the Archon in court, he was fined fifty drachmas; but if he threw him out from the stage and moved him from his place, a thousand.

units.la: Αν τις Χορηγὸς ἀγωνιζόμενον τὸν ξένον καλέσῃ μὲν πρὸς τὸν Ἄρχοντα, πεντή-κοντα δραχμὰς· ἐὰν δ' ἡ κατάξεσθαι χαλεπὸν, χιλίας ἀποτίνειν.
units.tr: "If any choregus summons a foreigner who is contending before the Archon, [he pays] fifty drachmas; but if he should drag him down, he shall pay a thousand."

units.la: Siquis Choragus saltantem in Choro hospitem rapiat in ius ad Archontem, drachmis quinquaginta: si suo moueat loco, mille drachmis multator.
units.tr: If any choregus drags a guest who is dancing in the chorus before the Archon in court, he is fined fifty drachmas; if he moves him from his place, he is fined a thousand drachmas.

units.la: Legem laudat Demosthenes in Midiana: ἡ μὲν γὰρ ἰσότης τῷ τοῦτο, ὅτι βαλλόμενοι μηδένα ἀγωνίζεσθαι ξένον, οὐκ ἐδώκατε ἁπλῶς τὸ Χορηγῶν οὐδὲν, ἀλλ' ἐὰν μὲν καλέσῃ, πεντήκοντα δραχμὰς· ἐὰν δ' ἡ κατάξεσθαι χαλεπὸν, χιλίας ἀποτίνειν ἐπέξατε. πῶς ἔνεκα; ὅπως μὲν τ' εἰς Φασωμένον, ἡ ἀληθεύουσι τὰ ποῖ ἡμέρας, καλῇ, μηδ' ἐπιπρεάζῃ, μηδ' ὑβρίζῃ μηδὲ ἐξεπίπτῃς. εἶτα τ' μὲν χορευτῶν ἀδ' ἀρτεσοκαλέσας χ' τ' νόμον ἀζήμιος ἔσται. Vlpianus: ἡ ἐπιεικὴς νόμος, αὖ τις Χορηγὸς ἀγωνιζόμενον τὸν ξένον καλέσῃ πρὸς Ἄρχοντα, ὅπως πᾶς, δοκιμάσοντα εἰ ξένος ἔστιν, ἐκβαλεῖν, ἀλλὰ δραχμὰς πεντήκοντα. ἐὰν δὲ καλέσῃ αὐτὸν ἀπολάβοντα εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καλέσαι ὡς ξένον, χιλίας ἀποδοῦναι. Rursum ibidem ad hæc verba: οὐκ ἐδώκατε ἁπλῶς. [ἔξεστι μὲν γὰρ, ἀλλ' ὡς ἔτυχεν, οὐδὲ πωλεῖσθαι, οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ θεάτρῳ ἔξω. Καλέσαι καλέσαι.] οἱ βιαίως ἀποπαίστι μὲν ἀπὸ τῆς χοροῦ. Χωρὶς ἢ καὶ μὴ τῷ ἄλλων καλέσαι ἀμαρτήσῃ. οἱ μὲν νόμοι ἡ δοκιμάζεσθαι μόνον τὸν ξένον ὅτως σκώλυσθαι.
units.tr: Demosthenes cites the law in the Midiana: "For the equality of it is this: since it was forbidden for any foreigner to contend, you did not simply give the choregus nothing, but if he summons him, fifty drachmas; but if he should drag him down, you imposed a fine of a thousand. For what reason? So that the choregus might not call him to Phasomenus, or treat him wrongly, or insult him, or cast him out. Then, if he should summon him [on] the wrong day, he shall be free from penalty by the law." Ulpian: "The equitable law: if any choregus summons a foreigner who is contending before the Archon, so that he may be examined whether he is a foreigner, he is to be cast out, but [only] for fifty drachmas. But if he summons him after he has been received into the crowd, [and] summons him as a foreigner, he is to pay a thousand." Again in the same place, on these words, "you did not simply give": [It is permitted, but as it happened, not even to be sold, nor in the theatre outside.] Those who violently drag him away from the chorus. Otherwise, if he should err by summoning [him] for others, the laws only permit the foreigner to be examined, and so to be restrained.

units.la: Nolebat enim quicquam inauspicati fieri in diebus illis festis. Vlpianus: ἐθέλει γὰρ ὁ δῆμος μηδένα γίνεσθαι ἐφορῶν [?] κατὰ τὴν ἑορτήν [?]. Ἐπὶ τῶν γὰρ καὶ ἀποδει-ρόμος τῆς ἡγωνίζετο, οὐ συνεχώρησεν αὐτὸν ἀξιωθῆναι, ἀλλὰ τότε μὲν ἀγωνίζεσθαι· μὴ ὥσπερ ἢ κεῖνεσθαι παρασιτεῖν [?]. Ludis igitur peractis, iudicia reddebantur, & Choragus, qui peregrinos in Choro saltantes induxerat, multabatur mille drachmis, vt iam ante diximus: an vero peregrinus ipse, qui saltauerat, multaretur, nondum legi.
units.tr: For the people wished that nothing inauspicious should happen in those festival days. Ulpian: "For the people wishes that no one should become [...] during the festival [...]. For in the case of one who was contending in the prize-contest, he did not permit him to be taken away, but then to contend, not as one who had been led away." Therefore, when the Games were over, judgments were given; and the choregus who had brought foreigners dancing in the chorus was fined a thousand drachmas, as we said before. But whether the foreigner himself who had danced was fined, I have not yet read.

units.la: Ignominia quoque notatis non licebat in Choro saltare, si secus facerent, licebat eos de scena deturbare, & loco mouere, ex hac Lege:
units.tr: Men marked with infamy were also not allowed to dance in the chorus; if they did otherwise, they could be thrust from the stage and moved from their place, by this law:

units.la: Ἐξέραι τοὺς ἀτίμους ἀγωνιζομένους Ἐπαλαμ-βάνεσθαι τῆς χορείας, καὶ ἐξάγειν ἐκ τῆς ἡμ-ῶν [?].
units.tr: "To cast out the infamous who contend, to be taken from the dance, and to lead them out of our [...]" [Ἐξέραι τοὺς ἀτίμους ἀγωνιζομένους Ἐπαλαμ-βάνεσθαι τῆς χορείας, καὶ ἐξάγειν ἐκ τῆς ἡμ-ῶν].

units.la: Ignominiosos in Choro saltantes de scena deturbare, fas esto.
units.tr: It is lawful to cast down from the stage those of infamous condition who dance in the chorus.

units.la: Legis meminit Demosthenes in Midiana, de Aristide ignominioso, qui in Choro saltauerat, loquens: ἐπὶ μὲν τῶν ἐξαγαγῶν, οὐδὲ καλῶς· ἡ δὲ ἀτιμωθέντα τῇ χορείᾳ πόλει ἡ τῶν πολιτῶν, καὶ μὴ προσκαλέσαθαι τοὺς τὸν Ἄρχοντα ἐξαγαγεῖν, ὥσπερ ἂν εἰ ξένον τις ἐξαγαγεῖν ἠβούλετο. Vlpianus: ἐκέλευε γὰρ νόμος, τοὺς ξένους προσκαλεῖν τοῖς τὸν Ἄρχοντα. Τοὺς δ᾽ ἀτίμους ἀτιμωθέντας τῆς χορείας, ἐξάγειν ἐκ τῆς ψυχῆς [?]. Atque ex his vides, quantum abfuerint à Romanis hac in parte. Athenienses, qui nonnisi è ciuibus Chorum constare volebant: at vero Romani habuere sibi priuatim Choros è seruis coæuis, qui cantare & saltare nouerant: vnde apud Celsum Lib. IX. Digestorum, Si Chorus aut familia legetur, perinde est, quasi singuli homines legati sint. Leg. LXXIX. D. de Legatis III. cuius Legis sensum optime assecutus est praestantissimus Iurisconsultorum Tractatu VI. ad Africanum, puta vt intelligatur, vno homine mortuo, non extinguil [?] legatum, sicut quadriga legata, vno equo mortuo non perit legatum, nisi vt ait Lex, Peculium §. Quadriga D. de Legatis II. is mortuus sit, qui demonstrabat quadrigam, id est, vt Graeci exponunt, ὁ κολλυνῶν ἐπ᾽ ἀξίας [?]. Sed Papiniani verba è Lib. XV. Quaestionum paucis illustrari, & si forte emendari debent: Quadriga legatum, equo postea mortuo, perire quidam ita credunt, si equus ille decessit, qui demonstrabat quadrigam: sed si medio tempore deminuta supplea-tur, ad legatarium pertinebit. Leg. LXV. §. I. D. de Legatis II. Tota Quadriga vnius Equi nomine designabatur, atque is sinister funalis est viro illi summo, quo maiorem nulla aetas vidit, nulla videt: is Equus, à quo Quadrigae nomen, intelligitur à Papiniano his verbis, qui demonstrabat quadrigam: Nam haec demonstratio est, Νίκωνος τεχνήματος, ὁ λεγατάριος [?], vt loquitur Theophilus, quadriga quae sit designat, QVADRIGA BVBALI. exempli gratia, is enim Bubalus equus est, cuius meminit Vetus Inscriptio: Iam vero si Bubalus decessit, verum est perire quadriga legatum, nam quadriga Bubali nusquam amplius est, cum Bubalus, à quo quadrigae nomen, quique demonstrabat quadrigam, decesserit: Addit: sed si medio tempore deminuta supplea-tur, ad legatarium pertinebit, quae verba, meo iudicio non sunt referenda ad equum illum, qui demonstrabat quadrigam, & cuius esse quadriga illa dicebatur: suppleri enim non poterat, qui periit, ita vt idem sit, qui prius quadrigam demonstrabat. Sed iugales equi intelliguntur, à quibus quadrigae nomen non est, quique quadrigam non demonstrant: soli enim funales equi, siue is sinister sit, siue dexter, quadrigam demonstrant, & alterius eorum quadriga esse dicitur: Referibendum igitur esse suspicor in verbis Papiniani: Sed si media tempore deminuta suppleantur, ad legatarium non pertinebit. Iugales equos intelligit, qui duo fuere in medio inter utrumque funalem. Scholia Comici: ζύγιοι ἵπποι κάμνοντες [?], οἱ ἐπὶ τοῦ ἁρμάτος ζυγῷ [?], ὁ μέσος δεξιὸς, καὶ ὁ μέσος ἀριστερός. Media appellat, quæ tempore intercedente deminuta suppleantur, equos iugales, qui in medio inter utrumque funalem, quique cum decessissent, supplentur. Atque de his satis est: Choragi enim Atheniensium velut ἐν χρείας νόμῳ [?] nos retrahunt.
units.tr: Demosthenes, in the Midiana, mentions this law in speaking of Aristides, who was infamous and had danced in the chorus: "Not in the case of those who were led out, nor rightly; but when a citizen, dishonoured by the chorus, is [not] called before the Archon to be led out, just as if someone wished to lead out a foreigner." Ulpian: "For the law ordered that foreigners be summoned before the Archon. But those dishonoured from the chorus, [the infamous], are to be led out from the soul [...]." And from these you see how far the Athenians, who wished the chorus to consist only of citizens, differed from the Romans in this part. But the Romans kept choruses privately for themselves, from home-born slaves who knew how to sing and dance; whence in Celsus, Book IX of the Digest: If a chorus or a household is bequeathed, it is just as if single men had been bequeathed. Law 79, D. de Legatis III, whose meaning the most excellent of jurists understood well in Tractate VI on Africanus: namely, that when one man dies, the legacy is not extinguished, just as a legacy of a team of four horses is not lost when one horse dies, unless, as the law says, Peculium §. Quadriga, D. de Legatis II, the one who designated the team has died, that is, as the Greeks explain, the one who [designates] the value. But the words of Papinian from Book XV of the Questions should be briefly illustrated, and emended if they perhaps need it: Some think that a legacy of a team of four, if after the horse is dead it perishes, if that horse which designated the team has died; but if in the meantime what is diminished is made up, it will pertain to the legatee. Law 65, §1, D. de Legatis II. The whole team was designated by the name of one horse, and that is the sinister funalis of that great man, of whom no greater age has seen or sees. That horse, from which the team takes its name, is understood by Papinian in these words, which designated the team: for this designation is, as Theophilus says, of Nicon's art, the legatee, which designates what team it is, THE TEAM OF BUBALUS, for example; for Bubalus is a horse, of which an old inscription speaks. Now if Bubalus has died, it is true that the legacy of the team perishes, for the team of Bubalus is nowhere any more, since Bubalus, from whom the team has its name, and who designated the team, has died. He adds: but if in the meantime what is diminished is made up, it will pertain to the legatee; in my judgment these words are not to be referred to that horse which designated the team, and whose the team was said to be: for he who perished could not be replaced, so that it would be the same one who first designated the team. But the yoked horses are meant, from which the team does not take its name, and which do not designate the team: for only the trace horses, whether that one be the left or the right, designate the team, and the team is said to be of one of them. I therefore suspect that in Papinian's words it should read: But if in the meantime what is diminished is made up, it will not pertain to the legatee. He means the yoked horses, which were two in the middle between the two trace horses. Scholia of the comic poet: the yoke horses which labour, those on the yoke of the chariot, the middle right and the middle left. He calls the middle horses, those which in the meantime are diminished and made up, the yoked horses, which are in the middle between the two trace horses, and which, when they have died, are replaced. Enough of these matters: for the choregi of the Athenians, as if by the law of necessity, draw us back.

units.la: Non tantum ciues præbebant hos sumptus τῆς χορηγίας, sed etiam inquilini, vt ex Alexandro docet Vlpianus ad Leptineam: Ἀλέξανδρος λέγει ἐξηγούμενος Φησίν, ὅτι ἐὰν πολυπραγμονεῖσθαι τῆς πόλεως, μήτε τοὺς ξένους, μήτε τοὺς μετοίκους παρέχοντας τῷ δημοσίῳ [?] ἀπολαύσεων καὶ ἐκ [?] ἐχρήσαντο ἐγχρήσαν [?] τοῖσι καὶ αὐτοὶ διαλυθῆναι, καὶ εἰσίωσαν ἀλλήλοις, ἵνα μηδεὶς ἀμελεῖ [?] ἢ τῷ πόλιν μετοίκιας τῆς ἑορτῆς. Verùm id fiebat tantum Lenæis Liberalibus. Scholia Comici ad Plutum: οὐκ ἔξεστιν ὁ ξένος χορηγὸν ἐν τῷ ἀσιχῷ χορῷ [?]. Ταῦτα τὸν πίπαιχεν, ὁ ὁ τῆς Αλωαίῳ ἐξελῶ, ἐπὶ καὶ μέτοικοι ἐχρήσαντο [?].
units.tr: Not only citizens bore these expenses of the choregia [τῆς χορηγίας], but also resident aliens, as Ulpian teaches from Alexander in his commentary on Leptinea. Alexander says, in explaining, that if strangers and metics did not contribute to the public expenses of the city, they were to be made to share in the festival and to feast together with the citizens, so that no one neglected the festival because of the cost. But this happened only at the Lenaean and Liberal festivals. The scholiast on Plutus says: a foreigner may not be choragus in the (...) chorus. These things were done by the metics as well.

units.la: Ἑστιάτωρ est, qui viscerationem atque epulum suæ præbebat Tribui. Vlpianus: Ἑστιάτωρ, ὁ τῇ Φυλῇ εἰς δεῖπνον κοινὸν. Meminit Pollux, & notat Harpocration, fuisse forte captos alios, alios etiam volentes: εἰσίων τὰς φυλὰς, οἱ μὲν ἱκανοί, οἱ δὲ ἑλκωτοί. Idque Lege institutum: id enim sonant hæc Athenæi verba Libro V. Τῶ δὲ νῦν δεῖπνον παρασκευάζοντες οἱ νομοθέται πάντα φυλεικὰ δεῖπνα, καὶ τὰ δημόσια παρασκευάζοντες. Habuerunt quoque inquilini suos Ἑστιατορας, vt constat è laudatis iam ante Vlpiani verbis: ἐχρήσαντο τῷ ὑμῶν καὶ Μέτοικοι καὶ ξένοι, καὶ εἰσίωσαν ἀλλήλοις. Quanquam & Choragi suam excipiebant Tribum conuiuio. Demosthenes in Midiana: εἰσήνεγκε τῇ φυλῇ ἐγὼ, καὶ Πρωταγόρας χορηγήσας. Vlpianus: ἀναλισκῶς δὲ τὸν Χορηγὸν τῇ φυλῇ εἰσιῶντος, ὁ Δημοσθένης διελῶν εἶπεν.
units.tr: A hestiator [Ἑστιάτωρ] was one who provided a banquet and feast for his tribe. Ulpian: a hestiator is one who provides a common dinner for the tribe [ἑστιάτωρ, ὁ τῇ φυλῇ εἰς δεῖπνον κοινόν]. Pollux mentions the office, and Harpocration notes that some tribes were given hestiators by lot, others were volunteers: some were chosen, others were willing. This was instituted by law; for these are the words of Athenaeus in Book V: the lawgivers arranged all the tribal dinners, and also the public ones. The metics and foreigners also had their own hestiators, as is clear from the words of Ulpian already quoted: the metics and foreigners also had their feasts, and they dined with one another. Yet the choragi also entertained their tribe at a banquet. Demosthenes in the Midiana: I brought the tribe to dinner, and Protagoras, when he was choragus. Ulpian: when the choragus was entertaining the tribe, Demosthenes said, having made a distinction.

units.la: Γυμνασίαρχος est, qui athletis oleum præbebat. Vlpianus: Γυμνασίαρχος, ὁ πρέγων τοὺς λαμπάδας τοῖς γυμνασιοδιδάσκαλοις. Γυμνάσιον γὰρ τὸν παλαιστῶν ἐκάλεσαν, καὶ κεραμέας ἐπὶ τὰ ἀθλητικὰ [?] τῆς βυλευομένης δημοσίας χρείας. Hi constituebantur à quaque Tribu. Anonymus in Argumento Midianæ: ἐν Γαναιωτοῖς γυμνασίοις ἐκληροῦντο [?], καὶ τοῦ ὑπολαβὼν ἀφ᾿ ἑκάστης φυλῆς εἰς Γυμνασίαρχος. Atque hæc quidem sunt munera & honores pacis τῶν Ἐιρήνης λειτουργία. Sequuntur ea quæ sunt τῶν πολέμων λειτουργία.
units.tr: A gymnasiarch [Γυμνασίαρχος] was one who supplied oil to the athletes. Ulpian: a gymnasiarch is the one who provides the torches for the gymnastic teachers. For they called the wrestling-ground a gymnasium, and the (...) of the public need decided the athletic contests. These were appointed from each tribe. The anonymous writer on the argument of the Midiana says: in the Gymnasia they were chosen by lot, and each tribe received a gymnasiarch. These are the duties and honours of peace [τῶν Εἰρήνης λειτουργία]. There follow those of war [τῶν πολέμων λειτουργία].

units.la: Ac primum quidem occurrit Εἰσφορά. Εἰσφέρειν εἰς πόλεμον est conferre stipem ad numeranda stipendia iis, qui pro patria in acie stant. Vlpianus: εἰσφέρειν εἰς πόλεμον, ὅταν ἔχωσιν ἀληθῶς τοῖς ὑπὸ τῆς πατρίδος ἀποπληρωθῶσιν. Præscribebatur autem τῷ εἰσφορᾷ, quantum conferre deberet: colligo ex his Anonymi ad Aphthonium verbis: Εἰσφορὰ δὲ ἐξ ὑπάρχης ἐπέγνω, καὶ εἰς πόλεμον.
units.tr: First comes the eisphora [Εἰσφορά]. To contribute to war [εἰσφέρειν εἰς πόλεμον] means to bring money together to pay the wages of those who stand in battle for their country. Ulpian: to contribute to war is when they truly must meet the needs laid on them by the fatherland. The amount each person had to contribute was fixed in advance; I infer this from the words of the anonymous commentator on Aphthonius: the eisphora was assessed according to means, and it was for war.

units.la: Trierarchus est,qui nauem bellicam præbet, armamentáque naualia, & eius generis alia. Vlpianus: Τριήραρχός ἐστιν ὁ ναῦν πρεχόμενος πολεμικὸν, καὶ σκευὴν τῆς νηὸς, καὶ ὅσα διαιρῶνται. Suidas: Τριηραρχία, λειτουργία τῶν Ἀθηναίοις δαπανωμένη· ἐξ ἡ γὰρ τῶν τριηρῶν πόλεως ἔχει εἰς πόλεμον διαπέμπει, ἀφ᾿ ἧς προεισφέρειν ὁ εἰς τὴν λειτουργίαν τούτων βαλλήσεις. Huic obeundo muneri adsignati sunt ditissimi quique, vt è Demosthene docent Grammatici: ἐχ ἀπὸ τῶ πλῆθος, ὥσπερ πρὸς ἡμῶν διήρητο εἰς τὰς συμμορίας Ἀθηναῖοι, ἀλλὰ μόνοι οἱ πλούσιοι καὶ εἰσφέρειν τὴν πόλιν δυναμένοι. Atque olim Ναυκαρίαι dicebantur, erantque vniuscuiusq; Tribus Ναυκαρίαι duodecim, & singulae Ναυκαρίαι nauem vnam instruebant. Pollux Libro VIII. Ναυκαρία δ' ὧν τίως φυλῆς δυοκαιδέκα μέρος, καὶ δυοῖδες Ναυκαρίαι ἦσαν, ὑπάρχουσι τῷ πεντήκοντα ἐκάστην ναῦν μίαν, ἀφ' ἧς ἔτος οὐκ ἀπεμέρισαν. Factum aliquando, vt vniuscuiusq; classis essent viri sedeni, docent Grammatici ex Hyperide, sed locus est corruptus, vulgo editur: Υπερίδης δ' ἐν τῷ κατὰ Πολυεύκτου φησὶν. εἰσὶ γὰρ ἐν τῇ Συμμορίᾳ ἑκάστῃ πεντακόσιοι ἄνδρες. Rescribo, ἑκατόν πεντακόσια. Emendationis fundus est Legislator ille quisquis est, qui tot, sedecim nimirum, iusserat τεσσαρακοντάκις. Auctus est tandem numerus: Nam Tribus vnaquaeque praebebat centum viginti viros: itaque, cum decem essent Tribus, vniuersae praebebant mille & ducentos viros: Hi centum viginti viri vniuscuiusque Tribus in duas distribuebantur συμμορίας, singulae συμμορίαι erant virorum sexaginta. Grammatici: ὁ γὰρ Δημοσθένης ἐν τῇ συμμορίων φησί, ὅτι τῶν χιλίων καὶ διακοσίων ἀνδρῶν λέγων τὴν πλουσιωτέρων, ἐκ τούτων εἴκοσι οἱμαι δὲ τῶν πεντήκοντα συμμορίας ὥσπερ εἶναι ναῦς εἰσὶ σωματα ἐξήκοντα ἐκατὸν ἔχουσιν. Demosthenis verba mendosa ita emendanda sunt: ἐκ τούτων εἴκοσι οἱμαι δὲ τῶν πεντήκοντα συμμορίας εἶκοσι, ὥσπερ τῶν εἰσι, σώματα ἐξήκοντα ἐκατὸν ἔχουσιν. Harum classium censusest à Naufinico Archonte, cuius Praetura incidit in annum tertium Olympiadis centesimae. Grammatici è Philochoro: ληρέ Σωσάν δὲ Ἀθηναῖοι καὶ συμμορίας ὅτι Ναυσινίκου Ἀρχοντος, ὡς φησὶ Φιλόχορος ἐν τῇ πέμπτῃ Ἀτθίδι. Eadem habet Anonymus in Descriptione Olympiadum ad hunc annum. In has classes distribuebantur inter adscitos ciues, qui opibus possent plurimum. Grammatici ex Hyperide: ὅτι δὲ καὶ οἱ δημοπόπται συνεχάφοντα εἰς τὰς συμμορίας διελάχιστον ὁ Υπερίδης ἐν τῷ καὶ Πολυεύκτου πολλάκις. Postea, auctore Demosthene, quinque classes eligebantur, quibus trecentorum ditissimorum numerus constaret, qui quotannis munera obirent. Grammatici ex Hyperide: ὅτι δὲ τῶν καταλόγῳ Δημοσθένης νόμους ἐξήκοντα τοῖς τεσσαράκοντα τελεσφόροις. Vlpianus ad Olynthiacam II. δίκας ὑσῶν φυλῶν ἐπὶ Ἀθηναίοις, ἡ εἰς δίκαια ὥσπερ μεμεσυμένης τῆς πόλεως, ἀνάγκῳ εἶχεν ὥσπερ ἑκάστῃ φυλῇ ἀπὸ πάσης ἀσβάλλεσθαι τοῖς πλουσιωτέροις αὐτῆς, ἑκατὸν εἶκοσι ἄνδρας τοῖς ἀλπυργιῶν ὑπ' αὐτῆς τῇ πόλει. Etiam oi ἑκατὸν εἶκοσι ὄντες, ἐμερίζοντο ἑαυτοὺς εἰς δύο μερίδας, ἵνα ἐξήκοντα αὐτῷ ἀνδρες ἔσωσαν οἱ πάνυ πλούσιοι. Oi δὲ ἄνδρες ἐξήκοντα ἦσαν πλούσιοι. Επειοιῶ ἢ τῶν, ἵνα μὴ ἐάω ἐξαίφνης πόλεμος αὐτοῖς ἐπιπέσῃ, καὶ τύχῃ πρὸς τὸ παγὸν μὴ ἔχειν χρήματα τοῖς ἦσαν πλουσίοις. εἰσφέρεσθαι γὰρ οἱ πλουσιώτεροι ὑπ' αὐτῆς, καὶ παρετέλεσαν, καὶ ἰδίᾳ ἐχοῦσι ὑπηρέσαι χρὴ ἀπολιμάνου. ἐλέγετο δὲ τὸ σύνημα αὐτῆς τῆν ἐξήκοντα, συμμυσεία. Δίκας σὺν ὧν ὧν φυλῶν, καὶ ἑκάστης παρέδωκαν ἀπὸ ἑκατὸν εἶκοσι, σὺν ἐπὶ τῆς πόλεως τῇ ἀλπυργιῶν χιλίους διακοσίους. ἐμίει ἔ οὖν αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ ἐξακοσίων αἰσθεῖν. ὅστε ἀπὸ δίκα συμμυσείων. πάλιν ἢ ἑκατέρᾳ τῶν δύο μερίδων τῶν ἐπιμένει εἰς δύο, ὅ ἐστιν εἰς τεσσαρακοσίους μὴ αὐτάρας, καὶ πᾶσα δὲ συμμορίας. ἔπει δὲ ἤσαν οἱ τεσσαράκοντα, οἱ πάνυ πλούσιοι οἱ πρῶτοι, οἵτινες παρεσφέρειν τὴν ἄλλων τι ἡ εἶχον αὐτοῖς ἐναχωρεῖσθαι εἰς πόλεως, ὥστε συμβαίνειν εἰς δύο μερίδας τοῖς πόλεως. εἴγε οἱ τῶν ἑκατέρων ἦσαν ὥσπερ ἰωμένοι τοῖς ἑκατέρων τεσσαράκοντα, τοῖς πλουσιωτέροις. εἶχεν ἢ ἑκάστη μέρις τῶν πασαρῶν, καὶ ἰδίᾳ Σπαρτηλᾶν, ἡ ἰδίᾳ Ῥήτορα. ὅμως δὲ πάλιν τὴν δευτέραν οἱ Ῥήτορες ἢ οἱ Σπαρτηλαὶ ἐπιλήσονται τοῖς τεσσαράκοντα. Anonymus in Argumento Orationis εἰς Φαίνιππον. ὧ συνταγμα πρὸς τοὺς Ἀθηναίους τειχο- κοπῶν αἰσθῶν χρὴ τὸν πλοῦτον ἐξελεγμένων, οἷς ἀνέκειντο τὴν λειτουργιῶν οἱ μείζονες. Ratio autem Trierarchiarum subinde mutauit, vt constat ex Vlpiano ad haec Midianae verba: ἐπειπεφράχειν ... [?] ὅτι σύνδυο ἦσαν οἱ τειχ- ἐφρῳ. Narrat enim aliquando duos fuisse, qui nauem instruerent, aliquando tres, aliquando decem, etiam mille, si DIs placet, fuisse quoque Demosthene Legem rogante, triremium duarum vnum Trierarchum: πολλαὶ πρὸς τὰς τειχοποιίας ἐγίγνοντο μεταβολαὶ, ἀλλ' ὁ μέγεθος τῶ ἀπαλώμεθος. καὶ ὅτε, καὶ, σύνδυο ἦσαν· ὅτε δὲ, σύντρεῖς· καὶ ὅτε δὲ καὶ δέκα Τειχοποιῷ, ὅτι δὲ, χίλιοι. ὁ γὰρ Δημοσθένης ὑπὲρ δύοιν τειχῶν εἶα Τειχοποιῷ ἐποίησε. Valde corruptus est hic locus: & primum quidem exterminandum est portentum illud lectionis, ὅτι δὲ χίλιοι. Quis enim ferat mille fuisse in vna instruenda naue, cum omnium συμμοριῶν hic fuerit numerus cum ducentis? Sed irrepserat haec lectio è sequentibus Demosthenis verbis, quae non ex fide, sed Rhetorice dicuntur. Sequitur, καὶ ὅτι δὲ καὶ δέκα Τειχοποιῷ. Referibo, καὶ ὅτε δ' ἐκκλίδεκα. De his Demosthenes εἰς τοῦ ἄλλοι γράφων. ὦ γὰρ αὐτοῖς, ἐκ μὲν τῶν πρῶτερων νόμων, σύνεκ καὶ δέκα ληρωγίῶν, αὐτοῖς μὲν μικρὰ καὶ Θεῖον ἀναλίσκοισι· τοῖς δ' ἄποροις τῶν πολιτῶν ὑπαιτεῖβοιεν. Melius idem Vlpianus ad eandem Midianam paulò post, vbi expendit haec Oratoris verba de Midia: τωνικαῦτα δὲ τὸ προσχρήματος ἥπαλον, ὅτε ἀφ' ἡμῶν μὲν ... δ' ἀγρίοις καὶ χιλίοις πεποίηκεν σύντελες ὑμεῖς, πρὸ ὧν εἰς προ-ηγ-πόλμοι πάλαι οὐκ ἐχοντο ... μαθόντες τοῖς τειχοποιίας ἔστι. Ad haec, inquam, Vlpianus: ἔστι ὁ σοφισμα ὁ ῥήτωρ. Φησι γὰρ ὅτι αὐτὸς δὲ τῶν χιλίων καὶ ἀλγυσίων εἰς προ-πόλμος ἑαυτοῦ, ἐπὶ πόλις μαθόντες τῷ τειχοποιίας, ὡς μιᾶς τειχήρεις ἀπὸ τῶν Σούντων γιγνωσκόμενοι. ἔστι δὲ ἀληθές. χίλιοι γὰρ καὶ ἀλγυσίοι ποιοῦσι τὰς τειχοποιίας ἀφωρισμένοι. Τούτων δὲ λοιπὸν, ἐν σύν- ἐκκλίδεκα, ἐν τῷ τειχη ἐπληρώσω, ἐν συντρεῖς, ἐν ὅσοι δὲ ποτε. καταλιπῶν οὖν ὁ λέγων ὅτι ναῶν ἐκκλίδεκας πρὸς, πολλαὶ τοῦ ὅτι τειχοποιίας ἀφωρισμένους ὠνόμασαν, ὡς πάντων μίαν πρηγοντων. Sed ista paullo accuratius expendamus. Distributi sunt Athenienses primum in Συμμορίας, Nausinico Athenis Praetore, vt scribit Philochorus Libro V. Ἀπίδες. Grammatici: ὁμολογοῦσι δὲ Ἀθηναῖοι καὶ Συμμορίας ὅτι Ναυσινίκου Ἀρχοντος, ὡς φησι Φιλόχορος ἐν τῇ πέμπτῃ Ἀπίδες. Nausi- nici Praetura incidit in annum tertium Olympiadis centesimae. Quot verò capitum fuerit tunc Συμμορία, quot item tunc fuerint Συμμορίαι, dicere non possumus, qui diuini non sumus. Cephisodoro Athenis Archonte, id est, anno tertio Olympiadis centesimae tertiae, aut saltem anno quarto eiusdem Olympiadis, Chione Athenis Praetore, Demosthenes Trierarchus fuit, tuncque duo vnam instruebant nauem: Demosthenes in Midiana: καλῶ μὲν κατ' ἐκείνους τοὺς χρόνους ἐπειπεφράχειν, ἀλλὰ ὁ ἂν παῖδων ἐξελθὼν, ὅτι σύνδυο ἦσαν οἱ τειχοποιοί. Demosthenes in viros transcriptus est, Cephisodoro Archonte, anno tertio Olympiadis centesimae tertiae. Quare circa illa tempora duo vnam instruebant nauem, σύνδυο ἦσαν οἱ Τειχοποιοί. Orationem in Midiam scripsit Demosthenes annos natus triginta duos, testis ipse eadem Oratione, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, γιγνώσκετε πεντήκοντα ἴσως, ἐν μικρὸν ἐλάττω, ὅσον ἐμοὶ πλείους λειτουργίας ὑμῖν λελειτούργηκαν, ὃς δύο καὶ τεσσαράκοντα ἔτη γέγονα. Annos natus est triginta duos, Diotimo Archonte; anno tertio Olympiadis centesimae
units.tr: A trierarch [Τριήραρχος] is one who provides a warship and its rigging, and the other things of that kind. Ulpian: a trierarch is one who supplies a warship and its equipment and whatever else is needed. Suidas: trierarchia was a public duty performed by the Athenians; for the one who held it provided and sent out the triremes for war, and from it he advanced the expense of this service. To undertake this office the wealthiest men were assigned, as the grammarians show from Demosthenes: not from the whole populace, as the Athenians had been divided into symmoriae by us, but only the rich, who were able to bear the cost for the city. And formerly they were called naucariae [Ναυκαρίαι], and each tribe had twelve naucariae, and each naucaria equipped one ship. Pollux in Book VIII: a naucaria was the twelfth part of a tribe, and there were twelve naucariae, and each one provided one ship with fifty men, from which they did not divide the year. It once happened that each class had sixty men, as the grammarians report from Hyperides, but the passage is corrupt, and the printed text reads: Hyperides, in his speech against Polyeuctus, says: for in each symmoria there are five hundred men. I would correct it to one hundred and five hundred. The source of the emendation is that legislator, whoever he was, who had ordered so many, namely sixteen, (...). The number was finally increased, for each tribe furnished one hundred and twenty men, so that, since there were ten tribes, all together they furnished twelve hundred men. These one hundred and twenty men of each tribe were divided into two symmoriae, and each symmoria had sixty men. The grammarians: for Demosthenes, in his speech on the symmoriae, says that of the twelve hundred men, the richer ones, from these twenty, I think, ... (corrupt) ... sixty men each. The mangled words of Demosthenes should be emended thus: from these twenty, I think, of the fifty symmoriae, twenty, as there are, have sixty men each. The census of these classes was made under the archon Nausinicus, whose praetorship fell in the third year of the hundred-and-first... (Olympiad). The grammarians, from Philochorus: the Athenians also agree that the symmoriae were established in the archonship of Nausinicus, as Philochorus says in the fifth book of the Atthis. The anonymous author of the Description of the Olympiads has the same for this year. Into these classes were distributed the adopted citizens who were most able by their wealth. The grammarians from Hyperides: that the demopoietae also were distributed into the symmoriae, Hyperides shows often in his speech against Polyeuctus. Afterwards, on the authority of Demosthenes, five classes were chosen, which together made up the number of the three hundred richest, who each year discharged these duties. The grammarians from Hyperides: that Demosthenes ... (corrupt). Ulpian on the second Olynthiac: the tribes were then taxed by the city for its needs, and each tribe had to furnish from its richest members one hundred and twenty men for the city. ... (The text here is too corrupt to render with confidence.) These sixty men were called symmoriae. Again each of the two parts was divided into two, that is into forty, and each symmoria had... The forty very rich men, the first, who advanced for the others whatever they had, to be paid back to the city, so that the people were divided into two parts... Each part had its own (...) and its own orator. Anonymous in the argument of the oration against Phaenippus: the (...) of those who were chosen by the wealth were to bear the greater share of the public duties. The method of the trierarchies, however, changed from time to time, as is clear from Ulpian on these words of the Midiana: ... that they were in pairs. For he reports that at one time there were two who equipped a ship, at another three, at another ten, and even, God willing, a thousand; and that Demosthenes, proposing a law, made one trierarch for two triremes. Many changes were made in the trierarchic arrangement, but the sum of it was ... and at times they were in pairs; at other times in threes; and at other times ten trierarchs, and at other times a thousand. For Demosthenes, on behalf of two ships, made one trierarch. The text here is very corrupt, and first of all that monstrous reading "a thousand" must be removed. For who could bear that there were a thousand men in equipping a single ship, when the total number of all the symmoriae was about two hundred? But this reading had crept in from the following words of Demosthenes, which are spoken not by fact but rhetorically. There follows: and at other times ten trierarchs. I would write: and at other times fifteen. Demosthenes, writing against the others, says of this: for under the earlier laws, with the ten liturgies, they spent little and modest sums, while they demanded (...) from the poorer citizens. Ulpian, on the same Midiana a little later, better weighs these words of the orator about Midias: ... Ulpian says: the orator is making a sophistical point. For he says that he himself, of the thousand and the others, ... had made the trierarchies, as though they were the fleet of Suns... But this is true, for a thousand and some others were appointed to equip the triremes. Of these there were fifteen, in others three, in others as many as... So the speaker, saying that the ships were equipped by fifteen men, many times called them the ... of the triremes, as though they had sole charge.

units.la: [?] Greek readings throughout this page are uncertain; the scan is blurred and the Greek has not been checked letter by letter. sextæ: intra hoc interuallum, quod est ab anno quarto Olympiadis centesimæ tertiæ, ὅτι Ζωίδυο ἤσαν οἱ Τεισαρχαι, ad annum tertium Olympiadis centesimæ sextæ, sepositi sunt ad obeundum Trierarchiæ munus mille ducentis ditioribus, horum meminit Philochorus Libro VI. Ἀτθίδος. Grammatici: οἱ πλουσιώτατοι Ἀθηναίων χίλιοι καὶ Ἀξιόχοι ἦσαν, οἳ καὶ ἐλλιπέρρων, μνημονεύει [?] σι δ' αὐτῷ καὶ ἀπὸ Ρήτορες, καὶ Φιλόχορος ἐν τῇ ἕκτῃ. & tunc primum Trierarchus factus est Midias, vt ipsi exprobrat Demosthenes: κἀγὼ μὲν κατ' ἐκείνους τοὺς χρόνους ἐπεπληρῶκειν, δίχως ἐκ παίδων ὄξελθων, ὅτι Ζωίδυο ἦσαν οἱ Τεισαρχαι. ἔστι δὲ ὅτε μὲν τῷ Ζωΐδυο τῷ ἀλιαΐ[?] ἀλλ' ἐγὼ ναῦν, οὐδὲν ποτε λάμπρυνεῖν ἡρ[?]χατο. τὴν ... καὶ τὴν παράσημον ἡσάν, ὅτε ... μὲν Ἀξιόχους καὶ χιλίους πεπλη[?]κεῖ[?] σὺν τῷ ἡμῖς. Mille hi ducenti distributi sunt in viginti Συμμορίας. Vnaquæque Συμμορία erat capitum sexaginta; ex his sexaginta Trierarchi vnam nauem instruebant sedeni suo anno. Atque ita conciliandus est Demosthenes cum Hyperide: nam τῇ Συμμορίᾳ capita adscribit Demosthenes sexaginta, ἐ quibus capiebantur οἱ λιπαρρυσώτες Sedeni: Trierarchorum vero vnam instruentium nauem Συμμορία erat sedecim capitum, atque ita intelligendus est Hyperides ἐν τῇ πρὸς Πολύκλειτον. Εἰσὶ γὰρ ἐν τῇ Συμμορίᾳ ἐκάστῃ πεντηκοντάδικα Ἀνδρες. Sed referendum in superioribus diximus ἐκκαιδικα ἀνδρες. Restituendus quoque eiusdem Hyperidis ἐν τῷ πρὸς Γαστρίλλους locus, qui ita legitur apud Grammaticos: ἕως μὲν οἱ πλουσιώτατοι ἀπέχρηνται τῷ πόλιν σὺν πέντε καὶ ἐξ τεσσαρακοστῶν μέτρια αἰλίσκον, ἡσύχιος ἦν ὅτι. ἐπεὶ δὲ τῶν κατὰ τὰ Δημοσθένης, νόμοις ἔθηκε τοῖς πελαχοσίοις τεσσαρακοστῶν, καὶ βασιλεῖ χαλκὸν ἐν Τεισαρχίᾳ, νῦν ὁ Φορμίων αὐτὸν ἐκκλείσθη. Restituendus, inquam, est ad hunc modum: ἕως μὲν οἱ πλουσιώτατοι ἀπέχρηνται τῷ πόλιν σύμπαντες, καὶ ἡ ἐξ (id est, ἐκκαιδεκα) τεσσαρακοστῶν μέτρια αἰλίσκον. Sed iuuat adhuc pressius inuestigare tempus, quo nondum mille ducenti sepositi erant ad obeundum Trierarchiæ munus; Quando Apollodorus, cui Orationem aduersus Polyclem scripsit Demosthenes, Trierarchus fuit, duo tantum vnam instruebant nauem. Habes hac ipsa Oratione: οὐ δὲ ἀπολαμβάνω τὸν ναῦν, ὥσπερ μὲν τὸν ἐν τῷ σταδίῳ χρόνον τεσσαρακοστὸν τοῖς ἐξ μιλίας. Rursus: Ἀλλὰ καὶ ποιήσειν Εὐεπίδη σύντεσσαρα ἀνέ, καὶ σὺν σὺν τοῖς ἡμῖν [?] ἐξ μιλίας ἐκάστῳ σιλεῖν. Apollodorus autem Trierarchus fuit, eo anno, quo Alexander Pheræorum Tyrannus Tenum vnam è Cycladibus Insulis diripuit, vastauitque. Demosthenes hac ipsa Oratione: ἐληφίσασθε τοῖς ναῦς καθελκεῖν τοῖς Τεισαρχαις· ὧν καὶ ἐγὼ ἐλ, καὶ τὸν μὲν χρόνον τὸν συμβεβηκότα τῇ πόλει ποτέ, ὅτε ἐμοὶ δεῖ διεξελθεῖν, ἀλλ' αὐτοὺς ὑμᾶς αἰσθάνεσθαι, ὅτι Τῶος μὲν καταλελειφθαι Ἀλεξάνδρῳ ἀξιωσαμεῖ. Tenus vna est Cycladum Insularum. Stephanus: Τῶος, ἤσος Κυκλάς. Tenum expugnauit Alexander, Archonte Nicophemo, si Diodorus Siculus Libro XV. audiendus est, ἐπάρχοντος δὲ Αθηναίοις Νικοφήμου, Ἀλέξανδρος μὲν ὁ Φεραῖων τύραννος, ληφθὶ[?]δας ταῖς ἐκπεμφας ὅτι ταῖς Κυκλάδας νήσους, ὧν μὲν ἐκπολιορκήσας, inter has, vt ex his Demosthenis constat, Tenum, πολλὰν ξυμ[?] ἐκυεί[?]σον. Sed Demosthenes testis est ista accidisse, Molone Archonte: præcedit enim, ἐξέλμη γὰρ Φίλιππος Μεγαχίτιος μῖλος, ὅτι Μίλωνος Ἀρχοντος, ὀκκλησίας ἡμέρῳ, καὶ εἰσαγελ[?]όντων ὑμῖν πολ-
units.tr: Greek readings throughout this page are uncertain; the scan is blurred and the Greek has not been checked letter by letter. Within this interval, from the fourth year of the hundred and third Olympiad, when the Trierarchs were two to a ship [ὅτι Ζωίδυο ἤσαν οἱ Τεισαρχαι], down to the third year of the hundred and sixth Olympiad, one thousand two hundred of the wealthier citizens were set apart to undertake the office of trierarch. Philochorus mentions them in Book 6 of the Atthis. The grammarian says: "The richest Athenians were a thousand and two hundred, and they were also called ... ; Philochorus in the sixth book also mentions them." It was then, for the first time, that Midias became a trierarch, as Demosthenes reproaches him: "And I, in those times, had already fulfilled [the duty], having come out of childhood, when the trierarchs were two to a ship..." Sometimes, with Zoidyo ..., but I [did not?] ... a ship, he never began to ... and the ... and the figurehead; when ... he had fulfilled [the duty] with the Axiochi and the thousand, together with us. These one thousand two hundred were distributed into twenty Symmoriae. Each Symmoria consisted of sixty persons, and from these sixty, the trierarchs equipped one ship each year. And so Demosthenes is to be reconciled with Hyperides: for Demosthenes assigns sixty persons to a Symmoria, from which the richest sedeni were drawn, whereas the Symmoria of those who equipped one ship had sixteen persons. Hyperides in his speech against Polycles should be understood in this way. For in each Symmoria there were fifty men. But we said above that it should be read as sixteen men. The passage of the same Hyperides in his speech against the Gastrilli also needs restoring, which is read thus among the grammarians: "As long as the richest men were sufficient for the city with all forty-six minae..., it was quiet; but when, in Demosthenes' time, he made laws for the nine hundred forties, and the king's bronze in the trierarchy, now Phormio ..." It must be restored, I say, in this way: "As long as the richest men were sufficient for the city as a whole, and the sixteen [i.e. sixteen] ... forties..." But it is still helpful to investigate more closely the time when the one thousand two hundred had not yet been set apart for the trierarchy. When Apollodorus, against whom Demosthenes wrote his speech against Polycles, was trierarch, only two equipped one ship. You have this in that same speech: "But I take back the ship, as in the stadium, the time of forty ... to the six miles." Again: "But also to make Euepides ... and with us ... six miles to each to sail." Apollodorus was trierarch in the year when Alexander, tyrant of Pherae, plundered and laid waste Tenos, one of the Cycladic islands. Demosthenes in the same speech: "You have voted that the trierarchs should launch the ships, and I too ... and the time that befell the city, when I must go through, but you yourselves perceive that ... you were willing to leave Tenos to Alexander." Tenos is one of the Cycladic islands. Stephanus: "Tenos, an island of the Cyclades." Alexander captured Tenum under the archon Nicophemus, if Diodorus Siculus in Book 15 is to be heard: "While Nicophemus was archon at Athens, Alexander, tyrant of Pherae, sent out ships against the Cyclades, and besieging some of them, among them, as is clear from Demosthenes, Tenum, ..." But Demosthenes is witness that these things happened under the archon Molon: he goes on, "For Philip ... Megachites of Melos was made ... in the time of Molon the archon, on the day of assembly, when many great matters were brought before you..."

units.la: λῶν λαὶ καὶ μεγάλων πραγμάτων, ἐπηφίσατο [?] τὰς ναῦς, & cetera quæ iam descripsimus. Molonis Prætura incidit in annum tertium Olympiadis centesimæ quartæ, vt liquet è Diodoro & Anonymo in Descriptione Olympiadum: Anno quarto Olympiadis centesimæ quartæ, Nicophemo Athenis Prætore, Polycles & Euripides σωτεῖναρχοι fuerunt, quando adhuc σῶσδυο ἦσαν οἱ Τριηράρχοι. Quare nonnisi post annum quartum Olympiadis centesimæ quartæ, & ante annum tertium Olympiadis centesimæ sextæ, Diotimo Archonte, institutum est, vt mille ducenti è ditioribus Trierarchiarum munera adirent, sedenis vnam instruentibus nauem: de quibus Lex ipsa ὡςλέγει hæc est:
units.tr: ... of many and great matters, he [the speaker] put the ships to the vote, and the rest, which we have already described. Molon's magistracy falls in the third year of the hundred and fourth Olympiad, as is clear from Diodorus and from the anonymous author of the Description of the Olympiads: "In the fourth year of the hundred and fourth Olympiad, with Nicophemus as prætor at Athens, Polycles and Euripides were trierarchs, when the trierarchs were still two to a ship." Therefore it was only after the fourth year of the hundred and fourth Olympiad, and before the third year of the hundred and sixth Olympiad, in the archonship of Diotimus, that it was instituted that one thousand two hundred of the wealthier men should undertake the trierarchic liturgies, with sixteen men equipping one ship. The law itself, concerning these men, says as follows:

units.la: ΤΟΥΣ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡΧΟΥΣ ΚΑΛΕΙΣΘΑΙ ΕΠΙ ΤΗΝ ΤΡΙΗΡΗ ΣΥΝΕΚΚΑΙΔΕΚΑ ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΛΟΧΟΙΣ ΣΥΝΤΕΛΕΙΩΝ ΑΠΟ ΕΙΚΟΣΙ ΚΑΙ ΠΕΝΤΕ ΕΤΩΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΕΤΤΑΡΑΚΟΝΤΑ ΕΠΙ ΙΣΟΝ ΤΗΙ ΧΟΡΗΓΙΑΙ ΧΡΩΜΕΝΟΝ.
units.tr: [ΤΟΥΣ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡΧΟΥΣ ΚΑΛΕΙΣΘΑΙ ΕΠΙ ΤΗΝ ΤΡΙΗΡΗ ΣΥΝΕΚΚΑΙΔΕΚΑ ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΛΟΧΟΙΣ ΣΥΝΤΕΛΕΙΩΝ ΑΠΟ ΕΙΚΟΣΙ ΚΑΙ ΠΕΝΤΕ ΕΤΩΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΕΤΤΑΡΑΚΟΝΤΑ ΕΠΙ ΙΣΟΝ ΤΗΙ ΧΟΡΗΓΙΑΙ ΧΡΩΜΕΝΟΝ.] The trierarchs for the trireme are to be summoned, sixteen in number, from among those in the lists who are contributors, from twenty-five years of age up to forty, and they are to use the same [expenditure] as for the choregia.

units.la: Trierarchi sedeni ad instruendam vnam triremem seponuntor è manipulorum contributionibus, munusque obeunto ab anno ætatis vicesimoquinto ad quadragesimum vsque, sumptusque ex æquo faciunto.
units.tr: The sixteen trierarchs are to be set apart from the contributions of the companies to equip one trireme, and they are to undertake the office from the twenty-fifth year of age up to the fortieth, and they are to bear the expenses equally.

units.la: Meminit huius Legis Demosthenes ἐν τῷ πρὸς Φαίνιππον. ὦ γὰρ ἀλλὰς, ἐκ τῶν πατρίων νόμων, συνεκκαίδεκα λειτουργίαν, αὐτὸς μὲν μικρὰ καὶ ὀλίγα, αἰαλίσχυ-σαι τοὺς δὲ ὑπόρους τῆς πολιτείας, ἐπιτελέσωσι. & paullo post, φέρε δὴ καὶ τὸν καλὸν καταλήγειν. ΤΟΥΣ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡΧΟΥΣ ΚΑΛΕΙΣΘΑΙ ΕΠΙ ΤΗΝ ΤΡΙΗΡΗ ΣΥΝΕΚΚΑΙΔΕΚΑ ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΛΟΧΟΙΣ ΣΥΤΕΛΕΙΩΝ ΑΠΟ ΕΙΚΟΣΙ ΚΑΙ ΠΕΝΤΕ ΕΤΩΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΕΤΤΑΡΑΚΟΝΤΑ ΕΠΙ ΙΣΟΝ ΤΗΙ ΧΟΡΗΓΙΑΙ ΧΡΩΜΕΝΟΝ. Vlpianus ad Midianam : Φησὶ γὰρ ὅτι τῶν χιλίων καὶ διακοσίων εἰσφερομένων πάλαντων, ἐπειδὴ μισθοῦ-σαι τὴν τριηραρχίαν, ὡς μιᾶς τριήρους τῷ Σοφοκλεῖ γίγνεσθαι, ἐκ ὅσ' ἂν δὴ ἀφήθη. χίλιοι γὰρ καὶ διακόσιοι ἦσαν οἱ τῆς τριηραρχίας ἀφωρισμένοι, ἐκτῶν δὲ λοιπὸν, ἵνα συνεκκαίδεκα τὴν τριήρη ἐπλήρωσαν, ἵνα σώσῃς, ἵνα ὅσοι δύνωνται. Ex hac Lege Trierarchiæ munus nemo obiit ante annum ætatis vicesimum quintum, nemo post quadragesimum: ΑΠΟ ΕΙΚΟΣΙ ΚΑΙ ΠΕΝΤΕ ΕΤΩΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΕΤΤΑΡΑΚΟΝΤΑ. Sed ante hanc Legem, vbi primum in viros transcripti fuerant, munia publica obibant: Χορηγίας exemplum habes apud Lysiam ἐν τῇ ἀπολογίᾳ δωροδοκίας. ἐγὼ γὰρ ἐδοκιμάσθην μὲν ὅτι Θεοπόμ-που Ἀρχοντος, καταξιοῦσι δὲ Χορηγὸς Τεραχωδὶς ἀμύλωσε τειχίσαι μυρίας. De Trierarchia testis Demosthenes in Midiana: καὶ γὰρ μὲν κατ' ἐκείνους τοὺς χρόνους ἐπειρᾶσθαι, θύεσθαι ἐν παίδων ἐξελθὼν, ὅτι σῶσδυο ἡμῶν οἱ Τριηράρχοι. Atque etiam pupilli ipsi, in τὰς συμμορίας de suo collaturi conscribebantur. Nam tutores Demosthenis, eius nomine contulerunt εἰς τὴν συμμορίαν. Habes apud eundem Demosthenem ἐν τῷ πρὸς Ἀφόβου α'. Τὸ δὲ πλῆθος τῆς οὐσίας, ὅτι τότ' ὡς τὸ καταλαβεῖν, μίαν μὲν αὐτοῖς Μαρτυρες μαι γεγόνασιν. εἰς γὰρ τὴν Συμμο-ρίαν ἐμοὶ σῶσπαξαντο καὶ πέντε καὶ εἴκοσι μυᾶς, πεντακοσίας ἀρχμὰς εἰσφέρειν, ὅσον ἂν Τιμόθεος ὁ Κόνωνος, καὶ οἱ τὰ μέγιστα κεκτημένοι πέμπτα, εἰσέφερον.
units.tr: Demosthenes mentions this law in his speech against Phaenippus: "For the others, from the ancestral laws, the sixteen liturgy, they themselves [are] small and few, ... they fulfil the needs of the state." And a little later: "Come now, let me also read the fine ..." [ΤΟΥΣ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡΧΟΥΣ ΚΑΛΕΙΣΘΑΙ ΕΠΙ ΤΗΝ ΤΡΙΗΡΗ ΣΥΝΕΚΚΑΙΔΕΚΑ ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΛΟΧΟΙΣ ΣΥΤΕΛΕΙΩΝ ΑΠΟ ΕΙΚΟΣΙ ΚΑΙ ΠΕΝΤΕ ΕΤΩΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΕΤΤΑΡΑΚΟΝΤΑ ΕΠΙ ΙΣΟΝ ΤΗΙ ΧΟΡΗΓΙΑΙ ΧΡΩΜΕΝΟΝ.] Ulpian on the speech against Midias: for he says that of the one thousand two hundred, when the talents were brought in, since they had hired the trierarchy, [so that] one trireme would be equipped for Sophocles, [it was] whatever was then released. For one thousand two hundred were set apart for the trierarchy, and from the rest, sixteen equipped the trireme, that they might be saved, that as many as could might [contribute]. By this law, no one undertook the trierarchic office before the twenty-fifth year of age, nor after the fortieth: "from twenty-five years to forty." But before this law, when men were first enrolled as adults, they undertook public duties. You have an example of the choregia in Lysias, in the speech in defence against a charge of bribery: "For I was examined in the archonship of Theopompus, and when I was given the choregia for the tragedy, I was charged with fortifying ten thousand..." Demosthenes is a witness about the trierarchy in the speech against Midias: "For in those times, as I was coming out of childhood, the trierarchs were two to a ship." And even the wards themselves were enrolled in the Symmoriae to contribute from their own property. For Demosthenes' guardians contributed on his behalf to the Symmoria. You have this in Demosthenes' first speech against Aphobus: "As for the size of the estate, at that time, to the extent that ... they have been made witnesses ... For into the Symmoria they put me, and [they wanted me] to contribute twenty-five minae, five hundred drachmas, as much as Timotheus son of Conon, and those who possessed the most, contributed."

units.la: Quibus è verbis praeterea docemur, cos qui in reditibus habere annuis viginti quinque minas, contulisse εἰς τὰ συμμορίας[?] illarum viginti quinque minarum partem quintam, nempe quingentas drachmas; atque ita, puto, pro hoc modulo maius vel minus: quanquam iniuriam sibi factam hac in re testatur Demosthenes, cum ex illis quatuordecim ferme talentis, quos pater in bonis reliquerat, superessent tantum talenta novem & semis, reliquis talentis quatuor & semis erogatis prout tabulis testamenti cautum fuerat.
units.tr: From these words we are also taught that those who had an annual income of twenty-five minae contributed to the Symmoriae a fifth part of those twenty-five minae, namely five hundred drachmas; and so, I think, for this rate more or less. Although Demosthenes testifies that he was wronged in this matter, since from those fourteen talents or so which his father had left in goods, only nine and a half talents remained, four and a half talents having been paid out according to the terms of the will.

units.la: Trierarchiae legitimum tempus annus fuit: (nam altero quoque anno [illegible, ~12 letters], unde intelligendus venit Isaeus [illegible, ~40 letters] καὶ τελευτῶν τὸν πόλεμον χρόνον διετέλεσεν[?]. Οὐκ ἐκ συμμορίας τὸ καινὸν ποιησάμενος, ὥσπερ οἱ ἄλλοι[?] ἀλλὰ οὐχ ἡ αὐτὴ διαπονῶν[?]: οὐδὲ δύο πέρας ὧν αὐτός, ἀλλὰ καὶ ταμίας[?] οὐδὲ δύο ἐπὶ τῆς καθαλίτων, ἀλλὰ σύνεχῶς[?]. nam pluribus annis continuis Trierarchus fuit, quatuor, puto; quorum duobus vacationem muneris habere potuit.) itaque cum οἱ δύο ἥδη οἱ Τριηράρχοι, singuli sex mensses munus obibant. Demosthenes ἐν τᾷ ἀρχῇ Πολυκλέα[?]. οὐ δὲ ἀλλὰ ἀπολαμβάνων ἢ ταμίας, ὅταν μὲν τὸν ἐπὶ πάντων χρόνον τριηραρχοῦντα τῆς ἐξ ἡμέρας. Rursus ibidem: ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπαρχῆσαι Εὐεργέτης, ἐκ τριηραρχῶν ὢν, καὶ οὐχ ὅτι ἡδὺ ἂν ἀλλὰ ἐξ ἡμέρας ἑκάστης πλὴν. Atque ita cum sedeni erant Trierarchi, munus illud suum obibant annuum vnusquisque ὡς ἀ αἰσθηταῖ βαῖ ἱ τὴν ἡρπμία χρῶμαι.Quanquam saepe accidebat, vt Trierarchiam locarent, atqueita accepto,exempli gratia, talento, quanti locauerant, ipsum annuum munus obibant. Vlpianus ad Midianam: Ὡς ἀκοῦσ ἐποιοῦντο ἐπὶ τῆς σιωπῆς ἄλλοι Τριηράρχη, καὶ τῶν λεπτῶν... ἐπὶ τὰς σιωπᾶς. πολλοί δὲ τῶν Τριηράρχων οἴκοι μένοντες, ἀφεῖς αὐτὸν ἐξέπεμπον καὶ λαμβάνοντες ἔλεος τὸ διαπόνειν, αἰσθάνεται τὴν λειτουργίαν. Atque hi, ἐσχατέλων, à ceteris vero, qui essent eiusdem Συμμορίας postea exigebant, quod impenderant: vnde dixit Demosthenes in Leptinea: Εἰς σιωπῆλαι ἀγαγεῖν τὰς τριηραρχίας. & Isaeus loco proximè laudato: Οὐκ ἐκ συμμορίας τὸ καινὸν ποιησάμενος, ὥσπερ οἱ πολλοί. Vlpianus ad Olynthiacam II. εἰσὶ φεύγουσι γὰρ οἱ πλούσιοι ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐσχάτως ἐπαλλαγεῖν, ὃ ἐδίχρη τῶν ἔτι ἐστὶν ἀλλὰ.
units.tr: The legal period of the trierarchy was one year. (For in the second year too [illegible] ..., whence Isaeus must be understood [illegible] ... and finishing the war over a period of time. He did not make the new [contribution] from the Symmoria, as the others did, but did not [perform] the same duties; nor did he serve two terms ... nor did he twice in the same ... but continuously. For he was trierarch for several consecutive years, four, I think; of which he could have had two years' exemption from the office.) So, since the two trierarchs, each served the office for six months. Demosthenes in the speech against Polycles: "... but when he [was] treasurer, whenever he [was] trierarch for the whole time out of the day..." Again in the same place: "But also to be a benefactor, being a trierarch, and not that it would be pleasant, but from each day ..." And so, when the trierarchs were sixteen, each performed that office for a year. Although it often happened that they let out the trierarchy, and so, having received, for example, a talent, [as much as] they had let it for, they performed the annual office themselves. Ulpian on the speech against Midias: "As others made [the payment] at the time of the silence, and of the small ... at the silences. But many trierarchs, remaining at home, sent others in their place and, taking the burden of performing the liturgy, ... Those who were in arrears, others of the same Symmoria afterwards demanded from them what they had expended; whence Demosthenes said in the speech against Leptines: 'To bring the trierarchies into silence.' And Isaeus in the passage just quoted: 'He did not make the new [contribution] from the Symmoria, as most people did.' Ulpian on the second Olynthiac: for the rich flee on account of them, and in the end they are released, which ... is still ..."

units.la: Non longe post Demosthenes Legem scripsit, qua cauetur, vt vnusquisque pro facultatum censu conferret:
units.tr: Not long after, Demosthenes wrote a law providing that each man should contribute according to the assessment of his means:

units.la: ΤΟΥΣ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡΧΟΥΣ ΑΙΡΕΙΣΘΑΙ ΕΠΙ ΤΗΝ ΤΡΙΗΡΗ ΑΠΟ ΤΗΣ ΟΥΣΙΑΣ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΙΜΗΣΙΝ ΑΠΟ ΤΑΛΑΝΤΩΝ ΔΕΚΑ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΓΑΛΕΙΟΝΩΝ Η ΟΥΣΙΑ ΑΠΟΤΕΤΙΜΗΜΕΝΗ Η ΧΡΗΜΑΤΩΝ, ΚΑΤΑ ΤΟΝ ΑΝΑΛΟΓΙΣΜΟΝ ΕΩΣ ΤΡΙΩΝ ΓΑΛΟΙΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΥΠΗΡΕΤΙΚΟΥ Η ΛΕΙΤΟΥΡΓΙΑ ΕΣΤΩ. ΚΑΤΑ ΤΗΝ ΑΥΤΗΝ ΔΕ ΑΝΑΛΟΓΙΑΝ ΕΣΤΩ ΚΑΙ ΟΙΣ ΕΛΑΤΤΩΝ ΟΥΣΙΑ ΕΣΤΙΤΩΝ ΔΕΚΑΤΑΛΑΝΤΩΝ ΕΙΣ ΣΥΝΤΕΛΕΙΑΝ ΣΥΝΑΓΟΜΕΝΟΙΣ ΕΙΣ ΤΑ ΔΕΚΑ ΤΑΛΑΝΤΑ.
units.tr: The trierarchs are to be chosen for the trireme from property, according to the valuation, from ten talents. If the property is assessed at more than ten talents of land or money, let the liturgy be performed in proportion, up to three ships, with a small boat and an attendant. In the same proportion, let those whose property is less than ten talents, when their property is combined to make up ten talents, also contribute. [ΤΟΥΣ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡΧΟΥΣ ΑΙΡΕΙΣΘΑΙ ΕΠΙ ΤΗΝ ΤΡΙΗΡΗ ΑΠΟ ΤΗΣ ΟΥΣΙΑΣ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΙΜΗΣΙΝ ΑΠΟ ΤΑΛΑΝΤΩΝ ΔΕΚΑ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΓΑΛΕΙΟΝΩΝ Η ΟΥΣΙΑ ΑΠΟΤΕΤΙΜΗΜΕΝΗ Η ΧΡΗΜΑΤΩΝ, ΚΑΤΑ ΤΟΝ ΑΝΑΛΟΓΙΣΜΟΝ ΕΩΣ ΤΡΙΩΝ ΓΑΛΟΙΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΥΠΗΡΕΤΙΚΟΥ Η ΛΕΙΤΟΥΡΓΙΑ ΕΣΤΩ. ΚΑΤΑ ΤΗΝ ΑΥΤΗΝ ΔΕ ΑΝΑΛΟΓΙΑΝ ΕΣΤΩ ΚΑΙ ΟΙΣ ΕΛΑΤΤΩΝ ΟΥΣΙΑ ΕΣΤΙΤΩΝ ΔΕΚΑΤΑΛΑΝΤΩΝ ΕΙΣ ΣΥΝΤΕΛΕΙΑΝ ΣΥΝΑΓΟΜΕΝΟΙΣ ΕΙΣ ΤΑ ΔΕΚΑ ΤΑΛΑΝΤΑ.]

units.la: Trierarchi ad triremem instruendam deliguntur è facultatum censu, qui sit denum talentum: si maior sit denis talentiu, pro census modo vel tres naves cum scapha instruunto: Eadem proportione observata, tot eorum, quorum census minor est talentis decem, vna conferuato, quot simul dabunt censum decem talentorum.
units.tr: Trierarchs for equipping a trireme are chosen from those whose property is assessed at ten talents. If the assessment is greater than ten talents, they must equip three ships with a boat, according to the size of the assessment; by the same proportion, one ship is to be furnished by as many men of lesser means as together make up ten talents.

units.la: Hac Lege fiebat, vt plures pauperes tantum conferrent, quantum vnus ditissimus, multorum re familiari quasi in vnum aceruum collata: exempli gratia, si Callias, cuius res familiaris est centum viginti talentorum, conferret viginti quatuor talenta: alij viginti viri, quorum opes sint intra sex talenta, vni Calliae aequabuntur, viginti quatuor & ipsi talentis conferendis. Meminit huius Legis Demosthenes ἐν τῷ [?] φάνου. ἐκ δὲ τῶν ἐμοῦ νόμου, ὃ γεγράμμενον [?] τὸν [?] ἴδιαν [?] ἐκ τῶν [?] Τεισφράσης, ὁ τῆς μιᾶς ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς καὶ δίκαιος ἂν [?] πεπρᾶσθαι [?] πόλεως. & paullo post, Legem ipsam describit: φέρε δὴ [?] τοὺς τριηράρχους [?] τὸν ἐκ τῆς ἐμοῦ νόμου καταλογον. TOYΣ TPIHPAPXOYΣ AIPEIΣΘΑΙ, &c. Hac autem Demosthenis Lege cauetur; vt is, cuius census est decem talentum, vnam triremem instruat: TOYΣ TPIHPAPXOYΣ AIPEIΣΘAI EPI THN TPIHPH ΑΠΟ ΤΗΣ ΟΥΣΙΑΣ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΙΜΗΣΙΝ ΑΠΟ ΤΑΛΑΝΤΩΝ ΔΕΚΑ.
