Quod si census denis maior esset talentis, ξὺν τὸν ἀναλογισμὸν decem talentorum ad vnam triremem, conferebat etiam ad aliam triremem instruendam, ita tamen, vt, quotquot esset talentorum census, non teneretur plures tribus instruere triremes cum vna scapha: ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΓΑΛΕΙΟΝΩΝ Η ΟΥΣΙΑ ΑΠΟΤΕΤΙΜΗΜΕΝΗ Η ΧΡΗΜΑΤΩΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΟΝ ΑΝΑΛΟΓΙΣΜΟΝ ΕΩΣ ΤΡΙΩΝ ΠΛΟΙΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΥΠΗΡΕΤΙΚΟΥ Η ΛΕΙΤΟΥΡΓΙΑ ΕΣΤΩ. Annum, quo lata est hæc Lex à Demosthene, si inuestigemus, nemo, opinor, nobis vitio vertet: Ipse Orator ἐν τῷ πρὸς [?] φάνη dicit esse annum, quo Polycles Prætor Athenis fuit: en Psephisma in hanc rem: ΕΠΙ ΑΡΧΟΝΤΟΣ ΠΟΛΥΚΛΕΟΥΣ ΜΗΝΟΣ ΒΟΗΔΡΟΜΙΩΝΟΣ ΕΚΤΗΙ ΕΠΙ ΔΕΚΑ ΦΥΛΗΣ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΥΟΥΣΗΣ ΙΠΠΟΘΟΩΝΤΙΔΟΣ ΔΗΜΟΣΘΕ-ΝΗΣ. ΔΗΜΟΘΕΝΟΥΣ ΓΑΙΑΝΙΕΥΣ ΕΙΣΗΝΕΓΚΕ ΝΟΜΟΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΟ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡΧΙΚΟΝ ΑΝΤΙ ΤΟΥ ΠΡΟΤΕΡΟΥ ΚΑΘ' Ο ΑΙ ΣΥΝΤΕΛΕΙΑΙ ΗΣΑΝ ΤΩΝ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡΧΩΝ, ΚΑΙ ΕΓΕΧΕΙΡΟΤΟΝΗΣΕΝ Η ΒΟΥΛΗ ΚΑΙ Ο ΔΗΜΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΑΓΗΝΕΓΚΕ ΠΑΡΑΝΟΜΩΝ ΓΡΑΦΗΝ ΔΗΜΟΣΘΕΝΕΙ ΠΑΤΡΟΚΛΗΣ ΦΛΥΕΥΣ ΚΑΙ ΤΟ ΜΕΡΟΣ ΤΩΝ ΤΗΦΩΝ ΟΥ ΛΑΒΩΝ ΑΠΕΤΙΣΕ ΤΑΣ ΠΕΝΤΑΚΟΣΙΑΣ ΔΡΑΧΜΑΣ. Sed in Polyclis Prætura nihil est auxilij, eorum enim veterum, quorum scripta ad nos peruenerunt, nullus meminit, si hunc Demosthenem excipias, Polyclis Archontis: Quare non possumus satis mirari ἀπορηθέντα [?], Viri Clarissimi & eruditissimi, qui hunc Demosthenis Polyclem Prætorem facit anno tertio Olympiadis centesimæ quartadecimæ, quemque Dionysius & Diodorus Philoclem, alij Dioclem nominant. Atqui anno tertio Olympiadis centesimæ duodecimæ, ὅτι Ἀρχοντος Ἀθηναίων Ἀεισθένης, Orationem ἐν τῷ πρὸς φάνη habuit Demosthenes, in eaque meminit huius Legis à se latæ aliquot annis ante. Anno tertio Olympiadis centesimæ - decimæ, Chæronda Athenis Prætore, Æschines postulauit Legum violatarum Ctesiphontem, quod populi scitum fecisset, vt corona donaretur Demosthenes, cum in Magistratu esset, necdum rationes reddidisset suas: intra vertentem autem annum accusauit Ctesiphontem. Æschines, adversus quem cum Ctesiphontem sua ipsius causa tueatur Demosthenes, offendit se egregie in Republica fuisse versatum, ad ea usque tempora, quibus hoc populi de coronando Demosthene scitum fecit Ctesiphon : ὅτι μὲν ... [?] ἐν ᾗς τοῦτ' ἐπεψηφίσατο, πολλὰς ... [?] τὴν πόλιν, &c. quibus expositis aggreditur probare violatas non fuisse Leges à Ctesiphonte, cum scripserit coronandum esse Demosthenem in Theatro Τραγῳδῶν, qui nondum rationes retulerat: ἡ δὲ ... [?] μὲν ... [?] τὴν κηρύγματος εἶπεν, καὶ τὴν ἀθωσιν· ὃ γὰρ ὡς τὰ ἀρίστα τι ἐπαγγεῖλαι ... [?] καὶ ἀλλὰ πάντων ... [?] ὑμᾶς, ἐκεῖνος εἰς τὴν εἰρηνικῶν διδαχθαί μοι νομίζω. Cum igitur probat Demosthenes se omnes boni civis, qui ad Rempublicam accesserit, partes impleuisse, docet, se auctore, Athenienses suppetias venisse Byzantinis adversus Philippum, urbemque ab imminenti periculo eripuisse : ὅτι ... [?] μόνον ὃ Χερρόνησον καὶ Βυζάντιον σῶσαι, οὐδὲ ὃ κωλύσαι τὸν Ἑλλησπόντιν ... [?] Φιλίππου ἠνώχθαι ποτὲ, οὐδὲ ὃ ὑμᾶς ... [?] τὴν πόλιν εἰς τοῦτον, ἡ ... [?] ἐμοί, καὶ ἡ πολιτεία διεπεραίσατο, ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶν αὐξήσεως ... [?] τῆς πόλεως καλο-καγαθίας, καὶ τῶν Φιλίππου καιρίαν. quae consilia sua & res gestas Atheniensium ubi comparavit cum maiorum suorum egregie factis, redit ad instituturn de rebus à se in Republica gestis sermonem, scribitque post liberatum suo consilio Byzantium, alterum suum πολίτευμα, & quidem egregium, fuisse hanc suam εἰς ὃ τεσσαρακοντα ... [?] Legem. βούλομαι ... [?] ἐπιμελεῖσθαι ἐφ' ἃ τούτων ἐξῆς ἐπολιτευόμεθα ... [?] ἀθηναῖοι, ὅ ἐαυτοῦ ... [?] ἡμῖν νόμων, &c.
units.tr: By this law it came about that several poor men contributed as much as one very rich man, the property of many being pooled, as it were, into one heap. For example, if Callias, whose estate is one hundred and twenty talents, contributed twenty-four talents, then twenty men whose means are under six talents each would equal Callias and would also contribute twenty-four talents. Demosthenes mentions this law in his speech [...] against Phaenippus, and again in the speech against Timocrates [...]. Shortly afterwards he describes the law itself: "Let us read the law on the trierarchs," and so on: [TOYΣ TPIHPAPXOYΣ AIPEIΣΘΑΙ, &c.] Now in this law of Demosthenes it is provided that the man whose census is ten talents shall equip one trireme: [TOYΣ TPIHPAPXOYΣ AIPEIΣΘAI EPI THN TPIHPH ΑΠΟ ΤΗΣ ΟΥΣΙΑΣ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΙΜΗΣΙΝ ΑΠΟ ΤΑΛΑΝΤΩΝ ΔΕΚΑ.] But if the census was greater than ten talents, he contributed, in proportion, towards equipping another trireme as well, yet not so that anyone whose census was of some amount of talents was obliged to equip more than three triremes with one boat: [ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΓΑΛΕΙΟΝΩΝ Η ΟΥΣΙΑ ΑΠΟΤΕΤΙΜΗΜΕΝΗ Η ΧΡΗΜΑΤΩΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΟΝ ΑΝΑΛΟΓΙΣΜΟΝ ΕΩΣ ΤΡΙΩΝ ΠΛΟΙΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΥΠΗΡΕΤΙΚΟΥ Η ΛΕΙΤΟΥΡΓΙΑ ΕΣΤΩ.] If we inquire into the year in which this law was proposed by Demosthenes, no one, I think, will blame us. The orator himself, in the speech against Phaenippus, says it was the year in which Polycles was praetor at Athens. There is a decree on this matter: [ΕΠΙ ΑΡΧΟΝΤΟΣ ΠΟΛΥΚΛΕΟΥΣ ΜΗΝΟΣ ΒΟΗΔΡΟΜΙΩΝΟΣ ΕΚΤΗΙ ΕΠΙ ΔΕΚΑ ΦΥΛΗΣ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΥΟΥΣΗΣ ΙΠΠΟΘΟΩΝΤΙΔΟΣ ΔΗΜΟΣΘΕΝΗΣ ... ] in which Demosthenes of Paeania proposed a law concerning the trierarchic office, replacing the earlier one under which the trierarchic liturgies had existed; the Council and the People ratified it, and it was ordered that an action for illegal proposal be brought against Demosthenes by Patrocles of Phlya, who, failing to obtain a fifth of the votes, was fined five hundred drachmas. But in the praetorship of Polycles there is no help, for of those ancient writers whose works have come down to us, none mentions Polycles as archon, except Demosthenes. Hence we cannot sufficiently wonder at the perplexity of those most distinguished and learned men who place this Demosthenic Polycles as praetor in the third year of the one hundred and fourteenth Olympiad, whom Dionysius and Diodorus call Philocles, and others Diocles. Yet in the third year of the one hundred and twelfth Olympiad, when Aristaenetus was archon of the Athenians, Demosthenes delivered the speech against Phaenippus, and in it mentions this law which he had proposed some years earlier. In the third year of the one hundred and tenth Olympiad, with Chaeronda praetor at Athens, Aeschines prosecuted Ctesiphon for violation of the laws, because he had proposed a decree that Demosthenes be crowned, although he was in office and had not yet rendered his accounts; within the year, however, he brought the charge against Ctesiphon. Demosthenes, defending Ctesiphon in his own cause against Aeschines, shows that he had been outstandingly active in public affairs up to the time when Ctesiphon proposed this decree to crown Demosthenes: [ὅτι μὲν ... ἐν ᾗς τοῦτ' ἐπεψηφίσατο, πολλὰς ... τὴν πόλιν, &c.] Having set this out, he sets about proving that Ctesiphon did not violate the laws, since he had written that Demosthenes should be crowned in the theatre at the festival of tragedies, although he had not yet rendered his accounts: [ἡ δὲ ... μὲν ... τὴν κηρύγματος εἶπεν, καὶ τὴν ἀθωσιν ...]. When Demosthenes shows that he has fulfilled all the parts of a good citizen who has entered public life, he explains that, on his advice, the Athenians came to the aid of the Byzantines against Philip and rescued the city from imminent danger: not only did he save the Chersonese and Byzantium, nor only prevent Philip from ever crossing the Hellespont, but he also increased the city's good name and thwarted Philip's plans. When he has compared these counsels and deeds of his own with the glorious achievements of the Athenians of old, he returns to the theme of what he had done in public affairs, and writes that after Byzantium was freed by his counsel, his other public service, and a most notable one, was this law of his, "in the forty ..." [εἰς ὃ τεσσαρακοντα ... Legem. βούλομαι ... ἐπιμελεῖσθαι ἐφ' ἃ τούτων ἐξῆς ἐπολιτευόμεθα ... ἀθηναῖοι, ὅ ἐαυτοῦ ... ἡμῖν νόμων, &c.]

units.la: &c. Philippus Byzantinis bellum intulit anno primo Olympiadis centesimæ decimæ, Prætore Athenis Theophrasto. Philochorus ἐν τῇ ἐκτῇ Ἀττίδος, apud Dionysium in Epistola ad Ammæum : ΘΕΟΦΡΑΣΤΟΣ ΑΛΑΕΥΣ ἐπὶ τούτου, Φίλιππος ὁ μὲν παρὰ ... [?] Πεισίθεω ... [?] βαλεῖν ... [?] ἐπὶ ... [?] Βυζάντιον ἐπολιόρκει, καὶ μηχανήματα ... [?]. Itaque iussit Demosthenes Athenienses ire suppetias Byzantinis, ut ipse scribit, ἐκ δὲ πλεγῶν ... [?] καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ἐπεργῶν ... [?] τῶν πολέμου, ut ibidem testatur Philochorus. Sequitur ex eodem Philochoro annus secundus Olympiadis centesimæ decimæ, Lysimachida Archonte: ΑΥΣΙΜΑΧΙΔΗΣ ΑΧΑΡΝΕΥΣ ἐπὶ τούτου, τὰ μὲν ἔργα τὰ πρὸς τὰς νεωστικὰς καὶ τὸν σκευο-ποιῶν ... [?] ἀνεβάλλοντο ἀφ' τῶν πολέμων τὸν ἀρχηγὸν Φιλίππων ... [?], τὰ δὲ χρήματα ἐπιφέροντα πολύτ' ... [?] γραλωτικά, Δημοσθένης χρήμασιν ... [?]. Occasione illius populi sciti, quod fecit Demosthenes anno primo Olympiadis centesimæ decimæ, Theophrasto Athenis Prætore, ut naves ad bellum contra Philippum instruerentur, Demosthenes, ut mea est suspicio, ineunte anno secundo Olympiadis centesimæ decimæ, Legem hanc scripsit εἰς ὃ τεσσαρακοντα ... [?], sed difficultatem parit, quod eius anni Prætorem facit ex Actis Demosthenes Polyclem, cùm Philochorus, Dionysius Halycarnasseus, Diodorus Siculus, alij, Prætorem fuisse dicant Athenis hoc anno secundo Olympiadis centesimæ decimæ Lysimachidam : Ego vero nullus dubito Polyclem Archontem fuisse primis anni secundi Olympiadis centesimæ decimæ mensibus: nam vertente Boëdromione præerat, ut habes in Plephismate:
units.tr: &c. Philip made war on the Byzantines in the first year of the one hundred and tenth Olympiad, when Theophrastus was praetor at Athens. Philochorus, in the sixth book of the Atthis, as quoted by Dionysius in his letter to Ammaeus: [ΘΕΟΦΡΑΣΤΟΣ ΑΛΑΕΥΣ ἐπὶ τούτου, Φίλιππος ... Βυζάντιον ἐπολιόρκει, καὶ μηχανήματα ...]. Therefore Demosthenes, as he himself writes, urged the Athenians to go to the aid of the Byzantines, and, as Philochorus attests in the same passage, [...] and the other preparations of war. From the same Philochorus follows the second year of the one hundred and tenth Olympiad, with Lysimachides as archon: [ΑΥΣΙΜΑΧΙΔΗΣ ΑΧΑΡΝΕΥΣ ἐπὶ τούτου, τὰ μὲν ἔργα τὰ πρὸς τὰς νεωστικὰς ... Δημοσθένης χρήμασιν ...]. On the occasion of that decree which Demosthenes proposed in the first year of the one hundred and tenth Olympiad, when Theophrastus was praetor at Athens, so that ships might be fitted out for war against Philip, I suspect that Demosthenes wrote this law, "in the forty ...", at the beginning of the second year of the one hundred and tenth Olympiad. But a difficulty arises, because from the public records Demosthenes makes Polycles praetor of that year, whereas Philochorus, Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Diodorus Siculus and others say that the praetor at Athens in this second year of the one hundred and tenth Olympiad was Lysimachides. For my part, I have no doubt that Polycles was archon in the first months of the second year of the one hundred and tenth Olympiad: for he presided while Boedromion was current, as you have in the decree:

units.la: ΕΠΙ ΑΡΧΟΝΤΟΣ ΓΟΥΛΚΛΕΟΥΣ ΜΗΝΟΣ ΒΟΗΔΡΟΜΙΩΝΟΣ ΕΚΤΗ, ΕΠΙ ΔΕΚΑ.
units.tr: In the archonship of Goulkles, in the month of Boedromion, on the tenth day.

units.la: Sed hic Polycles aut in Magistratu mortuus est, aut ea dignitate motus, cui successit, & reliquis illius anni mensibus Archon praefuit Lysimachidas ὁ [?]. Verum cum adhuc praeesset Polycles, Legem tulit Demosthenes ὁ [?]. Sed ad Trierarchiae munus redeamus. Strategorum erat ad Trierarchiam obeundam vocare, & censum delectumque habere: unde quibus male vellent factum, vocatis & designatis ad Trierarchiam, nauem
units.tr: But this Polycles either died in office or was promoted to the dignity to which he succeeded, and for the rest of that year's months Lysimachidas presided as archon [?]. Yet while Polycles was still in office, Demosthenes proposed a law [?]. But let us return to the office of trierarch. It was the task of the generals to summon men to serve as trierarchs and to hold the assessment and levy. So those who were unwilling to serve were summoned and designated as trierarchs, and they provided a ship

units.la: Sape tritam, sepe fixam, sepe excussam malleo, praebebant: Hinc Cleon apud Aristophanem Equitibus,
units.tr: Often worn thin, often patched, often beaten out with a hammer.

units.la: Ἐγὼ δὲ ποιῶ τὸν τέλ-ευτὴν, ἀλλ' ἀλίσκομαί σε [?] σαυτῆς, παλαιὰ ταῦτ' ἔχον-τ' εἰς τὸ ἀγαλμα [?] ἐφέξεις, οὐδὲ [?] κεκτημένος. Ὀ[?]μα[?]μι[?]ματα, ὅπως ἀν [?] ἰσον ζῶσ[?] ἀπο[?]. ἐώσ[?]ις ἐμοὶ καλλίω ἀ[?]κιω [?] ἐπο[?] Ἀ[?]λος [?] ἐμοὶ εἰσφορὰς [?]. ἐγὼ δ᾽ ἐκ τοῦ πλατοῦ [?] ἐπὶ τῶν [?] ἐξ[?]ϕ[?]ως.
units.tr: I, however, am making the ... but I am caught by you, holding these old things ... you will hold back ... not even possessing ... so that ... equal ... to me, a more beautiful ... contributions to me. But I, from the broad ... [Ἐγὼ δὲ ποιῶ τὸν τέλ-ευτὴν, ἀλλ' ἀλίσκομαί σε [?] σαυτῆς, παλαιὰ ταῦτ' ἔχον-τ' εἰς τὸ ἀγαλμα [?] ἐφέξεις, οὐδὲ [?] κεκτημένος. Ὀ[?]μα[?]μι[?]ματα, ὅπως ἀν [?] ἰσον ζῶσ[?] ἀπο[?]. ἐώσ[?]ις ἐμοὶ καλλίω ἀ[?]κιω [?] ἐπο[?] Ἀ[?]λος [?] ἐμοὶ εἰσφορὰς [?]. ἐγὼ δ᾽ ἐκ τοῦ πλατοῦ [?] ἐπὶ τῶν [?] ἐξ[?]ϕ[?]ως.]

units.la: Ex his vides olim, cum Equites scriberet Aristophanes, anno quarto Olympiadis octogesimae octavae, Praetore Athenis Stratocle, Trierarchos naues à Republica accepisse, quas πληρώματα instruerent. Sed istud mutauit: Nam eo tempore, quo ... Trierarchi naues comparabant, armamentis & remigibus instruebant, atque militibus fiue ... stipendia numerabant. Demosthenes in Midiana: ... Quare tunc Trierarchi accipiebant de publico in singulas triremes ... triginta minas. Demosthenes ... Apollodorus enim, cui hanc Orationem scripsit Demosthenes, fuit Trierarchus, ... vt in superioribus diximus. Postea, quando sedeni [?] vnam triremem instruxerunt, Trierarchi sola naue militabant, Respublica armamenta, nautas & omnia πληρώματα praebebat. Demosthenes in Midiana. [illegible, ~70 letters] Vlpianus ad haec Demosthenis verba: [illegible, ~60 letters] Atque haec armamenta Trierarchi vel, postquam rediissent, restituebant Reipublicae, vel iis, qui sibi in obeundo hoc munere ex eadem classe succedebant, tradebant. Demosthenes [illegible, ~45 letters] Ἐτέρῳ καὶ Μνησικούλῳ [illegible, ~50 letters] ἂν ἀπὸ τῆς Συμμορίας [illegible, ~20 letters].
units.tr: From these things you can see that long ago, when Aristophanes wrote the Knights, in the fourth year of the eighty-eighth Olympiad, with Stratocles as praetor at Athens, the trierarchs received ships from the Republic, which they equipped as complements [πληρώματα]. But this was changed. For at the time when the trierarchs were fitting out their ships, they supplied them with rigging and oarsmen, and paid the soldiers or ... their wages. Demosthenes in the Against Meidias: ... Therefore at that time the trierarchs received from the public treasury thirty minae for each trireme. Demosthenes ... For Apollodorus, to whom Demosthenes wrote this speech, was a trierarch, ... as we said above. Later, when they began to equip one trireme with a single ship, the trierarchs served with the ship alone, while the Republic supplied the rigging, the sailors and all the complements [πληρώματα]. Demosthenes in the Against Meidias. [illegible, about 70 letters] Ulpian, on these words of Demosthenes: [illegible, about 60 letters] And the trierarchs either handed back this rigging to the Republic when they had returned, or handed it over to those who succeeded them in this office from the same fleet. Demosthenes [illegible, about 45 letters] to another and to Mnesicoulos [illegible, about 50 letters] from the symmory [illegible, about 20 letters].

units.la: Si quis autem Trierarchus armamenta, quae à Republica acceperat, non restitueret, repetebat ab eo Trierarchus ex eadem classe, & classis eiusdem curator, ex Lege, quam tulit Periander,
units.tr: If any trierarch did not return the rigging that he had received from the Republic, the trierarch from the same fleet and the curator of that same fleet demanded it from him, under the law which Periander proposed.

units.la: Trierarchi munus suum fungentes, & curatores classium, nomina eorum recipiunto, qui armamenta debent Reipublicae, suntque eiusdem classis, atque ab iis armamenta repetunto.
units.tr: Let the trierarchs, performing their duty, and the curators of the fleets take down the names of those who owe rigging to the Republic, and who belong to the same fleet, and let them demand the rigging from them.

units.la: Hanc Legem laudat Demosthenes, si titulus auctorem non mentitur, & [illegible, ~30 letters] Ἐτέρῳ καὶ Μνησικούλῳ. Docetque eum, cui hanc Orationem scripsit, qui Trierarchus erat & curator suae classis, repetiisse à Demochare & Theophemo armamenta nauium, quae Reipublicae non restituerant, quia ita Lege Periandri cauebatur, ac praeterea populi scito iubebatur Magistratus nescio quis nomina eorum, qui armamenta debebant Reipublicae, dare curatoribus nauium: Curatores nauium iubebantur dare Trierarchis munus suum fungentibus & classium Curatoribus: Curatores classium & Trierarchi cogebantur ex Lege Periandri, nomina eorum, qui armamenta debebant Reipublicae, suae quisque classis recipere, & ab iis armamenta repetere: Ad haec alterum Plephisma iubebat, vt inter se partirentur operas Trierarchi & classium Curatores, & alius ab alio armamenta Reipublicae repeteret: Ex hoc igitur populi factum est scito, vt repeterentur armamenta à Trierarchis, qui ea Reipublicae debebant: ex Lege Periandri, vt Trierarchi & classium Curatores repeterent ab iis quisque, qui suae erant classis, vnde is, cui Orationem hanc scripsit Demosthenes, cum Trierarchus & classis suae Curator esset, necesse habuit repetere armamenta ab iis, qui debebant Reipublicae, erantque suae classis: denique posterius Plephisma in causa fuit, vt cum alius ab alio repetere deberet [illegible, ~20 letters], hic noster à Demochare & Theophemo Σωτει- [illegible, ~25 letters], qui fuerunt illi adtributi, repetere coactus fuerit: [illegible, ~70 letters] [illegible, ~60 letters] [illegible, ~50 letters]. πολὶ· οἱ ἢ τῶν νεωρίων Ἐπιμεληταὶ[?], τοῖς Τειηεάρχαις[?] τῆς ἐκπλέοντι[?] πότε, ἢ τῆς Ἐπι-μεληταῖς[?] τοῖς ἐν τῆς Συμμοείας[?]. ὁ δὲ νόμος ὁ τῆς Γεειαίδρου[?], ἰωάλκαζε[?] ἢ ἀποσπάσπῃ[?] τοῖς ὀφείλουσι[?] τὰ σκεύη[?], καθ' ὃν αἱ Συμμοείαι[?] σύνεπάσθησαν[?]. Ὡς δὲ τοῦτο, ἐπειδὴ ψηφισμα δήμου ἰωάλκαζε[?] πρὸς μέρος ἡμῖν ἀλλὰ τὴν ὀφελόντων ἐκα-στον τῆς σκεύης[?] ἐπυχον δὲ ἐγὼ μὲν τεινεφρχῶν[?], καὶ Ἐπιμεληταὶ ὧν τῆς Συμμοείας[?]. Δημοχάρης δὲ ὁ Παιαιεὺς[?], ἐν τῇ Συμμοείᾳ[?], ἢ ὀφείλων τῇ πόλει σκεύη μὲ Θεοφή-μου ζωτοῦ[?], Σωστεινάρχης ἀμόλμος[?]. γεγραμμένοις οὖν αὐτοῖς ἀμφοτέρους ἐν τῇ σκεύη ὀφείλοντας τὰ σκεύη τῆς πόλεως ἡ ἀρχὴ ἀποδαλεοῦσα ἀπὸ τῆς τεσσερᾶς ἀρχῆς, ἡμῖν πρέδωκε κατὰ τὰ τὸν νόμον ἢ ἐξ ἀ[?] τὰ ψηφίσματα ἐν τὸν νόμον. Sed hic quædam aduertenda sunt in verbis Demosthenis, quæ mendosa sunt. Editur: Τοῦτο τοίνυν τῆς ψηφίσματος γεγραμμένου[?], ἢ μὲν ἀρχὴ ἐπικλήρωσι[?], ἢ πρέδωκε τοὺς ὀφείλοντας τὰ σκεύη τῆς πόλεως· οἱ δὲ τῶν νεωρίων Ἐπιμεληταὶ, τοῖς Τειηεάρχαις τοῖς ἐκπλέοντι πότε, ἢ τῆς Ἐπιμεληταῖς τοῖς ἐν τῆς Συμμοείας[?]. Vox ἐπικληρῶσι[?] non est huius loci, meo iudicio, nam non agitur de vlla sortitione, sed tantum Magistratus hoc Psephismate iubetur dare nomina eorum, qui armamenta Reipublicæ debebant, nauium Curatoribus; quanquam enim id expressis verbis non dicat, tamen colligere licet ex eo quod scribit, nauium Curatores eadem nomina dedisse Trierarchis & Curatoribus classium; atqui Curatores nauium ab aliis acceperant: vnde in sequentibus dixit: ὀφείλοντες τὰ σκεύη τῆς πόλεως ἡ ἀρχὴ Curatores nauium ἀποδαλεοῦσα ἀπὸ τῆς τεσσερᾶς ἀρχῆς, ( de qua dixit: ἡ μὲν ἀρχὴ ἐπικλήρωσι, καὶ πρέδωκε τοὺς ὀφείλοντας τὰ σκεύη τῆς πόλεως ) ἡμῖν πρέδωκε κατὰ τὸ τὸν νόμον, καὶ ἐξ' τὰ ψηφίσματα. Si qua sortitio facta fuisset, haberet, quo se excusatum iret is, cui Orationem scripsit Demosthenes, neque prætermisisset proculdubio: sed, vt dixi, nulla sortitio facta, iubetur tantum Magistratus eorum, qui armamenta Reipublicæ debebant, nomina dare nauium Curatoribus, vt illi vicissim tradant Trierarchis & classium Curatoribus, vt hi ista repetant armamenta ab iis, qui illa Reipublicæ debent. Rescribendum est igitur: Τοῦτο τοίνυν τῆς ψηφίσματος γεγραμμένου, ἢ μὲν ἀρχὴ ἐπικληρῶσι, id est, facto hoc Psephismate, id Magistratus præstitit, & executioni mandauit. Sequitur: ὁ δὲ νόμος ὁ τῆς Γεειαίδρου, ἰωάλκαζε καὶ ἀποσπάσπῃ τοῖς ὀφείλουσι τὰ σκεύη, καθ' ὃν αἱ Συμμοείαι σύνεπάσθησαν. Vt vulgo illa eduntur, diceres hunc, nescio quem Periandrum auctorem fuisse τῆς Συμμοείας, quod an verum sit, nescio, cum aliunde mihi non constet, hoc tamen scio Demosthenem non habuisse in animo iddocere his verbis, sed tantum Trierarchos & Curatores classium repetiisse armamenta quemque ab iis, qui suæ erant classis: vnde is, cui Orationem scribit Demosthenes, repetiit à Demochare & Theophemo, qui eiusdem secum erant classis: ἐπειχον δὲ ἐγὼ μὲν τεινεφρχῶν[?], ἢ Ἐπιμεληταὶ ὧν τῆς Συμμοείας, Δημοχάρης ἢ ὁ Παιαιεὺς, ἐν τῇ συμμοείᾳ ὢν, καὶ ὀφείλων τῇ πόλει σκεύη μὲ Θεοφήμου ζωτοῦ, Σωστεινάρχης ἀμόλμος. Scribo igitur: ὁ δὲ νόμος ὁ τῆς Γεειαίδρου, ἰωάλκαζε καὶ ἀποσπάσπῃ τοῖς ὀφείλουσι τὰ σκεύη, καθ' ὃν αἱ Συμμοείαι σύνεπάσθησαν. Recipiunto Trierarchi & classium Curatores nomina eorum, qui armamenta debent, è quibus classes suæ constituuntur quisque recipito. Repetere autem multum Trierarchorum & classium Curatorum intererat, vbi nomina eorum, qui armamenta debebant, accepissent; nam ipsi reddere cogebantur Reipublicæ, aut successoribus suis tradere. Demosthenes hac ipsa Oratione: ἀλλ' ὅτο ἐν μὲν τῶν πρότερον αὐτὸς ἐκπλεῖν χρόνον[?] ἠυχίαν ἐξῆν, ἔως ἐγὼ τε ἐκπλέω, ἐὰν αἱ νῆες, ἡ χρήσιμος ἐξήμπτει, καὶ ἐμὲ δ' οὐκ ἄφλε σκεῦη, τῇ πόλῃ αἰσχυνθῆναι ἀποδοῦναι, ἡ[?] τῶν ἀνδρῶν[?], ὡς δὲ ἔλθη ἐκ τῆς συμμορίας ὅτι τῶν ναυῶν. τί γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἡ πελεγον αὐτοί, ψηφίσματα, καὶ νόμους προσχωμένας, ὡς παραχωρῆσαι ἐμὲ εἰσαγαγεῖν τὰ σκεύη. Si vero is, qui armamenta debebat, denegaret, aut moras necteret, in ius ad exercitus nauales præfectos & naualium Curatores, qui iudices sortiebantur in his causis, vocabatur. Demosthenes eadem Oratione: παραγγελλέσθω μὲν παρὰς τε τοῖς Ἀποστόλαις, ἡ παρὰς τοὺς τῶν νεωρίων Ἐπιμελητὰς. ὅτι γὰρ εἰσῆγον τότε τὰς ἀμφιδικασίας εἰς ὃ δικαστήριον, περὶ τῶν σκευῶν. Quod si omnino reddere nollet, Lege licebat post iudicium ab eo iam damnato pignora capere.
units.tr: Demosthenes praises this law, if the title does not misname its author, and [illegible, about 30 letters] to another and to Mnesicoulos. He teaches that the man to whom he wrote this speech, who was a trierarch and curator of his own fleet, demanded the ship's rigging from Demochares and Theophemus, which they had not returned to the Republic, because the law of Periander so provided; and besides, by a decree of the people, some magistrate, I know not who, was ordered to give the names of those who owed rigging to the Republic to the curators of the ships. The curators of the ships were ordered to give these to the trierarchs performing their duty and to the curators of the fleets. Under the law of Periander, the curators of the fleets and the trierarchs were compelled to take down the names of those who owed rigging to the Republic, each from his own fleet, and to demand the rigging from them. Moreover, another decree ordered the trierarchs and the curators of the fleets to divide their tasks between themselves, so that one would demand the Republic's rigging from another. Therefore, by a decree of the people, the rigging was to be demanded from those trierarchs who owed it to the Republic, under the law of Periander, so that the trierarchs and curators of the fleets should each demand it from those in their own fleet. Hence this man, to whom Demosthenes wrote this speech, since he was both trierarch and curator of his own fleet, was obliged to demand the rigging from those who owed it to the Republic and belonged to his fleet. Finally, the later decree was the reason why, when one was to demand from another [illegible, about 20 letters], this man of ours was compelled to demand from Demochares and Theophemus [Σωτει- illegible, about 25 letters], who had been assigned to him. [illegible, about 70 letters] [illegible, about 60 letters] [illegible, about 50 letters]. [Greek fragments, largely illegible: the curators of the dockyards, to the trierarchs of the ship which sails ... or the curators of the ... to those in the symmory. The law of Geraiadros ... to those who owe the equipment ..., according to which the symmories were ... Since this is so, since a decree of the people ... to each of the debtors of the equipment ... I was trierarch, and curator of the symmory. Demochares of Paiania, in the symmory, owing equipment to the city with Theophemus ..., Sosteinarchos ... Since both were written as owing the city's equipment, the magistrate, removing them from the fourth office, delivered them to us according to the law and the decrees.] But here some things in the words of Demosthenes must be noted, which are corrupt. The text is printed: "Therefore, when this decree had been written, the magistrate [ἐπικληρῶσι] ... delivered those who owed the city's equipment; and the curators of the dockyards, to the trierarchs who sail ..., or to the curators of the symmory." The word ἐπικληρῶσι does not belong here, in my judgment, for no allotment is in question; the magistrate is ordered by this decree only to give the names of those who owed equipment to the Republic to the curators of the ships. Although he does not say this in express words, it may nonetheless be gathered from his writing that the curators of the ships gave the same names to the trierarchs and the curators of the fleets; yet the curators of the ships had received them from others. Hence he says in what follows: "who owed the city's equipment, the magistrate ... [Curators of the ships] removing them from the fourth office" (of which he said: "the magistrate allotted, and delivered those who owed the city's equipment"), "delivered them to us according to the law, and by the decrees." If some allotment had been made, the man to whom Demosthenes wrote this speech would have had a reason to plead exemption, and he would undoubtedly not have omitted it. But, as I said, no allotment was made; the magistrate is only ordered to give the names of those who owed equipment to the Republic to the curators of the ships, so that they in turn may hand them to the trierarchs and the curators of the fleets, so that these may demand the equipment from those who owe it to the Republic. It must therefore be rewritten: "When this decree had been written, the magistrate [ἐπικληρῶσι]," that is, "when this decree had been made, the magistrate carried it out and put it into execution." There follows: "the law of Geraiadros ... and demanded from those who owed the equipment, according to which the symmories were ..." As these words are commonly printed, one would take this Periander, whoever he was, as the author of the symmory; whether that is true I do not know, since it is not otherwise established for me. I do know this much, however: Demosthenes did not intend to teach this by these words, but only that the trierarchs and curators of the fleets demanded the rigging each from those of his own fleet. Hence the man to whom Demosthenes writes this speech demanded it from Demochares and Theophemus, who belonged to the same fleet as himself. [Greek: and I was trierarch, and curator of the symmory, Demochares of Paiania, being in the symmory, and owing equipment to the city with Theophemus ..., Sosteinarchos ...]. I write therefore: "The law of Geraiadros ... and demanded from those who owe the equipment, according to which the symmories were arranged." The trierarchs and curators of the fleets shall take down the names of those who owe the equipment, from which each shall take down his own fleets. It was of great importance to the trierarchs and curators of the fleets to demand the equipment after they had received the names of those who owed it; for they themselves were compelled to return it to the Republic, or to hand it to their successors. Demosthenes in this same speech: [Greek: but, while I was on a voyage, the ships were sailing for a time in quiet; when I sailed, if the ships were useful, and I did not take the equipment away, it was shameful to return it to the city, ... of the men; but when it came out of the symmory with the ships. For what did they themselves order, decrees and laws proposed, so that I might be allowed to bring in the equipment.] But if he who owed the equipment refused, or delayed, he was summoned to court before the naval commanders and the curators of the dockyards, who drew the judges for such cases. Demosthenes in the same speech: [Greek: let him be summoned either before the Apostoloi or before the curators of the dockyards. For at that time they brought the cases of this kind into court, concerning the equipment.] If he still refused to return it altogether, the law allowed that, after judgment had been given against him, pledges could be seized from him.

units.la: Τὸν ὀφείλοντα τὰ σκεύη τῇ πόλῃ, ἢ ἀποδι-δόναι τὰ σκεύη· εἰ δὲ μή, ἐσχυρὰς λήψε- σθαι.
units.tr: The man who owes the city its equipment must either return the equipment; otherwise he shall be subject to seizure.

units.la: Legem laudat Demosthenes hac ipsa Oratione, è cuius serie constat Theophemum iudicio iam fuisse damnatum. ἡ ἀξιοῦν πάλιν τὸν Θεόφημον, ἡ ἀποδοῦναι τὰ σκεύη· εἰ δὲ μή, ἐσχυρὰς ἔφλω λήψεσθαι κατὰ τὸ τοὺς νόμους ἡ τὰ ψηφίσματα.
units.tr: Demosthenes cites this law in the same speech, from whose sequence it is clear that Theophemus had already been condemned in a trial. "Either Theophemus must be required to return the equipment, or, if he does not, he shall be seized [for the sum], in accordance with the laws or the decrees." [ἢ ἀξιοῦν πάλιν τὸν Θεόφημον, ἢ ἀποδοῦναι τὰ σκεύη· εἰ δὲ μή, ἐσχυρὰς ἔφλω λήψεσθαι κατὰ τὸ τοὺς νόμους ἢ τὰ ψηφίσματα.]

units.la: Verum quoniam hic sumus, paucula addamus necesse est, quæ facient ad circumscribendum angustioribus spatiis tempus, intra quod institutum est, ut mille ducenti ad obeunda Trierarchiarum munera seponerentur, ἡ συνεκχ[?]δικα ἤσαν οἱ Τριήραρχοι, & sedeni unam instruerent triremem. Diximus in superioribus, Nicophemo Athenis Prætore, anno quarto Olympiadis centesimæ quartæ, adhuc σὺν δυο fuisse τοὺς Τριηράρχους. Quando is, cui hanc Orationem scripsit Demosthenes, Trierarchus fuit, iam mille ducenti sepositi erant ad obeunda Trierarchiarum munia, iam συνεκχ[?]δικα ἤσαν οἱ Τριήραρχοι. Nam armamenta præbebat Respublica, ut ex Orationis argumento & contextu manifestum fit, sola nave militabant συνεκχ[?]δικα οἱ Τριήραρχοι. Trierarchus autem ille fuit anno quarto Olympiadis centesimæ quintæ, Agathocle Archonte, quod ex his Orationis eius liquet: καὶ ταῦτα ὡς ἀληθῆ λέγω, ὑμῖν τε λέγω, ὅτι ἐξουλλον ἐπὶ Ἀγαθοκλέους Ἄρχοντος Φαῦλλη τῆς Ἀθηναίων Δημοῦς. Ergo ante hunc annum quartum Olympiadis centesimæ quintæ, sed tamen post annum quartum Olympiadis centesimæ quartæ, lata est hæc Lex, ut sedeni unam præberent navem. Quare quæ eadem Oratione ab illo dicuntur: ἐξ αἰτίας τῶν λόγων μοι ταχαμεδαύῃ, ἐπὶ ὁ τῶν ἐμπορεύεσθαι χρόνῳ πολλαὶ τριηραρχίαι τετριηραρχηκῶς ζῶντ ποτ' ἐπλεον σκεῦη ἐκ τῆς νεωρίου. ἀλλ' αὐτὸς ἰδίᾳ προσαδίᾳ, ὅπως δεῖ, ἵνα ὡς ἐληλυθὼς ἐχθραῖνοντες τοῖς λόγοις ἔχοιμι τοῖς πόλει. Rhetorica sunt, & ex artis præcepto, non autem ex vero: quod enim armamenta domo ipse attulerit antea, si unam aut alteram τετριηραρχῆσθαι excipias, fiebat ex Lege & populi Athenienstis instituto: nam ὅτι συνῳδυο ἤσαν οἱ Τριήραρχοι, καὶ τὰ δυάλω-μένα πάντα ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων εἶχον, καὶ τὰς ναῦς ἐπλήρωσαν αὐτοῖς, ut alibi Demosthenes scripsit.
units.tr: But since we are here, we must add a few points that bear on narrowing the period, within which it was ordained that twelve hundred men should be set aside to perform the duties of trierarchs, and that the trierarchs should together equip one trireme each. I said above that, when Nicophemus was praetor at Athens, in the fourth year of the 104th Olympiad, the trierarchs were still [paired together] [σὺν δυο] [the trierarchs] [τοὺς Τριηράρχους]. When he to whom Demosthenes addressed this speech served as trierarch, the twelve hundred had already been set aside for the trierarchic duties, and the trierarchs were already [sharing the cost] [συνεκχ[?]δικα ἤσαν οἱ Τριήραρχοι]. For the Republic supplied the rigging, as is plain from the argument and context of the speech, and the trierarchs [sharing the cost] [συνεκχ[?]δικα οἱ Τριήραρχοι] served only with the ship. That trierarch served in the fourth year of the 105th Olympiad, in the archonship of Agathocles, as is clear from these words of the speech: "And I say this is true; I tell you that it was in the archonship of Agathocles, when Phaulles was of the tribe of Demos..." [καὶ ταῦτα ὡς ἀληθῆ λέγω, ὑμῖν τε λέγω, ὅτι ἐξουλλον ἐπὶ Ἀγαθοκλέους Ἄρχοντος Φαῦλλη τῆς Ἀθηναίων Δημοῦς.] Therefore this law, that they should equip one ship each, was passed before the fourth year of the 105th Olympiad, but after the fourth year of the 104th. Hence what Demosthenes says in the same speech: "Because of the words I have spoken, I was made trierarch many times in the time when I was sailing with ships from the arsenal... but I myself, by my own resources, as was required, so that as one who has served I might be useful to the city..." [ἐξ αἰτίας τῶν λόγων μοι ταχαμεδαύῃ, ἐπὶ ὁ τῶν ἐμπορεύεσθαι χρόνῳ πολλαὶ τριηραρχίαι τετριηραρχηκῶς ζῶντ ποτ' ἐπλεον σκεῦη ἐκ τῆς νεωρίου. ἀλλ' αὐτὸς ἰδίᾳ προσαδίᾳ, ὅπως δεῖ, ἵνα ὡς ἐληλυθὼς ἐχθραῖνοντες τοῖς λόγοις ἔχοιμι τοῖς πόλει.] These are rhetorical flourishes, following the precepts of the art, and not the truth. For that he had previously furnished the rigging from his own house (except perhaps for one or two occasions when he [served as trierarch] [τετριηραρχῆσθαι]) happened by law and the institution of the Athenian people. For, as Demosthenes wrote elsewhere, "the trierarchs were [paired] [ὅτι συνῳδυο ἤσαν οἱ Τριήραρχοι], and they had all the necessary expenses from their own resources, and they equipped the ships for themselves."

units.la: Finito Trierarchiæ constituto tempore, designati Trierarchi, qui aliis succedebant, debebant postquam designati fuerant, abire ad naues, ex hac Lege: Τοὺς ἀλφυρχίας ἀπιέναι ἐπὶ τὰς ναῦς, ὅταν καταςαθῶσιν. Designati Trierarchiæ successores ad naues abeunto, ubi designati fuerint.
units.tr: When the set time of the trierarchy had ended, the designated trierarchs who were to succeed the others were obliged, once they had been designated, to go to the ships under this law: "Those designated for the trierarchy shall go to the ships when they have been appointed." [Τοὺς ἀλφυρχίας ἀπιέναι ἐπὶ τὰς ναῦς, ὅταν καταςαθῶσιν.] The designated successors of the trierarchs are to go to the ships once they have been designated.

units.la: Legis meminit Demosthenes ἐν τῷ πρὸς Πολυκλέα ὑπὲρ τριηραρχήματος, ὅτι ἡ ὡς ἐμοὶ ἰδίων μᾶλλον λειτουργιῶν Πολυκλέα, ἡ ἐπὶ ὑμῶν αὐτὸν, οὐδὲ τὸν τριηράρχων ὑπὸ μίσθου ποιησάμενον μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν μισθοῦντα τῶν τριηρῶν, ὥστε μήτε τοῖς λειτουργοῦσιν ἀγωνίζεσθαι, μήτε τοῖς ἀφοδίοις καταφέρειν τὴν νόμον· ἀλλ' ἀπιέναι ὅτι εἰς τὰς ναῦς, ὅταν καταςαθῶσιν. Atque multæ Legibus irrogabantur iis, si præfinito tempore nam accepissent.
units.tr: Demosthenes mentions this law in his speech against Polycles concerning the trierarchy: "...that Polycles, in my opinion, should not only be called to account for the public services, but also before you, not only the trierarch who took the ship for hire, but also the one who let it out, so that they neither contend against those performing the service nor fail to bring forward the appointed ones; but they must go to the ships when they have been appointed." And many penalties were imposed by the laws on those who had accepted the ship at the appointed time.

units.la: Εαὶ τις μὴ ἐξαδίξηται τὴν ναῦν ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τῷ εἰρημένῳ, ἐπίτιμα [?] ἔστω. . . .
units.tr: "If anyone does not take over the ship within the stated time, let him be liable to a penalty..." [Εαὶ τις μὴ ἐξαδίξηται τὴν ναῦν ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τῷ εἰρημένῳ, ἐπίτιμα [?] ἔστω. . . .]

units.la: Si quis præfinito tempore nauem non acceperit, multator. . . .
units.tr: If anyone does not take over a ship within the set time, he shall be fined. . . .

units.la: Multam non expressit Demosthenes Oratione proxime laudata, è quo Legis fragmentum descripsimus. βούλεσθαι δ' ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ νόμῳ διαγωνωθῆναι τὴν πε-ρὶ τῶν ἀφοδίων, ἵνα εἰδῆτε, πλίκων τῶν ἐπιτιμίων ὄντων, ἐὰν τις μὴ ἐξαδίξηται τὴν ναῦν ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τῷ εἰρημένῳ, καταφεύγοντι οὐχ ἑμοῦ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑμῶν, καὶ τῶν νόμων. Itaque Strategorum erat, eos, vt nauem suscipernt, cogere, qui ad eas successores venerant. Demosthenes loco laudato: ἴσως οὖν, ὦ ἀνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, ποθεῖτε ἀκοῦσαι ἀφ' ἡ τότε ὁ Στρατηγὸς οὐκ ἐλάσκεξε τὴν τριηραρχίαν τὴν ναῦν, ἀφοδίζειν ἡκοντα ἐπ' αὐτὸν, τῶν νόμων ὥσπερ ἰχυρὰν ὄντων.
units.tr: Demosthenes did not state the fine in the speech just cited, from which we have taken the fragment of the law. "Now you wish to have the law read concerning the handover, so that you may know how great the penalties are if anyone does not take over the ship within the stated time; he has recourse not only to me, but also to you and to the laws." [βούλεσθαι δ' ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ νόμῳ διαγωνωθῆναι τὴν περὶ τῶν ἀφοδίων, ἵνα εἰδῆτε, πλίκων τῶν ἐπιτιμίων ὄντων, ἐὰν τις μὴ ἐξαδίξηται τὴν ναῦν ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τῷ εἰρημένῳ, καταφεύγοντι οὐχ ἑμοῦ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑμῶν, καὶ τῶν νόμων.] Therefore it was the duty of the generals to compel those who had come as successors to take over the ships. Demosthenes, in the passage cited: "Perhaps, then, men of Athens, you wish to hear from the time when the general did not drive out the trierarchy... the ship, when he came to hand it over to him, as the laws were strong." [ἴσως οὖν, ὦ ἀνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, ποθεῖτε ἀκοῦσαι ἀφ' ἡ τότε ὁ Στρατηγὸς οὐκ ἐλάσκεξε τὴν τριηραρχίαν τὴν ναῦν, ἀφοδίζειν ἡκοντα ἐπ' αὐτὸν, τῶν νόμων ὥσπερ ἰχυρὰν ὄντων.]

units.la: Iubentur Lege Trierarchi rationes referre obiti à se Trierarchiæ muneris.
units.tr: By law the trierarchs are ordered to render an account of the trierarchic duty they have discharged.

units.la: Τοῖς Τριηράρχοις [?] ἀπολύουσι ἔστω. Trierarchi muneris sui rationes referunto.
units.tr: "Let the trierarchs, when they are released, render their accounts." [Τοῖς Τριηράρχοις [?] ἀπολύουσι ἔστω.] The trierarchs are to render an account of their trierarchic duty.

units.la: Legem laudat Æschines ἐν τῷ κτησιφῶντος. πάλιν τοῖς τριηράρχοις ἀπολυ-όντοις ἔστω· κελεύει ὁ νόμος, οὐ τὰ καινὰ ἀφελείσθαι, οὐδὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ὑμετέρων πεσοῦσαν πολλὰ μὲν ὑφαιρούμενον, βεαχία ἢ καταπίπτειν, ἐπιδιδόναι δὲ φάσκοντας, ἀποδιδόντας δὲ ὑμῖν τὰ ὑμέτερα. Ἀλλ' ὁμολογουμένως τὰς πατρῷας οὐσίας εἰς τὸ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἀνθρώπους φιλοτιμίαν.
units.tr: Aeschines cites the law in his speech against Ctesiphon: "Again, let the trierarchs, when they are released, [render their accounts]. The law orders that they not take away the new things, nor take away much from what has fallen from your property, nor claim that they have added to it, and return your property to you. But they confess that they have spent their patrimonies on rivalry with you men..." [πάλιν τοῖς τριηράρχοις ἀπολυ-όντοις ἔστω· κελεύει ὁ νόμος, οὐ τὰ καινὰ ἀφελείσθαι, οὐδὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ὑμετέρων πεσοῦσαν πολλὰ μὲν ὑφαιρούμενον, βεαχία ἢ καταπίπτειν, ἐπιδιδόναι δὲ φάσκοντας, ἀποδιδόντας δὲ ὑμῖν τὰ ὑμέτερα. Ἀλλ' ὁμολογουμένως τὰς πατρῷας οὐσίας εἰς τὸ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἀνθρώπους φιλοτιμίαν.]

units.la: Cum graue admodum esset onus Ἀλφυρχίαν, neque omnes ferendo pares essent, succurrit Solon lata ἀφοδίων Lege; eius quippe auctor Solon, vt ex his Demosthenis verbis ἐν τῷ πρὸς Φαίνιππον constat: ἔπειτα δὲ, καὶ Σόλων τὸν νομοθέτην, τὸν ἀφοδίων νόμον. Quanuis enim post Solonem institutum paululum mutauerit, & Naufinico Prætore Athenienses distribuæti sint εἰς Συμμορίας, deinde mille ac ducenti sepositi ad obeunda grauissima Trierarchiarum munera, atque ex his selecti trecenti, nihilo tamen minus obtinuerunt semper Solonis ἀφοδίων Leges accommodatæ tantum ad distributionem ciuium post Solonem vsu receptam: Sunt autem Legis ἀφοδίων Kapita hæc.
units.tr: Since the burden of the trierarchy was very heavy, and not all were equal to bearing it, Solon came to the rescue by a law on the handover (ἀφοδίων). For Solon was its author, as is clear from these words of Demosthenes in the speech against Phaenippus: "Then also Solon, the lawgiver, [proposed] the law on handovers." For although after Solon's time the institution was somewhat altered, and under the praetor Nausinicus the Athenians were divided into groups (symmoriae), and then twelve hundred were set aside to undertake the very heavy trierarchic duties, and three hundred were chosen from these, nevertheless the laws of Solon on handovers always remained in force, adapted only to the distribution of citizens that came into use after Solon. These are the chapters of the law on handovers.

units.la: Καθ' ἕκαστον ἔτος ἐπὶ ποιῆσαι τὰς ἀφοδίας.
units.tr: "Each year let the exchanges be made." [Καθ' ἕκαστον ἔτος ἐπ[ι]ποιεῖσθαι τὰς ἀφοδίας.]

units.la: Quotannis ad facultatem permutationes prouocanto.
units.tr: Each year, let the parties be called to exchange their property.

units.la: Τὸν εἰς ἀλφυρχίαν τινὰ χρεωπονούμενον ὑπεξελθεῖν ἐκ τῆς σώματος, εἴ τινα ἑαυτῷ πλουσιώτερον ὁρᾷ ἐπιδείκνυε. καὶ εἰ μὲν ὁ πεφωλημένος ὁμολογῇ πλουσιώτερος εἶναι, εἰς τοὺς τεσσαράκοντα ἀνήχεται. εἰ δὲ ἠρνήσατο, τὸν ὑδίαν ἀμφοτέρων.
units.tr: "The man designated for some trierarchic duty may withdraw from the group, if he sees someone richer than himself and points him out. If the one who was named admits that he is richer, he is to be entered in the three hundred in place of the other; if he denies it, they shall exchange their property with each other." [Τὸν εἰς ἀλφυρχίαν τινὰ χρεωπονούμενον ὑπεξελθεῖν ἐκ τῆς σώματος, εἴ τινα ἑαυτῷ πλουσιώτερον ὁρᾷ ἐπιδείκνυε. καὶ εἰ μὲν ὁ πεφωλημένος ὁμολογῇ πλουσιώτερος εἶναι, εἰς τοὺς τεσσαράκοντα ἀνήχεται. εἰ δὲ ἠρνήσατο, τὸν ὑδίαν ἀμφοτέρων.]

units.la: Sepositus ad obeunda munera classe sua excedito, si quem se locupletiorem vacantem ostenderit. Si is, qui designatus est, locupletiorem se esse fassus sit, in trecentos alterius loco referior: si neget, facultates inter se permutanto.
units.tr: "A man designated to perform the duties should withdraw from his class, if he points out someone richer who is free [for the service]. If the man who has been designated admits that he is richer, he shall be referred back into the three hundred in place of the other; if he denies it, they shall exchange their property between themselves."

units.la: Γαρ ... τὰ εἰκήματα τῆς ἀπογραφῆς [illegible, ~12 letters].
units.tr: For ... the ... of the registration [illegible, about twelve letters].

units.la: Eius, qui ad facultatem permutationem prouocatus est, ædes obsignantor.
units.tr: The house of the man who has been summoned to an exchange of property is to be sealed.

units.la: ΤΟΥΣ ΑΝΤΙΔΟΝΤΑΣ ΑΛΛΗΛΟΙΣ, ΟΤΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΑΝΤΕΣ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ-ΣΙ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΠΡΟΣΟ-ΜΝΥΕΙΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟΝΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΟΡ-ΚΟΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΜΑΥΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙ-ΚΑΙΩΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΡΓΟΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΕΙΟΙΣ ΟΣΑ ΟΙ ΝΟΜΟΙ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΠΕΠΟΙΗΚΑΣΙ. ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ, ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟ-ΣΗ, ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ.
units.tr: "Those who exchange property with each other, when they have sworn, shall declare their property and shall remain bound by the oath in the following words: I shall declare my property rightly and justly, except those things which are in the silver mines, which the laws have made exempt. They shall give the declaration within three days from the day on which they swear." [ΤΟΥΣ ΑΝΤΙΔΟΝΤΑΣ ΑΛΛΗΛΟΙΣ, ΟΤΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΑΝΤΕΣ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ-ΣΙ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΠΡΟΣΟ-ΜΝΥΕΙΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟΝΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΟΡ-ΚΟΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΜΑΥΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙ-ΚΑΙΩΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΡΓΟΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΕΙΟΙΣ ΟΣΑ ΟΙ ΝΟΜΟΙ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΠΕΠΟΙΗΚΑΣΙ. ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ, ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟ-ΣΗ, ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ.]

units.la: Qui facultates inter se permutant, se indicaturos facultates suas iuranto his conceptis verbis: Indicabo facultates meas rectè & iuste, exceptis iis, quae in argentifodinis sunt, quas Leges immunes faciunt. Intra tres, ex quo iurarunt, dies facultates suas indicanto.
units.tr: Those who exchange their property with one another, having sworn, shall declare their property, swearing in these words: "I shall declare my property rightly and justly, except those things which are in the silver mines, which the laws have made exempt. Within three days from the day on which they swear, they shall make the declaration."

units.la: Cum igitur, vt diximus, Athenienses patres non erant ferendo τῷ λειτουργῶν oneri, subuenit illis Solon hac Lege: Καθ' ἕκαστον ἔτος τοῖς [?] ποιεῖν τὰς ἀντιδόσεις. Quotannis ad facultatum permutationes pronocanto. Idque puto, maxime institutum propter Trierarchiarum munera: quanquam etiam fiebant ἀντιδόσεις propter χορηγίας. Docet Demosthenes in Leptinea: οὔπω φυλὴ πώποτε ἐναγκαίη [?] ἐπλήρωσεν [?] Χορηγόν, ὅτι ἐνεχείρησεν αὐτὸς ἄλλος ἀντιδοῦναι, & in Midiana: Τραγωδὸς χορηγήσαι ποτε [?] ἐγὼ ὁ αὐλητὴς αἰσθάνομαι [?] ὅτι τὴν ὁ ἀνάλωμα ἐκείνης τῆς δαπάνης πολλῷ πλέον ἐστίν, ἀλλὰς ἀγεσθαι δήπου. καὶ γὰρ ἐπιλεκτὴς τῶν. [?] Sed maxime fiebant propter Trierarchias, idque apud Strategum. Demosthenes ἐν τῷ πρὸς Φαιν[?]πον. Ἀλλὰ τὴν γὰρ οἱ νόμοι καθ' ἕκαστον ἔτος ποιοῦσι τὰς ἀντιδόσεις, ὅτι ὃ διδ[?]ν σ[?]ν[?] ἡ οὐσία, οὐ πολλοὶς τὴν πολιτὴν ἀξιωσμένη εἰ[?] τὰς ἀντιδόσεις. Fiebat autem ἀντιδόσεως hoc modo. Si quis è trecentis, qui sepositi erant ad obeundas Trierarchias, sumptus tolerare non posset, Lege licebat ea classe excedere, si quem se locupletiorem vocantem offendisset. Quod si is qui designabatur, se ditiorem esse fateretur, in trecentos alterius loco referebatur: si negaret, permutabant inter se facultates Hypothesis Orationis Demosthenis ... Suidas: τοὺς εἰς λειτουργίαν τινὰ ... ἀντιδιδόναι. Is qui citauerat atque designauerat alterum, qui vicem suam munus Trierarchiae obiret, eius aedes obsignabat, ne qua inde alio exportarentur, ex hac Lege, [?]. Eius, qui ad facultatum permutationem pronocatus est, aedes obsignantor. Meminit non semel Demosthenes Oratione laudata: αὐτὸ δὲ τῆς τὰ σημεῖα ἐκ τῆς οἰκημάτων, ἀ προσημαίνειν, ἐλθὼν εἰς ἀγρὸν ἀνέῳξε, καὶ τὰς κειλὰς ἐξεφόρησε, καὶ τὰ ἄλλα. Sed totum hunc morem ita graphice ibidem describit DemoDemosthenes, vt in rem præsentem deducere videatur. ἐξ ἀρχῆς δ' ὑμῖν ἀ-πάντα τὰ ῥηθέντα ἐπὶ τῷ αἰτίᾳ διηγήσομαι. τῷ γὰρ Μεγαλοπολίτῃ μέλλως, ὦ ἄν-δρες δικασταί, τῇ δευτέρᾳ ἰσαυθίς, ἐπαίνων οἱ Σπαρτιῆται τῆς πεποιημένης τὰς αἰτιάσεις. ἐπὶ τούτοις ἐκάλεσα τὸν νόμον Φαίδρου τοῦ Τυρδάρου(?) καλέσας δ' ἐν ταῖς ἀδελφῶν ἀπεδίδου ἐκ τῆς ἐχαρίας ἄπ' ἀντί. καὶ ἔφη τὸν νόμου ἐπεκανομοίως ὑπ' ἀλλήλων ἐξαρτῆσαι πλέον ἢ ἀφ' ὧν ἐπαισθῆσαι. κυκλῳ ἐδίδα καὶ ἐδεμοσκοπούμενος ὅ[?] ὅπο Φαίδρου, ὅτι ἐαν ἔτυχε ἐχαρίᾳ. Hisperactis & ædibus obsignatis, is qui prouocabat ad facultatum permutationem, ad sacra vocabat eum quem suo loco obire munera volebat. Demosthenes verbis, quæ paullo ante descripsimus. καὶ ἐπαισχύνας ὅτι τὰ ἱερὰ Φαίδρου τὸν νόμον ἀπώλεσεν, ὡς χρήμων ἀπὼν εἰς ἄχρον. nempe inter hæc tacra iusiurandum ab vtroque concipiebatur ex hac Lege: ΤΟΥΣ ΑΝΤΙΔΙΔΟΝ-ΤΑΣ ΑΛΛΗΛΟΙΣ ΟΤΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΑΝΤΕΣ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩΣΙ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΠΡΟΣΟΜΝΥΕΙΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟΝΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΟΡΚΟΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΜΑΥΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΩΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΡΓΟΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΕΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣΑ ΟΙ ΝΟΜΟΙ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΓΕΠΟΙΗΚΑΣΙ. Qui facultates inter se permutant, se suas indicaturos facultates iuranto conceptis his verbis. Indico facultates meas recte atque iuste, exceptis iis, quæ in argentifodinis sunt, quas Leges immunes faciunt. Laudat hanc Legem Demosthenes ἐν τῷ πρὸς Φαίδρον. Καὶ κατηγορῶ τῆς ὅρκου, ὃν ὠ-μοσα περὶ τῆς ἀποφάσεως, λέγων, ὅτι πλὴν τὴν ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις ὑπεισφέρω ἀποφαί-νειν τὴν ἄλλην οὐσίαν, ὥσπερ ὃ κ' ἐς νόμος ὁμοίως, τὸ δ' ἄξιον κατηγορεῖας ἐν. ὑμεῖς δ' ἔχε, ὦ ἄνδρες δικασταί. ὑμεῖς γὰρ ἐτάξατε τὸν νόμον, ὃς δ[?] ἀπορρήδην οὕτω λέγει, ΤΟΥΣ ΑΝΓΙΔΙΔΟΝΤΑΣ ΑΛΛΗΛΟΙΣ, &c. Indicare igitur oportebat omnes suas facultates, præterquam eas, quæ in fodinis sunt, Lege enim non tenentur.
units.tr: Therefore, as we said, since the Athenian fathers could not bear the burden of the liturgies, Solon came to their aid by this law: "Each year let the exchanges be proposed." [Καθ' ἕκαστον ἔτος τοῖς [?] ποιεῖν τὰς ἀντιδόσεις.] I think this was instituted chiefly on account of the trierarchic duties, although exchanges also took place because of the choregiae. Demosthenes shows this in the speech against Leptines: "No tribe has ever yet equipped a chorus-leader, since another has undertaken to exchange..." And in the speech against Meidias: "When a tragic poet has ever furnished a chorus, I, the flute-player, perceive that the cost of that expense is much greater..." But most exchanges took place because of the trierarchies, and that before the general. Demosthenes in the speech against Phaenippus: "But the laws require exchanges each year, since the property is not sufficient for..., and many have been summoned to the exchanges." The summons was made in this way: if someone from the three hundred, who had been set aside for the trierarchies, could not bear the expense, the law allowed him to withdraw from that class if he found someone richer whom he could name. If the man who was designated admitted that he was wealthier, he was referred back into the three hundred in place of the other; if he denied it, they exchanged their property with one another. Hypothesis of Demosthenes' speech... Suidas: those summoned to some liturgy... to exchange. He who had summoned and designated the other to perform his trierarchic duty in his place had the other's house sealed, lest anything be carried out of it elsewhere, under this law: "The house of the man who has been summoned to an exchange of property is to be sealed." Demosthenes mentions this more than once in the speech cited: "...and going into the country, he opened the sealed rooms, carried out the chests, and the rest." But Demosthenes describes this whole custom so vividly in the same place that he seems to bring the thing before our eyes: "From the beginning I shall narrate to you all that was said about the charge. For the Megalopolitan, men of the jury, was about to ... the second time, and the Spartans praised the accusations made. After this I summoned the law of Phaidros... and having summoned, he gave back in the sanctuaries the ... by a law..." Once these things were done and the houses sealed, he who had summoned the other to the exchange of property called to the sacred rites the man whom he wished to take his place in the duties. Demosthenes, in the words we quoted a little earlier: "And they were ashamed that the law of Phaidros had destroyed the sacred things, as a man absent in the Acropolis..." Namely, among these sacred rites an oath was taken by both parties under this law: "Those who exchange their property with each other, when they have sworn, shall declare their property and shall remain bound by the oath in the following words: I shall declare my property rightly and justly, except those things which are in the silver mines, which the laws have made exempt." Demosthenes cites this law in the speech against Phaidros: "And I accuse the oath which I swore concerning the declaration, saying that, except for what is in the works, I am bringing forward the rest of the property as the law similarly says; but this is worthy of accusation. You, however, men of the jury, hold on. For you set the law which speaks thus in plain words: 'Those who exchange with each other,' etc." It was therefore necessary to declare all one's property, except what was in the mines, for these were not subject to the law.

units.la: Τῶν δὲ τὰς ἐργάσιας μηδὲν ἀποφαίνειν:
units.tr: Of those who declare nothing of their workshops or enterprises [Τῶν δὲ τὰς ἐργάσιας μηδὲν ἀποφαίνειν]

units.la: Meminit huius Legis præcedens, quam descripsimus: ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΜΑΥΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΩΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΡΓΟΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΕΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣΑ ΟΙ ΝΟΜΟΙ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΓΕΠΟΙΗΚΑΣΙ. Laudat Demosthenes hac Oratione. ὥσπερ δὲ μοι τὸν λόγον ἐκ[?] διάγωμεν, τὸν οὐκ ἐώντα τὴν ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις ἐσθεῖν ἀποφαίνειν.
units.tr: The preceding law, which we have set out, refers to this: I declare my property rightly and justly, except what is in the workings, the silver mines, which the laws have made exempt [ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΜΑΥΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΩΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΡΓΟΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΕΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣΑ ΟΙ ΝΟΜΟΙ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΓΕΠΟΙΗΚΑΣΙ]. Demosthenes praises this law in his speech: just as we pass over the argument that does not allow what is in the workings to be declared [ὥσπερ δὲ μοι τὸν λόγον ἐκ[?] διάγωμεν, τὸν οὐκ ἐώντα τὴν ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις ἐσθεῖν ἀποφαίνειν].

units.la: Indicium autem facultatum suarum intra tres, ex quo iurauerant, dies dare debebant ex hac Lege: ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΗι ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ. Intra tres, ex quo iurarunt, dies facultates suas indicanto. Legem laudat Demosthenes hac Oratione: ὁμοίως γὰρ τῇ ἐνδικίᾳ τῇ Βοηδρομιῶνος μηνὸς, ἀποφαίνειν ὀρθῶς & δικαίως τὴν οὐσίαν, τὸν νόμον ἀξιῶν λέγοντος, ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ, ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΗ. ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ. ἐδίκασα μὲν ταῦτα τοῦ δικαστηρίου μὴ Πολυάκτου καὶ Τερεντίου, ὥστε τὸν μὲν ἀπὸ Ἀλκιβιάδου ἐπιτιμῆσαι ἑαυτῷ· ἐπειτα τὴν ἀποφανσιν τῆς οὐσίας ἀναβαλέσθαι μὴ πολλὰς ἡμέρας. ὑπεπιμῶν δ' ἐγὼ ἐμαυτῷ μετὰ τὸν ἀπογραφόμενον εἰς τὸν δικαστὴν βασίλειον, ἐπιδείξω τὴν μὲν συνωδὸν τοῖς ταῦτα τὴν ἀδικίαν ἐπὶ τῆς ἀλγύσεως, τῇ ἰδίᾳ φίλοντος τὸν Βοηδρομιῶνος μηνὸς, ὁμολογήσαι ποιήσασθαι· τὴν δ' ἀποφανσιν τῆς οὐσίας, τῇ ἐκτῇ φίλοντος. Atque ex his supplendus est Demosthenis locus, qui hac primore Oratione legitur. αὐτὴ μὲν τῆς τελευτῆς ἡμέρας ἀφ' ἧς ὥμοσαν τὴν ἀποφανσιν δοῦναί μοι τῆς οὐσίας τῆς αὐτοῦ χρὴ τὸν νόμον, ἢ εἰ μὴ πότε εἰσοῖλεται, τῇ γὰρ ἐκτῇ δοῦναι τῆς Βοηδρομιῶνος μηνὸς, ὧν δείξεις μου εἴπετο, καὶ οὐ ἡ ὁμολόγησιν δώσειν τὴν ἀποφανσιν. Rescribendum enim est, ex iis quae ante descripsimus: τῇ γὰρ ἐκτῇ δοῦναι φήνοντος τῆς Βοηδρομιῶνος μηνὸς, ὧν δείξεις μου εἴπετο. Rursum meminit huius Legis: ἀλλ' ἀλλ' εἰς δύο νόμους ἔχει πρὸς ὑμᾶς ταξιαρχικοὺς, ἕνα μὲν, τὸν χελιοντα τελευτῆς ἡμέρας, ἀφ' ἧς αὐ ὁμοίον, τὴν οὐσίαν ἀποφαίνειν. Eaque maxime nititur, & invidiam facit Phaenippo: ἔστιν ὁ δεύτερος μὲν τὴν ἀποφανσιν ἐδωκας μοι, τὸν νόμον κελεύοντας τελευτῆς ἡμερῶν, ὧν ἥκει δανείσαι, καὶ ἐφλήμεταί πλέον, ἡ τελευτῶν ταλάντων. Scripto dabatur hoc indicium. Harpocration: ἀποφασις, ὁ ἀποφαίνειν ἀφ' γραμμὴ χρὴ μέρος ὁποῖον ὕστερ ἐχέ. ἂν δὲ τῆς ἐπιδόσεως μάλιστα ἡ ἱᾶς. Dabatur Strategis hoc indicium. Demosthenes hac Oratione: εἰς ὃ Στρατηγὸν εἴδωκε τὴν ἀποφανσιν. rursum: ἀπηγγέλλει ὡς τὰς Στρατηγοὺς τοῦτο τὴν ἀπογραφὴν. Litigantibus Strategi iudices sortiebantur. εἰσῆγεσαν οἱ Στρατηγοὶ περὶ τειχεφρᾶς καὶ ἐπιδόσεως. At cum apud quia maiores, quibusdam festis, quam aliis, sumptus fiebant, disceptabant Choragi, ut hoc vel illo definito tempore necessum illis esset λειτουργεῖν. ita interpretor hæc Suidæ verba. ἐξηγήσεως ἐστὶν, ὡς ποιοῦσιν τὰς ἐνεῖς τοῖς μήνωσι χορηγεῖν· οἱ αὐ δεκαθλῶν βούλεσθαι ποτὲ χρὴ λειτουργεῖν αὐτοῖς.
units.tr: The statement of one's property had to be given within three days from the day on which they had sworn, according to this law: within three days from which they swear, they shall give the declaration [ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΗι ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ]. That is: within three days from when they swore, they shall declare their property. Demosthenes praises the law in the same speech: for, just as in the suit of the month Boedromion, he claimed that the law, which says "within three days from when he swears, to give the declaration," required that the property be declared correctly and justly [ὁμοίως γὰρ τῇ ἐνδικίᾳ τῇ Βοηδρομιῶνος μηνὸς, ἀποφαίνειν ὀρθῶς & δικαίως τὴν οὐσίαν, τὸν νόμον ἀξιῶν λέγοντος, ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ, ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΗ. ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ]. The court, not Polyactus and Terentius, judged these matters, so that the one from Alcibiades should punish himself; then the declaration of property was to be postponed by not many days. I, adding to my own case after the man who registered with the royal judge, will show that those who say these things made the injustice of the ... [text corrupt], declaring it on the day of the month Boedromion; but the declaration of property on the sixth day. Let this be taken as the sense of the passage of Demosthenes read in this first speech: the declaration of property must be given to me within the time of the law from the day on which they swore, unless it was postponed; for on the sixth day of Boedromion, as you have shown, they had to give the declaration. It should be read as: on the sixth day of Boedromion, as you have shown. Again, he mentions this law: but they have two laws against you, one concerning the trierarchs, the other the day of the declaration of property [ἀλλ' ἀλλ' εἰς δύο νόμους ἔχει πρὸς ὑμᾶς ταξιαρχικοὺς, ἕνα μὲν, τὸν χελιοντα τελευτῆς ἡμέρας, ἀφ' ἧς αὐ ὁμοίον, τὴν οὐσίαν ἀποφαίνειν]. This is the point on which he chiefly relies, and it rouses ill-feeling against Phaenippus: the second law requires the declaration within days from the time of death, on which he came to lend, and the greater part was lost, or the talents [ἔστιν ὁ δεύτερος μὲν τὴν ἀποφανσιν ἐδωκας μοι, τὸν νόμον κελεύοντας τελευτῆς ἡμερῶν, ὧν ἥκει δανείσαι, καὶ ἐφλήμεταί πλέον, ἡ τελευτῶν ταλάντων]. This declaration was given in writing. Harpocration: a declaration is what must be made in writing of the part which one has [ἀποφασις, ὁ ἀποφαίνειν ἀφ' γραμμὴ χρὴ μέρος ὁποῖον ὕστερ ἐχέ]. This declaration was given to the Generals. Demosthenes in the same speech: he gave the declaration to the General [εἰς ὃ Στρατηγὸν εἴδωκε τὴν ἀποφανσιν]; again: he announced that the Generals had this registration [ἀπηγγέλλει ὡς τὰς Στρατηγοὺς τοῦτο τὴν ἀπογραφὴν]. When the parties litigated, the Generals drew the judges by lot: the Generals brought in the cases concerning the fortification and the delivery [εἰσῆγεσαν οἱ Στρατηγοὶ περὶ τειχεφρᾶς καὶ ἐπιδόσεως]. But since some festivals required greater expenses than others, the Choregi disputed, so that at a fixed time, one or the other, they would be obliged to perform the public service [λειτουργεῖν]. I so interpret these words of Suidas: it is the explanation of how they make the choregia in the months; those who wish to perform the ten-fold service must at some time perform it for them. [ἐξηγήσεως ἐστὶν, ὡς ποιοῦσιν τὰς ἐνεῖς τοῖς μήνωσι χορηγεῖν· οἱ αὐ δεκαθλῶν βούλεσθαι ποτὲ χρὴ λειτουργεῖν αὐτοῖς].

units.la: DE EXCVSATIONIBVS MVNERVM.
units.tr: On Excuses from Public Services

units.la: TITVLVS QVINTVS.
units.tr: TITLE FIVE.

units.la: VI eorum munerum, de quibus praecedenti Titulo a nobis actum est, aliquod obibat, immunis erat a ceteris, ex hac Lege: Μὴ δύο λειτουργίας λειτουργεῖν. Duo munera simul ne obeunto.
units.tr: Whoever performed one of those public duties (munera) discussed in the preceding title was, by this law, exempt from the rest: "Not to perform two liturgies" [Μὴ δύο λειτουργίας λειτουργεῖν]. "Let no one undertake two duties at once."

units.la: Laudat Legem Demosthenes ἐν τᾷ ἀρχῇ Πολυκλέα. Καὶ τούτων ἐγὼ συλλαμβάνω ποιησάμενος, ὅτε ὅτι τειχεφρᾷ, καὶ οὐκ ἂν δυναμένη δύο λειτουργίας λειτουργεῖν, ὥστε οἱ νόμοι ἰσότ, ἔθηκα τὰς πολυφορέας πρὸς ἐμὲ. Igitur, qui Trierarchus erat, non debebat secundum Leges tributum conferre, ut hic habes, neque Choragus esse, ut idem docet Demosthenes in Leptinea: οἱ μὲν Τύπων πλουσιωτάτοι τειμωρρωθῆναι ἀεὶ τὴν χορηγίαν ἀπολεῖς [?] καταφρονεῖν. Vlpianus ad eandem, τειμωρρωτὸς δὲ οὐκ εἰπεῖν χορηγίαν. ἡ γὰρ ἀμφοτέρα [?] διωρίσθαι [?].
units.tr: Demosthenes cites the law in his speech against Polycles: "And I, taking these matters into account, since he is a trierarch and cannot perform two liturgies, have set the wealthy men against him, so that the laws may be equal." Therefore one who was a trierarch was not bound by law to pay the tax, as you have here, nor to be a choregus, as Demosthenes also shows in the speech against Leptines, where he says that the richest men of the Typus have always been let off the choregia [text corrupt]. Ulpian, on the same speech, says that it is not lawful to name a choregia as an exemption [text corrupt], for both were distinguished [text corrupt].

units.la: Munerum autem, quae pacis sunt, τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην λειτουργίαι, immunitates dabantur viris de Republica bene meritis. Vlpianus ad Leptineam: ἔφος δὲ ὧ πρὸς Ἀθηναίους τοὺς διεργέτας τῆς πόλεως λαμβάνειν ἀτέλειαν. Sed oppido pauci: nam sua aetate Demosthenes aduersus Leptinem, qui neminem immunem esse volebat, disputans, ostendit vix esse cives quinque aut sex, totidemque inquilinos, qui immunes sint. Sed locus adscribendus est, vt mendo liberetur: ὁ ἀρχὴ δὲ ὑπωσὶ, εἰσὶ τὴν ξένων ἀτελείς, δίκης ἴσου, καὶ μὲ τὰς ἀρχὰς, ὅτε εἶπον λέγω-των, οὐκ οἶμαι πέντε εἶ. καὶ μέλλω, τὴν γὰρ πολιτῶν, οὐκ εἰσὶ πέντε λ' ἐξ. Οἰκοῦν ἀμφοτέρων, ἐκ χρὴ δίκης ποιεῖσθαι αὐτοῖς εἰκοσιν. Εἰ ὁ βάλεσθ', τειμάχοσι. ποσὶ δ' ἤπου εἰσὶν οἱ κατ' αὐτὸν τὰς ἐγχυκλίους λειτουργίας λειτουργοῦντες ὑμῖν, Χορηγοὶ, καὶ Γυμνασίαρχοι, καὶ Ἐστιάτορες. ἐξήκοντα ἴσως, λ' μικρῷ πλείους συμπεπτωκότες ἦσι. ἵνα δὲω τειμάχοσι αὐτοὶ, λ' πλείους τῶνδε πόντα τὸν χρόνον λειτουργήσωσιν ὑμῖν, τοὺς ἀπωλείας ἀπίστεις τοῖς ὑμᾶς αὐτοὺς ἀφέσθων; Corruptus est proculdubio hic numerus, ἐξήκοντα ἴσως, λ' μικρῷ πλείους συμπεπτωκότες ἦσι. Nam aut intelligendus est in vniuersum de omnibus, qui toto vertente anno Choragi, aut Gymnasiarchi erant, aut epulum tribulibus suis praebebant: Atqui certum est longe plures fuisse; aut de immunibus tantum, quos ad obeunda munera haec cogi volebat Leptines, de quibus certe intelligendus est: Iam vero cum e ciuibus, tum ex inquilinis, immunes pluros non erant triginta, vt hic Demosthenes testatur: Quare non potuerunt esse sexaginta, aut paullo plures. Adde quod, si quidem triginta tantum sunt, ne quidem triginta quotannis haec obire munera potuerunt; cum nonnisi altero quoque anno ex Lege munera obeantur. Adde quod non tot erant Choragi, aut Gymnasiarchi, aut Estiatores inquilinorum, quot fuerunt Ciuium: non enim omnibus festis, quibus Cives ludos praebebant, praebebant quoque inquilini, vt in superioribus diximus. Referibo igitur apud Demosthenem: πολιτῶν ἀξίως εἶχεν, εἰ ὁ βάλεσθ', τειμάχοσι. ποσὶ δ' ἤπου εἰσὶν οἱ κατ' αὐτὸν τὰς ἐγχυκλίους λειτουργίας λειτουργοῦντες ὑμῖν, Χορηγοὶ, καὶ Γυμνασίαρχοι, καὶ Ἐστιάτορες. ἐξήκοντα τ' αἱ ἴσως, λ' μικρῷ πλείους συμπεπτωκότες ἦσι. id est, praeteriti erunt vndecim forte, aut paullo plures, hi omnes. Altero tantum quoque anno obire solebant munera Athenienses: Ergo e quindecim, totidem demus, ciuibus immunibus, singulis annis septem, aut octo munera obibunt: Adde pauculos ex inquilinis, nam, vt diximus, tot munera non obibant, aut toties, quot aut quoties obibant cines: Ergo vndecim fere, aut paullo plures ex his triginta immunibus, qui obire possent munera, quotannis illa non obibunt.
units.tr: Immunities were granted from those public duties that concern peace (τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην λειτουργίαι) to men who had deserved well of the commonwealth. Ulpian, on the speech against Leptines: "The law gave the Athenians the right to receive exemption, the benefactors of the city." But these were very few indeed. For in his own time Demosthenes, arguing against Leptines, who wanted no one to be exempt, shows that there were scarcely five or six citizens, and as many resident aliens, who were immune. The passage must be quoted, however, so that it may be freed from its corruption: "...and in the case of the offices, when they were speaking, I do not think there were five... for of the citizens there are not five and thirty..." Therefore, if we read both, the sentence should be made thus: "If you take those who perform the public liturgies for you in the course of the year, choregi, gymnasiarchs and hosts of banquets, about sixty, or a little more, have fallen together." Corruption undoubtedly lies in this number, "about sixty, or a little more." For either it must be understood of all in general who were choregi or gymnasiarchs, or who provided a feast for their tribesmen, throughout the whole year; yet it is certain there were far more; or it must be understood only of the exempt men whom Leptines wanted compelled to perform these duties, and of these it must certainly be understood. Now, however, both among citizens and among resident aliens there were not more than thirty exempt men, as Demosthenes here testifies. Therefore they cannot have numbered sixty, or a little more. Add that, even if there are only thirty, not even thirty could perform these duties every year, since by law the duties were performed only every other year. Add further that there were not as many choregi, gymnasiarchs or hosts among the resident aliens as there were among the citizens; for the resident aliens did not provide the games on all the festivals on which the citizens did, as we said above. I therefore read in Demosthenes: "...it was proper for citizens..., if you take those who perform the public liturgies for you, choregi, gymnasiarchs and hosts, about sixty, or a little more, have fallen together." That is, perhaps eleven or a little more of all these will have been passed over. The Athenians discharged these duties only every other year. Therefore of the fifteen, let us grant as many, citizens who were exempt, seven or eight will perform duties each year. Add a few resident aliens, for, as we said, they did not perform so many duties, or as often, as the citizens did. Therefore about eleven, or a little more, of these thirty exempt men who could perform duties will not perform them in any given year.

units.la: Sed munerum, quae bellum spectant, nemo erat immunis. Vlpianus ad Leptineam: ἔφος δὲ ὧ πρὸς Ἀθηναίους τοὺς διεργέτας τῆς πόλεως λαμβάνειν ἀτέλειαν, ἀλλ' ὁ πασῶν τῶν λειτουργιῶν· ὁ δὲ ποτὲ γὰρ ἐλάμβανον, ὅτι τὴν τειμωρρωτὴν, οὔτε τὴν εἰσφορῶν τῆς πολέμων ἀτέλειαν. Et quidem ὥσὲ τὴν τειμωρρωτῶν legitur haec legis:
units.tr: But of the duties that concern war, no one was exempt. Ulpian, on the speech against Leptines: "The law gave the Athenians the right to receive exemption, the benefactors of the city, but not from all the liturgies; for they did not receive exemption from the trierarchy, nor from the taxes for war." And indeed the following law is read concerning the trierarchy:

units.la: ΑΤΕΛΗ ΔΕ ΜΗΔΕΝΑ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡ-ΧΙΑΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝΝΕΑ ΑΡΧΟΝ-ΤΩΝ.
units.tr: "NO ONE SHALL BE EXEMPT FROM THE TRIERARCHY, EXCEPT THE NINE ARCHONS."

units.la: Nemo, praeter Noemvi-ros, triremis instruendae immunis esto. Laudat hanc Legem Demosthenes in Leptinea: [illegible, ~40 letters] ATELH DE MHDENA EINAI TRIHPARXIAS PLHN TWN ENNEA ARXON-TWN. Vlpianus: [illegible, ~30 letters]. Ac ne ipsi quidem inquilini immunes erant. Demosthenes hac Oratione: [illegible, ~25 letters] MHDENA, μήτε τῆς πολιτῶν, μήτε τῆς ἰσοπολιτῶν, μήτε τῆς ξένων, EINAI ATELH. adeoque cogi ad obeunda hæc munera inquilinos docent Grammatici: [illegible, ~20 letters]. Certè qui λειτουργίας sibi mandaras non obibat, in vincula conijciebatur. Demosthenes in Timocratea: [illegible, ~45 letters].
units.tr: Let no one be exempt from equipping a trireme, except the nine archons. Demosthenes cites this law in the speech against Leptines: [text illegible]. Ulpian: [text illegible]. Nor were even resident aliens exempt. Demosthenes, in this speech: [text illegible] "Let no one, either of the citizens, or of those with equal citizenship, or of the aliens, be exempt." And the grammarians show that resident aliens were likewise compelled to perform these duties: [text illegible]. Certainly one who did not perform the liturgy assigned to him was cast into prison. Demosthenes, in the speech against Timocrates: [text illegible].

units.la: Neque item immunes erant τῆς εἰσφορᾶς, quæ conferebantur imminente bello: Τῶν εἰς τὸν πόλεμον πασῶν εἰσφορῶν μηδὲν | Conferenda in bellum pecuniæ nemo ἀτελῆ. | immunis esto.
units.tr: Nor were they likewise exempt from the tax (εἰσφορά) that was levied when war was imminent: "Let no one be exempt from any tax levied for war." [Τῶν εἰς τὸν πόλεμον πασῶν εἰσφορῶν μηδὲν ἀτελῆ.] Money to be contributed for war: no one shall be immune.

units.la: Legis meminit Demosthenes in Leptinea: τῆς γὰρ εἰς τὸν πόλεμον καὶ τὴν Γ-πηγείας τῆς πόλεως πασῶν εἰσφορῶν καὶ τειναφρχιῶν, ἐρῶς καὶ δικαίως, ὥσπερ ἐξ ἀτελῆς ἐκ τῶν παλαιῶν νόμων. Rursum: τῆς γὰρ εἰς τὸν πόλεμον πασῶν εἰσφορῶν καὶ τειναφρχιῶν ἐκ τῶν παλαιῶν νόμων οὐκ εἰσὶν ἀτελεῖς. Vlpianus ad hanc Leptineam: ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτὸς παρέχεσθαι νόμον τοιοῦτον, ἢ κελεύοισι μηδὲν ἀτελῆ εἴη τῆς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον.
units.tr: Demosthenes mentions the law in the speech against Leptines: "For of the taxes levied for war and for the fortification of the city, and of the trierarchies, no one is exempt, rightly and justly, as is the case under the ancient laws." And again: "For, according to the ancient laws, no one is exempt from all taxes levied for war and from the trierarchies." Ulpian, on this speech against Leptines: "But he himself also cites such a law, which orders that no one be exempt from the taxes for war."

units.la: Quanquam mercatores immunes fuisse τῆς εἰσφορᾶς colligimus ex hoc Aristophanis versu Pluto:
units.tr: Although we gather that merchants were exempt from the tax (εἰσφορά), from this verse of Aristophanes in the Plutus:

units.la: ΔΙ. ἀλλ' ἐμπορεῖς; ΣΥ. καὶ σκήπτομαί γ' ὅτου τύχω.
units.tr: DI. "But are you a merchant?" SY. "Yes, and I plead some pretext."

units.la: Euphroniusque apud Scholiastem Comici expressis verbis docet: τοὺς τῆς πολιτῶν ἰωίας χρημάτων ὧν εἰσφορὰ πρὸς τὴν πόλιν, τῶν ἐμπορείαν ἐπαγγέλλοιτο, τῶν εἰσφορῶν βουλόμενοι φυγεῖν. ἀζημίως γὰρ ὅπερ διεφυλάττοντα, ὡς φησὶν Εὐφρόνιος, ὡς τὴν πόλιν ὀφελῶντες πλάστα, ἀφ' τῆς αὐτῆς ἐμπορείας δὲ ὁ συκοφάντης λέγει, ὅτι ὅταν ἡμῖν ἡ πόλις πολεμῶν καὶ εἰσφορᾶς ἐμπορεύεσθαι ἀποκαλῶ.
units.tr: Euphronius, in the Scholiast on the comic poet, teaches it in express words: those citizens who possessed property upon which a tax was levied for the city, and who professed to be merchants, wished to escape the taxes. For, as Euphronius says, they kept themselves safe without penalty, benefiting the city in appearance only, from the same trade; and the sycophant says that when the city is at war, he calls on us to trade to avoid the taxes.

units.la: Conferebantur autem aliquando hæ pecuniæ, si periculum esset in mora, à ditioribus, qui postea à popularibus suis exigebant: εἰσφορὰ autem fiebat ob bona, quæ possidebat quisque, ita si quis in pluribus Atticæ populis agros possideret, & inter plures & diversos populares pecuniam conferebat. Ista omnia facile est colligere ex his Demosthenis verbis: [illegible, ~60 letters] Ἀρχοντ. Ὅτι ἀλλ' [illegible, ~50 letters] μὴ ἐγὼ [illegible, ~70 letters] ἀλλὰ ἐξ ὧν [illegible, ~40 letters] τῆς [illegible, ~30 letters]
units.tr: Moreover, these sums were sometimes collected, if there were danger in delay, from the wealthier men, who afterwards exacted them from their fellow citizens. The tax (εἰσφορά) was assessed on the property each man possessed; thus if someone held fields in several Attic demes, he contributed money among several and different demes. All this may easily be gathered from these words of Demosthenes: [text illegible] "Archon..." [text illegible].

units.la: [illegible, ~80 letters] ἀποφ[?] ὑφ᾽ ἑτέρων [?]παρεξελλεγμένα, τὰ δὲ ἄπορα [?], [illegible, ~6 letters] Quare si quis tributum non inferret, publicanda erant eius bona, non vero is vinciendus. Demosthenes in Androtiana: εἴ τις ἔσπλο[?] αὐτὸν, τὰς εἰσφορὰς, πότερον τὰ κτήματα, ἢ τὰ σώματα ἐφείλε[?]; τὰ κτήματα, φησὶ δή· ἐπὶ γὰρ τούτων εἰσφέρειν. τίνος οὖν ἕνεκα ἀφεὶς δὲ τὰ χρέα δημεύειν, ἐὰν τὰς οἰκίας, καὶ τῶν [?] ἀπογραφὴν, ἐᾶσι καὶ ὑβρίζεις πολίτας αἰδέσπης.
units.tr: [text illegible] [Greek fragment corrupt]. Therefore, if anyone did not pay the tax, his goods were to be confiscated, and he was not to be imprisoned. Demosthenes, in the speech against Androtion: "If someone... the taxes, whether they levied on his property or on his persons? On his property, he says; for it is on these that the tax is levied. Why, then, having left the debts, should they confiscate the houses..., and allow the insolent to treat citizens shamefully?"

units.la: DE PRÆMIIS BENE DE Republica meritorum,
units.tr: ON THOSE WHO HAVE DESERVED WELL OF THE COMMONWEALTH: REWARDS

units.la: TITULUS VI.
units.tr: TITLE VI.

units.la: QUanquam nullo honestamento virtus negat, honore tamen ad eius studium excitari homines, nemo est tam averso ab omni laude animo, qui non id ultro fateatur: itaque præmiis ad bene de Republica merendum suos cives invitarunt Athenienses Legislatores. Inter ea primum quod occurrit, προεδρία est, de qua Aristophanes Equitibus:
units.tr: Although virtue refuses any reward for itself, no one is so indifferent to all praise that he does not readily admit that men are stirred to pursue it by honour. The Athenian legislators therefore invited their citizens to deserve well of the commonwealth by rewards. The first of these that comes to mind is proedria (front seats), of which Aristophanes speaks in the Knights:

units.la: πῶς δὲ ἐὰν μὴ προεδρίας φέρωσι, καὶ τὰ σιτία,
units.tr: And how if they do not bring front seats, and the meals too, [πῶς δὲ ἐὰν μὴ προεδρίας φέρωσι, καὶ τὰ σιτία]

units.la: ὃ μαχεῖσθαί φασιν.
units.tr: which they say they fight for. [ὃ μαχεῖσθαί φασιν]

units.la: Quæ προεδρία quid sit, optime explicat Interpres Comici ad hunc locum, & ex eo Suidas: Ἰμῖν καὶ ἐστ᾽ ἔστι τύπος. ἔχω δὲ τὰς ἡμῖν τούτοις τυχεῖσι, καὶ ἐν βουλευτηρίῳ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, καὶ ἐν παρόδοις, ἢ ἐν ἄλλῳ πομπὴ συλλόγῳ τῶν προεδρίαν ἐχόντων οἱ ἴνες ἦσαν ἐξειλέγοντας, αὐτοὶ εἰς τὸν ἐκείνων τόπον καθῆσαν. Erant autem in Theatris sedes secretæ aliæ & aliis, & assignatæ ordinibus pro eorum dignitate, unde apud Comicum Avibus:
units.tr: What proedria was is best explained by the commentator on the comedy at this passage, and from him by Suidas: There is a kind of sign for us. I have, for those of us who obtain this, a seat both in the council-chamber, in the assembly, and in the processions, or in other gatherings, of those who hold precedence; those who were chosen sat in their places. [Ἰμῖν καὶ ἐστ᾽ ἔστι τύπος. ἔχω δὲ τὰς ἡμῖν τούτοις τυχεῖσι, καὶ ἐν βουλευτηρίῳ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, καὶ ἐν παρόδοις, ἢ ἐν ἄλλῳ πομπὴ συλλόγῳ τῶν προεδρίαν ἐχόντων οἱ ἴνες ἦσαν ἐξειλέγοντας, αὐτοὶ εἰς τὸν ἐκείνων τόπον καθῆσαν.] Moreover, in the theatres there were separate seats for different people, assigned to the orders according to their dignity; hence in the Birds of the comic poet:

units.la: χαῖρ᾽ ἐξ ἀὐδρα τῆς γυναικὸς ἐν Βουλευτικῷ.
units.tr: Hail, man, from the woman's place in the council-chamber. [χαῖρ᾽ ἐξ ἀὐδρα τῆς γυναικὸς ἐν Βουλευτικῷ]

units.la: Ἐπὶ τὴν[?] τῶν, inquit Scholiastes, τὴν Ἀλκιβ[?]ν, ὁ αἰσχρῶν τῶν Βουλευτῶν, ὡς καὶ ὁ τῶν Εφ[?]βοις Εφηβικός. Distinctæque erant virorum & feminarum sedes ex Sphyromachi Psephismate: ὁ δὲ Σφυρομάχος ψήφισμα εἰσηγήσατο, τὰ γυναικὰς ἐν τοῖς ἀνδρὰς χωρὶς καθίζεσθαι.
units.tr: The scholiast says: at the seat of ... Alcibiades, the shameful seat of the councillors, as the seat of the ephebi is the ephebic one. [Ἐπὶ τὴν τῶν, inquit Scholiastes, τὴν Ἀλκιβν, ὁ αἰσχρῶν τῶν Βουλευτῶν, ὡς καὶ ὁ τῶν Εφβοις Εφηβικός.] The seats of men and women were also kept apart by the decree of Sphyromachus: Sphyromachus proposed a decree that the women should sit apart from the men. [ὁ δὲ Σφυρομάχος ψήφισμα εἰσηγήσατο, τὰ γυναικὰς ἐν τοῖς ἀνδρὰς χωρὶς καθίζεσθαι.]

units.la: Fuit & ἄτιμος è Solonis instituto, cuius hæc est Lex:
units.tr: There was also atimia (loss of honour) under Solon's institution, whose law is this:

units.la: Τὸν αὐτὸν μὴ ἀποδειπνεῖν πολλάκις· ἐὰν δὲ ὁ κεκλημένος μὴ βούληται, κολάζεσθαι.
units.tr: The same man is not to be invited to dinner often; if the invited man does not wish to come, he is to be punished. [Τὸν αὐτὸν μὴ ἀποδειπνεῖν πολλάκις· ἐὰν δὲ ὁ κεκλημένος μὴ βούληται, κολάζεσθαι.]

units.la: Eidem epulum in Prytaneio sapius ne præbetor: qui hunc honorem præterhabuerit, multator.
units.tr: The same man was not to be given the public banquet in the Prytaneum too often; whoever neglected this honour was to be fined.

units.la: Legis huius ἀποδειπνήσεως meminit Plutarchus in Solone: εἶχον δὲ τῆς Σόλωνος καὶ ὁ ἀπὸ τῆς ἐν δημοσίᾳ ἀτιμίας, ὅταν αὐτὸς ἀποδειπνῶν κέκληκε. τὸν γὰρ αὐτὸν ζῆν ἐξ ἀτιμίας πολλάκις· ἐὰν δὲ ὁ κεκλημένος μὴ βούληται, κολάζει. Ratio est, ὃ μὲν, ἡγεμόνας πλεονεξίας· ὃ δὲ, ἀσφαλείας τῆς κοινῆς, Domus, in qua epulabantur, dicebatur πρυτανεῖον. Suidas & Interpres Comici non semel: Πρυτανεῖον, ἀποδείπνον δὲ τῆς Αθηναίοις οἰκίαις δημοσίας, ἔνθα ἐσπιπτ[?]ων δημοσίᾳ τῆς ἐκείνων τιμῆς παρ᾽ αὐτῶν τυχόντες, ἐπεὶ γὰρ μεγάλοις καθορῶμεν πλὴ [illegible, ~14 letters] χάριν. Auctor Etymologici: Πρυτάνεῖον, τόπος ὦ[?] ἔνθα αἱ κοιναὶ σίτήσεις τῶν δημοσίων [?] εἰσῄεσαν. Pollux Libro IX. cap. V: [illegible, ~30 letters] Quid verò apponendum fuerit, Lege sanxit Solon:
units.tr: Plutarch, in his Life of Solon, mentions this law on apodeipnesis (the public dinner): There was also, from Solon's law, the loss of honour in public, whenever he invited someone to dine. For the same man was not to be fed often; if the invited man did not wish to come, he was punished. [εἶχον δὲ τῆς Σόλωνος καὶ ὁ ἀπὸ τῆς ἐν δημοσίᾳ ἀτιμίας, ὅταν αὐτὸς ἀποδειπνῶν κέκληκε. τὸν γὰρ αὐτὸν ζῆν ἐξ ἀτιμίας πολλάκις· ἐὰν δὲ ὁ κεκλημένος μὴ βούληται, κολάζει.] The reason was: the one was to check greed, the other to secure the common safety. The house in which they dined was called the Prytaneum. Suidas and the commentator on the comedy say more than once: Prytaneum, the public dining-house of the Athenians, where those who were honoured by them received public meals... [Πρυτανεῖον, ἀποδείπνον δὲ τῆς Αθηναίοις οἰκίαις δημοσίας, ἔνθα ἐσπιπτ[?]ων δημοσίᾳ τῆς ἐκείνων τιμῆς παρ᾽ αὐτῶν τυχόντες, ἐπεὶ γὰρ μεγάλοις καθορῶμεν πλὴ [illegible] χάριν.] The author of the Etymologicum: Prytaneum, a place where the common meals of the public men were taken. [Πρυτάνεῖον, τόπος ὦ[?] ἔνθα αἱ κοιναὶ σίτήσεις τῶν δημοσίων [?] εἰσῄεσαν.] Pollux in Book IX, chapter 5: [illegible]. What was to be set before them Solon laid down by law:

units.la: Τοῖς ποτ[?]ἀπαυ[?]μένοις μάζαν πρύτανιν, ἄρτον ἢ Conniuantibus in Prytaneio mazam, ταῖς ἑορταῖς [?] diebus verò festis, panis apponitor.
units.tr: [Τοῖς ποτ[?]ἀπαυ[?]μένοις μάζαν πρύτανιν, ἄρτον ἢ Conniuantibus in Prytaneio mazam, ταῖς ἑορταῖς [?] diebus verò festis, panis apponitor.] (That is: for those who were dining in the Prytaneum, a barley-cake was to be set out; on feast days, bread.)

units.la: Qua in re Homerum inuitari voluit Solon. Athenaeus Libro IV. Σόλων δὲ τοῖς ἐν Πρυτανείῳ σιτουμένοις μάζαν πρύτανιν κελεύει· ἄρτον δὲ τοῖς ἑορταῖς παρέχειν, μιμούμενος τὸν Ὅμηρον· καὶ ἐκ τῆς τοῖς ἡρῷσιν [?] ἐπὶ τὸν Ἀχαμέμνονα, φύρετο δ' ἀλφίτα φησίν. Ac obtinuit aliquamdiu Lex Solonis, nec passim hic τῆς σίτήσεως honos est habitus; Aristophanes Equitibus de Strategis, qui ἐτάτεμ Cleonis praecesserunt:
units.tr: In this matter Solon wished to imitate Homer. Athenaeus in Book IV: Solon orders that barley-cake be given to those who dine in the Prytaneum, and bread on feast days, imitating Homer, who says, from the passage about the heroes at Agamemnon's, that the barley-meal was kneaded. Solon's law held for some time, and this honour of the meal was not everywhere granted; Aristophanes in the Knights speaks of the generals who preceded Cleon:

units.la: καὶ Στρατηγὸς ὁδ' ἀπὸ εἰς τὴν πρυτανεῖον ἡ σίτησις, ἐφιδωες Κλεαίνετον. νῦν δ' ἐκ ἐμὲ μὴ παρεδρίαν φέρωσι, τὰ [?] σίτια, μαχαιροφόρος φασίν.
units.tr: And the general, that one, from there to the Prytaneum, the meal, [they gave] to Cleaenetus... but now, unless they bring me front seats, they say the meals too, the sword-bearers.
