units.la: Quid hic fit, ἐφιδωες Κλεαίνετον, dicere non est adeo procliue, neque enim Graecus Interpres quicquam nos hic iuuat, cuius haec est nota: ἔστ' ὁ Κλεαίνετος Φαίνεται κατεδαπάσχως τὰ ὄσιαν καὶ ἠδυπαθήσας. οἱ δὲ, ὅτι ἔσσ' ἐγχρίσμα μὴ δίν δοῦναι τοῖς Στρατηγοῖς σίτησιν. ἀσφαλῶς δὲ μεμνῆσθαι τῆς Κλεαίνετου καὶ ἀφεδοτ' εἴπωμ μόνον. [?]. Nam si hic Cleanetus bona sua decoxit, quid opus est illo in petenda aut impetranda à populo σίτησι? Si populi scitum fecerat de non donandis Strategis σίτησι, multo minus commoda est hoc loco illius mentio: Quod si dicas hunc esse, qui Cleoni σίτησιν impetrauit, non video, quid ἐφιδωες hic significet. Vt dicam igitur quod sentio, inque tenebris micem, puto leuiter corruptum esse hunc locum, & duas voces in vnam coaluisse, vnde natum hoc nomen, quod proprium esse putarunt Δημαγωγὸς alicuius ex illo aeuo, fruftra, meo quidem iudicio: nam siue fecisset populi scitum μὴ δίν διδῶναι τοῖς Στρατηγοῖς σίτησιν, siue eam Cleoni à populo impetrasset, frequentius illius meminisset Aristophanes: nullus igitur dubito referendum esse,
units.tr: What is meant by "ephidoes Kleainneton" is not easy to say, for the Greek commentator helps us not at all; his note is: "Cleaenetus was evidently one who had squandered his goods and lived in luxury. Others say that there was a decree not to give the generals a meal. Surely he mentions Cleaenetus and the rest only..." For if this Cleaenetus squandered his property, what need was there for him to seek or obtain a meal from the people? If the people had passed a decree that no meal should be given to the generals, the mention of him is still less suitable here. But if you say that he is the one who obtained a meal for Cleon, I do not see what ephidoes means here. So, to say what I think, and since I grope in the dark, I suppose the passage has been slightly corrupted and two words have fused into one, from which this name arose, which they thought was the proper name of some demagogue of that age, in vain, in my judgement at least: for whether he had passed the decree not to give the generals a meal, or had obtained a meal for Cleon from the people, Aristophanes would have mentioned it more often. I therefore have no doubt that this should be read:

units.la: καὶ Στρατηγὸς ὁδ' ἀπὸ εἰς τὴν πρυτανεῖον, σίτησιν ἢ πρὸ ἐφιδωες, κλέ' αἰνετόν.
units.tr: And the general, that one, from there to the Prytaneum, [he gave] a meal, or before ... that is praiseworthy glory.

units.la: Strategorum priorum nullus petiit à populo σίτησιν, dicens, prædica laude dignum, κλέος αἰνετὸν, ex κλείομαι fit κλέομαι, ita à κλείω fit κλέω. Nemo quippe σίτησι donabatur à populo, qui eadem non prædicaretur omni dignus laude. In populi scito , quod fecit Stratocles Euthydemi F. Anaxicrate Athenis Praetore, anno secundo Olympiadis centesimae decimae octauae, de Lycurgo Oratore donando σίτησι haec verba leguntur: ΑΓΑΘΗΙ ΤΥΧΗΙ ΔΕΔΟΧΘΑΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ, ΕΠΑΙΝΕΣΑΙ ΜΕΝ ΛΥΚΟΥΡΓΟΝ ΛΥΚΟΦΡΟΝΟΣ ΒΟΥΤΑΔΗΝ ΑΡΕΤΗΣ ΕΝΕΚΑ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΟΣΥΝΗΣ, ΚΑΙ ΣΤΗΣΑΙ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΤΟΝ ΔΗΜΟΝ ΧΑΛΚΗΝ ΕΙΚΟΝΑ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑΙ· ΓΑΗΝ ΕΙ ΠΟΥ Ο ΝΟΜΟΣ ΑΓΑΓΟΡΕΥΕΙ ΜΗ ΙΣΤΑΝΑΙ, ΔΟΥΝΑΙ ΔΕ ΣΙΤΗΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΩΙ ΤΩΝ ΕΓΓΟΝΩΝ ΓΟΝΩΝ ΑΕΙ ΤΩΝ ΛΥΚΟΥΡΓΟΥ ΤΩΙ ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΑΤΩΙ ΕΙΣ ΑΠΑΝΤΑ ΤΟΝ ΧΡΟΝΟΝ. Atque ex his praeterea docemur, Solonis Legem, Ne quis saepe in Prytaneio excipiretur, mutasse: nam multi ἀτίμοι ἐκ ὑμῶν[?] fuerunt, ut loquitur Pollux, honosque is heredes sequebatur: ita ut interdum, quo possent defunctorum liberi eo uti, mortuis peteretur, & impetraretur, quod Demostheni accidit, cui hic honos impetratus est anno primo Olympiadis centesimae vicesimae quintae, Gorgia Athenis Praetore: Plutarchus in eius Vita Libro de X. Rhet. χρόνῳ δ' ὕστερον Ἀθηναῖοι αἴτησιν τε εἰς Πρυτανεῖα τῆς συγγενέσι τῷ Δημοσθένους ἐδόθη, καὶ αὐτῷ πεπλευτηκότι τῷ εἰκόνα ἀνέθεσαν ἐν ἀγορᾷ, ὑπὸ Γοργίου Ἀρχοντος[?]. Extat in hanc rem Psephisma scriptum à Demochare Lachetis F. apud eundem Plutarchum: ΔΗΜΟΧΑΡΗΣ ΛΑΑΧΗΤΟΣ ΛΕΥΚΟΝΟΕΥΣ ΑΙΤΕΙ ΔΗΜΟΣΘΕΝΕΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΟΣΘΕΝΟΥΣ ΠΑΙΑΝΙΕΙ ΔΩΡΕΑΝ ΧΑΛΚΗΝ ΕΙΚΟΝΑ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑΙ, ΚΑΙ ΣΙΤΗΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΩΙ, ΚΑΙ ΠΡΟΕΔΡΙΑΝ ΑΥΤΩΙ, ΚΑΙ ΕΚΓΟΝΩΝ ΑΕΙ ΤΩΙ ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΑΤΩΙ ΕΥΕΡΓΕΤΗΙ, ΚΑΙ ΣΥΜΒΟΥΛΩΙ ΓΕΓΟΝΟΤΙ ΓΟΛΛΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΚΑΛΩΝ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ ΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΤΕ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΟ ΚΟΙΝΟΝ ΚΑΘΕΙΚΟΤΙ ΤΗΝ ΕΑΥΤΟΥ. Beneficia deinde Demosthenis in populum singillatim recenseт Demochares, quemadmodum & Democharis ipsius filius eius Laches, in Psephismate, quod in hanc rem scripsit, Archonte Pytharato, anno secundo Olympiadis centesimae vicesimae septimae: extat hoc Psephisma apud Plutarchum extremo Libro de X. Rhet. in haec verba: ΑΡΧΩΝ ΓΥΘΑΡΑΤΟΣ ΛΑΑΧΗΣ ΔΗΜΟΧΑΡΟΥΣ ΛΕΥΚΟΝΟΕΥΣ ΑΙΤΕΙ ΔΩΡΕΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΒΟΥΛΗΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟΝ ΔΗΜΟΝ ΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ ΔΗΜΟΧΑΡΕΙ ΛΑΑΧΗΤΟΣ ΛΕΥΚΟΝΟΕΙ ΕΙΚΟΝΑ ΧΑΛΚΗΝ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑΙ, ΚΑΙ ΣΙΤΗΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΩΙ, ΚΑΙ ΤΩΝ ΕΓΓΟΝΩΝ ΑΕΙ ΤΩΙ ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΑΤΩΙ, ΚΑΙ ΠΡΟΕΔΡΙΑΝ ΕΝ ΠΑΣΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΓΩΣΙΝ ΕΥΕΡΓΕΤΗΙ, ΚΑΙ ΣΥΜΒΟΥΛΩΙ ΓΕΓΟΝΟΤΙ ΑΓΑΘΩΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ ΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΥΕΡΓΕΤΗΚΟΤΙ ΤΟΝ ΔΗΜΟΝ ΤΑΔΕ.
units.tr: None of the earlier generals sought a meal from the people, since the phrase "praiseworthy glory" (kleos aineton, from kleiomai, as kleo comes from kleiō) means one worthy of praise. Indeed no one was granted a meal by the people who was not thought worthy of all praise. In the decree of the people, which Stratocles, son of Euthydemus, proposed when Anaxicrates was archon at Athens, in the second year of the 118th Olympiad, granting a meal to Lycurgus the orator, these words are read: Resolved by the Council and the People: since Lycurgus, son of Lycophron, of the deme of Boutadae, praises virtue and justice, and the People has set up a bronze statue of him in the marketplace; and if there is a law forbidding him to be set up, the Prytaneum shall give him a meal, as long as the descendants of Lycurgus, the eldest of his line, live. [ΑΓΑΘΗΙ ΤΥΧΗΙ ΔΕΔΟΧΘΑΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ, ΕΠΑΙΝΕΣΑΙ ΜΕΝ ΛΥΚΟΥΡΓΟΝ ΛΥΚΟΦΡΟΝΟΣ ΒΟΥΤΑΔΗΝ ΑΡΕΤΗΣ ΕΝΕΚΑ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΟΣΥΝΗΣ, ΚΑΙ ΣΤΗΣΑΙ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΤΟΝ ΔΗΜΟΝ ΧΑΛΚΗΝ ΕΙΚΟΝΑ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑΙ· ΓΑΗΝ ΕΙ ΠΟΥ Ο ΝΟΜΟΣ ΑΓΑΓΟΡΕΥΕΙ ΜΗ ΙΣΤΑΝΑΙ, ΔΟΥΝΑΙ ΔΕ ΣΙΤΗΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΩΙ ΤΩΝ ΕΓΓΟΝΩΝ ΓΟΝΩΝ ΑΕΙ ΤΩΝ ΛΥΚΟΥΡΓΟΥ ΤΩΙ ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΑΤΩΙ ΕΙΣ ΑΠΑΝΤΑ ΤΟΝ ΧΡΟΝΟΝ.] From these things we further learn that Solon's law, that a man should not often be entertained in the Prytaneum, was changed: for many were deprived of honour by you, as Pollux says, and this honour passed to heirs; so that sometimes the meal was asked for and granted to the dead, so that the children of the deceased could enjoy it. This happened to Demosthenes, to whom this honour was granted in the first year of the 125th Olympiad, when Gorgias was archon at Athens. Plutarch, in his Life of Demosthenes, in the Book on the Ten Orators: Later the Athenians granted that a meal in the Prytaneum should be given to Demosthenes' relatives, and they set up his statue in the marketplace, while he was in exile, under the archon Gorgias. [χρόνῳ δ' ὕστερον Ἀθηναῖοι αἴτησιν τε εἰς Πρυτανεῖα τῆς συγγενέσι τῷ Δημοσθένους ἐδόθη, καὶ αὐτῷ πεπλευτηκότι τῷ εἰκόνα ἀνέθεσαν ἐν ἀγορᾷ, ὑπὸ Γοργίου Ἀρχοντος.] There is a decree written on this matter by Demochares, son of Laches, also quoted in Plutarch: "Demochares, son of Laches, of the deme of Leuconoe, proposes that Demosthenes, son of Demosthenes of Paeania, be given a bronze statue in the marketplace, a meal in the Prytaneum, the front seat, and that his descendants forever be given the eldest privileges, and that he be a councillor and a benefactor of the Athenian people, and that his property be returned to the common treasury." [ΔΗΜΟΧΑΡΗΣ ΛΑΑΧΗΤΟΣ ΛΕΥΚΟΝΟΕΥΣ ΑΙΤΕΙ ΔΗΜΟΣΘΕΝΕΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΟΣΘΕΝΟΥΣ ΠΑΙΑΝΙΕΙ ΔΩΡΕΑΝ ΧΑΛΚΗΝ ΕΙΚΟΝΑ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑΙ, ΚΑΙ ΣΙΤΗΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΩΙ, ΚΑΙ ΠΡΟΕΔΡΙΑΝ ΑΥΤΩΙ, ΚΑΙ ΕΚΓΟΝΩΝ ΑΕΙ ΤΩΙ ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΑΤΩΙ ΕΥΕΡΓΕΤΗΙ, ΚΑΙ ΣΥΜΒΟΥΛΩΙ ΓΕΓΟΝΟΤΙ ΓΟΛΛΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΚΑΛΩΝ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ ΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΤΕ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΟ ΚΟΙΝΟΝ ΚΑΘΕΙΚΟΤΙ ΤΗΝ ΕΑΥΤΟΥ.] Demochares then lists the benefits of Demosthenes to the people one by one, as did Laches, son of Demochares, in the decree he wrote on this matter, under the archon Pytharatus, in the second year of the 127th Olympiad. This decree survives in Plutarch's final book on the Ten Orators, in these words: [ΑΡΧΩΝ ΓΥΘΑΡΑΤΟΣ ΛΑΑΧΗΣ ΔΗΜΟΧΑΡΟΥΣ ΛΕΥΚΟΝΟΕΥΣ ΑΙΤΕΙ ΔΩΡΕΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΒΟΥΛΗΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟΝ ΔΗΜΟΝ ΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ ΔΗΜΟΧΑΡΕΙ ΛΑΑΧΗΤΟΣ ΛΕΥΚΟΝΟΕΙ ΕΙΚΟΝΑ ΧΑΛΚΗΝ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑΙ, ΚΑΙ ΣΙΤΗΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΩΙ, ΚΑΙ ΤΩΝ ΕΓΓΟΝΩΝ ΑΕΙ ΤΩΙ ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΑΤΩΙ, ΚΑΙ ΠΡΟΕΔΡΙΑΝ ΕΝ ΠΑΣΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΓΩΣΙΝ ΕΥΕΡΓΕΤΗΙ, ΚΑΙ ΣΥΜΒΟΥΛΩΙ ΓΕΓΟΝΟΤΙ ΑΓΑΘΩΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ ΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΥΕΡΓΕΤΗΚΟΤΙ ΤΟΝ ΔΗΜΟΝ ΤΑΔΕ.]

units.la: Quinctiam feminis id concessum, ut de Polycrite Aristidis neptè Callisthenes refert apud Plutarchum in Aristide: ἐπὶ δὲ Λισιμάχου γυναικὸς Πολυκρίτῳ ὑπολιπόντος, ὡς Καλλισθένης φησί· καὶ ταύτῃ σίτησιν ὅσων καὶ τοῖς Ολυμπιονίκαις ὁ δῆμος ἐψηφίσατο. Demetrio quoque Phalereo populi scitum faciente dedit populus Aristidis neptibus triobolum in dies singulos: ὁ δὲ Φαληρεὺς ἐν τῷ Σωκράτει φησὶ μνημονεύειν Ἀρισείδου γυναικῶν, δ' μάλα πένητα Λεισίμαχον. τῇ δὲ μητρὶ καὶ τῇ ταύτης ἀδελφῇ ψήφισμα γράψας δωρεὰν ἐπιτιμᾶν τὸν δῆμον ἀδόναι, τεσσάρων [illegible, ~12 letters] ΓΑΣ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ. αὐτὸς μὲν φησιν ὁ Δημήτριος νομοθετῶν ἐψηφίσατο δραχμὴν ἑκάστης ἡμέρας τὰς γυναῖκας. Hanc sibi esse praebendam iocose respondit Socrates iam primis iudicum sententiis damnatus: Cùm interrogatus Socrates esset, inquit M. Tullius Libro I. de Oratore, respondit sese meruisse, ut amplissimis honoribus, & praemijs decorarentur, & ut ei victus quotidianus in Prytaneo publice praeberetur, qui honos apud Graecos maximus haberetur.
units.tr: Even women were granted this honour, as Callisthenes reports of Polycrite, granddaughter of Aristides, in Plutarch's Life of Aristides: In the time of Lysimachus, when Polycrite had been left a widow, as Callisthenes says, the people voted her a meal for as long as the Olympic victors had one. [ἐπὶ δὲ Λισιμάχου γυναικὸς Πολυκρίτῳ ὑπολιπόντος, ὡς Καλλισθένης φησί· καὶ ταύτῃ σίτησιν ὅσων καὶ τοῖς Ολυμπιονίκαις ὁ δῆμος ἐψηφίσατο.] Demetrius of Phalerum also, proposing a decree, gave the granddaughters of Aristides a triobol a day: Phalereus, in his Socrates, says that he remembers the wives of Aristides, a very poor family, Lysimachus; and having proposed a decree that the mother and her sister be given... for four ... days. [ὁ δὲ Φαληρεὺς ἐν τῷ Σωκράτει φησὶ μνημονεύειν Ἀρισείδου γυναικῶν, δ' μάλα πένητα Λεισίμαχον. τῇ δὲ μητρὶ καὶ τῇ ταύτης ἀδελφῇ ψήφισμα γράψας δωρεὰν ἐπιτιμᾶν τὸν δῆμον ἀδόναι, τεσσάρων [illegible] ΓΑΣ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ.] Demetrius himself says, while legislating, that he proposed a drachma a day for the women. [αὐτὸς μὲν φησιν ὁ Δημήτριος νομοθετῶν ἐψηφίσατο δραχμὴν ἑκάστης ἡμέρας τὰς γυναῖκας.] Socrates, already condemned by the first votes of the judges, jokingly replied that this same honour should be given to him. Marcus Tullius, in Book I of On the Orator, says: when Socrates was asked, he replied that he had earned to be decorated with the highest honours and rewards, and to have his daily sustenance provided at public expense in the Prytaneum, which was regarded as the greatest honour among the Greeks.

units.la: Statuae quoque honorem habitum fuisse benemeritis de Republica, non sinunt nos dubitare Psephismata honori Demosthenis, Democharis, Lycurgi, scripta, quae iam descripsimus: eaeque statuae, ut plurimum, in foro positae, quanquam & pars quaedam erat fori, in qua statuas ponere Legi non licebat.
units.tr: The Psephisms that we have already described, written in honour of Demosthenes, Demochares and Lycurgus, leave no doubt that statues were also given as honour to those who had deserved well of the Republic. Such statues were generally placed in the forum, although one part of the forum was a place where it was not lawful to set up statues.

units.la: DE NON PONENDIS IN ALIQUA FORI PARTE STATUIS LEX.
units.tr: ON THE LAW AGAINST PLACING STATUES IN CERTAIN PARTS OF THE FORUM

units.la: Huius Legis meminit Psephisma à Stratocle scriptum in honorem Lycurgi: ΑΓΑΘΗ ΤΥΧΗ ΔΕΔΟΧΘΑΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ ΕΠΑΙΝΕΣΑΙ ΜΕΝ ΛΥΚΟΥΡΓΟΝ ΛΥΚΟΦΡΟΝΟΣ ΒΟΥΤΑΔΗΝ ΑΡΕΤΗΣ ΕΝΕΚΑ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΟΣΥΝΗΣ, ΚΑΙ ΣΤΗΣΑΙ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΤΟΝ ΔΗ-ΜΟΝ ΧΑΛΚΗΝ ΕΙΚΟΝΑ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑΙ· ΓΡΑΦΗΝ[?] ΕΙ ΠΟΥ Ο ΝΟ-ΜΟΣ ΑΠΑΓΟΡΕΥΕΙ ΜΗ ΙΣΤΑΝΑΙ.
units.tr: The Psephisma written by Stratocles in honour of Lycurgus mentions this law: "With good fortune, it has been resolved by the people to praise Lycurgus, son of Lycophron, of the deme Boutadae, for his virtue and justice, and to set up for him a bronze statue in the agora by the people; but if any law forbids it, it is not to be set up." [ΑΓΑΘΗ ΤΥΧΗ ΔΕΔΟΧΘΑΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ ΕΠΑΙΝΕΣΑΙ ΜΕΝ ΛΥΚΟΥΡΓΟΝ ΛΥΚΟΦΡΟΝΟΣ ΒΟΥΤΑΔΗΝ ΑΡΕΤΗΣ ΕΝΕΚΑ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΟΣΥΝΗΣ, ΚΑΙ ΣΤΗΣΑΙ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΤΟΝ ΔΗΜΟΝ ΧΑΛΚΗΝ ΕΙΚΟΝΑ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑΙ· ΕΙ ΠΟΥ Ο ΝΟΜΟΣ ΑΠΑΓΟΡΕΥΕΙ ΜΗ ΙΣΤΑΝΑΙ.]

units.la: Inter praemia numerandum quoque est monumentum publice extructum. Nam benemeritis de Republica id concedebatur. Plutarchus in Aristide: [illegible, ~70 letters] Psephisma in honorem Zenonis apud Diogenem Laertium in eius vita: ΤΥΧΗ ΤΗΙ ΑΓΑΘΗΙ ΔΕΔΟΧΘΑΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ, ΕΠΑΙΝΕΣΑΙ ΜΕΝ ΖΗΝΩΝΑ ΜΝΑΣΕΟΥ ΚΙΤΤΙΕΑ, ΟΙΚΟΔΟΜΗΣΑΙ ΔΕ ΑΥΤΩΙ ΚΑΙ ΤΑΦΟΝ ΕΠΙ ΤΟΥ ΚΕ-ΡΑΜΕΙΚΟΥ ΔΗΜΟΣΙΑΙ. Dixit in Ceramico suburbano, in quo sepulcra eorum, qui in bello occubuissent. Grammatici: δύο δὲ οἱ Κεραμικοὶ Ἀθη-ναῖοι, ὁ μὲν ἔνδον τῆς πόλεως, ὁ δὲ ἔξω. ἔνθα καὶ τοὺς ἐν πολέμῳ πεπτωκότας ἐθάπτοντο δημοσίᾳ, καὶ τοὺς ὑπὸ[?] ... ἐλεγον. εἰσὶ δὲ ἔνθα καὶ ἕτερον[?] ... τῆς δημοσίας πεμπομένοις, ἕκαστος ὑπογράφαι[?] πᾶς ἑκάστῳ τάφος[?].
units.tr: Among the rewards must also be counted a monument erected at public expense, for this was granted to those who had deserved well of the Republic. Plutarch, in the Life of Aristides: [illegible passage]. A Psephisma in honour of Zeno, in Diogenes Laertius' Life of him: "With good fortune, it has been resolved by the people to praise Zeno, son of Mnaseas, of Kition, and to build him a tomb at public expense in the Kerameikos." [ΤΥΧΗ ΤΗΙ ΑΓΑΘΗΙ ΔΕΔΟΧΘΑΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ, ΕΠΑΙΝΕΣΑΙ ΜΕΝ ΖΗΝΩΝΑ ΜΝΑΣΕΟΥ ΚΙΤΤΙΕΑ, ΟΙΚΟΔΟΜΗΣΑΙ ΔΕ ΑΥΤΩΙ ΚΑΙ ΤΑΦΟΝ ΕΠΙ ΤΟΥ ΚΕΡΑΜΕΙΚΟΥ ΔΗΜΟΣΙΑΙ.] He spoke of the Kerameikos in the suburbs, where the tombs of those who had fallen in war lay. The grammarians say: there were two Kerameikoi at Athens, one inside the city and one outside it, where those who had fallen in war were buried at public expense; and there were also other places where ... each received a tomb.

units.la: Honoris quoque ergo Coronae donabantur viris benemeritis: Diogenes Laertius in Zenone: ἐτίμησι δὲ τῶν Ἀθηναῖοι σφόδρα τὸν Ζήνωνα ὥστε, ὡς καὶ τὴν πύλην αὐτοῦ τὰς κλεῖς καταπιστεύσαι, καὶ χρυσοῦ στεφάνῳ τιμῆσαι, καὶ χαλκῆ εἰκόνι. etiam fato functis hic honos habebatur, ut è populi scito facto in gratiam Zenonis iam mortui constat: ΤΥΧΗ ΤΗΙ ΑΓΑΘΗΙ ΔΕΔΟΧΘΑΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ ΕΠΑΙΝΕΣΑΙ ΜΕΝ ΖΗΝΩΝΑ ΜΝΑΣΕΟΥ ΚΙΤΤΙΕΑ, ΚΑΙ ΣΤΕΦΑΝΩΣΑΙ ΧΡΥΣΩΙ ΣΤΕΦΑΝΩΙ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΟΝ ΝΟΜΟΝ ΑΡΕΤΗΣ ΕΝΕΚΑ ΚΑΙ ΣΩΦΡΟΣΥΝΗΣ. Coronae autem istae donabantur ci-vibus, vel à Senatu, vel à populo Atheniensi, vel à popularibus, vel à tribulibus, vel denique ab exteris civitatibus. Qui à populo corona donabatur, in concione donari debebat, qui à Senatu, itidem in Senatu, idque ex hac Lege:
units.tr: Crowns of honour were likewise given to men who had deserved well. Diogenes Laertius, in the Life of Zeno: "The Athenians honoured Zeno so greatly that they entrusted to him the keys of the gate, and honoured him with a golden crown and a bronze statue." [ΕΤΙΜΗΣΑΝ ΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΖΗΝΩΝΑ ΟΙ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΙ ΣΦΟΔΡΑ ...] This honour was also paid to the dead, as is clear from a decree of the people passed in favour of Zeno after his death: "With good fortune, it has been resolved by the people to praise Zeno, son of Mnaseas, of Kition, and to crown him with a golden crown according to the law, for virtue and temperance." [ΤΥΧΗ ΤΗΙ ΑΓΑΘΗΙ ΔΕΔΟΧΘΑΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ ΕΠΑΙΝΕΣΑΙ ΜΕΝ ΖΗΝΩΝΑ ΜΝΑΣΕΟΥ ΚΙΤΤΙΕΑ, ΚΑΙ ΣΤΕΦΑΝΩΣΑΙ ΧΡΥΣΩΙ ΣΤΕΦΑΝΩΙ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΟΝ ΝΟΜΟΝ ΑΡΕΤΗΣ ΕΝΕΚΑ ΚΑΙ ΣΩΦΡΟΣΥΝΗΣ.] These crowns were given to citizens either by the Senate, by the people of Athens, by their fellow demesmen, by their fellow tribesmen, or finally by foreign states. Whoever was crowned by the people had to be proclaimed in the assembly; whoever by the Senate, likewise in the Senate; and this by the following law:

units.la: Εαὶ μὴ ἕνα ὁ δῆμος ὁ Ἀθηναίων στέφανοι, ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τ στέφανον ἀναγορεύεως· ἐαν δὲ ἡ βουλὴ, ἐν τῇ βουλευτηρίῳ· ἀλλαχῇ δ', μὴ ἐξῇναι.
units.tr: [If the people of Athens crown anyone, the crown is to be proclaimed in the assembly; if the Council, in the council chamber; otherwise it is not permitted.] [ΕΑΝ ΜΕΝ ΤΙΝΑ Ο ΔΗΜΟΣ Ο ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ ΣΤΕΦΑΝΟΙ, ΕΝ ΤΗΙ ΕΚΚΛΗΣΙΑΙ ΤΟΝ ΣΤΕΦΑΝΟΝ ΑΝΑΓΟΡΕΥΕΣΘΑΙ· ΕΑΝ ΔΕ Η ΒΟΥΛΗ, ΕΝ ΤΩΙ ΒΟΥΛΕΥΤΗΡΙΩΙ· ΑΛΛΑΧΟΙ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΕΞΕΙΝΑΙ.]

units.la: Qui corona à populo donantur, in concione donantor: qui à Senatu, itidem in Senatu: alibi vero ius non esto.
units.tr: Those who are crowned by the people are to be proclaimed in the assembly; those by the Senate, likewise in the Senate; elsewhere let it not be lawful.

units.la: Meminit Legis Aeschines ἐν τῇ πρὸς Κτησιφῶντα. δὲ ὑμῖν λεξάλλον τοὺς ὡς τῶν χαρισμάτων νόμους, ἐν οἷς ἀγορᾷ ἀπίρηται, τὸν ἐπὶ τῆς δήμου στεφανωθῆναι μὴ κηρύττεσθαι ἔξω τῆς ἐκκλησίας. M. Tullius Libro de Optimo genere Oratorum extremo: Cum esset Lex Athenis, EOS QVI A POPVLO CORONA DONARENTVR, IN CONCIONE DONARI DEBERE. Libanius in Argumento Orationis Demosthenis τῶν τῆς φιλίας, καὶ πάλιν προσηχόμενος νόμοι, τὸν καλλίονα, Εαὶ μὴ ἕνα ὁ δῆμος ὁ Ἀθηναίων στέφανοι, ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τὸν στέφανον ἀναγορεύεως· ἐαν δὲ ἡ βουλὴ, ἐν τῇ βουλευτηρίῳ· ἀλλαχῇ ἢ, μὴ ἐξῇναι. Anonymus in Argumento eiusdem: δὲ ὑπὲρ δὲ ἀναγινώσκει νόμων, τὸν καταλλίοντα ἐν Πνυκὶ στεφανοῦσθαι, οὐκ ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ. Pnyx olim locus legitimæ concionis, quod nomen cùm in Lege proculdubio occurreret, optime interpretatur Anonymus, si αὐτὴ τῆς οὐκ rescribas τοῦ, hoc modo, τὸν καλλίοντα ἐν Πνυκὶ στεφανοῦσθαι, τοῦ; ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, Pnyce corona donari: ubi? in concione. Legis ratio est apud eundem Æschinem, ne is qui corona donatur, apud posteros se ostenter, aut in praeconiis quaestum aucupetur: ὁ γὰρ νόμος Ἀλφρῶν καλλίοντα, EAN MEN TINA ΣΤΕΦΑΝΟΙ Η ΒΟΥΛΗ, ΕΝ ΤΩι ΒΟΥ-ΛΕΥΤΗΡΙΩι ΑΝΑΚΗΡΥΤΤΕΣΘΑΙ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ Ο ΔΗΜΟΣ, ΕΝ ΤΗι ΕΚΚΛΗΣΙΑι, ΑΛΛΟΘΙ ΔΕ ΜΗΔΑΜΟΥ. ἔστ' ὁ νόμος, ὦ Ἀθηναῖοι, καὶ μάλα καλῶς ἔχει. ὁ γὰρ (εἶμι) ὅτι τὴν ὁ νομοθέτης τὸν Ῥητορα σιμινιώσθαι τοὺς ἐξωθεν, ἀλλ' ἀγαπᾶν ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ πόλει ἡμῶν ὄντων τοῦ δήμου, καὶ μὴ ἐρχόλεσθαι ἐν τῆς κηρύγματα. ἀκούετε, ὦ Ἀθηναῖοι, ὅτι ὁ μὲν νομοθέτης καλῶς ἐν ΤΩι ΔΗ-ΜΩι ΕΝ ΠΝΥΚΙ ΤΗι ΕΚΚΛΗΣΙΑι. ἀναχηρύττειν τὸν ὑπὸ τοῦ δήμου στεφανούμενον, ΑΛΛΟΘΙ ΔΕ ΜΗΔΑΜΟΥ. Hæ Coronæ quæ in concione donantur, non consecrabantur, sed domi adseruabantur, futurum posteris paternæ virtutis monumentum, quo ad illam excitarentur. Æschines eadem Oratione: ἀλλ' οὐχ ὡς ἐκεῖνον τὸν ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀναρρηθέντα στέφανον γνῶτε καλεῖσθαι· ἀλλ' ἔξεστι κεκτῆσθαι, ἵνα μὴ μόνον αὐτὸς, ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ ἐξ ἐκείνων, ἔχοντες ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ὃ ὑπόμνημα, μηδέποτε κακοὶ τῷ ψυχῷ εἰς τὸν δῆμον γίνωνται. Cum igitur in concione tantum, aut in Senatu corona donari iubeant Leges, sequitur non licere in Theatro, Ludis. Anonymus in Argumento Orationis Æschinis κτησιφῶντα. δὲ ὑπὲρ δὲ, ὅτε τοῦ ἡμέρου ἀναγεγραμμένη τὸν στέφανον, ἀπαγορεύοντες τὸν νόμον μηδένα στεφανοῦσθαι ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ. Ratio est, quia illi qui in Theatro, Ludis, corona donantur, maiorem gloriam consequerentur, cum interfint ex universis Græci nominis populis aliqui, quam ij, qui in concione, in qua solis Athenien-sibus interesse ciuibus licebat. Æschines: ὃς δὲ τοῦτο τῷ ἔξω στεφθῆναι ἐκεῖς ἀναχηρυττομένους ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ μείζονα ὑμῖν ὑμᾶς τὴν ὑπὸ τοῦ δήμου στεφανωθῆναι. τῶν μὲν γὰρ ἀπεδείξατο ὁ τόπος ἡ ἐκκλησία, ἐν ᾗ ἔχῃ στεφανοῦσθαι, καὶ ἀπίρητο ἀρχῇ μυδαμοῦ κηρύττεσθαι· οἱ δ' ἀπηγορεύοντο ἐνώπιον ἀπὸ τῶν Ἑλλήνων.
units.tr: Aeschines mentions this law in his speech against Ctesiphon: "For you, I shall read out the laws concerning rewards, in which it is forbidden that anyone crowned by the people be proclaimed outside the assembly." [ΔΕΙ ... ΤΟΝ ΝΟΜΟΝ ... ΜΗ ΚΗΡΥΤΤΕΣΘΑΙ ΕΞΩ ΤΗΣ ΕΚΚΛΗΣΙΑΣ.] Cicero, at the end of his book On the Best Kind of Orator: "Since there was a law at Athens that those whom the people gave a crown should receive it in the assembly." Libanius, in the argument to a speech of Demosthenes, quotes the law again: "If the people of Athens crown anyone, the crown is to be proclaimed in the assembly; if the Council, in the council chamber; otherwise it is not lawful." The Anonymous writer, in the argument to the same speech, reads the law as requiring that the one crowned be proclaimed in the Pnyx and not in the assembly. The Pnyx was once the place of the lawful assembly; since that name would undoubtedly occur in the law, the Anonymous writer interprets it best if one rewrites the text as "that he be crowned in the Pnyx" with "not" placed in the phrase "in the assembly": "Let the one crowned be proclaimed in the Pnyx: where? In the assembly." The reason for the law is given by Aeschines in the same place: the one who receives a crown should not show himself to posterity or seek profit from proclamations. For the law says: "If the Council crowns someone, it is to be proclaimed in the council chamber; if the people, in the assembly, and nowhere else." [ΕΑΝ ΜΕΝ ΤΙΝΑ ΣΤΕΦΑΝΟΙ Η ΒΟΥΛΗ, ΕΝ ΤΩΙ ΒΟΥΛΕΥΤΗΡΙΩΙ ΑΝΑΚΗΡΥΤΤΕΣΘΑΙ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ Ο ΔΗΜΟΣ, ΕΝ ΤΗΙ ΕΚΚΛΗΣΙΑΙ, ΑΛΛΟΘΙ ΔΕ ΜΗΔΑΜΟΥ.] Aeschines adds: "This law, men of Athens, is very good. For the lawgiver did not wish the orator to be applauded by outsiders, but to be content with the approval of the people in our own city, and not to be carried away by proclamations. Hear, men of Athens, that the lawgiver rightly ordered that the one crowned by the people be proclaimed in the assembly on the Pnyx, and nowhere else." Crowns that were given in the assembly were not dedicated but kept at home, as a memorial of their ancestors' virtue to be a spur to their descendants. Aeschines in the same speech: "But you may not know that the crown proclaimed in the assembly is to be consecrated; rather, it may be kept, so that not only he himself but also his descendants, keeping the memorial in their house, may never become bad for the people." Since the laws order a crown to be given only in the assembly or in the Senate, it follows that it could not be given in the theatre or at the games. The Anonymous writer, in the argument to Aeschines' speech against Ctesiphon, says that the law forbade anyone to be crowned on the day of the festival. The reason is that those who were crowned in the theatre or at the games would win greater glory, since some from all the peoples of the Greek name were present, than those crowned in the assembly, which only Athenian citizens could attend. Aeschines: "For the place of the assembly, where it is permitted to be crowned, has been appointed for the crowned, and it was forbidden to proclaim them anywhere else; but the others were proclaimed before the Greeks."

units.la: Quando coronæ dabantur à tribulibus aut popularibus, Lege cautum est, ne darentur in Theatro, Ludis, sin fieret secus, praeco, qui praeconium fecisset, infamia notabatur:
units.tr: When crowns were given by tribesmen or fellow demesmen, the law provided that they should not be given in the theatre or at the games; and if it were done otherwise, the herald who made the proclamation was marked with infamy.

units.la: Μὴ [?] τὴν φυλὴν ἢ δῆμον ἀναγορεύ- σθαι στεφανωθέντα ἐν τῷ θεάτρῳ · ἢ ἂν [?] ἢ κήρυκα.
units.tr: [Not in the theatre is the tribe or the deme to proclaim one crowned; otherwise the herald is to be ...] [ΜΗ ΕΝ ΤΩΙ ΘΕΑΤΡΩΙ ΣΤΕΦΑΝΩΘΕΝΤΑ ΑΝΑΓΟΡΕΥΣΘΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΦΥΛΗΝ Η ΔΗΜΟΝ· ΕΙ ΔΕ ΜΗ, ΑΤΙΜΟΝ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΟΝ ΚΗΡΥΚΑ.]

units.la: Qui corona à tribulibus aut populari-bus donantur, ne donantor in Theatro, Ludis; si secus factum, praeco ignominiosus esto.
units.tr: Those who are given a crown by their tribesmen or fellow demesmen are not to be crowned in the theatre or at the games; if it is done otherwise, the herald is to be held in disgrace.

units.la: Meminit Legis Æschines Oratione iam sæpius laudata ἐν Κτησιφῶντος. μ[?]ὴ ... [?] ὁ ἀγορεύειν τὴν τῆς ... [?] τὴν ... [?] φυλὴν, ἐπειδὴ δὲ τὸν τοῦ δήμου. Οὐ[?] ... δὲ ... Ἡ ... [?]
units.tr: Aeschines, in the speech already often quoted against Ctesiphon, mentions this law: [the text is too damaged to be read reliably].

units.la: At si quis priuatim ab alio corona donaretur, donari non poterat, nisi in Senatu, aut in concione, aut in tribu, aut in populo, ex hac Lege:
units.tr: But if someone was given a crown privately by another person, it could not be given except in the Senate, in the assembly, in the tribe, or among the people, by this law:

units.la: Μηδὲ ... ἄλλῳ μηδενὸς ἀναχρῆσθαι στεφάνῳ, ὑπὸ βουλῆς, ἢ δήμου, καὶ φυλετῶν, ἢ δημοτῶν. [?]
units.tr: [Nor shall a crown be used by anyone else, except by the Senate, or the people, or the tribesmen, or the demesmen.]

units.la: A nemine alio quàm corona donetur, nisi in Senatu, aut in concione, aut inter tribules, aut inter populares.
units.tr: A crown is to be given by no one else, except in the Senate, in the assembly, among the tribesmen, or among the fellow demesmen.

units.la: Meminit Legis Æschines ἐν τῷ κτλ Κτησιφῶντος. παραπαίπτειν δὲ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ, μηδὲ ἄλλῳ μηδενὸς ἀναχρῆσθαι, ὑπὸ βουλῆς, καὶ δήμου, καὶ φυλετῶν, καὶ δημοτῶν.
units.tr: Aeschines mentions this law in his speech against Ctesiphon: "The law also departs from this, that no one may be crowned by anyone except by the Senate, the people, the tribesmen and the demesmen."

units.la: Verum hospitales coronæ ciuibus Athenien-sibus ab exteris ciuitatibus donabantur, idque in Theatro, Ludis, si id sciuisset populus Atheniensis: atque ita hac Lege, quam Διονυσιακὸν νόμον dixit Æschines, cautum est:
units.tr: Yet hospitality crowns were given to Athenian citizens by foreign states, and this could be done in the theatre or at the games, if the people of Athens knew of it. And so this law, which Aeschines called the Dionysiac law, provides:

units.la: Μὴ κηρύττεσθαι τ' Διονυσίων στέφανον ἐν τῷ θεάτρῳ, ἐὰν μὴ ψηφίσηται ὁ δῆμος· αὐτὸν δὲ τὸν στέφανον ἐεῖν [?] τῆς Ἀθηνᾶς.
units.tr: [It is not to be proclaimed in the theatre at the Dionysia, unless the people has voted for it; and the crown itself is to be ... of Athena.] [ΜΗ ΚΗΡΥΤΤΕΣΘΑΙ ΤΟΝ ΔΙΟΝΥΣΙΩΝ ΣΤΕΦΑΝΟΝ ΕΝ ΤΩΙ ΘΕΑΤΡΩΙ, ΕΑΝ ΜΗ ΨΗΦΙΣΗΤΑΙ Ο ΔΗΜΟΣ· ΑΥΤΟΝ ΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΣΤΕΦΑΝΟΝ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΑΘΗΝΑΣ.]

units.la: Nemo ab exteris ciuitatibus corona donator in Theatro Ludis, nisi id sciuerit populus. Corona Mineruæ sacra esto.
units.tr: No one from foreign cities shall be proclaimed with a crown in the theatre at the Games unless the people has been informed of it. The crown of Minerva shall be sacred.

units.la: Legem laudat Æschines ἐν τῷ κτλ Κτησιφῶντος. καὶ ἀλλ' ... τῶν νομοθέτης, μὴ κηρύττεσθαι. τὸν Διονυσίων στέφανον ἐν τῷ θεάτρῳ, ἐὰν μὴ ψηφίσηται ὁ δῆμος· ἵνα ἡ πόλις βαλομένη ... ὑμετέρων στεφάνων, ... δὲ τῷ δήμῳ ἵνα κηρυττόμενος μείζων χάρειν εἰδῇ τῷ στεφάνῳ ὑμῖν, ἵ' τοῖς στεφανοῦσι, ὅτι κηρύξαι ὑπηρέται. ἐπειδὴ τοῖς ... ἐξαπατῶντες ὑμᾶς λέγουσι, ὡς ... [?] ... (add[?] ... ἐν τῷ θεάτρῳ) ἐὰν ψηφίσηται ὁ δῆμος, ... [?] ... καὶ εἴγε σὲ τῆς ... πόλις στεφανοῦσι.
units.tr: Aeschines praises this law in his speech against Ctesiphon, where he says that the lawgiver ordered that a crown not be proclaimed in the theatre at the Dionysia unless the people has voted for it, so that the city, when it wishes to honour some of its own citizens with a crown, may make the proclamation greater, and so that the one crowned may know that the crown was given to him by you, and that the proclamation was made by your officials. Since [the opponents] deceive you by saying that ... (add [?] ... in the theatre) if the people votes it, ... and if indeed [they crown] you ... the city crowns them.

units.la: Anonymus in Argumento Orationis Æschinis: ... [?] ... Δημοσθένους ... νόμον ἐπεγον, κηλθῆναι αἰ ἀκηρύττειν ἐν ... θεάτρῳ, ἐὰν ψηφίσηται ὁ δῆμος, Αἰσχίνης ... ἐπὶ τὴν πολιτικὴν αὐτὸν ... φυλὴν, ἀλλὰ ... ξενικὴν στέφανον. Demosthenes ἐν τῷ περὶ στεφ. ὅσους στεφανοῦσιν ... δήμων, ... ἀποχειροτονίας τὴν στέφανον ποιεῖσθαι ἐν αὐτοῖς ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῖς ἰδίοις δήμοις, ἐὰν μὴ τινες ὁ δῆμος ὁ τῆς Ἀθηναίων, ἢ ἡ βουλὴ στεφανοῖ, τούτους δ' ἐξεῖναι ἐν τῷ θεάτρῳ Διονυσίοις ἀναγορεύεσθαι. Sed abutitur Orator hoc Legis Kapite: nam reuera intelligendum est de hospitali corona. Vlpianus: Τοῦτος ἢ ἀναγορεύεται ἐν τῷ θεάτρῳ Διονυσίοις ὁ κήρυξ, οἷς ἂν ὁ δῆμος ἕλῃται, ἢ ἡ βουλή· ἴσον ἦν ὅτι καὶ τὴν ξενικὴν ὁ νόμος ταῦτα διείρηκεν. Argumento est, quod hæ coronæ, quæ dabantur in Theatro, Ludis, hac Lege Mineruæ erant sacræ, quia videlicet hospitales erant. Æschines: αὐτὸν τὸν χρυσοῦν στέφανον, ὃς ἂν εἰς τὸ θέατρον ἀπὸ ἀρχῆς ἐπὶ ἀγῶνι ἱερὸν ἐστι τῆς Ἀθηναίων χαλκοῦ ὁ νόμος, ἀφελόμενος τὸν στέφανον. καὶ τοι τῆς αὐ ὑμῖν ξελμάτων τούτῳ αἰσχυνθείῳ καὶ ξενίαν τὸ δῆμου τῆν Ἀθηναίων; μὴ γὰρ ὅτι πόλις; ἀλλ' οὐδ' αὐ ἰδιώτης ἀπὸ εἰς ὕπως ἀχρηστὸν ἡμοῖτο, ὥστε ὃν αὐτὸς ἔδωκε στέφανον, ἁ- μα ἀποκηρύξαι, ἡ ἀφαιρεθῆναι, ἡ κεκλεγεῖν. Ἀλλ', ὅμως, ἀφ' ὧν ξενικὸν εἰ τὸν στέφανον, ἡ κεκλαιρώσεις γεγόνηται, ἵνα μισθὸς ἀλλοτείᾳ ὕνοιαν ἀεὶ πλείονος ποιούμενος τῆς πατρίδος χεῖρων ἡμῖν τῷ ψυχῷ. Ciuitas, quæ vellet ciuem Athenien-sem corona donare, id iuris per Legatos sibi concedi petebat. Æschines verbis iam ante laudatis: ἵνα ἡ πόλις βουλομένη τινὰ τῶν ὑμετέρων στέφανοῦ, ἀφεῖσ-θαι πίμ-λα-σθαι, δὴ δὴ τὸ δήμου.
units.tr: The anonymous writer in the Argument to Aeschines' speech says: ... [?] ... Demosthenes proposed a law that the crowns given by the demes should not be proclaimed in the theatre unless the people decided; Aeschines ... for the civic tribe, but ... the foreign crown. Demosthenes, in his speech On the Crown, says that whoever are crowned by the demes ... the crown is to be made in the assembly of the demes themselves, and that these men may be proclaimed in the theatre at the Dionysia, unless the people of Athens or the Council crowns them. But the orator abuses this chapter of the law; for it must really be understood of the hospitable crown. Ulpian: "Whoever the herald proclaims in the theatre at the Dionysia, whom the people or the Council chooses; the meaning is that the law set out these things also for the hospitable crown." The argument is that these crowns, which were given in the theatre at the Games, were sacred to Minerva under this law, because they were, of course, hospitable. Aeschines: "The golden crown itself, which from the beginning in the theatre at the contest is sacred..., the law of bronze, removing the crown." And indeed, do you feel shame at this, and the Athenian people's hospitality? For not only a city, but not even a private citizen, should ever be so useless as to proclaim publicly the crown he himself gave, or have it taken away, or ... Yet, since the hospitable crown has been made a thing of mockery, ... so that someone, always seeking the favour of another above that of the fatherland, becomes worse in soul for us. A city that wished to crown an Athenian citizen with a crown asked the Athenians, through its envoys, for this right to be granted to it. Aeschines, in the words quoted above: "so that the city, wishing to crown one of your citizens, may be permitted [to do so] ... by the people."

units.la: Qui corona donandus erat hospitali, rationem anteactæ vitæ reddebat, qua probaret dignum se esse, cui hic honos haberetur:
units.tr: Whoever was to be crowned with a hospitable crown rendered an account of his past life, by which he showed that he was worthy to receive this honour.

units.la: Τὸν στεφανούμενον ξενικῷ στεφάνῳ τὸν λόγον ποιεῖσθαι, εἰς βίον ἀξιολόγεων καὶ ἔπειτα σωφρονα. Qui corona donandus est hospitali rationes vitæ honeste & temperanter acta reddito.
units.tr: The one to be crowned with the hospitable crown should make his plea, giving an account of a life that is honourable and then temperate. He who is to be crowned with a hospitable crown shall render an account of a life lived honourably and temperately.

units.la: Legis meminit Æschines Oratione laudata: ὅταν τῶν λέγοντι Ῥήτορα ξενικῷ στεφάνῳ καὶ κηρύγματι ἐν τῆς Ἑλλησιν [?], ἐπιμαχὴν αὐτὸν χελιδὲ, καὶ τὸν λόγον, τῆς βεβαιώσεις τῆς κηρυγμάτων; ὥσπερ ὁ νόμος χελιδὴ, ποιεῖσθαι, εἰς βίον ἀξιο-λόγεων, καὶ ἔπειτα σώφρονα. Si vitam suam approbasset, populus scitum faciebat, quo posset corona, Mineruæ postea consecranda, donari in Theatro, Liberalibus τῆς κατ' ἄγρῳ.
units.tr: Aeschines, in the speech praised above, mentions the law: whenever ... the orator ... with the hospitable crown and proclamation ... and the speech ... of the confirmation of the proclamations; as the law says, [the man should] make his account of a life worthy of praise and then of a temperate one. If he had approved his life, the people passed a decree by which the crown, to be afterwards consecrated to Minerva, could be given in the theatre at the Liberalia [of the ...].

units.la: Demum inter præmia referenda est excusatio munerum, ἀπαλλαγὴ τῶν λειτουργιῶν, non quidem omnium, vt præcedenti Titulo à nobis dictum est, sed tantum ὁπόσοις ἐπιφανῶν, quam impetrabant ab Athenien-sibus viri de iis bene meriti: At vero Leptines Legem scripsit, qua cauetur, vt irrita sint populi dona, quibus concesserat ἀπαλλαγὰς benemeritis, neue quis in posterum petat excusationem munerum à populo: qui secus faxit, ignominiosus esto:
units.tr: Finally, among the rewards must be counted the excusing from public services (ἀπαλλαγὴ τῶν λειτουργιῶν). This was not granted to all, as we said in the preceding title, but only to certain illustrious persons, whom men who had deserved well of them obtained from the Athenians. Leptines, however, wrote a law by which it was provided that the gifts of the people, by which exemptions had been granted to the benefactors, be void, and that no one in future ask the people for exemption from public services. Whoever acts otherwise shall be disgraced.

units.la: ὅΠΩΣ ΑΝ ΠΛΟΥΣΙΩΤΑΤΟΙ ΛΕΙΤΟΥΡΓΟΥΣΙ ΜΗΔΕΝΑ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΕΙΝΑΙ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ἈΦ' ἈΡΜΟΔΙΟΥ ΚΑΙ ΑΡΙΣΤΟΓΕΙΤΟΝΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΤΩΝ ΕΝΝΕΑ ΑΡΧΟΝΤΩΝ, ΜΗΔΕ ΤΟΛΟΙΓΟΝ ΕΞΕΙΝΑΙ ΤῼΙ ΔΗΜῼΙ ΑΙΤΗΘΕΝΤΙ ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ. ΕΙ ΔΕ ΤΙΣ ΑΛΛῼΙ ΑΙΤΩΝ ΑΤΙΜΟΝ ΑΥΤΟΝ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΚΑΙ ΓΕΝΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΟΙΚΙΑΝ ΚΑΙ ΥΠΟΚΕΙΣΘΑΙ ΓΡΑΦΑΙΣ ΚΑΙ ΕΝΔΕΙΞΕΣΙΝ. ΕΙ ΔΕ ΚΑΙ ΕΝ ΤΟΥΤΟΙΣ ΑΛΛῼΙ ΕΝΟΧΟΝ
units.tr: That the richest men should perform the public services, and that none be exempt, except the descendants of Harmodius and Aristogeiton and the Nine Archons; and that no one further be granted, to the people asking for it, [exemption]. If anyone is convicted of asking for exemption, let him be disgraced, and his family and household, and let him be subject to written accusations and public denunciations. And if in these matters [anyone] ...

units.la: Ditissimi quique munera obeunto: nemo immunis esto, exceptis Harmodij & Aristogitonis posteris, itemque Nonemuiris. Neque in posterum populus petenti excusationem munerum concedito. Si quis petere conuincatur, ignominiosus esto cum genere suo & familia: eumque si quid, quod ignominioso non liceat, faciat, deferre cui-
units.tr: Let the wealthiest all perform the public services; no one shall be immune, except the descendants of Harmodius and Aristogeiton, and likewise the Nonemuires. In future the people shall not grant exemption from public services to one who asks for it. If anyone is convicted of asking, let him be disgraced together with his kin and his household; and if he does anything that the disgraced are not permitted to do, let it be lawful for anyone to lay information against him.

units.la: ΤΟΥΣ ΑΝΤΙΔΟΝΤΑΣ ΑΛΛΗΛΟΙΣ, ΟΤΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΑΝΤΕΣ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ-ΣΙ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΠΡΟΣΟ-ΜΝΥΕΙΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟΝΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΟΡ-ΚΟΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΜΑΥΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙ-ΚΑΙΩΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΡΓΟΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΕΙΟΙΣ ΟΣΑ ΟΙ ΝΟΜΟΙ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΠΕΠΟΙΗΚΑΣΙ. ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ, ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟ-ΣΗ, ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ.
units.tr: Those who exchange property with one another, when they have sworn, shall declare their estate and swear this oath: that they declare their own property rightly and justly, except for the silver works, which the laws have made exempt. Within three days from the day on which they swear, they shall give in the declaration.

units.la: Cum igitur, vt diximus, Athenienses pates non erant ferendo τῷ λειτουργῶν[?] oneri, subuenit illis Solon hac Lege: Καθ' ἕκαστον ἔτος εἰς πωλῆν τὰς ἀντιδόσεις. Quotannis ad facultatum permutationes pronocanto. Idque puto, maxime institutum propter Trierarchiarum munera: quanquam etiam fiebant ἀντιδόσεις propter χορηγίας. Docet Demosthenes in Leptinea: οὔτε φυλὴ πώποτε ἐκεγχεῖν ἐπιλαμβάνειν τὰς ἀντιδόσεις, ὅτι ἐπ' ἐκείνων Χορηγὸν, ὅτι ἐνεχθῆναι αὐτῷ ἄλλος τοῦτο αἰτιδιδῶναι, & in Midiana: Τραγωδὸς χειρονήχει ποτε τὸν ἐγὼ ἡ ἀνήρ ἀπὸ τῆς ἡλικίας ἀνδρῶν. ἡ ὅτι τὸν ὃ ἀνάλωμα ἐκείνης τῆς δαπάνης πολλῷ πλέον ὄντων, ὁποῖος ἀρχῇ δῆμον. καίγε ἐκεῖ ἐλάχιστα τῶν. ἐκ δὲ κλῆσις ἐξ ἀντιδόσεως. Sed maxime fiebant propter Trierarchias, idque apud Strategum. Demosthenes ἐν τῷ πρὸς Φαινίππον, ἀλλ' τὸν γὰρ οἱ νόμοι κατ' ἕκαστον ἔτος πειθοῦ τὰς ἀντιδόσεις, ὅτι ὃ διδυχὴν συνεχῶς τῇ οὐσίᾳ, οὐ πολλοῖς τὴν πολιτικὴν δημοκρατίαν εἴησαν. τῆς γὰρ Μαζυχιτηλίος μισθὸς, ὦ ἀνδρες δικάσαι, τῇ δευτέρᾳ ἰσάζοντά ἐπὶ οἶων οἱ Σπαρτιῆται τῆς τεσσάρων τῆς ἀντιδόσεως. ἐν τῷ ὡς ἐκάλεσεν τὸν νόμου Φαινίππων ξυνωνί. Fiebat autem ἀντίδοσις hoc modo. Si quis è trecentis, qui sepositi erant ad obeundas Trierarchias, sumptus tolerare non posset, Lege licebat ea classe excedere, si quem se locupletiorem vocantem ostendisset. Quod si iis qui designabatur, se ditiorem esse fateretur, in trecentos alterius loco referebatur: si negaret, permutabant inter se facultates Hypothesis Orationis Demosthenis ΠΡΟΣ Φαινίππον. ὧν σύνταγμα ἀπὸ τῆς Α Ἑλλησποντίων τεσσάρων ἀνδρῶν χρήματος τῆς πλούτου ἐξηλεγμένων, εἰς αὐτὸ καινὸν τὴν λειτουργίαν αἰ μείζονες. νόμος ὁ ἐδίδου τοῖς πεπονηκόσι τούτων ἀπολειπομένων. Suidas: Τοὺς εἰς λειτουργίαν τινὰ χρηστηριμένους, ἢ μὴ βιαλυσθέντας λειτουργεῖν, ἐπὶ ποιέω πείας, ἀπιδιδῶναι ἑπὶ τῆς ἑαυτῶν οὐσίας, λέγοντες, ἐπιλαβῶσι τὰς ἐκείνων λειτουργίας. ὅς ἂν ἰσάσκιζοντο ἢ διδύαις τὰς οὐσίας οἱ ἀποστατοπομπάι, ἢ λειτουργία. ὃ οὖν αἰτιδιδόναι τινὰς τὰς ἑαυτῶν οὐσίας, ἐὰν λαμβάνῃ τὰς ἑτέρων τῶν ἀποστατοπομπῶν λειτουργίαν, ἐλέγετο ἀντίδοσις. Is qui citauerat atque designauerat alterum, qui vicem suam munus Trierarchiæ obiret, eius ædes obsignabat, ne qua inde alio exportarentur, ex hac Lege, Παρασημαίνειν τὰ οἰκήματα τῆς ἀποξηλώνης. Eius, qui ad facultatum permutationem pronocatus est, ædes obsignantur. Meminit non semel Demosthenes Oratione laudata: αὐτὸ δὲ τὸ σημεῖα ἐὰν τῶν οἰκημάτων, ἃ παρεσημαίνειν, ἐλθὼν εἰς ἀγρὸν ἀνέῳξε, καὶ τὰς κειθᾶς ὀξίφορος, καὶ τὰ ἄλλα. Sed totum hunc morem ita graphice ibidem describit DemoDemosthenes, vt in rem praesentem deducere videatur. ἐξ ἀρχῆς δ' ὑμῖν ἀ-πόφαιν ... [?] τὰ ἡμέτερα ... [?] τῷ αἰτιᾶσθαι ... [?] διηγήσομαι. τῷ γὰρ Μεταγειτνίου μέλιος, ὦ ἀν-δρες δικασταί, τῇ δευτέρᾳ ἱσταμένου, ἐπαίων οἱ Σπαρτηλοὶ ... [?] τὰς αἰτιάσεις ... [?] τας αἰτιάσεις. ἐν τούτοις ἐκάλεσα ... [?] τὸν νόμον Φαρίππου ... [?] ... καλέσας ἡ τὴν ἀρχὴν ... [?] οἰκείων τινας ἢ φίλων, ἐπορευόμην Κυθηρῷ εἰς τὴν ἐχθρὰν αὐτοῦ. καὶ ... [?] ... ἐδέξα καὶ ... [?] ἐδεήθην ... [?] ... ἐπιστολὴν Φαρίππου ... [?] ... εἰ δὲ φησιν, ἐκέλευσον αὐτὸν εἰπεῖν ἤδη ἡ δίκη ... [?] ... τὴν ἀρχὴν ... [?] ... εἰς ἔαυτὸν ... [?] ... ἐπειτα προσεμηνάμην ... [?] τὰ οἰκήματα, ἡ τῆν ἐκέλευσον εἰς ... [?] Βασιλέα. μηδὲ ... [?] ... ὁ αὐτὸς ... [?] ... ὁ δὲ ἀπεκείνατο μοι, ὅτι ὁ λόγ, παρεγενεῖτο ... [?] ... ὁ δὲ, ἐνδον ... [?] ... τέλος δέ, ἵνα μὴ μακρηγορῶ, καθαρὰς φυλακῆν ἐνδον ... [?] ... μὴ ἐξάγαν τῷ ὕλῳ ... [?] ... ἐπαγγείλας ὅτι τὰ ἱερὰ Φαρίππου ... [?] τὸν νόμον ἀπώλεσεν, ὡς ἐχόμενον ἀπὸν εἰς ἄγυ, & paullo post rursum de obsignatione ædium. Τοιαῦτ' ἐν, ὦ ἀνδρες δικασταί, Φαρίππον, ἀρρήτιτα ... [?] ... ἡ τῆς αὐτῆς ἡμέρας, ἀρξάμενον τῷ μηδὲν δίκαιον ποιεῖν. προσεμηνάμην τὰ οἰκήματα, τὸν νόμον μοι διδωκέναι· οὕτω αἰσθέσθε.
units.tr: Since, as we said, the Athenians were not able to bear the burden of public services, Solon came to their aid with this law: each year the exchanges of property [ἀντιδόσεις] are to be demanded. I believe this was instituted chiefly on account of the trierarchies, although exchanges of property also took place on account of the choregiae. Demosthenes, in the speech against Leptines, shows that no tribe had ever been prevented from demanding exchanges, and that when the choregus was thus burdened, another could be asked to take on the duty instead. And in the speech against Meidias, he says that a tragic chorus-leader was once ... from the age of men, or because the expense of that outlay was much greater ... Yet there were very few ... by lot, from exchange. But they were made chiefly on account of the trierarchies, and that among the generals. Demosthenes, in the speech against Phaenippus: "For the laws order that each year exchanges of property be demanded, so that the wealth of the citizens may be continually distributed, and not many men may be burdened with the same service. For the trierarchy of Mazychtelius, gentlemen of the jury, was ... in the second ... the Spartans of the four ... exchange. In the speech in which I called upon the law of Phaenippus..." An exchange [ἀντίδοσις] was made in this way. If someone from among the three hundred, who had been set apart to undertake the trierarchies, could not bear the expense, the law allowed him to leave that class, if he named someone he claimed was wealthier than himself. If the man so named admitted that he was richer, he was entered in the three hundred in place of the other; if he denied it, they exchanged their estates with each other. Hypothesis to Demosthenes' speech against Phaenippus: of the men ... four men of the Hellespontine ... were examined for their wealth, and the greater ones were compelled to take on the new public service; the law gave to those who were ... of these. Suidas: those who were designated for some public service, or who did not wish to perform it, ... on account of ..., were said to give up their estates, saying that they should take over the public services of those others. Those who were summoned, or who gave their estates to the trierarchs, undertook the public service; so if some men gave up their estates, and in exchange received the public service of others, it was called an exchange [ἀντίδοσις]. He who had summoned and designated another, who would perform the trierarchy in his place, sealed that man's house, so that nothing might be carried out of it elsewhere, under this law: "to seal the houses of the one who has been challenged." The house of the one who has been challenged to exchange of property is sealed. Demosthenes mentions this more than once in the speech quoted: "the seals of the houses, which he had put on, he went into the country and opened them, and took the keys [and the rest]." But Demosthenes describes this whole custom so vividly in the same passage that he seems to bring it before our eyes: "From the beginning, men of the jury, I will set out for you ... In the month of Metagitnion, on the second day, when the Spartans ... the challenges ... I summoned ... the law of Phaenippus ... and, having summoned, I went ... some of my relatives or friends to Cythera, to his enemy ... and I received and begged ... the letter of Phaenippus ... and if he says, let him bid him speak ... then I sealed the houses ... to the king ... and he answered me that ... and he inside ... and finally, that I might not talk too long, ... the guard inside ... proclaiming that the sacred rites of Phaenippus and the law he destroyed, as being about to ... and a little after, again about the sealing of the houses." Such things, men of the jury, Phaenippus did, beginning on the same day to do nothing just; I sealed the houses, and the law gave me this right. Thus judge.

units.la: His peractis & aedibus obsignatis, is qui prouocabat ad facultatum permutationem, ad sacra vocabat eum quem suo loco obire munera volebat. Demosthenes verbis, quae paullo ante descripsimus. καὶ ἐπαγγείλας ὅτι τὰ ἱερὰ Φαρίππου καὶ τὸν νόμον ἀπώλεσεν, ὡς ἐχόμενον ἀπὸν εἰς ἄγυ, nempe inter haec sacra iusiurandum ab utroque concipiebatur ex hac Lege: ΤΟΥΣ ΑΝΤΙΔΙΔΟΝ-ΤΑΣ ΑΛΛΗΛΟΙΣ ΟΤΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΑΝΤΕΣ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩΣΙ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΓΡΟΣΟΜΝΥΕΙΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟΝΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΟΡΚΟΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΜΑΥΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΩΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΡΓΟΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΕΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣΑ ΟΙ ΝΟΜΟΙ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΓΕΠΟΙΗΚΑΣΙ. Qui facultates inter se permutant, se suas indicaturos facultates iurante conceptis his verbis. Indico facultates meas recte atque iuste, exceptis iis, quae in argentifodinis sunt, quas Leges immunes faciunt. Laudat hanc Legem Demosthenes ἐν τῷ ... ΚΑΙ ΚΑΤΗΞΙΡΗ ΤΗ ΟΡΚΟΥ, ἐν ὧ-μοσι ... [?] τῆς ἀποφάσεως, λέγων, ὅτι πλὴν τῶν ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις ... [?] ἀποφαίνειν τῶν ἄλλων ... [?] ὥσπερ ὁ χρὴ τοῖς νόμοις ὀμνύειν, τῶτ' ἄξιον κατηγορίας ὅν. ὑμεῖς ἐστε, ὦ ἄνδρες δικασταί, ὑμεῖς γὰρ ἐτάξατε τὸν νόμον, ὃς ἀφορρήσω οὕτω λέγ, ΤΟΥΣ ΑΝΤΙΔΙΔΟΝΤΑΣ ΑΛΛΗΛΟΙΣ, &c. Indicare igitur oportebat omnes suas facultates, praeterquam eas, quae in fodinis sunt, Lege enim non tenentur.
units.tr: When these things were done and the houses sealed, the man who challenged the other to an exchange of property summoned to the sacred rites the man whom he wished to take over his public duties. Demosthenes, in the words we quoted a little earlier, says: "and having declared that he had destroyed the sacred rites and the law of Phaenippus, as being in the clutches of the court" [καὶ ἐπαγγείλας ὅτι τὰ ἱερὰ Φαρίππου καὶ τὸν νόμον ἀπώλεσεν, ὡς ἐχόμενον ἀπὸν εἰς ἄγυ]. Namely, among these sacred rites both parties swore an oath under this law: "Those who exchange property with one another, when they have sworn, shall declare their property rightly and justly, except for what is in the silver mines, which the laws make exempt" [ΤΟΥΣ ΑΝΤΙΔΙΔΟΝΤΑΣ ΑΛΛΗΛΟΙΣ ΟΤΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΑΝΤΕΣ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩΣΙ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΠΡΟΣΟΜΝΥΕΙΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟΝΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΟΡΚΟΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΜΑΥΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΩΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΡΓΟΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΕΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣΑ ΟΙ ΝΟΜΟΙ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΓΕΠΟΙΗΚΑΣΙ]. Those who exchange their property with each other, having sworn, shall declare their property, rightly and justly, excepting those things that are in the silver mines, which the laws make exempt. Demosthenes praises this law in the speech ... and, having recited the oath, where the declaration is made, says that, except for what is in the mines, the other things are to be declared as the law requires; "for the law commands that the oath be sworn in this way," and this is worthy of accusation. "You are the ones, men of the jury, for you enacted the law, which I shall read as it is written: those who exchange with each other..." Therefore all their property had to be declared, except what lay in the mines, since by law those are not included.

units.la: Τῶν δὲ τῆς ἐργασίας μηδὲν ἀποφαίνειν: Bonorum, quae in fodinis sunt, nihil indicaio.
units.tr: Of the goods of the mining works they declare nothing [Τῶν δὲ τῆς ἐργασίας μηδὲν ἀποφαίνειν]. Of the goods that are in the mines they declare nothing.

units.la: Meminit huius Legis praecedens, quam descripsimus: ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΜΑΥΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΩΣ, ΓΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΡΓΟΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΕΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣΑ ΟΙ ΝΟΜΟΙ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΓΕΠΟΙΗΚΑΣΙ. Lauda: Demosthenes hac Oratione. ὥσπερ δὲ μοι τὸν νόμον ἐκέλευσεν ἀναγνῶναι, τῶν οὐκ ἐῶντα τὴν ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις οὖσαν ἀποφαίνειν.
units.tr: The preceding law, which we have quoted, recalls this law: "I declare my property rightly and justly, except what is in the silver mines, which the laws make exempt" [ΑΠΟΦΑΙΝΩ ΤΗΝ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΜΑΥΤΟΥ ΟΡΘΩΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΩΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝ ΤΟΙΣ ΕΡΓΟΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΕΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣΑ ΟΙ ΝΟΜΟΙ ΑΤΕΛΗ ΓΕΠΟΙΗΚΑΣΙ]. Praise: Demosthenes in this speech. And just as he ordered me to read the law, which forbade declaring what is in the mines.

units.la: Indicium autem facultatum suarum intra tres, ex quo iurauerant, dies dare debebant ex hac Lege: ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΗι ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ. Intra tres, ex quo iurarunt, dies facultates suas indicanto. Legem laudat Demosthenes hac Oratione: ὁμοίως γὰρ τῇ ἐνδικάτῃ τῆς Βοηδρομιῶνος μηνὸς, ἀποφαίνειν ὀρθῶς ἐ δικαίως τὴν οὐσίαν, τὸν νόμον ἀφορίζοντος λέγοντος, ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ, ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΗ ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ. ἐδίδοτο μὲν τοῖς ποσολληταὶ ... [?] πρὸς τὸ δικαστήριον μὴ Πολυδύκτου καὶ Τερεντίου, ὥστε τὸν μὲν ἀπὸ Αἰσχύλου σιωπᾶν ἑαυτῷ· ἐπειτα τὴν ἀποφάνσιν τῆς οὐσίας ἀκριβέστερον μὴ πολλὰς ἡμέρας. ἡγησάμενος δ' ἐγὼ ἡ μετέλου ἡ ἀποδιδόμενος ἐν πολίτῃ μὴ διὰ ... [?] τὴν κεφαλὴν εἰς τὸ δικαστήριον βαδίζειν, ἐπισθὼν τὴν μὲν σιωπᾶσθαι τοῦτον τὴν ἀπὸ τῆς Αἰσχύλου, τῇ εἰδὴ φήμης τοῦ Βοηδρομιῶνος μηνὸς, ὁμολογῆσαι ποιήσασθαι τὴν δ' ἀποφάνσιν τῆς οὐσίας, τῇ ἐκτῇ φήμης. Atque ex his supplendus est Demosthenis locus, qui hac primore Oratione legitur. αὐτὴ μὲν τῇ τεταρτῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἀφ' ἧς ὅμως τὴν ἀποφάνσιν δοῦναί μοι τῆς οὐσίας τῆς αὐτῆς χρὴ τὸν νόμον, ἢ εἰ μὲν πότε ἐβούλετο, τῇ γὰρ ἐκτῇ δοῦναι τῆς Βοηδρομιῶνος μηνὸς, ὧν δὲ ληξίς μου ἔσται, καὶ οὐ ἡ ὁμολόγησις δοῦναι τὴν ἀποφάνσιν. Rescribendum enim est, ex iis quae ante descripsimus: τῇ γὰρ ἐκτῇ δοῦναι φήμης τῆς Βοηδρομιῶνος μηνὸς, ὧν δὲ ληξίς μου ἔσται. Rursum meminit huius Legis: ἀλλ' ἀλλ' ἐάς δύο νόμους ἔχει πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἀποβεβηκώς, ἕνα μὲν, τὸν χιλιοστὸν τεταρτὴν ἡμέραν, ἀφ' ἧς ἂν ὁμοίως, τὴν οὐσίαν ἀποφάνειν. Eaque maxime nititur, & in invidiam facit Phaenippo: ὅτι δὲ δευτέρῳ μὲν τὴν ἀποφάνσιν ἐδωκας μοι, τὸν νόμον χελεύοντος τεταρτὴν ἡμέραν, πῶς ἴσχειν δια[?]κλεισαί, καὶ ἐφλήμησε πλέον, ἢ τεταρτῇ ζαλαίτων. Scripto dabatur hoc indicium.
units.tr: The declaration of their property they had to give within three days from when they swore, under this law: "Within three days from the time they swear, let them give the declaration" [ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΗι ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ]. Within three days from when they have sworn, let them declare their property. Demosthenes cites the law in this speech: in like manner, on the ninth day of the month Boedromion, one must declare the property rightly and justly, the law fixing the limit and saying: "within three days, from when they swear, they shall give the declaration" [ΤΡΙΩΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ, ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΟΜΟΣΗ ΔΙΔΟΝΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΑΠΟΦΑΝΣΙΝ]. The declaration was given to the officials before the court [...]; so that the one who was ... should keep silent; then the more exact declaration of the property, not many days later. And I, thinking that the one who has been challenged to an exchange should not go to the court with his head ..., caused him to be silent about the things from Aeschylus, and to make the acknowledgment on the sixth day of Boedromion, and to give the declaration of the property on the sixth day. And from this the passage of Demosthenes, which is read in this first speech, must be supplied. On the fourth day from which they must give me the declaration of the property, as the law says, or if he wished at some other time: for on the sixth day of the month Boedromion, and on the day of my ..., and the acknowledgment should give the declaration. For it must be read, from what we described before: on the sixth day of the month Boedromion, and on the day of my ... Again he recalls this law: but Phaenippus, having two laws against you, one, the thousandth ... on the fourth day from which they should similarly declare their property. And this argument rests most heavily on it, and it stirs up hatred against Phaenippus: that you gave me the declaration on the second day, when the law ordered the fourth day, how could ... and he was more than ... on the fourth day. The declaration was given in writing.

units.la: Harpocration: ἀπόφασις, ὃ ἀποφαίνειν ἀφ' γεγραμμένῃ χρὴ μέρος ὁποῖον ὑπὸ ἐγὼ ἐὰν ἃ ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως μάλιστα ἔχει. Dabatur Strategis hoc indicium. Demosthenes hac Oratione: εἰς ὃ Στρατηγοῖ ἐδωκε τὴν ἀποφάνσιν. rursum: ἀπιγραφόμενον τοῖς τοῖς Στρατηγοῖς τούτῳ τὴν ἀπογραφήν. Litigantibus Strategi iudices sortiebantur. εἰσάγεσαν οἱ Στρατηγοὶ περὶ τειχεσφρχίας καὶ δυνάμεως. At cum tempus illius Choragi. quia maiores, quibusdam festis, quam aliis, sumptus fiebant, disceptabant Choragi, ut hoc vel illo definito tempore necessum illis esset λειτουργεῖν. ita interpretor haec Suidae verba. ὅτι διὰ ἐκ ἀπόκρισι[?] ἐστὶν, ὡς ποιοῦσι τοῖς μὴ ὅλοις χορηγῶν. εἰς ἂν ἀπελθεῖν βούλονται ποτὲ χρὴ λειτουργεῖν αὐτοῖς. [illegible, ~60 letters] Vlpianus ad can-dem, [illegible, ~40 letters].
units.tr: Harpocration: a declaration, which one ought to make in writing, is a part of which ... [garbled]. This declaration was given to the Strategi. Demosthenes in this speech: he gave the declaration to the Strategi. Again: the declaration written out to the Strategi. When the Strategi were in litigation, the judges were chosen by lot. The Strategi brought cases concerning the fortification and the forces. But when the time of a particular choragus came, since greater expenses were incurred for some festivals than for others, the choragi disputed, so that at this or that appointed time it would be necessary for them to perform the public service [λειτουργεῖν]. I interpret these words of Suidas thus: because it is not a declaration, as those who are not wholly choragi do, when they wish to depart, they must perform the service at some time. [illegible] Ulpian on the same, [illegible].

units.la: Munerum autem, quæ pacis sunt, [illegible, ~25 letters] immunitates dabantur viris de Republica bene meritis. Vlpianus ad Leptineam: [illegible, ~40 letters]. Sed oppido pauci: nam sua ætate Demosthenes aduersus Leptinem, qui neminem immunem esse volebat, disputans, ostendit vix esse cives quinque aut sex, totidemque inquilinos, qui immunes sint: Sed locus adscribendus est, vt mendo liberetur: [illegible, ~70 letters], [illegible, ~50 letters]. Corruptus est proculdubio hic numerus, [illegible, ~40 letters]. Nam aut intelligendus est in vniuersum de omnibus, qui toto vertente anno Choragi, aut Gymnasiarchi erant, aut epulum tribulibus suis præbebant: Atqui certum est longe plures fuisse; aut de immunibus tantum, quos ad obeunda munera hæc cogi volebat Leptines, de quibus certè intelligendus est: Iam verò cum è ciuibus, tum ex inquilinis, immunes plures non erant triginta, vt hic Demosthenes testatur: Quare non potuerunt esse sexaginta, aut paullo plures. Adde quod, si quidem triginta tantum sunt, ne quidem triginta quotannis hæc obire munera potuerunt; cum nonnisi altero quoque anno ex Lege munera obeantur. Adde quod non tot erant Choragi, aut Gymnasiarchi, aut [illegible, ~10 letters] inquilinorum, quot fuerunt Ciuium: non enim omnibus fe[?]tis, quibus Cives ludos præbebant, præbebant quoque inquilini, vt in superioribus diximus. Referibo igitur apud Demosthenem: [illegible, ~45 letters]. id est, præteriti erunt vndecim forte, aut paullo plures, hi omnes. Altero tantum quoque anno obire solebant munera Athenienses: Ergo è quindecim, totidem demus, ciuibus immunibus, singulis annis septem, aut octo munera obibunt: Adde pauculos ex inquilinis, nam, vt diximus, tot munera non obibant, aut toties, quot aut quoties obibant cives: Ergo undecim fere, aut paullo plures ex his triginta immunibus, qui obire possent munera, quotannis illa non obibunt.
units.tr: Of the public burdens, however, which concern peace, [illegible] exemptions were given to men who had deserved well of the commonwealth. Ulpian on Leptines: [illegible]. But very few: for in his own age Demosthenes, arguing against Leptines, who wanted no one to be exempt, showed that there were scarcely five or six citizens, and as many resident aliens, who were exempt. But the passage must be quoted so that it may be freed from the error: [illegible]. Without doubt this number is corrupt, [illegible]. For either it must be understood generally of all who, through the whole year, were choragi or gymnasiarchs, or who provided a feast for their tribesmen; yet it is certain that there were far more; or it must be understood only of the exempt, whom Leptines wanted to compel to undertake these burdens, and of whom it must certainly be understood. Now, truly, neither among the citizens nor among the resident aliens were there more than thirty exempt, as this Demosthenes testifies. Therefore there could not have been sixty, or a few more. Add that, if there are only thirty, not even thirty could have undertaken these burdens each year, since by law the burdens are undertaken only every second year. Add that there were not as many choragi or gymnasiarchs, or [illegible] of resident aliens, as there were of citizens: for not all the festivals for which the citizens provided games had resident aliens providing them too, as we said above. I therefore refer to Demosthenes: [illegible]. That is, there will be passed over perhaps eleven, or a few more, all of these. The Athenians used to undertake burdens only every second year. Therefore out of fifteen, we assign as many exempt citizens, so that yearly seven or eight will undertake burdens. Add a few of the resident aliens, for, as we said, they did not undertake as many burdens, nor as often, as the citizens did. Therefore about eleven, or a few more, of these thirty exempt, who could undertake burdens, will not undertake them yearly.

units.la: Sed munerum, quæ bellum spectant, nemo erat immunis. Vlpianus ad Leptineam: [illegible, ~50 letters], [illegible, ~30 letters]. Et quidem [illegible, ~20 letters] legitur hæc
units.tr: But of the burdens which concern war, no one was exempt. Ulpian on Leptines: [illegible], [illegible]. And indeed [illegible] this is read.

units.la: Lex:
units.tr: Law:

units.la: ΑΤΕΛΗ ΔΕ ΜΗΔΕΝΑ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡ-ΧΙΑΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝΝΕΑ ΑΡΧΟΝ-ΤΩΝ.
units.tr: ΑΤΕΛΗ ΔΕ ΜΗΔΕΝΑ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΡΙΗΡΑΡΧΙΑΣ, ΠΛΗΝ ΤΩΝ ΕΝΝΕΑ ΑΡΧΟΝΤΩΝ [Let no one be exempt from the trierarchy, except the nine archons].

units.la: Nemo, præter Nouemviros, triremis instruendæ im-munis esto.
units.tr: Let no one be exempt from fitting out a trireme, except the Nine Archons.

units.la: Laudat hanc Legem Demosthenes in Leptinea: ἀλλὰ μὲν, ὅτι τῆς τειχεραρχίας χιῶν ... ἀτελὴς ἐς᾽ ἀτελής, εἴμη μὴ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι πόλεως. ὅμως δὲ καὶ τὸν νόμον ὑμῖν αὐτὸν ἀπαγγεῖλαι. λέγει τῶν δὲ τῆς τειχεραρχῶν νόμον, καὶ λέγε τοῦτο αὐτοῖς ATEΛH ΔΕ MHΔΕΝΑ EINAI TPIHPAPXIAΣ ΠΛΗΝ TΩN ENNEA APXON-TΩN. Vlpianus: πρὸς τῆς γὰρ ὁ τῶν τειχεραρχίας σωσεῖλαι [?] πλὴν τὴν ἐκείνου Ἀρχόν-των. Ac ne ipsi quidem inquilini immunes erant. Demosthenes hac Ora-tione: ἀρξ' ὃ γεγράφθαι ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ἀφρόδεν MHΔΕΝΑ, μήτε τῆς πολιτῶν, μήτε τῶν ἰσοτελῶν, μήτε τῶν ξένων, EINAI ATEΛH. adeoque cogi ad obeunda hæc munera inquilinos docent Grammatici: ἐπεβάλλοντ᾽ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἰατὰς ἐκ τῶν μὲ-πρὸς τὰς. Certè qui λῃτουργίας sibi mandatas non obibat, in vincula conijciebatur. Demosthenes in Timocratea: αἰτίαν τὰ ζυκατῶν ἐδὲ ἐπ᾽ ἐκ ἀφ᾽ ἀφο-σμάτων ἐν λόγῳ, τοὺς μὲν εἰσφέρειν ἐπὶ ἐπιποίησας, τοὺς δ᾽ τειχεραρχῆν κελεύοντας, τοὺς δὲ πόλεῖ, τοὺς δὲ ἕκαστα ποιεῖν, ὧν διαι. Οὐκοῦν ἐκ τοῦτο γίγνεσθαι, διαταξεῖα πληγωδτι, καὶ καταγ-γνώσκει διαμένειν τῶν ἀκοσμοιούντων.
units.tr: Demosthenes praises this law in the speech against Leptines: but, because of the fortress-commander's office ... exempt, unless you know of the city. Nevertheless, let the law itself be announced to you. It speaks of the law of the fortress-commanders, and says this to them: [ATEΛH ΔΕ MHΔΕΝΑ EINAI TPIHPAPXIAΣ ΠΛΗΝ TΩN ENNEA APXON-TΩN]. Ulpian: for the ... of the fortress-commanders ... except the nine archons. And not even the resident aliens were exempt. Demosthenes in this speech: from what is written in the law, "no one" [MHΔΕΝΑ], neither of the citizens, nor of the equal-taxed, nor of the strangers, "shall be exempt" [EINAI ATEΛH]. Accordingly the grammarians teach that the resident aliens too were compelled to undertake these burdens. Certainly whoever did not perform the public service assigned to him was cast into chains. Demosthenes in the speech against Timocrates: for the ... of those who ... in the speech, some to bring in contributions, others to command the fortresses, others to the city, others to do each thing ... Therefore, if this were done, they ordered ... and he condemns those who persisted in disobedience.

units.la: Neque item immunes erant τῶν εἰσφορῶν, quæ conferebantur imminente bello:
units.tr: Nor were they exempt from the levies that were raised when war threatened:

units.la: Τῶν εἰς τὸν πόλεμον πασῶν εἰσφορῶν μηδεμία ἀτελής.
units.tr: None of all the levies for war was exempt. [Τῶν εἰς τὸν πόλεμον πασῶν εἰσφορῶν μηδεμία ἀτελής.]

units.la: Conferenda in bellum pecunia nemo immunis esto.
units.tr: No one shall be immune from contributing money for war.

units.la: Legis meminit Demosthenes in Leptinea: τῆς γὰρ εἰς τὸν πόλεμον καὶ τῆν Γ-πολιτείας τῆς πόλεως πασῶν εἰσφερῶν καὶ τειχεραρχῶν, ἐρῶς καὶ δικαίως, ςοῦτις ἐς᾽ ἀτελὴς ἐν τῇ παλαιῶν νόμων. Rursum: τῆς γὰρ εἰς τὸν πόλεμον πασῶν εἰσφορῶν καὶ τειχεραρχῶν ἐκ τῆς παλαιῶν νόμων οὐκ εἰσὶν ἀτελεῖς. Vlpianus ad hanc Leptineam: ἀλ-λὰ καὶ αὐτὸς πρέχεσθαι νόμῳ ἐκουτ᾽, τ κελεύοντα μηδένα ἀτελῆ εἴ τῆς εἰς τὸν πόλε-μον.
units.tr: Demosthenes mentions this law in the Leptinea: "For of all the levies for war and of the trierarchies of the city, none is exempt, according to the old laws." [τῆς γὰρ εἰς τὸν πόλεμον καὶ τῆν Γ-πολιτείας τῆς πόλεως πασῶν εἰσφερῶν καὶ τειχεραρχῶν, ἐρῶς καὶ δικαίως, ςοῦτις ἐς᾽ ἀτελὴς ἐν τῇ παλαιῶν νόμων.] Again: "For of all the levies for war and of the trierarchies, none is exempt according to the old laws." [τῆς γὰρ εἰς τὸν πόλεμον πασῶν εἰσφορῶν καὶ τειχεραρχῶν ἐκ τῆς παλαιῶν νόμων οὐκ εἰσὶν ἀτελεῖς.] Ulpian, on this Leptinea, says: "But he himself is also bound by the law, which orders that no one be exempt from the levy for war." [ἀλ-λὰ καὶ αὐτὸς πρέχεσθαι νόμῳ ἐκουτ᾽, τ κελεύοντα μηδένα ἀτελῆ εἴ τῆς εἰς τὸν πόλε-μον.]

units.la: Quanquam mercatores immunes fuisse τῆς εἰσφορᾶς colligimus ex hoc Aristophanis versu Pluto:
units.tr: That merchants were exempt from the levy we gather from this verse of Aristophanes in the Plutus:

units.la: ΔΙ. ἀλλ᾽ ἔμπορος; ΣΥ. καὶ σκέπτομαί γ᾽ ὅταν τύχω.
units.tr: DI. But a merchant? SY. Yes, and I take care of myself whenever I get the chance. [ΔΙ. ἀλλ᾽ ἔμπορος; ΣΥ. καὶ σκέπτομαί γ᾽ ὅταν τύχω.]

units.la: Euphroniusque apud Scholiastem Comici expressis verbis docet: πῶς τῆς πολιτῶν ἰωΐκα χρημάτων ὡ εἰσφορᾷ ἀρ᾽ εἰς τὴν πόλιν, τὴν ἐμπορείαν ἐπερωτήσαι, τὰ εἰσφορᾶν βουλόμενοι φυγεῖν. ἀζήμιοι γὰρ ὅτι διεφυλάττοντο, ὡς φησὶν Εὐφρόνιος, ὡς τὴν πόλιν ἀφελοῦντες πλάσται, ἀφ᾽ τῆς αὐτῶν ἐμπορείας ὅ̇θ̇ ... λέγει, ὅτι ὅταν χρόνοις πόλεμον εἰσφοράς, ἐμποσῶν ἐμαυτῶν ἀποκαλῶ.
units.tr: Euphronius too, in the scholiast on the comic poet, teaches this in express words: that when the citizens were asked to contribute to the city from their property, the merchants, wishing to escape the levy, sought to be counted as traders; for, as Euphronius says, they were not punished, since they were regarded as benefiting the city by their trade. He says that when war and levies came, he called himself a merchant. [πῶς τῆς πολιτῶν ἰωΐκα χρημάτων ὡ εἰσφορᾷ ἀρ᾽ εἰς τὴν πόλιν, τὴν ἐμπορείαν ἐπερωτήσαι, τὰ εἰσφορᾶν βουλόμενοι φυγεῖν. ἀζήμιοι γὰρ ὅτι διεφυλάττοντο, ὡς φησὶν Εὐφρόνιος, ὡς τὴν πόλιν ἀφελοῦντες πλάσται, ἀφ᾽ τῆς αὐτῶν ἐμπορείας ὅ̇θ̇ ... λέγει, ὅτι ὅταν χρόνοις πόλεμον εἰσφοράς, ἐμποσῶν ἐμαυτῶν ἀποκαλῶ.]

units.la: Conferebantur autem aliquando hæ pecuniæ, si periculum esset in mora, à ditioribus, qui posteà à popularibus suis exigebant: εἰσφορὰ autem fiebat ob bona, quæ possidebat quisque, ita si quis in pluribus Atticæ populis agros possideret, & inter plures & diuersos populares pecuniam conferebat. Ilta omnia facile est colligere ex his Demosthenis verbis ὁ τῶν τοῖς Γολυχλία. ὑ μόνον ζήνων, ὦ ἀδύρεις δικαστὰ, τὰ τῶν τειχεραρχίας ἀπλίσκων τότε οὔτε πολυτελῆ ὄντα, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν χρημάτων, ὥστε εἰς τὴν ἐκπλεῖον ἐπιφέσαι ... μὴ ἐς ἐλάχιστον ἐγὼ ὑμῖν πεσοῦσα. δόξαν δὲ ὑμῖν ... τὴν δημοτῶν τοὺς βυλᾶς ... ἀπ-νεγκεῖν τοὺς πεσοῦσας τὴν τε δημοτῶν, καὶ τῶν ἐγκεκλημένων, ... ὁ ἐπὶ μὴ τὸν ὁ̇ ... ἐποίησαν. καὶ ὅταν ἐγὼ ὁ̇ ... φασὶ ποιησάμενος, ὅτι ὅ̇ τειχεραρχῶ, καὶ οὐκ ἀν δυναίμην δύο λῃτουργίας λειτουργεῖν, ὅτε αἱ νόμοι ἐῶσιν. ἀπορα, ὑφ᾽ ἑτέρων προεξειλεγμένα, τὰ δὲ ἄπορα, ὑπολείπα. Quare si quis tributum non inferret, publicanda erant eius bona, non vero is vinciendus. Demosthenes in Androtiana: εἰ τις ἐχθρὸς αὐτὸν, τὰς εἰσφορὰς, ποτέρων τὰ κτήματα, ἐκ τῶν ἐχθρῶν; τὰ κτήματα, φησὶν δὲ· ἀπὸ γὰρ τούτων εἰσφέρομεν. τίνος οὖν ἕνεκα ἀφεὶς δὲ τὰ χώρια δημεύει, τὰς οἰκίας, καὶ τῶν ἀπογραφῶν, ἐδὲς καὶ ἴδιοις ἐς πολίτας αἰδέσιμους.
units.tr: Such contributions were sometimes collected, if there was danger in delay, from the wealthier men, who afterwards exacted the sums from their fellow citizens. The levy was imposed on the goods that each person possessed; so if someone held land in several demes of Attica, he paid money among several different demes. All of this is easily gathered from these words of Demosthenes: "Not only did I, men of the jury, perform the trierarchy at that time, which was not costly, but also the money, so that I was the first to contribute ... not to the least extent ... and when you decided that the poorer ones should bear ... you took from the rich and from those who were listed ... and when I ... they say I was a trierarch and could not perform two liturgies, since the laws do not allow it ... the poor, chosen by others ... the poor, left behind." [ὁ τῶν τοῖς Γολυχλία. ὑ μόνον ζήνων, ὦ ἀδύρεις δικαστὰ, τὰ τῶν τειχεραρχίας ἀπλίσκων τότε οὔτε πολυτελῆ ὄντα, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν χρημάτων, ὥστε εἰς τὴν ἐκπλεῖον ἐπιφέσαι ... μὴ ἐς ἐλάχιστον ἐγὼ ὑμῖν πεσοῦσα. δόξαν δὲ ὑμῖν ... τὴν δημοτῶν τοὺς βυλᾶς ... ἀπ-νεγκεῖν τοὺς πεσοῦσας τὴν τε δημοτῶν, καὶ τῶν ἐγκεκλημένων, ... ὁ ἐπὶ μὴ τὸν ὁ̇ ... ἐποίησαν. καὶ ὅταν ἐγὼ ὁ̇ ... φασὶ ποιησάμενος, ὅτι ὅ̇ τειχεραρχῶ, καὶ οὐκ ἀν δυναίμην δύο λῃτουργίας λειτουργεῖν, ὅτε αἱ νόμοι ἐῶσιν.] Hence, if anyone did not pay a tax, his goods were to be confiscated, not he himself imprisoned. Demosthenes, in the Androtion: "If someone is hostile to him, [does he pay] the contributions, and from whose goods? From the goods, he says; for from these we pay. Why then, leaving aside the country estates, does he confiscate the houses ..." [εἰ τις ἐχθρὸς αὐτὸν, τὰς εἰσφορὰς, ποτέρων τὰ κτήματα, ἐκ τῶν ἐχθρῶν; τὰ κτήματα, φησὶν δὲ· ἀπὸ γὰρ τούτων εἰσφέρομεν. τίνος οὖν ἕνεκα ἀφεὶς δὲ τὰ χώρια δημεύει, τὰς οἰκίας, καὶ τῶν ἀπογραφῶν, ἐδὲς καὶ ἴδιοις ἐς πολίτας αἰδέσιμους.]

units.la: DE PRÆMIIS BENE DE Republica meritorum, TITVLVS VI.
units.tr: On the rewards for those who have deserved well of the Commonwealth, Title VI.

units.la: Quanquam nullo honestamento virtus negat, honore tamen ad eius studium excitari homines, nemo est tam auerso ab omni laude animo, qui non id vltro fateatur: itaque praemiis ad bene de Republica merendum suos ciues inuitarunt Athenienfium Legislatores. Inter ea primum quod occurrit, προεδρία est, de qua Aristophanes Equitibus:
units.tr: Although virtue needs no honour to recommend it, there is nobody so averse to all praise that he would not readily admit that men are roused to its pursuit by honour. Accordingly the lawgivers of Athens invited their citizens to deserve well of the Commonwealth by rewards. The first of these that comes to mind is proedria [προεδρία] (front seating), of which Aristophanes says in the Knights:

units.la: νῦν δ᾽ ἐὰν μὴ προεδρίας φέρωσι, καὶ τὰ σῖτα, ὃ μαχεῖσθαί φασιν.
units.tr: "But now, if they do not bring proedriai and the meals, they say they will fight." [νῦν δ᾽ ἐὰν μὴ προεδρίας φέρωσι, καὶ τὰ σῖτα, ὃ μαχεῖσθαί φασιν.]

units.la: Quae προεδρία quid sit, optime explicat Interpres Comici ad hunc locum, & ex eo Suidas: Ἰμῖν καὶ ἐξ ἕδρας ἕτερος. δέξω δὲ τὰς ἡμῖν τούτοις τυχοῦσι, καὶ ἐν βουλευτηρίῳ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, καὶ ἐν θεάτρῳ, ἡ ἐν ἄλλῳ πομπῇ συλλόγῳ τῶν προεδρίαν συλλόγων οἱ ἂν ἐκεῖνοι εἰσελθόντες, αὐτοὶ εἰς τὸν ἐκεῖνον τόπον καθίσαι. Erant autem in Theatris sedes secretae aliae & aliis, & assignatae ordinibus pro eorum dignitate, unde apud Comicum Auibus:
units.tr: What proedria is, the commentator on the comic poet explains very well at this passage, and Suidas after him: "Another from a seat. I will receive those who happen to be among us in the council-chamber, in the assembly, in the theatre, or in any other procession or gathering, and who have entered and sat down in that place as holders of proedria." In the theatres, moreover, there were seats set apart for different people, assigned to the orders according to their rank. Hence in Aristophanes' Birds: [Greek: χαῖρ᾽ ἐκ, ἀὐδρα τῆς γυναικὸς ἐν Βουλευτικῷ] (Hail, you who are from the wife's place in the Council-chamber).

units.la: χαῖρ᾽ ἐκ, ἀὐδρα τῆς γυναικὸς ἐν Βουλευτικῷ.
units.tr: "Hail, you who are from the wife's place in the Council-chamber." [χαῖρ᾽ ἐκ, ἀὐδρα τῆς γυναικὸς ἐν Βουλευτικῷ.]

units.la: Ἐκ πῆς, inquit Scholiastes, τῇ ἡκ᾽ ξυ, ὁ αἰχμῶν τῶν Βουλευτῶν, ὡς καὶ ὁ τῶν Εφήβοις Εφηβικὸς. Distinctaeque erant virorum & feminarum sedes ex Sphyromachi Psephismate: ὁ δὲ Σφυρομάχης ψήφισμα εἰσηγήσατο, τὰς γυναῖκας ἐν τοῖς ἄνδρας χωρὶς καθίζεσθαι.
units.tr: "From the ...," says the Scholiast, "the front seat of the councillors, as also the Ephebic seat of the Ephebes." Men's and women's seats were also separated by a decree proposed by Sphyromachus: [ὁ δὲ Σφυρομάχης ψήφισμα εἰσηγήσατο, τὰς γυναῖκας ἐν τοῖς ἄνδρας χωρὶς καθίζεσθαι] (Sphyromachus proposed a decree that the women should sit apart from the men).

units.la: Fuit & ἀτιμία ἐ Solonis instituto, cuius haec est Lex:
units.tr: There was also atimia [ἀτιμία] (loss of civic rights) under Solon's institution, whose law is this:

units.la: Τὸν αὐτὸν μὴ προεδρεῖν πολλάκις· ἐὰν δὲ ὁ καθῆκεν μὴ βάλλειν, κολαζέσθαι. Eidem epulum in Prytaneio sapius ne praebeto r: qui hunc honorem praeterhabuerit, multator.
units.tr: "The same man should not hold proedria often; and if the one appointed does not ..., he is to be punished." [Τὸν αὐτὸν μὴ προεδρεῖν πολλάκις· ἐὰν δὲ ὁ καθῆκεν μὴ βάλλειν, κολαζέσθαι.] Likewise, the same man should not be given the public meal in the Prytaneum too often; whoever has refused this honour is to be fined.

units.la: Legis huius ἐκ προεδρίας meminit Plutarchus in Solone: ἴσλον δὲ τῆς Σόλωνος καὶ ὁ ἐκ τῆς ἐν δημοσίῳ ἀτιμίας, ὅταν αὐτὸς προεδρίαν καθήκει. τὸν γὰρ αὐτὸν ἐκ ἐξ σιτεῖσθαι πολλάκις· ἐὰν δὲ ὁ καθῆκεν μὴ βάλλειν, κολαζέσθαι. Ratio est, ὃ μὲν, ἡγεμόνας πλεονεξίας ὃ ὁ, ἀσφαλίας τῆς κοινῆς, Domus, in qua epulabantur, dicebatur πρυτανεῖον. Suidas & Interpres Comici non semel: Πρυτανεῖον, καὶ ἐκ τῆς Αθηναίοις οἰκίαν δημοσίαν, ἔπειτα ἑστιῶντο δημοσίᾳ τῆς Σιαύτης τιμῆς παρ᾽ αὐτοῖς τυγχάνοντες, ἐξ εἰσιὼν δὲ ἐν τῇ τοιαύτης δωρεᾶς τυχεῖν· ὅτι γὰρ μεγάλοις καὶ ρηθέντοις ἐπί τῶν. ταυτῷ ἀπεδίδοτο χάριν[?]. Auctor Etymologici: Γρυτάμειον, τόπος τῶν ἀπ' Ἀθηναίοις, ἐν ᾧ κοιναὶ σιτήσεις τῆς δημοσίας ἐπιδίδοντο. Pollux Libro IX. cap. V: Ὅτι δὲ ταύτην, Γρυτάμεων ἡ ἑστία τῆς πόλεως, ἐπὶ ἡ ἑστιῶσθαι, εἰ τε ἐκ δημοσίας ἀπεσθαι ἥκοντες, εἰ οἱ ἀλλ' ἀπέξιοι ἵνα αἰτήσεως ἀξιωθέντες, ἢ εἰ ἐς ἐκ ὑμῆς ἀείσπως ὦ. Quid vero apponendum fuerit, Lege sanxit Solon:
units.tr: Plutarch in his Solon mentions this law concerning proedria: [ἴσλον δὲ τῆς Σόλωνος καὶ ὁ ἐκ τῆς ἐν δημοσίῳ ἀτιμίας, ὅταν αὐτὸς προεδρίαν καθήκει. τὸν γὰρ αὐτὸν ἐκ ἐξ σιτεῖσθαι πολλάκις· ἐὰν δὲ ὁ καθῆκεν μὴ βάλλειν, κολαζέσθαι.] The reason is that the one thing guards against greed and the other protects the common safety. The house in which they dined was called the prytaneion [πρυτανεῖον]. Suidas and the commentator on the comic poet say more than once: [Πρυτανεῖον, καὶ ἐκ τῆς Αθηναίοις οἰκίαν δημοσίαν, ἔπειτα ἑστιῶντο δημοσίᾳ] (the Prytaneum is the public house at Athens, where they were feasted at public expense, those who obtained this honour and this gift). The author of the Etymologicum says: [Γρυτάμειον, τόπος τῶν ἀπ' Ἀθηναίοις, ἐν ᾧ κοιναὶ σιτήσεις τῆς δημοσίας ἐπιδίδοντο] (the Prytaneum, a place at Athens where common meals were given at public expense). Pollux, Book IX, chapter 5, says that the hearth of the city was the place where those who had been honoured with the public meal, or who had come to ask for it, were fed.

units.la: Conniuantibus in Prytaneio maza, diebus vero festis, panis apponitor. Τοῖς προσσιτουμένοις μάζαν πρυτανείῳ, ἄρτον δ' [?] τῆς ἑορτῆς [illegible, ~8 letters]
units.tr: Solon by law determined what was to be set before them: [Τοῖς προσσιτουμένοις μάζαν πρυτανείῳ, ἄρτον δὲ τῆς ἑορτῆς] (for those dining in the Prytaneum, a barley cake; on festival days, bread).

units.la: Quæ in re Homerum inuitari voluit Solon. Athenæus Libro IV. Σόλων δὲ τοῖς ἐν Πρυτανείῳ συνουσίοις, μάζαν πρέχειν κελεύει· ἄρτον δὲ τῆς ἑορτῆς πανηγυρίζουσι, μιμούμενος τὸν Ὅμηρον, καὶ γὰρ ἐκεῖνος τοὺς ἀριστεῖς σιτήσαι πρὸς τὸν Ἀγαμέμνονα, φύρετο δ' ἀλφίτα φησίν. Ac obtinuit aliquamdiu Lex Solonis, nec passim hic τῆς αἰτήσεως honos est habitus; Aristophanes Equitibus de Strategis, qui ætatem Cleonis præcesserunt:
units.tr: In this matter Solon wished to imitate Homer. Athenaeus, Book IV: "Solon orders that those who dine in the Prytaneum be given a barley cake, and that bread be served at the festival celebrations, imitating Homer; for Homer too has the prize-winners fed by Agamemnon, and says that he mixed barley meal." The law of Solon held for some time, and this honour was not everywhere given to the same people. Aristophanes in the Knights speaks of generals who preceded the time of Cleon:

units.la: καὶ Στρατηγὸς ἀλλ' ἀλλ' εἰς τῷ πόρῳ, αἴτησιν ἡτήσ' ἐρώμενος Κλεαίνετον. νῦν δ' ἐὰν μὴ πρεσβείαν φέρωσι, τῆς δὲ αἰτία, ἡ μαχεῖσθαι φασιν.
units.tr: [καὶ Στρατηγὸς ἀλλ' ἀλλ' εἰς τῷ πόρῳ, αἴτησιν ἡτήσ' ἐρώμενος Κλεαίνετον. νῦν δ' ἐὰν μὴ πρεσβείαν φέρωσι, τῆς δὲ αἰτία, ἡ μαχεῖσθαι φασιν.] (And the general ... having asked for a grant, ... of Cleainetos. But now, if they do not bring an embassy, they say they will fight over the cause.)

units.la: Quid hic sit, ἐρώμενος[?] Κλεαίνετον, dicere non est adeo procliue, neque enim Græcus Interpres quicquam nos hic iuuat, cuius hæc est nota: ἔστ' ὁ Κλεαίνετος Φαίνεται κατεδιδάσκως τῷ ὁσίας καὶ ἡδυπαθήσας. οἱ δ', ὅτι ἔστ' ἐγκαλοῦ ψήφισμα μὴ δῶν δεδωκέναι τοῖς Στρατηγοῖς αἴτησιν. ἀσφαλῶς δὲ μιμνήσκει τῆς Κλεαίνετου καὶ χεδὴν εὐθὺ μόνον. τραλέζουσι οὖν ἡμεῖς ἑτὶ ἔστ' αὐ εἴη ὁ τῷ αἴτησιν ἀξιοποίησας τοῦ Κλέων. Nam si hic Cleanetus bona sua decoxit, quid opus est illo in petenda aut impetranda à populo αἴτησιν? Si populi scitum fecerat de non donandis Strategis αἴτησιν, multo minus commoda est hoc loco illius mentio: Quod si dicas hunc esse, qui Cleoni αἴτησιν impetrauit, non video, quid ἐρώμενος hic significet. Vt dicam igitur quod sentio, inque tenebris micem, puto leuiter corruptum esse hunc locum, & duas voces in vnam coaluisse, vnde natum hoc nomen, quod proprium esse putarunt Δημαγωγὸς alicuius ex illo ævo, frustra, meo quidem iudicio: nam siue fecisset populi scitum μὴ δῶν δεδωκέναι τοῖς Στρατηγοῖς αἴτησιν, siue eam Cleoni à populo impetrasset, frequentius illius meminisset Aristophanes: nullus igitur dubito rescribendum esse,
units.tr: It is not very easy to say what this means, "asking ... Cleainetos", for the Greek commentator helps us not at all here; his note runs: "Cleainetos is shown to have squandered his substance in luxury and self-indulgence; others say that there was a decree against granting the generals any aitesis." He is also mentioned again only once. If, then, this Cleainetos squandered his goods, what need was there for him to ask for or obtain an aitesis from the people? If the people had passed a decree that no aitesis be granted to generals, his mention here would be even less appropriate. But if you say he is the one who obtained an aitesis for Cleon, I do not see what eromenos means here. To say what I think, groping in the dark, I suspect this passage is slightly corrupted, and two words have run together into one, from which this name arose, which they thought was the proper name of some demagogue of that age. This is in vain, in my judgement; for whether he had carried a decree that no grant be made to the generals, or had obtained an aitesis for Cleon from the people, Aristophanes would have mentioned it more often. I therefore have no doubt that the passage should be rewritten as follows:

units.la: καὶ Στρατηγὸς ἀλλ' ἀλλ' εἰς τῷ πόρῳ, αἴτησιν ἡτήσ' ἐρώμενος, κλεῖ' αἰνετόν.
units.tr: [καὶ Στρατηγὸς ἀλλ' ἀλλ' εἰς τῷ πόρῳ, αἴτησιν ἡτήσ' ἐρώμενος, κλεῖ' αἰνετόν.] (And the general ... having asked for a grant, ... "worthy of praise".)

units.la: Strategorum priorum nullus petiit à populo αἴτησιν, dicens, prædica laude dignum, κλὲς αἰνετὸν, ex κλείομαι fit κλέομαι, ita à κλείω fit κλέω. Nemo quippe αἴτησις donabatur à populo, qui eadem non prædicaretur omni dignus laude. In populi scito, quod fecit Stratocles Euthydemi F. Anaxicrate Athenis Prætore, anno secundo Olympiadis centesimæ decimæ octauæ, de Lycurgo Oratore donando αἴτησις hæc verba leguntur: ΑΓΑΘΗ, ΤΥΧΗ, ΔΕ-ΔΟΧΘΑΙ ΤΩΙ ΔΗΜΩΙ, ΕΠΑΙΝΕΣΑΙ ΜΕΝ ΛΥ-ΚΟΥΡΓΟΝ ΛΥ-ΚΟΦΡΟΝΟΣ ΒΟΥΤΑΔΗΝ ΑΡΕΤΗΣ ΕΝΕΚΑ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΚΑΙΟΣΥ-ΝΗΣ, ΚΑΙ ΣΤΗΣΑΙ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΤΟΝ ΔΗΜΟΝ ΧΑΛΚΗΝ ΕΙΚΟ-ΝΑ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑΙ. ΓΑΗΝ ΕΙ ΠΟΥ Ο ΝΟΜΟΣ ΑΓΑΓΟΡΕΥΕΙ ΜΗ ΙΣΤΑΝΑΙ, ΔΟΥΝΑΙ ΔΕ ΣΙΤΗΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΩΙ ΤΩΝ ΕΓΓΟΝΩΝ ΑΕΙ ΤΩΝ ΛΥΚΟΥΡΓΟΥ ΤΩι ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΑΤΩι ΕΙΣ ΑΓΑΝΤΑ ΤΟΝ ΧΡΟΝΟΝ. Atque ex his praeterea docemur, Solonis Legem, Ne quis saepe in Prytaneio exciperetur, mutasse: nam multi ἀξίωσι ἐκ ὑμῶν fuerunt, ut loquitur Pollux, honosque is heredes sequebatur: ita ut interdum, quo possent defunctorum liberi eo uti, mortuis peteretur, & impetraretur, quod Demostheni accidit, cui hic honos impetratus est anno primo Olympiadis centesimae vicesimae quintae, Gorgia Athenis Praetore: Plutarchus in eius Vita Libro de X. Rhet. χρόνῳ δὲ ὕστερον Ἀθηναῖοι αἰτησάντι τε ἐκ Πρυτανείου τῆς συγκλήτου τῆς Δημοσθένους ἐδόσθη, καὶ αὐτὸς πεπλεκτικὸς τῷ εἰκόνα ἀνέθηκεν ἐν ἀγορᾷ, ὅτι Γοργίου Ἀρ-γείας. Extat in hanc rem Psephisma scriptum à Demochare Lachetis F. apud eundem Plutarchum: ΔΗΜΟΧΑΡΗΣ ΛΑΧΗΤΟΣ ΛΕΥΚΟ-ΝΟΕΥΣ ΑΙΤΕΙ ΔΗΜΟΣΘΕΝΕΙ ΤΩι ΔΗΜΟΣΘΕΝΟΥΣ ΠΑΙΑ-ΝΙΕΙ ΔΩΡΕΑΝ ΧΑΛΚΗΝ ΕΙΚΟΝΑ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑι, ΚΑΙ ΣΙΤΗ-ΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΩι, ΚΑΙ ΠΡΟΕΔΡΙΑΝ ΑΥΤΩι, ΚΑΙ ΕΚ-ΓΟΝΩΝ ΑΕΙ ΤΩι ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΑΤΩι ΕΥΕΡΓΕΤΗι, ΚΑΙ ΣΥΜ-ΒΟΥΛΩι ΓΕΓΟΝΟΤΙ ΠΟΛΛΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΚΑΛΩΝ ΤΩι ΔΗΜΩι ΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΗΝ ΤΕ ΟΥΣΙΑΝ ΕΙΣ ΤΟ ΚΟΙ-ΝΟΝ ΚΑΘΕΙΚΟΤΙ ΤΗΝ ΕΑΥΤΟΥ. Beneficia deinde Demosthenis in populum singillatim recensèt Demochares, quemadmodum & Democharis ipsius filius eius Laches, in Psephismate, quod in hanc rem scripsit, Archonte Pytharato, anno secundo Olympiadis centesimae vicesimae septimae: extat hoc Psephisma apud Plutarchum extremo Libro de X. Rhet. in haec verba: ΑΡΧΩΝ ΓΥΘΑΡΑΤΟΣ ΛΑ-ΧΗΣ ΔΗΜΟΧΑΡΟΥΣ ΛΕΥΚΟΝΟΕΥΣ ΑΙΤΕΙ ΔΩΡΕΑΝ ΤΗΝ ΒΟΥΛΗΝ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟΝ ΔΗΜΟΝ ΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ ΔΗΜΟΧΑΡΕΙ ΛΑΧΗΤΟΣ ΛΕΥΚΟΝΟΕΙ ΕΙΚΟΝΑ ΧΑΛ-ΚΗΝ ΕΝ ΑΓΟΡΑι, ΚΑΙ ΣΙΤΗΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΠΡΥΤΑΝΕΙΩι, ΚΑΙ ΤΩΝ ΕΓΓΟΝΩΝ ΑΕΙ ΤΩι ΠΡΕΣΒΥΤΑΤΩι, ΚΑΙ ΠΡΟΕΔΡΙΑΝ ΕΝ ΠΑΣΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΑΓΩΣΙΝ ΕΥΕΡΓΕΤΗι, ΚΑΙ ΣΥΜΒΟΥΛΩι ΓΕΓΟΝΟΤΙ ΑΓΑΘΩι ΤΩι ΔΗ-ΜΩι ΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΥΕΡΓΕΤΗΚΟΤΙ ΤΟΝ ΔΗΜΟΝ ΤΑΔΕ. Quinctiam feminis id concessum, ut de Polycrite Aristidis 'nepte Callisthenes refert apud Plutarchum in Aristide: ἐπὶ δὲ Αἰσιμάχου γυναικὶ Πολυχρίτῳ ἁπλῶς πάντως, ὡς Καλλισθένης φησί, καὶ ταύτῃ αἰτήσαι ὅσῳ καὶ τοῖς Ὀλυμπιονίκαις ὁ δῆμος ἐψηφίσατο. Demetrio quoque Phalereo populi scitum faciente dedit populus Aristidis neptibus triobolum in dies singulos: ὁ δὲ Φαληρεύς ἐν τοῖς Σωκράτει φησὶ μνημονεύειν Αἰσχίδου γυναικῶν δ' μάλιστα πάντα Λεσβίαν· τῇ δὲ μητρὶ καὶ τῇ ταύτης ἀδελφῇ ψήφισμα χαλκᾶς δωρεὰν ἐπιστῶν τὸν δῆμον ἰδίναι, τεσσαρῶν ἑκάστης ἡμέρας· αὐτὸς μάντι φησὶν ὁ Δημήτριος νομοθετῶν ἐψηφίσατο δραχμῶν ἑκατέρᾳ πέντε τὴν γυναῖκα. Hanc [?] sibi esse praebendam iocose respondit Socrates iam primis iudicum sententiis damnatus: Cùm interrogatus Socrates esset, inquit M. Tullius Libro I. de Oratore, respondit sese meruisse, ut amplissimis honoribus, & praemijs decoraretur, & ut ei victus quotidianus in Prytaneo publice praeberetur, qui honos apud Graecos maximus haberetur.
units.tr: None of the earlier generals asked the people for an aitesis, calling him "worthy of praise", [κλὲς αἰνετόν]; from κλείομαι comes κλέομαι, just as from κλείω comes κλέω. Indeed no one was granted an aitesis by the people who was not declared worthy of all praise.
