units.tr: Aelian praises this law in his Varia Historia Book V, chapter 14: "There is an Attic law that the plough-ox, or the one that works under the yoke to till the land or to plough, or that draws the wagon, must not be sacrificed." Although they forbade not only the ox that was already a companion of men in rustic labour and a minister of Ceres, but in former times they wanted no ox at all to be slaughtered, and secured this by law.

units.la: Βοῦς μὴ καταθύειν.
units.tr: Not to sacrifice oxen [Βοῦς μὴ καταθύειν].

units.la: Boues ne mactanto.
units.tr: Do not slaughter oxen.

units.la: Philochorus apud Athenæum Libro IX. Legis meminit, eaque cur sit lata, indicat: καὶ τί χρέιον δὲ ἴνα ἐκ λιπόντων τὴν βοῦν, φησὶν ὁ Φιλόχορος, νομοθετῆσαι ἀφ᾽ τοῦ αὐτῶν ἀπέχεσθαι αὐτοῖς τῶν ζώων σωτηρίαν βουλομένους ἢ πλησθῆναι τῶν μὴ καταθύεσθαι. Varro de R.R. Libro II.cap. V. vbi de Bone agit: Hic socius hominum in rustico opere, & Cereris minister. Ab hoc antiqui manus ita abstineri voluerunt, vt capite sanxerint, si quis occidisset. Qua in re testis Attice, testis Peloponnesos. Sed forte ad bouem aratorem referenda sunt M. Varronis verba. Ad hanc Legem alludit Plato Libro VI. de Legibus: ὅτι οὐδὲ βοῦς ἐπαλμῶν ἀμφὶ [?] ζώων, ἱστορίας, παλαιοῖς, ἐν τῆς ἀγαθὸν τῆς μάλιστα ζωα. Atque eadem hac de causa Lege vetabatur agni tenelli, & anniculo minoris, cui nec vulsa nec tonsa læua est, eius:
units.tr: Philochorus, quoted by Athenaeus in Book IX, mentions the law and indicates why it was passed: "And why was it necessary, says Philochorus, to legislate that the ox be spared, unless, wishing to preserve the animals for themselves, they abstained from them, or on account of the ploughing?" Varro, On Agriculture Book II, chapter 5, where he treats of the ox: "This is the companion of men in rustic labour and a minister of Ceres. The ancients wanted hands to be kept from it in such a way that they made it a capital offence if anyone killed it. Attica is witness to this, and the Peloponnese is witness." But perhaps Varro's words should be referred to the plough-ox. Plato alludes to this law in Book VI of the Laws: that the ox is among the animals most useful and best for men.

units.la: Μὴ σφάττην ἀρνίδα ἀπέκτεινε ἀπέκτειν.
units.tr: Not to slaughter the young lamb [Μὴ σφάττειν ἀρνίδα].

units.la: Agnum anniculo minorem ne mactato.
units.tr: Do not slaughter a lamb younger than one year.

units.la: Laudat hanc Legem idem Philochorus apud Athenæum Libro I. Φιλόχορος ἱστορεῖ, ἢ κεκωλύεται Ἀθηναίων ἀπέκτειν ἔτους μηδὲν μαλακὰ, ὑπαλφιούσης ποτὲ τῆς τῶν ζώων τύπων ἡμεῖς.
units.tr: The same Philochorus, quoted by Athenaeus in Book I, praises this law: "Philochorus relates that it was forbidden for the Athenians to kill any lamb less than a year old, since the nature of the animals was then still tender."

units.la: Androtion apud eundem Athenæum Libro IX. ὧν δὲ καὶ παλαιὸς νόμος, ὡς φησὶν Ἀνδροτίων τῆς ὑπηρέτης ἕνεκα τῶν Ἁρεμίδῳ μὴ σφάττην ἀρνίδα ἀπέκτειν ἐὰν ἀπ-ἀκτεν. Eustathius ad Iliad. Ω. ἐπὶ τι δὲ Ἀθηναῖον, γενόμενοι ἥγω ὁμολογῶ ἀπέκτευ ἀρνὲς μηδὲ γ᾽ ἐλέας ὑπαλφιούσης ποτὲ φασὶ τῆς τῶν ζώων τύπων ἡμεῖς.
units.tr: Androtion, in the same Athenaeus, Book IX: "There is also an ancient law, as Androtion says, on account of the service of Hermes, that one must not slaughter a lamb." Eustathius on the Iliad Omega: "In Athens, as I say, a law was in force that a lamb was not to be killed, not even one that was still young, since the nature of the animals was then tender."

units.la: Atque longe ante Triptolemus Lege interdixerat omnium animalium esu: Ζῷα μὴ σίνεσθαι. [?] Carnibus ne vescitor.
units.tr: And long before, Triptolemus had prohibited by law the eating of all animals: "Not to harm living creatures [Ζῷα μὴ σίνεσθαι]." Let no one eat flesh.

units.la: Meminit Hermippus Libro II. de Legislatoribus è Xenocrate apud Porphyrium περὶ ἀποχῆς. Τῶν γὰρ Ἀθηναίων νομοθετῶν Τριπτόλεμον πάλαι φασὶ προσηγορευκέναι, ὡς ἐν ταῖς ἐλήφθη, ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν Ἐρμιῶν [?] ἐν ἀλλήλαις [?] νομοθετῶν γεγράφειν τοῦτο. Φασὶ γὰρ Τριπτόλεμον Ἀθηναίοις νομοθετῆσαι, ἐν τῷ νόμῳ αὐτῶν τεῖς ἐπὶ Ξενοκράτης ὁ φιλόσοφος λέγει Ἐλθόντα, ὡς ἡμῖν, θεοὺς καρπῶς ἀγαλλεῖν, ζῷα μὴ σίνεσθαι. A Porphyrio accepit noster Hieronymus Libro adversus Jovinianum II. Xenocrates Philosophus de Triptolemi Legibus apud Athenienses tria tantum praecepta in Templo Eleusina residere scribit: Honorandos parentes: Venerandos Deos: CARNIBUS NON VESCENDUM.
units.tr: Hermippus, Book II On Lawgivers, quoting Xenocrates in Porphyry's On Abstinence, mentions this: "For they say that Triptolemus was long ago named as a lawgiver of the Athenians, as is recorded in the ancient writings; but in the later lawgivers this was written differently. For they say that Triptolemus legislated for the Athenians, and in his law, as the philosopher Xenocrates says, it is written that men should honour the gods with fruits, and not harm living creatures." Our Jerome took this from Porphyry in Book II against Jovinianus: "Xenocrates the philosopher writes, in his work on the laws of Triptolemus among the Athenians, that only three precepts remained in the temple at Eleusis: Parents are to be honoured; the gods are to be venerated; FLESH IS NOT TO BE EATEN."

units.la: TITULUS III. DE EMPTIONE, VENDITIONE, & evictione.
units.tr: TITLE III. CONCERNING BUYING, SELLING, AND EVICTION.

units.la: IN emptione, venditione satis commodè ab Atheniensibus cautum est, ut obviam irent molestiis controversiarum, haec observari: Venditionis atque emptionis Leges palam apud Magistratum proscribi diebus ante sexaginta: Centesimam pretij partem deponi, ut si quis velit controversiam movere, ei per Leges, & sub hac quasi sacramenti Lege liceat. Theophrastus apud Stobæum Sermone XLII. Ἐνίοι δὲ προεγγράφειν τὸ πωλῶν τῇ ὀχῇ παρὰ ἡμερῶν μὴ ἐλαττόνων, ἵ' ἐξῆναι, καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ Ἀθηναῖοι, καὶ τὸν ἀριθμὸν ἐκάστοτε ἀθέται τῆς ἡμῶν, ὅπως ἀμφισβητήσωσι τι ἐξῆ, καὶ ἀμφισβητησαι παρὰ βουλευτῶν, καὶ ὁ δικαίως ἐωνημένος, φανερὸς ἦ τὰ πόλει. His praestitis, si postea de re empta & transacta controversia moveretur, Legibus erat sancitum, ut si de agro aut domo lis esset, primo disceptaretur de agri proventu & reditu, aut aedium obvencione, cuiusnam haec futura essent. Τὸν ἀμφισβητοῦντα χωρεῖν, δικάζεσθαι τὰς [?] ἐγγαῖα αὐτῶν, καρπὸς ἐπὶ δὲ οἰκίας, οἰκοῖς. | Qui de agro litigat, possessori de proventu, qui de domo, dicam de obvencione scribito.
units.tr: In buying and selling, the Athenians took fairly sensible precautions against the troubles of disputes, observing these rules: the laws of sale and purchase were posted publicly before the magistrate sixty days in advance, and a hundredth part of the price was deposited, so that if anyone wished to bring a dispute, he might do so under the laws and under this kind of oath-law. Theophrastus in Stobaeus, Sermon 42: Some required that the sale be announced in advance for not fewer than days, and the Athenians did so elsewhere too, and each time the number of the days was set, so that anyone who wished might dispute the matter, and the one who bought lawfully might be known to the city. [Ἐνίοι δὲ προεγγράφειν τὸ πωλῶν τῇ ὀχῇ παρὰ ἡμερῶν μὴ ἐλαττόνων, ἵ' ἐξῆναι, καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ Ἀθηναῖοι, καὶ τὸν ἀριθμὸν ἐκάστοτε ἀθέται τῆς ἡμῶν, ὅπως ἀμφισβητήσωσι τι ἐξῆ, καὶ ἀμφισβητησαι παρὰ βουλευτῶν, καὶ ὁ δικαίως ἐωνημένος, φανερὸς ἦ τὰ πόλει.] When these measures had been taken, if a dispute arose afterwards over a thing bought and transacted, the laws had enacted that, if the suit concerned a field or a house, it should first be decided whose the produce and yield of the field, or the income of the house, were to be. [Τὸν ἀμφισβητοῦντα χωρεῖν, δικάζεσθαι τὰς [?] ἐγγαῖα αὐτῶν, καρπὸς ἐπὶ δὲ οἰκίας, οἰκοῖς.] Whoever disputes about a field: let the possessor be sued for the produce; whoever disputes about a house: let the claim concern the income.

units.la: Legis meminit Lysias, si titulus non mentitur auctorem, ὁ παῖς τῆς Δημοσθένους [?] ἐπὶ ξυσπᾶς [?], ἐὰν γὰρ ἐπιτιμήσης [?] ἐὰν τῆς ἄλλης [?] μισθωχῇ, καὶ τῷ σῶν τι ἔχῃ, δίκασαι αὐτῷ χῷ ἐπὶ τῶν νόμων, εἰ μὴ χωρεῖν ἀμφισβητῆσαι, καρπού, ἐπὶ δὲ οἰκίας, οἰκοῖς. Suidas: οἱ ἀμφισβητοῦντες ὡς ἐπὶ γεωργοῦσι αὐτῶν, λαμβάνουσι τοῖς Δημοσθένους. εἶτα ἐλθόντες λαμβάνουσι πεπ' ἐξ ἐπιμελείας. Sequebatur postea actio possessoria de agri aut domus possessione. Denique dabatur actio Unde vi. Qui ceciderat actione καρπού, aut possessoria, poterat nihilominus in possessione agri, aut domus esse; at post peractum judicium Unde vi, possidere jubetur is, cui lis est addicta. Harpocration : ὑπὲρ ὧν δίκην, οἱ δικαζόμενοι περὶ χωρίων, ὅτι οἰκιῶν, ὅτε ὅτι τὸν ἐχθρὸν ὑπὲρ οἰκίας, εἰ δικαζόμενοι τὴν ὑπὲρ ἐνοικιάσεως δίκην [?] ἐνοικίσεως ... ἢ δὲ ἀποτίμησις [?] ... ἐχθρὸν ... καρπὸς [?] ... ὅπως τὸ ... [illegible, ~40 letters] ... ἀγῶνα ... [illegible, ~60 letters] ... οἰκίας ... [illegible, ~50 letters] ... ἀλλ' ἐξίσα [?] ... τῆς χαρακτήρος [?].
units.tr: Lysias mentions the law, if the title does not misstate its author: "...if you bring an accusation ... and he holds something ... let him be judged under the laws, if he does not withdraw from the dispute, for the produce; for the house, for the rent." Suidas: those who dispute over the land, as in the case of their produce, take up the matter of Demosthenes; then, having come, they take it up with care. There followed afterwards the possessory action concerning the possession of a field or house. Finally the action Unde vi was granted. He who had lost by the action for the produce, or by the possessory action, could nonetheless be in possession of the field or house; but after the trial Unde vi had been completed, he is ordered to possess whom the suit has been awarded to. Harpocration: concerning which cases the litigants about fields or houses... the enemy over the house... the rent... [Several words here are illegible in the scan.]

units.la: Mota emptori quaestione, vel ipse per se litigabat emptor, vel eum qui controuersiam faciebat, ad venditorem ducebat, venditorem indicabat, & ad illum ibat, eiusque nomine litigabat. facile colligere est, ex his Harpocrationis, quae Suidas illustrat: ἀλλομαχεῖν, ὃ δὲ ἑαυτῷ δικάζεσθαι, ἀλλὰ μὴ δι' ἑτέρου· εἰ δὲ τις εἰς ἀποσπᾶσθαι [?] ἀντιμάχης ἀγωνίζεσθαι, ὡς τὸν Ἀρχίδαμον [?] τὸν δίκην ἐδίδου. ἐὰν τις ποιῇ τὸν Ἀρχιμάρτυρα [?] εἰσαγώγιμον εἶναι τὴν δίκην, αὐτὸς μὲν γὰρ αὐτὸν οὐκ ἀγωνίζεσθαι, ὡς δὲ τὸν Ἀρχιμάρτυρα [?] ὁ ἀγών δέξι. Λεύκιας δὲ τοῦ Εὐθυκλέους χωρίου ἐξώλης. Docet his verbis Harpocration quid sit ἀλλομαχεῖν, nempe ὃ δὲ ἑαυτῷ δικάζεσθαι, non autem per alium, ἀλλὰ μὴ δι' ἑτέρου. quomodo autem per alium litigetur, duobus exemplis probat: vnum est, si quis proferat in iudicio testem, qui testatur μὴ εἰσαγώγιμον εἶναι τὴν δίκην. nam aduersus testem tota lis mouebatur. Alterum exemplum est, si quis auctorem suum laudet, eumque conueniat, ἐὰν δὲ εἰς ἀποσπᾶσθαι ἀγῶνα, ὡς ἐκεῖνον ἀποφαίνεται τὴν δίκην ὅσον. Non enim laudabatur auctor, aut conueniebatur, ab eo qui vellet ἀλλομαχεῖν, quamquam certe is non ignorabat auctorem suum esse idoneum ad pretium soluendum. Suidas: καὶ ἀλλομαχῆσαι, ὅταν ἀπαιτοῦσι τὰς οἰκίας [?] ... χωρίον, καὶ εἰν ὁ προσαχὼς μὲν ἀξιόχρεως, ὥστε δίκην ἀποτίσαι τὴν ζημίαν, καὶ συνίσταθαι τὴν δίκην πρὸς τὸν ἀμφισβητοῦντα, βιβλίῳ δὲ ὁ Ἁρπα-κρατίων τὴν οἰκίαν [?] τὸ χωρίον, ἰδίου αὐτοῦ ἡνέσθαι ἀγῶνα πρὸς τὸν ἀμφισβητοῦντα. τὴν ἀλλομαχῆσαι καλεῖσθαι. Si emptore litigante res euinceretur, habebat regressum emptor, vt cum Vlpiano dicam, in venditorem Lege I. D. de euictionibus: collige ex his Suidae iam laudatis verbis, καὶ εἰν ὁ προσαχὼς μὲν ἀξιόχρεως, ὥστε δίκην ἀποτίσαι τὴν ζημίαν, ἡ συνίσταθαι τὴν δίκην πρὸς τὸν ἀμφισβητοῦντα. At vero si nollet emptor ἀλλομαχῆσαι, ad auctorem ibat: nam mota quaestione, inquit Hermogenianus Libro II. iuris Epitomarum, interim non ad pretium restituendum, sed ad rem defendendam venditor conuenirti potest. Lege LXXIV. §. II. D.eod. Graeci αἰάγχν dicunt. Harpocration cum Suida: αἰάγχν, ὃ μιμοῦμαι τὸν προσαχότα ἐπ' ἐκεῖνον ἰέναι. & verbis, quae iam ante descripsimus: ἐὰν δὲ εἰς ἀποσπᾶσθαι ἀγῶνα, ὡς ἐκεῖνον ἀποφαίνεται τὴν δίκην ὅσον. Conuentus ab eo emptore venditor, debebat emptori cauere de euictione, si cauere recusaret, aduersus eum agebat emptor βεβαιώσεως actione. Pollux Libro VIII. cap. VI. ἡ δὲ βεβαιώσεως δίκη, ὁπότε ὡς ἀρχαῖοι τὰ οἰκία, ὅτι χωρίον, ἀμφισβητοῦν τῆς γῆς, αἰάγχ ὅτι τὸν προσαχότα· τὸν δὲ προσαχότα βεβαιῶν, ἡ μὴ βεβαιοῦντα ἀναδίδωσι τὴν βεβαιώσεως. Harpocration : βεβαιώσεως, δίκης ὄνομά ἐστιν, ᾧ δικάζονται οἱ ἀποκαλοῦντες ἢ τὰ πωλοῦντα ἀλλ' ἐτέρας μὲν ἀμφισβητῆ, τῷ προσθέντος δὲ μὴ βεβαιοῖ. Si vero caueret venditor, eius nomine agebat emptor, quod si causa caderet, rem controuersam à se emptam amittebat, sed licebat ei multam aut condemnationem petere ab auctore & venditore qui cauerat, tanquam à venditore fallace. Pollux loco laudato: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ αἰάγων ὅτι τὸν προσαχότα ἡπιθεῖν, ὃ μὲν ἀμφισβητηθὲν τῷ χαρτισθύλας κρατήρας. ἐχίγνετο. ὁ δὲ ἡπηθεὶς τῷ ἡμίλῳ [?] τῆς συκοφαντήσεως ἐχομί-ξετο.
units.tr: Once a question had been raised by the buyer, either the buyer himself litigated in person, or he led the one who was making the objection to the seller, pointed out the seller, and went to him and litigated in his name. This is easily gathered from these words of Harpocration, which Suidas illustrates: to litigate through another [ἀλλομαχεῖν] is to litigate for oneself, not through another [ἀλλὰ μὴ δι' ἑτέρου]. If someone brings in a rival to contend, as Archidamus did when he gave the suit ... if anyone makes the witness Archimartyras liable to be summoned to the trial, he himself does not contend, but the contest falls on the witness Archimartyras. Harpocration, in these words, explains what allomachein is, namely to litigate for oneself, and not through another. He shows by two examples how one litigates through another. One is when someone produces a witness in court, who testifies that the suit is not liable to be brought; for the whole case was moved against the witness. The other example is when someone praises his author and summons him; this is the contest by which he shows that the suit is ... For the author was not praised, nor summoned, by one who wished to allomachein, although certainly he knew that his author was able to pay the price. Suidas: and to allomachein, when they demand the house or field, and the one who is responsible is sufficiently solvent to pay the penalty of the suit, and the suit is brought against the claimant; Harpocration calls this allomachein, when a man conducts his own contest against the claimant. If the buyer, litigating, lost the thing, he had a right of recourse against the seller, as I say with Ulpian, in Law 1 D. de evictionibus; gather this from the words of Suidas already quoted: "and when the one who is responsible is sufficiently solvent to pay the penalty, or the suit is brought against the claimant." But if the buyer did not wish to allomachein, he went to the author; for once the question had been raised, says Hermogenianus in Book II of the Epitomes of Law, the seller may be summoned not to restore the price meanwhile, but to defend the thing. Law 74, §2, D. eod. The Greeks call this aiachein [αἰάγχν]. Harpocration with Suidas: aiachein is to imitate the one who goes against the author; and in the words we described earlier: "if he is to contend for the suit, as he shows that the suit is his own." When the seller was summoned by the buyer, he had to give security to the buyer concerning eviction; if he refused to give security, the buyer proceeded against him by the action of guarantee [βεβαιώσεως]. Pollux, Book VIII, chap. VI: the action of guarantee, when, as the ancients said, the houses or fields were claimed by another, was aiachein against the author; and the author, if he guaranteed, or did not guarantee, rendered the guarantee. Harpocration: guarantee is the name of a suit by which those who are summoned, or sell things, are sued when another disputes the thing and the seller does not guarantee it. If, however, the seller gave security, the buyer acted in his name; and if the cause went against him, he lost the thing he had bought and disputed, but he was permitted to seek a fine or condemnation from the author and seller who had given security, as from a deceitful seller. Pollux, in the passage cited: if the one who was summoned to the author did not obey, the disputed thing was given to the claimant... and the one who was not obeyed was liable to the charge of calumny.

units.la: Volebant namque Athenienses sine dolo malo agi inter se, itaque Legem tulerunt, quae vetabat in foro mentiri, idque [?] ἀληθῶν maxime. Ἀψευδεῖν τῇ ἀγορᾷ.
units.tr: For the Athenians wished that dealings between them be conducted without malice, and so they passed a law which forbade lying in the marketplace, and especially about true things. Not to lie in the marketplace. [Ἀψευδεῖν τῇ ἀγορᾷ.]

units.la: Laudat hanc Legem Hyperides ἐν τῷ κατ' Ἀλκιβιάδου α' apud Harpocrationem: ἀψευδεῖν τῷ ἀγορᾷ ἀψευδεῖν. Υπαρίδης ἐν τῷ κατ' Ἀλκιβιάδου α'. ὁ μὲν Ξίνων νόμος καλεῖ ἀψευδεῖν ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ· ἔοικεν ὁ νόμος αὐτὸ τὸ ὠνίων κεῖσθαι. Demosthenes in Leptinea: πᾶς γὰρ εἰκ ἀγορᾷ, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, καὶ μὴ τῷ ἀγορᾷ ἀψευδεῖν νόμων γεγράφθαι, ἐφ' οἷς οὐδὲν δεῖ δημοσίᾳ βλάβος, εἰ τις φύσεται. Vlpianus: πολιτικῶν γὰρ ἀψευδεῖν μάχεται τῶν ὠνίων διωκοῦντες. Videbant Agoranomi ut religiose haec Lex observaretur: nam ad illos cura rerum venalium pertinebat. Harpocration alibi: Ἀγορανόμοι, οἱ κατὰ τὸ ἀγορᾶν ὤνια διοικοῦντες ἀρχοντες. Vlpianus ad Demosthenis Timocrateam: ἐπὶ δὲ Ἀγορανόμος ὁ ἐπόπτης τῶν ὠνίων τῆς ἀγορᾶς. Quare etiam Agoranomis curae erat, ne imponerent, & fraudem facerent sive venditores, sive emptores. Theophrastus in Libris Legum: Σιοῖν ἐπιμελεῖσθαι τῶν Ἀγορανόμων, τῆς τε ὁ τῆς ἀγορᾶς διοικούσης, καὶ τὰ ἀψευδῆ μὴ μόνον τοὺς πωλοῦντας, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς ὠνουμένους. illi, sive in rebus ipsis venalibus, sive in falsis comminiscendis. Nam ait Lysias fieri solitum saepius Athenis, ut sitonae, quo impunitius annonam flagellarent, falsa quaedam comminiscerentur, & in vulgus spargerent: ὅτι δὲ ἀσφαλεῖς τοῖς συμφορᾶς τοῖς ὑμετέρας ἀπολῆσαι, ὥστε τοῖς μὲν πεισθῆναι τὴν ἀγορὰν πωλοῦντας, τοῖς δὲ ἐπὶ λαγῶν εἰσὶν. [?] Vtrique venditores & emptores ne qua falsitas esset in contractibus & commerciis. Quare re etiam nondum emptori tradita, sed arra tantum à venditore accepta, si venditor à contractu recedere vellet, aduersus eum emptori competebat βεβαιώσεως actio. Harpocration è Lysia: εἰ ὅτι καὶ Ξέρξης Ἀλκιβιάδου μὲν ἀποθνήσκοντος [?] τῆς παραγραφῆς, ἐλαγχάνει τῷ τῆς βεβαιώσεως δίκῃ ὁ τὸν Ξέρξην δεῖ δὲ λαβεῖν. Λυσίας ἐν δυοῖ λόγοις. Itaque in prouerbium abiit ἀπιστῶν πίστις. Quanquam vix res venales dabant sine praesenti pecunia, unde dixit Plautus Asinaria, Graeca mercari fide: eoque referunt viri summi verba Theophrasti in Charactere ἀπιστίας. καὶ τοῖς ἐλαφροῖς τὸ πᾶν αὐτὸ καὶ λέγειν, πώσου, καλάδου. ἡ γὰρ ἀγορᾶζω πίμπλη, &, vertunt: Postremo ijs qui cum aliquid ab ipso sumserint, dicunt illi, Refer in rationes: Imo, ait, depone: non enim vacat mittere flagitasum. Sed ποσσῶν non est referre in rationes, vt constat è charactere ἀπιστίας ἀληθείας. Puto rescribendum: καὶ τοῖς ἐλαφροῖς τὸ πᾶν αὐτὸ καὶ λέγειν πῶς ἡ, καλάδου, ἡ γὰρ ἀγορᾶζω πίμπλη. Iis, qui cum aliquid quod eius sit, acceperint, & dicunt, Nonne? (supple licet accipero.) Imo, inquit, depone, non enim vacat mittere qui ferat: Praetextu scilicet pueri, qui illud ferat in amici domum, quem sibi praesto non esse dicit, amico denegat. Dicet forte aliquis praecessisse hoc ipso charactere eandem hominis ἀπίστου notationem his verbis: καὶ ὅταν ἥκῃ τῆς ἀπιστούμενος ἐκ πώματος, μάλιστα μὲν μὴ δώσῃ. Sed locus est insignis elegantiae, quem corrupte esse nemo ibit inficias, nec quicquam facere ad sequentem ἀπίστου hominis notationem, de qua iam diximus. Rescribo: καὶ ὅταν ἥκῃ τῆς ἀπιστούμενος, ἐκ πῶ μαθάν, μάλιστα μὲν μὴ δώσῃ. Quod si
units.tr: Hyperides quotes this law in his first speech against Alcibiades, according to Harpocration: "not to lie in the marketplace." Hyperides, in the first speech against Alcibiades: the law of Xenon calls it "not to lie in the marketplace"; the law seems to have been laid down about the goods for sale itself. Demosthenes in the Leptinean speech: for there is a law, men of Athens, written not for the marketplace alone, that one should not lie, in matters where no public harm is done if anyone is deceived. Ulpian: for the law against lying in the marketplace opposes those who prosecute sales. The market-inspectors saw that this law was observed scrupulously, for the care of saleable goods belonged to them. Harpocration elsewhere: the market-inspectors, the magistrates who manage saleable goods in the market. Ulpian on Demosthenes' Timocratea: the market-inspector is the overseer of the saleable goods of the market. Hence it was also the market-inspectors' task to prevent fraud, whether by sellers or by buyers. Theophrastus in his books of laws: the market-inspectors ought to take care of the market and its dealings, and that falsehoods be avoided not only by sellers but also by buyers. Those whose duty it was, whether in the saleable goods themselves or in inventing falsehoods. For Lysias says that it was often done at Athens that the sitophylakes, so that they might whip up the price with less risk, invented certain falsehoods and spread them among the people: [Greek]. Both sellers and buyers should avoid any falsehood in contracts and dealings. Hence, even when the thing had not yet been handed over to the buyer, but only an earnest had been received from the seller, if the seller wished to withdraw from the contract, the buyer had the action of guarantee against him. Harpocration from Lysias: [Greek], so that the one who sought the guarantee suit was entitled to it, and it was the one who must take it. Lysias in two speeches. Hence the proverb arose: "untrustworthy trust" [ἀπιστῶν πίστις]. Although saleable goods were scarcely given without present money, whence Plautus in the Asinaria says "to trade Greek goods on credit"; and to this the great man refers the words of Theophrastus in the Character of Distrust: [Greek]. They translate it: finally, to those who have taken something from him they say, "Put it on my account"; no, he says, deposit it, for I have no time to send. But "pōssōn" [ποσσῶν] does not mean to put on account, as is clear from the Character of Distrust. I think it should be rewritten: [Greek]. To those who have received something that is theirs, and say, "Is it not?" (supply, "let me receive it"), he says "No, deposit it, for I have no time to send someone to carry it." Under the pretext, of course, of a boy who would carry it to a friend's house, whom he says is not with him, he denies it to his friend. Perhaps someone will say that the same notation of the distrustful man was already given in this same character with the words: "and when he comes, being distrusted, from the drink, let him by all means not give." But the passage is of notable elegance, and no one will deny that it is corrupt, nor does it contribute anything to the following notation of the distrustful man, which we have already discussed. I rewrite: "and when he comes, being distrusted, from drink, let him by all means not give." Which if anyone asks anything from him, he wastes time in vain by asking how and to what extent he may be able to give, but he will mostly refuse.

units.la: [?] Greek passages above are read with uncertainty where marked. quis ab illo quicquam petat, vane tempus terat interrogando, quomodo & quatenus dare possit, maxime tamen deneget. Sed ad forum & res in eo venales redea-mus.
units.tr: [?] The Greek passages above are read with uncertainty where marked. Whoever asks anything of him wastes his time asking how and how far he could give, yet he will for the most part refuse. But let us return to the market and the goods sold in it.

units.la: Adeo volebant Athenienses Ἐχ τὸ ἀγορᾶν ἀφεδ[?]σίν, vt Aristonici Lege cautum sit, ne piscarij pisces minoris quam indicassent, venderent: si secus fecissent, in carcerem raperentur.
units.tr: So eager were the Athenians Ἐχ τὸ ἀγορᾶν ἀφεδ[?]σίν that a law of Aristonicus provided that fishmongers were not to sell fish for less than they had declared, and if they did otherwise they were to be dragged off to prison.

units.la: Τοὺς ἰχθυοπώλας μὴ ἀποδόσθαι τοὺς ἰχθύας ἐλάττονος ἧς εἶπον ὑμῖν, εἰ δὲ εἰς ὃ διομωτή[?]ειν ἀπάγεσθαι.
units.tr: The fishmongers are not to sell the fish for less than they told you; if they do otherwise, they are to be led off to the court. [Τοὺς ἰχθυοπώλας μὴ ἀποδόσθαι τοὺς ἰχθύας ἐλάττονος ἧς εἶπον ὑμῖν, εἰ δὲ εἰς ὃ διομωτή[?]ειν ἀπάγεσθαι.]

units.la: Piscarij pisces minoris quam indicarint, ne vendunto: si secus fecerint, in carcerem abducuntor.
units.tr: Fishmongers are not to sell fish for less than they have declared; if they do otherwise, they are to be led off to prison.

units.la: Legem hanc laudat Alexis Comicus in Lebete: ὁ γάρ τε χρεῖ[?]ων ὀμολιθεὶς ὁ πλούσιος Ἀεισώκου. ἀλλ' ἡ ἐκ πωί[?] ἡμῶν, τὴν ἰχθυοπωλῶν ἄσις αὐ πωλεῖν γὰρ τὴν ἰχθὺν ἀποτιμήσας, ἀπόδος ἐλάττονος ἧς εἶπε ὑμῶν, εἰς ὃ διομωτήριον ἀὐτὰς ἀπάγεσθαι τῶν.
units.tr: Alexis the comic poet praises this law in his Lebes: "For the rich man, ... Aeisocus ... but from our ... the fishmongers ... for having valued the fish, he is to sell it for less than he declared to us, and be led off to the court." [ὁ γάρ τε χρεῖ[?]ων ὀμολιθεὶς ὁ πλούσιος Ἀεισώκου. ἀλλ' ἡ ἐκ πωί[?] ἡμῶν, τὴν ἰχθυοπωλῶν ἄσις αὐ πωλεῖν γὰρ τὴν ἰχθὺν ἀποτιμήσας, ἀπόδος ἐλάττονος ἧς εἶπε ὑμῶν, εἰς ὃ διομωτήριον ἀὐτὰς ἀπάγεσθαι τῶν.]

units.la: Legis latæ tempus indicat, nempe sub id, quo drama hoc docuit Alexis, lata autem Lex, ne carius indicarent: nam si carius indicassent, cum vendere non possent, putres reportaturi erant domum: atque ita illis periret piscatum. Sequitur ibidem: ἵνα διδικῶτες τῆς ἀξίας ἀγαπῶσιν, εἰ τῆς ἐσπέρας Γαστρὸς ἀπόντες ἀπορροφῶσιν εἰκῇ.
units.tr: The time of the law is indicated: namely, about when Alexis produced this play, and the law was passed that they should not price fish higher. For if they priced it higher and could not sell it, they would carry the rotten fish home again, and so their catch would perish for them. It follows in the same place: "so that, having been assessed at its worth, they may be content, if in the evening they gulp down ... at random from the belly ..." [ἵνα διδικῶτες τῆς ἀξίας ἀγαπῶσιν, εἰ τῆς ἐσπέρας Γαστρὸς ἀπόντες ἀπορροφῶσιν εἰκῇ.]

units.la: Non licebat enim illis pisces putres vendere: itaque ne fierent, Lege erat pi-scariis interdictum, pisces, qui iam essent aut putres aut marcidi, aqua rigare, ut viderentur recentes.
units.tr: For it was not permitted for them to sell putrid fish. So, to prevent this happening, the fishmongers were forbidden by law to sprinkle with water fish that were already putrid or rotting, so that they would look fresh.

units.la: Τοὺς ἰχθυοπώλας μὴ ῥαίνειν τοὺς ἰχθύας σ-ραίνειν.
units.tr: The fishmongers are not to sprinkle the fish with water. [Τοὺς ἰχθυοπώλας μὴ ῥαίνειν τοὺς ἰχθύας σ-ραίνειν.]

units.la: Piscarij pisces putres aqua ne rigan-to.
units.tr: Fishmongers must not sprinkle putrid fish with water.

units.la: Legem refert Xenarchus Πορφύρ[?]ιος, vbi de piscariis agitur ἐπεὶ γὰρ αὐτῆς οὐκ ἔτ' ἐξ ἰδεσίας ῥαίνειν, ἀπείρητον ἢ τῶτο τοῦ νόμου.
units.tr: Xenarchus Porphyrius (?) refers to the law where fishmongers are concerned: "for since it was no longer permitted to sprinkle them, this was forbidden by law." [ἐπεὶ γὰρ αὐτῆς οὐκ ἔτ' ἐξ ἰδεσίας ῥαίνειν, ἀπείρητον ἢ τῶτο τοῦ νόμου.]

units.la: Erat Opsonomorum, qui duo siue tres numero à Senatu eligebantur, curæ commissum forum piscarium, & vt Leges hæ obseruarentur. De iis Sophilus apud Athenæum Libro VI. Ὃ δὲ ἔχος τῶν τὸ Ἀθηναῖοι εἴ) ἀξιεῖ Σοφίλος ἐν Ἀνδροκλῇ, Ὀψονόμους ἀξιοῦν αἱρεῖσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς βουλῆς δύο δὲ κα τῆς. Eustathius ad Iliad. Λ. ἐξοφαγεῖν ὅτι ἐπ' ἐκ ὅτι ἐπ' ἐκ ὅτι ἐπ' ἐκ ὅτι ἐπ' ἐκ ὅτι ἐπ' ἐκ. Sed, vt dixi, in vniuersum, rerum venalium in foro cura erat penes Agoranomos, qui eos, qui in forum conuenerant, si quid in Leges committerent, flagris cædebant. Græcus Interpres ad hæc Comici Acharnensibus: Ἀγορανόμους δὲ τῆς ἀγορᾶς καθίσαμεν τεῖς ἔις λαχόντας, ἔις οἱ ἰμάτας ἐκ λεσθῶν. ὀλίγῳ μὴ τι συκοφαντῆς εἰσίτω, μήτ' ἄγος ἀδας φασιαῖος ἐγ' αἰτῶν.
units.tr: There were the Opsonomi, two or three in number, chosen by the Senate, to whom the fish market and the enforcement of these laws were committed. Sophilus, in Athenaeus book VI, speaks of them: the Athenians ought to choose Opsonomi from the Council, two ... Eustathius on Iliad Λ, [garbled Greek as printed]. But, as I said, in general the care of saleable goods in the market lay with the Agoranomi, who beat with whips those who gathered in the market if they committed anything against the laws. The Greek interpreter, on Aristophanes' Acharnians, says: "We appointed the Agoranomi of the market by lot, who were to ... so that no sycophant should enter a little ... nor ..." [Ἀγορανόμους δὲ τῆς ἀγορᾶς καθίσαμεν τεῖς ἔις λαχόντας, ἔις οἱ ἰμάτας ἐκ λεσθῶν. ὀλίγῳ μὴ τι συκοφαντῆς εἰσίτω, μήτ' ἄγος ἀδας φασιαῖος ἐγ' αἰτῶν.]

units.la: Ὃ παλαιὸν, inquit, Φερεκράτης ἐπυνθάνετο οἱ Ληκηταὶ τῶν ἀγορᾶς. Ληκηταὶ sunt Agoranomi, vt idem docet paullo ante, Ἀγορανόμοις οἱ Λογίας καλοῦλιν. His Agoranomis vectigal pendebant, qui Athenas aliunde adportassent in forum quicquam mercimonij. Hinc Dicæopolis apud Aristophanem eodem dramate Acharnensibus anguillam à Bœoto sibi dari petit ἀγορᾶς τέλος.
units.tr: "Of old," he says, "Pherecrates asked the Lēkētai of the market." The Lēkētai are the Agoranomi, as the same author teaches a little before: the Agoranomi are called Logistai. From these Agoranomi those who brought any merchandise into the market at Athens from elsewhere paid a toll. Hence Dicaeopolis in Aristophanes, in the same play, the Acharnians, asks the Boeotian for an eel as the market toll.

units.la: <bl>ἀγορᾶς τέλος ζωύτων γ᾽ ἀ που δώσης ἐμοί.</bl>
units.tr: "You will surely give me some of these as the market toll." [ἀγορᾶς τέλος ζωύτων γ᾽ ἀ που δώσης ἐμοί.]

units.la: Scholiastes: <bl>ἔθος ἦν ὁ παλαιὸν, ὃς ἂν τῇ ἀγορᾷ πωλοῦντος τέλος λιδόναι τῆς Λογίας.</bl>
units.tr: The scholiast: "It was an ancient custom that whoever sold in the market had to pay the toll to the Logistae." [ἔθος ἦν ὁ παλαιὸν, ὃς ἂν τῇ ἀγορᾷ πωλοῦντος τέλος λιδόναι τῆς Λογίας.]

units.la: DE VSVRIS. TITVLVS IV.
units.tr: ON USURY. TITLE IV.

units.la: Nter pecuniæ quærendæ rationes secundam in Politicis recenset Philosophus <bl>τὴν ζωσμόν</bl>, <bl>τῆς δὲ</bl> <bl>μεταβλητικῆς δύπερον εἴδος, τοκισμός.</bl> Quam rationem ipse improbat, vt quæ maxime à natura abhorreat: <bl>τῆς δὲ μεταβλητικῆς φορὰν ...</bl> [illegible, ~12 letters] <bl>μεταβολῆς γὰρ ἐχθιστον εἴπληφεν. ὁμοια γὰρ τὰ ἐκπόμωνα τῆς ...</bl> [illegible, ~20 letters] Atque in genere fenerari, idem est quod hominem occidere, vt maior Cato aiebat. Verum Athenis maxima erat fenerandi licentia, approbata veteri hac Solonis Lege:
units.tr: Among the ways of acquiring money, the Philosopher in the Politics lists second the ... and, a kind of exchange, lending at interest (τοκισμός). He himself disapproves of it, as being most contrary to nature, since money is the least fitting thing to breed money. [Part of the Greek is illegible in the scan.] To lend in general is the same as to kill a man, as the elder Cato used to say. Yet at Athens the licence to lend at interest was very great, approved by this ancient law of Solon:

units.la: TO ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΝ ΣΤΑΣΙΜΟΝ ΕΙ-NAI, ΕΦ᾽ ΟΠΟΣΟΝ ΑΝ ΒΟΥΛΗ-TAI Ο ΔΑΝΕΙΖΩΝ.
units.tr: The money shall be a standing sum, at whatever rate the lender wishes. [τὸ ἀργύριον στάσιμον εἶναι, ἐφ᾽ ὁποσονἂν βούληται ὁ δανείζων]

units.la: Legem hanc laudat Lysias <bl>ἐν τῷ κατὰ Θεομνήστου</bl> α᾽. <bl>καὶ</bl> μὴ <bl>ἀμάγωγὴν τοὺς νόμους τὰς Σόλωνος τὰς</bl> <bl>παλαιούς</bl>, NOMOΣ TO APΓΥPION ΣΤΑΣΙΜΟΝ EINAI, EΦ᾽ OΠOΣOΝ AN BOYAHTAI O ΔANEIZΩN <bl>ὃ ΣΤΑΣΙΜΟΝ. τῶν ὃ ἐστιν, ὦ βέλτιστε, ἡ ζυγὰ ἰσάναι, ἀλλὰ τῶν ἀφέλειας ὁποσον ἂν βάλλῃ.</bl>
units.tr: Lysias praises this law in the first book of his speech against Theomnestus, and says that the laws of Solon are not to be set aside: "The law says that money is a standing sum, at whatever rate the lender wishes." He means, my good sir, not that the sums must be equal, but that the lender may charge whatever interest he likes.

units.la: Vetustissima videtur vsura apud Athenienses ἐφεκλος τόκος fextantalis; cum obolus menstruus in drachmam datur, atque dicitur δανείζει ὅτι ἑκτῶ δραχμῆς. Nam ideo veteres Attici apud Pollucem Libro XIII. cap. IX. ὀβολοστάτῳ feneratorem vocauerunt. Hesychius: ὀβολοστάπις, τοὺς δανείστας ἐλεγον. Hinc Aristoteles τοκισμὸν dixit ὀβολοσταλικῷ, quia prima vsura fuit ὀβολὸς ἰμμένvesis δραχμῶν. Hinc quoque Hesychij glossa, ἐπωβελία, τόκος. Significatur enim τόκος ὅτι ὀβολὸς, vt singulis mensibus pro drachma obolus penderetur: pro mina drachmæ sedecim cum obolis quatuor: certe in iudiciis dicitur ἐπωβελία ὀπάσιον, vt in luperioribus diximus, & exemplum adscripsimus huius vsurae fextantalis. Usitatissimus vero fenerandi modus erat centesima usura, quae τόκος ἑκατοστὴ [?] δραχμῆ [?] dicitur, ut pro mina quot mensibus drachma penderetur: Exemplum dabimus, Deo dante, infra, ubi de dote agemus: alterum extat apud Æschinem ὁ παῖς [?] Κτησιφῶντος. ὃ τὴν [?] ὠνούμενος Δημοσθένει [?] τῆς δωδεκαδραχμίας [?] δραχμὴν τῆς μνᾶς τῆς μνᾶς [?], ἕως ὃ καὶ Φάλαιον ἀπέδοσαν [?].
units.tr: The oldest form of usury among the Athenians seems to have been the sixth-part rate (τόκος ἕκτος, fextantal), where a monthly obol was paid on each drachma, so that the rate was one-sixth of the principal. For this reason the old Attic writers called a lender an "obol-collector" (ὀβολοστάτης), as Pollux says in Book 13, chapter 9. Hesychius: "obolostatis, they called the moneylenders." Hence Aristotle called usury "obol-interest" (ὀβολοστατικός), because the first interest was an obol per drachma. Hence too the gloss of Hesychius, "epobelia: interest." For epobelia means interest of an obol, namely that an obol was paid monthly for each drachma; so for a mina of a hundred drachmas, sixteen drachmas and four obols. Certainly in the courts the epobelia is spoken of, as we said above, and I have added an example of this sixth-part usury. The most common mode of lending, however, was the hundredth usury, a rate of one drachma per mina each month. I shall give an example, God willing, below, where we treat of dowry; another is found in Aeschines, concerning the son of Ctesiphon, who bought from Demosthenes... [the rest of the Greek is too garbled to render].

units.la: Trientale fenus, τόκος τριταῖος [?], Ἰσαῖος ὁ παῖς [?] Κτησιφῶντος, ἐξακοσίαις δραχμῆς τριτημορίου [?]. Quomodo intelligendum istud sit, docet Suidas, qui addit Isæi verbis: αἰ [?] τὴν [?] τὴν ἡ [?] ἡμισείας [?] τῆς [?] ἡμισείας [?], ὃ τρεῖς [?] τῆς [?] μικρᾶς [?] τῆς [?] τῆς [?] ἡμισείας [?] τῆς [?]. Itaque octo oboli menstrui dabantur in tetradrachmum, sive duo oboli in drachmam.
units.tr: Trientale fenus, a third-part interest (τόκος τριταῖος). Isaeus, the son of Ctesiphon, [lent] six hundred drachmas at a third part. How this is to be understood Suidas explains, who adds to the words of Isaeus... [illegible]. Thus eight monthly obols were given on a tetradrachm, or two obols on a drachma.

units.la: Τόκος ἐπιγόνου [?] apud Demosthenem exponitur ab Harpocratione & Suida, cum tres oboli pro tetradrachma feneratori dantur: ἐπιγόνου [?]. Δημοσθένης ἐν τῷ πρὸς Πολυκλέα [?] τῷ τριταίῳ [?] ἐπιγόνου [?] τριωβόλου [?]. εἰ̓ν δ' ἢ αἱ̓ ἐπιγόνου, ὅ ὅταν διδῷ [?] ὅσπερ τὴν καφαλαίαν [?] ὅ[?] ὅ[?] μέρος [?] δωδεκάτην [?] τῆς δυνάμεως [?]. Ὅ[?] πειδῶλον [?] τῆς τετραδράχμου [?]. In mina sunt tetradrachma viginti quinque, proinde in minam redeunt singulis mensibus feneratori oboli septuaginta quinque, quod est ἐπιγόνου τῆς μνᾶς, quemadmodum triobolum est ἐπιγόνου τῆς τετραδράχμου. Quare anno vertente una mina, quæ in sortem data erat, sesquiminam commodi lucrabitur, & pro una mina, duæ cum semisse feneratori restituentur. Sed ista non placent Viro Incomparabili, quia ὁ ἐπιγόνου in minam dabatur, non in tetradrachmum. ὁ ἐπιγόνου interpretatur triobolum: additque esse nauticum fenus, ac proinde diarium, non menstruum: Itaque in singulas minas annui debebantur oboli mille octoginta, si annum facias dierum trecentum sexaginta, id est, debebantur drachmæ centum octoginta. In suam sententiam ire vult Xenophontem ὡς [?] τὸ μὲν γὰρ αὐτὸ ἀλλὰ [?] μνᾶ [?] εἰσφορᾷ [?] ζήτησιν [?] ὥσπερ ναυλικὸν [?] ἐκεῖνο [?] ἐπιτιμῶν [?] οὐκ [?] γίγνεται [?] τοιοῦτον [?] τῆς ἡμέρας [?] λαμβάνειν [?]· ὃ δ' ἢ γ' ἀ̓ [?] πέντε [?] μνᾶς [?], πλεῖον [?] ἢ ἐπιτιμῶν [?]. Eius verba ista interpretatur. Ex decem minis capientem triobolum diurnum ait lucrifacere quintam partem sortis, & sane centum octoginta drachmæ sunt quinta pars decem minarum, & præterea ; Sed verum non est, quod ait eadem centum octoginta drachmas esse plus quam tertiam partem quinque minarum. Hoc verum erat, si centum octoginta esset plus quam tertia pars [?] quingentorum. Verum non possumus eadem cum Viro magno sentire: Nam triobolum non est ὁ ἐπιγόνου minæ, sed tetradrachmi: Ergo si in minam ὁ ἐπιγόνου triobolum non videtur fuisse. Præterea annum facit dierum trecentum sexaginta, qui tamen lunaris observabatur in exigendo fenore, ut è Nebulis Aristophanis liquido constat. Deinde, ut mittam eius calculum in quinta, aut tertia parte, decem, aut quinque minarum, designanda, quem plane non cupio, Xenophon non ait lucrifacere tantum centum octoginta drachmas, quæ sunt, ex sententia τῆς μακελέιτου [?], usura unius minæ, agit enim de usura decem minarum, quæ est, ut quidem vult ὁ πάνυ [?], mille octingentarum drachmarum. In alia igitur eundum est: & certè Xenophontis hic locus probat datum fuisse triobolum in tetradrachmum. Sors est decem minarum, id est, drachmarum mille, quæ sunt ducenta quinquaginta tetradrachma: Singula tetradrachma fenore nautico occupata pariunt in singulos dies triobolum: Ergo ducenta quinquaginta tetradrachma dant singulis diebus obolos septingentos quinquaginta, id est, drachmas centum viginti quinque. Itaque hæc ducenta quinquaginta tetradrachma dabunt drachmas termille septingentas quinquaginta: accedat huic fenori sors ipsa, decem minæ, fient drachmæ quatermille septingentæ quinquaginta, has per quinque divide, quinta pars erit drachmarum nongentarum quinquaginta. Quare Ἔκα μὲν εἰσφορᾷ ἀρδὸν ὑπὲρ πέμ-πτον ἀπὸ γίγνεται [?], decem hæ minæ, quando vertente mense cum fenore nautico restituentur, erunt tantum quinta ferme pars totius illius summæ, quæ restituetur: Nam quinta pars est drachmarum nongentarum quinquaginta: decem vero minæ sunt drachmæ mille: Itaque quinta hæc pars omnino non est sors ipsa, id est, decem minæ; desunt enim quinquaginta drachmæ. De quinque minis fenore nautico, item occupatis addit ἢ δὲ γ' ἀὴ πέντε μναῖ, πλέον ἢ ὀκτάπειτον [?]. Minæ hæ quinque sunt tetradrachma centum viginti quinque, quæ dant in dies singulos drachmas sexaginta duas cum triobolo. Ergo menstruum fenus harum quinque minarum est drachmarum mille octingentarum septuaginta quinque. Adde fenori sortem ipsam, fient drachmæ bis mille trecentæ septuaginta quinque; quem numerum si per quinque divid as, quinta quæque pars erit drachmarum quadringentarum septuaginta quinque. Ergo, quemadmodum quinta pars vsurarum menstruarum, quæ datæ sunt in decem minas fenori nautico occupatas, accedente ipsa decem minarum sorte, vt in superioribus diximus, paullo minor est sorte ipsa decem minarum: ita contra vice versa, quinque minæ paullo maiores sunt quinta parte totius illius summæ, quam collegimus, cum ex sorte ipsa quinque minarum, tum ex vsuris earum, quæ competunt intra mensem quinque minis istis fenore nautico occupatis: atque hoc est quod dixit Xenophon, qui docet quanti maior sit, nempe fenore ὀκτάπειτον [?] septuaginta quinque drachmarum menstruo. Vnde rescribo apud Xenophontem: ἢ δὲ γ' ἀὴ πέντε μναῖ, πλέον ἢ ὀκτάπειτον [?]. Huic corrumpendo loco fuit, quod sequitur apud Xenophontem: οἱ δὲ γ' πλέον ἢ Ἀθηναῖον [?], &c. nam veteres ὃ οἱ [?] pronunciabant vt ος. Ος autem, quod præcedebat, cum non intelligerent, librarij, expunxerunt, atque ita locum deprauarunt, πλέον ἢ ὀκτάπειτον [?]. hoc est ἑξδομήκοντα πέντε [?] scilicet δραχμῶν [?], minæ quinque sunt quinta parte maiores, fenore menstruo scilicet ὀκτάπειτον [?] drachmarum septuaginta quinque: τὰς ὀκτάπειτος [?] menstruus vnius drachmæ sunt oboli duo: Ergo fenus drachmarum septuaginta quinque sunt oboli centum quinquaginta, siue drachmæ viginti quinque, quot drachmis maiores sunt minæ quinque parte illæ quinta, de qua diximus. In collocanda autem pecunia fenori nautico, aliquando fenerator commeatus & remeatus periculum suscipiebat, id est, fenus accipiebat sub hac Lege, si nauis, nulla iactura facta, è negotiatione rediisset. Pollux Lib. VIII. cap. XII. ἀμφοτερόπλοιον [?], ἀμφοτερόπλοιον [?]. Grammatici: ἀμφοτερόπλοιον [?]. Δημοσθένης [?] πρὸς [?] Διονυσοδώρου [?], ὅταν τῆς ναυτικῆς δίκης [?]. Aliquando commeatus tantum, non reditus, periculum suscipiebat, quod ἐπὶ ἀμφοτερόπλοιον [?] Polluci dicitur. Exigebant & magis horrendum fenus, si vellent, [illegible, ~9 letters] tocullliones. Theophrastus περὶ ὀπωνίας. καὶ τῆς ὀραχμῆς τόκον [?] ἡμιωβόλια τῆς ἡμέρας [?] drachma obolum semis quotidie parit. Vsura autem, quae non soluebatur, forti accedebat, atque deinceps fenus pariebat, quod ἀνατοκισμὸν [?] nuncupant. Theophrastus περὶ μικρολογίας. Ἡ ὅτι τόκων τόκον [?].
units.tr: The "epigonos" interest in Demosthenes is explained by Harpocration and Suidas, when three obols are given to the lender per tetradrachm. Demosthenes, in the speech against Polycles, speaks of the third-part epigonos of a triobol... In a mina there are twenty-five tetradrachms; so in a mina, each month, the lender receives seventy-five obols, which is the epigonos of the mina, just as the triobol is the epigonos of the tetradrachm. Hence in a year a mina lent as principal would yield a profit of one and a half minas, and for one mina two and a half would be returned to the lender. But these figures do not please the Incomparable Man, because the epigonos was given on a mina, not on a tetradrachm. He interprets the epigonos as a triobol, and adds that it was nautical interest, and therefore daily, not monthly. So on each mina there would be due 1,080 obols a year, if you take a year of 360 days; that is, 180 drachmas would be due. He wants Xenophon to agree with his view, when Xenophon, criticising the ... says that the sum yields a triobol daily... Xenophon's words are explained thus: from ten minas one who takes a triobol daily gains a fifth part of the principal, and indeed 180 drachmas are a fifth part of ten minas. But it is not true, as he says, that these 180 drachmas are more than a third part of five minas. That would be true only if 180 were more than a third part of five hundred. We cannot agree with the great man on this point: for the triobol is not the epigonos of the mina but of the tetradrachm; so if the triobol were the epigonos of the mina, it does not seem to have been a triobol. Moreover, he makes the year 360 days, though the lunar year was observed in collecting interest, as is clear from Aristophanes' Clouds. Further, to pass over his calculation of a fifth or third part of ten or five minas, which I do not at all want to pursue, Xenophon does not say that one gains only 180 drachmas, which by the reckoning of ... is the usury of one mina; he is speaking of the usury of ten minas, which, as the same great man wishes, is 1,800 drachmas. So we must go another way; and certainly this passage of Xenophon shows that a triobol was given per tetradrachm. The principal is ten minas, that is a thousand drachmas, which are 250 tetradrachms. Each tetradrachm put out at nautical interest yields a triobol per day; so 250 tetradrachms give 750 obols per day, that is, 125 drachmas. Thus these 250 tetradrachms will yield 750 drachmas a month... [the calculation continues]. Add to this interest the principal itself, ten minas, and there are 4,750 drachmas; divide these by five, and the fifth part is 950 drachmas. So these ten minas, when returned at the end of the month with nautical interest, will be only about a fifth part of the whole sum that is restored; for a fifth part is 950 drachmas, while ten minas are 1,000 drachmas. Thus this fifth part is not the principal itself, that is ten minas, for it is fifty drachmas short. On five minas put out at nautical interest, Xenophon adds: "the five minas yield more than 85 ..." These five minas are 125 tetradrachms, which give 62 and a triobol drachmas per day. So the monthly interest on these five minas is 1,875 drachmas. Add the principal, and there are 2,375 drachmas; if you divide this by five, each fifth part will be 475 drachmas. So, just as a fifth part of the monthly interest given on the ten minas put out at nautical interest, with the principal of ten minas added, as we said above, is a little less than the principal of ten minas, so conversely five minas are a little more than the fifth part of the whole sum we have gathered, both from the principal of five minas and from the interest on them falling due within the month. This is what Xenophon meant, who teaches how much more the sum is, namely by 75 drachmas of monthly interest. Hence I would correct the text of Xenophon. The passage was corrupted by what follows in Xenophon, "the others more than Athenian," etc. For the old writers pronounced the hoi like os; and copyists, not understanding the os which preceded, struck it out and so corrupted the passage. That is, five minas are a fifth part greater, namely by the monthly interest of seventy-five drachmas. Now, the monthly interest of one drachma is two obols; so the interest of seventy-five drachmas is 150 obols, or twenty-five drachmas, by which the five minas exceed that fifth part of which we spoke. When lending money at nautical interest, the lender sometimes undertook the risk of the outward and return voyage; that is, he received interest under this condition: that if the ship returned from its trading without any loss. Pollux, Book 8, chapter 12, [speaks of a loan covering both ways]. The grammarians: [a loan for both voyages]. Demosthenes, against Dionysodorus, [speaks of a maritime suit]. Sometimes the lender undertook the risk only of the outward voyage, not the return, which Pollux calls "loan on the outward voyage only." They also exacted an even more dreadful interest, if they wished, from ... the tokullions. Theophrastus, in his work on Avarice: a drachma yields a half obol daily. Usury that was not paid was added to the principal, and then the interest itself bore interest, which they call compound interest (ἀνατοκισμός). Theophrastus, in his work on Meanness: the interest of interest.

units.la: Sed videtur impositus huic tocullionum auaritiae impuritatique modus: nam Legem tulerunt, ne immenso fenori pecuniam locarent.
units.tr: But it seems that a limit was set on this avarice and shamelessness of the usurers: they passed a law that they should not lend money at an immoderate rate of interest.

units.la: Laudat hanc Legem Vlpianus ad extremam Timocrateam. εἰσὶ γὰρ ἰδιωτικοὶ νόμοι, οἷς, μὴ λαμβάνειν πολλοῖς τόκοις.
units.tr: Ulpian praises this law at the end of the Timocratea: "For there are private laws by which one may not take interest at high rates" [εἰσὶ γὰρ ἰδιωτικοὶ νόμοι, οἷς, μὴ λαμβάνειν πολλοῖς τόκοις].

units.la: Temere autem pecuniam suam mutuo non dabant Danistae, nisi ἔπι ἐπιχρῶσι, vel coram testibus, vel scriptis etiam tabulis, vt constat ex his Demosthenis ἐν τῇ πρὸς Τιμόθεον λόγῳ ἔχοντος. Κατὰ σφαλέντος μὲν τοῦ ἀπωλλύντο ἡ τῶν πατέρων τὰ ἑαυτῶν ὅ συμβόλαιον· ὅτι γὰρ ἐπ' ἐκχρῶσι, ὅτε μὴ μαρτύρων, ἔδωκα.
units.tr: The lenders did not lend their money rashly, but only on security, either before witnesses or in written documents, as is clear from Demosthenes' speech against Timotheus: "If the contract failed, they would be ruined, and their fathers' property would be lost; for I lent on security, and not before witnesses" [Κατὰ σφαλέντος μὲν τοῦ ἀπωλλύντο ἡ τῶν πατέρων τὰ ἑαυτῶν ὅ συμβόλαιον· ὅτι γὰρ ἐπ' ἐκχρῶσι, ὅτε μὴ μαρτύρων, ἔδωκα].

units.la: Rursum: ἀναλισκόμοι μοι δοκεῖ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἀπόντα διηγήσασθαι ὑμῖν τὰ ὀφειλόμενα, ἡ εἰς ὅ, τὶ ἑκάστος αὐτῶν κατεχρήσατο, καὶ τὰς χρήσεις, ἐν οἷς ὅ συμβόλαιον ἐξήνεγκα.
units.tr: Again: "It seems to me necessary to set out for you from the beginning the debts, and to what use each of them put the money, and the loans under which I made the contract" [ἀναλισκόμοι μοι δοκεῖ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἀπόντα διηγήσασθαι ὑμῖν τὰ ὀφειλόμενα, ἡ εἰς ὅ, τὶ ἑκάστος αὐτῶν κατεχρήσατο, καὶ τὰς χρήσεις, ἐν οἷς ὅ συμβόλαιον ἐξήνεγκα].

units.la: Sed praestat exemplum dare συγγραφῆς, cuiusmodi extat apud Demosthenem ἐν τῇ πρὸς τὸν Λακείπου ἀπογραφήν.
units.tr: But it is better to give an example of a written contract (συγγραφή), of the kind that survives in Demosthenes, in the speech against Lacritus, an inventory of the kind [ἐν τῇ πρὸς τὸν Λακείπου ἀπογραφήν].

units.la: ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗ.
units.tr: Syngraphe [ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗ]

units.la: ΕΔΑΝΕΙΣΕΝ ΑΝΔΡΟΚΛΗΣ ΣΦΗΤΤΙΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΝΑΥΚΡΑΤΗΣ ΚΑΡΥΣΤΙΟΣ ΑΡΤΕΜΩΝΙ ΚΑΙ ΑΠΟΛΛΟΔΩΡΩ ΦΑΣΗΛΙΤΑΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΥ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΑΣ ΔΡΑΧΜΑΣ ΑΘΗΝΗΘΕΝ ΕΙΣ ΜΕΝΔΗΝ Η ΣΚΙΩΝΗΝ, ΚΑΙ ΕΝΤΕΥΘΕΝ ΕΙΣ ΒΟΣΠΟΡΟΝ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΒΟΥΛΩΝΤΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΕΓ' ΑΡΙΣΤΕΡΑ ΜΕΧΡΙ ΒΟΡΥΣΘΕΝΟΥΣ ΚΑΙ ΠΑΛΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΕΠΙ ΔΙΑΚΟΣΙΑΙΣ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΠΕΝΤΕ ΤΑΣ ΧΙΛΙΑΣ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΕΤ' ΑΡΚΤΟΥΡΟΝ ΕΚΠΛΕΥΣΩΣΙΝ ΕΚ ΤΟΥ ΓΟΝΤΟΥ ΕΦ' ΙΕΡΟΝ ΕΠΙ ΤΡΙΑΚΟΣΙΑΙΣ ΤΑΣ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΑΣ ΕΓΙ ΟΙΝΟΥ ΚΕΡΑΜΙΟΙΣ ΜΕΝΔΑΙΟΙΣ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣ ΠΛΕΥΣΕΙΤΑΙ ΕΚ ΜΕΝΔΗΣ Η ΣΚΙΩΝΗΣ ΕΝ ΤΗ ΕΙΚΟΣΟΡΩΙ, ΗΝ ΥΒΛΗΣΙΟΣ ΝΑΥΚΛΗΡΕΙ. ΥΠΟΤΙΘΕΑΣΙ ΔΕ ΤΑΥΤΑ ΟΥΚ ΟΦΕΙΛΟΝΤΕΣ ΕΠΙ ΤΟΥΤΟΙΣ ΑΛΛΩΙ ΟΥΔΕΝΙ ΟΥΔΕΝ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΝ ΟΥΔ' ΕΠΙΔΑΝΕΙΣΩΝΤΑΙ, ΚΑΙ ΑΠΑΞΟΥΣΙ ΤΑ ΧΡΗΜΑΤΑ ΤΑ ΕΚ ΤΟΥ ΟΙΝΟΥ ΑΝΤΙΦΟΡΤΙΣΘΕΝΤΑ ΠΑΛΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΕΝ ΤΩΙ ΑΥΤΩΙ ΓΑΛΟΙΩΙ ΑΓΑΝΤΑ. ΣΩΘΕΝΤΩΝ ΔΕ ΤΩΝ ΧΡΗΜΑΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΑΠΟΔΩΣΟΥΣΙΝ ΟΙ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΜΕΝΟΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ ΤΟ ΓΙΓΝΟΜΕΝΟΝ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΝ, ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΕΛΘΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΕΝΤΕΛΕΣ ΓΑΛΗΝ ΕΚΒΟΛΗΣ, ΗΝ ΑΝ ΟΙ ΣΥΜΓΑΛΟΙ ΨΗΦΙΣΑΜΕΝΟΙ ΚΟΙΝΗΙ ΕΚΒΑΛΛΩΝΤΑΙ ΚΑΙ ΕΝ ΤΙ ΠΟΛΕΜΙΟΙΣ ΑΓΟΤΙΣΩΣΙ ΤΩΝ ΑΛΛΩΝ ΑΓΑΝΤΩΝ ΕΝΤΕΛΕΣ ΚΑΙ ΓΑΡΕΞΟΥΣΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ ΤΗΝ ΥΠΟΘΗΚΗΝ ΑΝΕΠΑΦΟΝ ΚΡΑΤΕΙΝ, ΕΩΣ ΑΝ ΑΠΟΔΩΣΙ ΤΟ ΓΙΝΟΜΕΝΟΝ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΑΠΟΔΩΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΤΩΙ ΣΥΓΚΕΙΜΕΝΩΙ ΧΡΟΝΩΙ ΤΑ ΑΠΟΚΕΙΜΕΝΑ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙΝ, ΕΞΕΣΤΩ ΥΠΟΘΕΙΝΑΙ ΚΑΙ ΑΠΟΔΟΣΘΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΥΠΑΡΧΟΥΣΗΣ ΤΙΜΗΣ ΚΑΙ ΕΑΝ ΤΙ ΕΛΛΕΙΠΗ, ΤΟΥ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΥ, Ο ΔΕΙ ΓΕΝΕΣΘΑΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΑΡΤΕΜΩΝΟΣ, ΚΑΙ ΑΠΟΛΛΟΔΩΡΟΥ ΕΣΤΩ Η ΠΡΑΞΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ, ΚΑΙ ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΤΟΥΤΩΝ ΑΠΑΝΤΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΓΓΕΙΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΝΑΥΤΙΚΩΝ ΠΑΝΤΑΧΟΥ, ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΩΣΙ ΚΑΘΑΡΩΣ ΔΙΚΗΝ ΩΦΑΗΚΟΤΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΥΠΕΡΗΜΕΡΩΝ ΟΝΤΩΝ, ΚΑΙ ΕΝΙ ΕΚΑΤΕΡΩΙ ΤΩΝ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΝΤΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΑΜΦΟΤΕΡΟΙΣ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΕΙΣΒΑΛΛΩΣΙ ΜΕΙΝΑΝΤΕΣ ΕΠΙ ΚΥΝΙ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ ΔΕΚΑ ΕΝ ΕΛΛΗΣΠΟΝΤΩ, ΕΞΕΛΟΜΕΝΟΙ, ΟΡΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑ ΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΙΣ, ΚΑΙ ΕΝΤΕΥΘΕΝ ΚΑΤΑΠΛΕΥΣΑΝΤΕΣ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΤΟΥΣ ΤΟΚΟΥΣ ΑΠΟΔΙΑΔΟΝΤΩΝ ΤΟΥΣ ΓΕΡΥΣΙ ΓΡΑΦΕΝΤΑΣ ΕΙΣ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΤΙ Η ΝΑΥΣ ΠΑΘΗ, ΑΝΗΚΕΣΤΟΝ ΑΝ Η, ΑΝ ΠΛΕΗ ΤΑ ΧΡΗΜΑΤΑ ΣΩΤΗΡΙΑ ΕΣΤΩ ΤΩΝ ΥΠΟΚΕΙΜΕΝΩΝ, ΤΑ ΔΕ ΠΕΡΙΓΕΝΑ ΚΟΙΝΑ ΕΣΤΩ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ. ΚΥΡΙΟΤΕΡΟΝ ΔΕ ΠΕΡΙ ΤΟΥΤΩΝ ΑΛΛΟ ΜΗΔΕΝ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΣ ΜΑΡΤΥΡΕΣ ΦΟΡΜΙΩΝ ΓΕΙΡΑΙΕΥΣ ΚΗΦΙΣΟΔΟΤΟΣ ΒΟΙΩΤΙΟΣ ΗΛΙΟΔΩΡΟΣ ΠΙΤΘΕΥΣ.
units.tr: Androcles of Sphettus and Naucrates of Carystus lent to Artemon and Apollodorus of Phaselis three thousand drachmas of silver, from Athens to Mende or Scione, and from there to the Bosporus. If they wish to sail on the left as far as Borysthenes, and again to sail back to Athens with the cargo at the voyage's end, with the interest at the same rate... If they sail from Byzantium [i.e., beyond the Bosporus] after the rising of Arcturus, from the Pontus to Hieron, at three hundred drachmas per thousand, they shall pay back the three thousand [ΕΔΑΝΕΙΣΕΝ ΑΝΔΡΟΚΛΗΣ ΣΦΗΤΤΙΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΝΑΥΚΡΑΤΗΣ ΚΑΡΥΣΤΙΟΣ ΑΡΤΕΜΩΝΙ ΚΑΙ ΑΠΟΛΛΟΔΩΡΩ ΦΑΣΗΛΙΤΑΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΥ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΑΣ ΔΡΑΧΜΑΣ ΑΘΗΝΗΘΕΝ ΕΙΣ ΜΕΝΔΗΝ Η ΣΚΙΩΝΗΝ, ΚΑΙ ΕΝΤΕΥΘΕΝ ΕΙΣ ΒΟΣΠΟΡΟΝ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΒΟΥΛΩΝΤΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΕΓ' ΑΡΙΣΤΕΡΑ ΜΕΧΡΙ ΒΟΡΥΣΘΕΝΟΥΣ ΚΑΙ ΠΑΛΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΕΠΙ ΔΙΑΚΟΣΙΑΙΣ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΠΕΝΤΕ ΤΑΣ ΧΙΛΙΑΣ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΕΤ' ΑΡΚΤΟΥΡΟΝ ΕΚΠΛΕΥΣΩΣΙΝ ΕΚ ΤΟΥ ΓΟΝΤΟΥ ΕΦ' ΙΕΡΟΝ ΕΠΙ ΤΡΙΑΚΟΣΙΑΙΣ ΤΑΣ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΑΣ ΕΓΙ ΟΙΝΟΥ ΚΕΡΑΜΙΟΙΣ ΜΕΝΔΑΙΟΙΣ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣ ΠΛΕΥΣΕΙΤΑΙ ΕΚ ΜΕΝΔΗΣ Η ΣΚΙΩΝΗΣ ΕΝ ΤΗ ΕΙΚΟΣΟΡΩΙ, ΗΝ ΥΒΛΗΣΙΟΣ ΝΑΥΚΛΗΡΕΙ. ΥΠΟΤΙΘΕΑΣΙ ΔΕ ΤΑΥΤΑ ΟΥΚ ΟΦΕΙΛΟΝΤΕΣ ΕΠΙ ΤΟΥΤΟΙΣ ΑΛΛΩΙ ΟΥΔΕΝΙ ΟΥΔΕΝ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΝ ΟΥΔ' ΕΠΙΔΑΝΕΙΣΩΝΤΑΙ, ΚΑΙ ΑΠΑΞΟΥΣΙ ΤΑ ΧΡΗΜΑΤΑ ΤΑ ΕΚ ΤΟΥ ΟΙΝΟΥ ΑΝΤΙΦΟΡΤΙΣΘΕΝΤΑ ΠΑΛΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΕΝ ΤΩΙ ΑΥΤΩΙ ΓΑΛΟΙΩΙ ΑΓΑΝΤΑ. ΣΩΘΕΝΤΩΝ ΔΕ ΤΩΝ ΧΡΗΜΑΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΑΠΟΔΩΣΟΥΣΙΝ ΟΙ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΜΕΝΟΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ ΤΟ ΓΙΓΝΟΜΕΝΟΝ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΝ, ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΕΛΘΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΕΝΤΕΛΕΣ ΓΑΛΗΝ ΕΚΒΟΛΗΣ, ΗΝ ΑΝ ΟΙ ΣΥΜΓΑΛΟΙ ΨΗΦΙΣΑΜΕΝΟΙ ΚΟΙΝΗΙ ΕΚΒΑΛΛΩΝΤΑΙ ΚΑΙ ΕΝ ΤΙ ΠΟΛΕΜΙΟΙΣ ΑΓΟΤΙΣΩΣΙ ΤΩΝ ΑΛΛΩΝ ΑΓΑΝΤΩΝ ΕΝΤΕΛΕΣ ΚΑΙ ΓΑΡΕΞΟΥΣΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ ΤΗΝ ΥΠΟΘΗΚΗΝ ΑΝΕΠΑΦΟΝ ΚΡΑΤΕΙΝ, ΕΩΣ ΑΝ ΑΠΟΔΩΣΙ ΤΟ ΓΙΝΟΜΕΝΟΝ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΑΠΟΔΩΣΙΝ ΕΝ ΤΩΙ ΣΥΓΚΕΙΜΕΝΩΙ ΧΡΟΝΩΙ ΤΑ ΑΠΟΚΕΙΜΕΝΑ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙΝ, ΕΞΕΣΤΩ ΥΠΟΘΕΙΝΑΙ ΚΑΙ ΑΠΟΔΟΣΘΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΥΠΑΡΧΟΥΣΗΣ ΤΙΜΗΣ ΚΑΙ ΕΑΝ ΤΙ ΕΛΛΕΙΠΗ, ΤΟΥ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΥ, Ο ΔΕΙ ΓΕΝΕΣΘΑΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΑΡΤΕΜΩΝΟΣ, ΚΑΙ ΑΠΟΛΛΟΔΩΡΟΥ ΕΣΤΩ Η ΠΡΑΞΙΣ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ, ΚΑΙ ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΤΟΥΤΩΝ ΑΠΑΝΤΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΓΓΕΙΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΝΑΥΤΙΚΩΝ ΠΑΝΤΑΧΟΥ, ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΩΣΙ ΚΑΘΑΡΩΣ ΔΙΚΗΝ ΩΦΑΗΚΟΤΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΥΠΕΡΗΜΕΡΩΝ ΟΝΤΩΝ, ΚΑΙ ΕΝΙ ΕΚΑΤΕΡΩΙ ΤΩΝ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΝΤΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΑΜΦΟΤΕΡΟΙΣ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΕΙΣΒΑΛΛΩΣΙ ΜΕΙΝΑΝΤΕΣ ΕΠΙ ΚΥΝΙ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ ΔΕΚΑ ΕΝ ΕΛΛΗΣΠΟΝΤΩ, ΕΞΕΛΟΜΕΝΟΙ, ΟΡΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΙΣ, ΚΑΙ ΕΝΤΕΥΘΕΝ ΚΑΤΑΠΛΕΥΣΑΝΤΕΣ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΤΟΥΣ ΤΟΚΟΥΣ ΑΠΟΔΙΑΔΟΝΤΩΝ ΤΟΥΣ ΓΕΡΥΣΙ ΓΡΑΦΕΝΤΑΣ ΕΙΣ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΤΙ Η ΝΑΥΣ ΠΑΘΗ, ΑΝΗΚΕΣΤΟΝ ΑΝ Η, ΑΝ ΠΛΕΗ ΤΑ ΧΡΗΜΑΤΑ ΣΩΤΗΡΙΑ ΕΣΤΩ ΤΩΝ ΥΠΟΚΕΙΜΕΝΩΝ, ΤΑ ΔΕ ΠΕΡΙΓΕΝΑ ΚΟΙΝΑ ΕΣΤΩ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ. ΚΥΡΙΟΤΕΡΟΝ ΔΕ ΠΕΡΙ ΤΟΥΤΩΝ ΑΛΛΟ ΜΗΔΕΝ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΣ ΜΑΡΤΥΡΕΣ ΦΟΡΜΙΩΝ ΓΕΙΡΑΙΕΥΣ ΚΗΦΙΣΟΔΟΤΟΣ ΒΟΙΩΤΙΟΣ ΗΛΙΟΔΩΡΟΣ ΠΙΤΘΕΥΣ.] The witnesses to this contract are Phormion of Geiraeus, Cephisodotus of Boeotia, Heliodorus of Pitthis.

units.la: Sed in hac syngrapha nonnulla sunt obseruanda. Termille drachmas vsuris maritimis mutuas dederunt Androcles & Naucrates Artemoni atque Apollodoro Phaselitis. ΕΔΑΝΕΙΣΕΝ ΑΝΔΡΟΚΛΗΣ ΣΩΤΤΙΟΣ[?] ΚΑΙ ΝΑΥΚΡΑΤΗΣ ΚΑΡΥΣΤΙΟΣ ΑΡΤΕΜΩΝΙ ΚΑΙ ΑΠΟΛΛΟΔΩΡΩ, ΦΑΣΗΛΙΤΑΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΥ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΑΣ ΔΡΑΧΜΑΣ. Traiectitiæ huius pecuniæ drachmæ mille pariebant in dies (nam fenus nauticum diarium est, non menstruum.) singulos drachmas ducentas viginti quinque, vt quidem editur: ΕΡΙ ΔΙΑΚΟΣΙΑΙΣ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΠΕΝΤΕ ΤΑΣ ΧΙΛΙΑΣ.
units.tr: But several things must be noted in this contract. Androcles and Naucrates lent three thousand drachmas on maritime loans to Artemon and Apollodorus of Phaselis [ΕΔΑΝΕΙΣΕΝ ΑΝΔΡΟΚΛΗΣ ΣΩΤΤΙΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΝΑΥΚΡΑΤΗΣ ΚΑΡΥΣΤΙΟΣ ΑΡΤΕΜΩΝΙ ΚΑΙ ΑΠΟΛΛΟΔΩΡΩ, ΦΑΣΗΛΙΤΑΙΣ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΥ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΑΣ ΔΡΑΧΜΑΣ]. The drachmas of this sea-loan yielded, each day, (for maritime interest is reckoned by the day, not by the month) two hundred and twenty-five drachmas per thousand, as the text is printed [ΕΡΙ ΔΙΑΚΟΣΙΑΙΣ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΠΕΝΤΕ ΤΑΣ ΧΙΛΙΑΣ].

units.la: Sed mendum occupauit hunc locum: Nam triobolum singulis diebus dabatur in tetradrachmum. In mille drachmis sunt tetradrachma ducenta quinquaginta, quæ in singulos dies pariunt obolos septingentos quinquaginta, siue drachmas centum viginti quinque. Atque numerus hic, meo iudicio, legebatur in syngrapha, sed quia litera numerali ρ conceptus fuerat, facile mutauit litera hæc in sequentem σ, quæ eiusdem fere figuræ est cum præcedenti, sed in latum, non in longum porrectæ. Referibendum est itaque, me auctore, ΕΠΙ ΕΚΑΤΟΝ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΠΕΝΤΕ ΤΑΣ ΧΙΛΙΑΣ. Dabant igitur hæ termille drachmæ in singulos dies drachmas trecentas septuaginta quinque. Legitur tamen in eadem syngrapha verbis immediate sequentibus. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΕΤ' ΑΡΚΤΟΥΡΟΝ ΕΚΠΛΕΥΣΩΣΙΝ ΕΚ ΤΟΥ ΠΟΝΤΟΥ ΕΦ' ΙΕΡΟΝ ΕΠΙ ΤΡΙΑΚΟΣΙΑΙΣ ΤΑΣ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΑΣ. Merces è traiectitia pecunia comparatæ cum periculo creditoris nauigabant. Leg. I. D. de fenore nautico, vt etiam ex hac syngrapha constat. A die autem sexto Iduum Martiarum vsque in Idus Maias periculose maria tentantur, neque tamen propterea negotiatorum cessat industria. Contra vero à die sexto Kalendarum Iuniarum in diem decimum octauum Kalendarum Octobrium secura creditur nauigatio: id est, ab Arcturi occasu ad eiusdem ortum. Nam, ex Euctemonis sententia, ad diem octauum Kalendarum Iuniarum Ἀρκτοῦρος ἐὰς Νύ[?]κτα. Quare Androcles atque Naucrates, qui hanc vsuris maritimis mutuam pecuniam dederant, paululum de fenore remittunt, vigintiquinque nempe drachmas ex illis centum vigintiquinque, quas mille traiectitiæ drachmæ paricbant[?], ut hoc ivcello invitati Artemon Apollodorusque, non eo, quo incerta est & discrimini propior navigatio, tempore maria tentent; sed post Arcturi occasum, ΜΕΤ' ΑΡΚΤΟΥΡΟΝ, quando secure navigatur, ut ita possint nullo cum suo, nullo cum creditorum periculo Athenas redire: secura quippe tunc creditur navigatio. Atque ex his exponenda quoque sunt illa, quæ in eadem habentur syngrapha. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΕΙΣΒΑΛ-ΛΩΣΙ ΜΕΙΝΑΝΤΕΣ ΕΠΙ ΚΥΝΙ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ ΔΕΚΑ ΕΝ ΕΛΛΗΣ-ΠΟΝΤΩι ΕΞΕΛΟΜΕΝΟΙ, ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑ ΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΙΣ ΚΑΙ ΕΝΤΕΥΘΕΝ ΚΑΤΑΠΛΕΥΣΑΝΤΕΣ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΤΟΥΣ ΤΟΚΟΥΣ ΑΠΟΔΙΔΟΝΤΩΝ ΤΟΥΣ ΓΕΡΥΣΙ ΓΡΑΦΕΝ-ΤΑΣ ΕΙΣ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ. Varie scribitur huius periodi particula, ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑ ΩΣΙΝ. nam nonnulli codices habent, ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΛΑΛΩΣΙΝ. alij legunt: ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥ-ΛΑΙ ΩΣΙΝ. Ego vero existimo legendum esse unica voce: ΕΞΕΛΟΜΕΝΟΙ ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΥΣ. appulerint eo, vbi Athenienses non violent, sed potius sacrosancti sint, quod explicat ea quæ in præcedentibus dixerat: ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΕΤ' ΑΡΚΤΟΥΡΟΝ ΕΚΠΛΕΥΣΩ-ΣΙΝ ΕΚ ΤΟΥ ΠΟΝΤΟΥ ΕΠ' ΙΕΡΟΝ. Hic enim ΕΠ' ΙΕΡΟΝ idem est, quod, ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΥΣ, vbi Athenienses non violentur, sed sacro'ancti[?] sint. Dixit ΜΕΙΝΑΝΤΕΣ ΕΠΙ ΚΥ-ΝΙ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ ΔΕΚΑ ΕΝ ΕΛΛΗΣΠΟΝΤΩι. Si diebus decem post Canicula ortum ex Hellesponto non solverint. Ex observatione Metonis, cuius Enneadecaeteris cum hæc syngrapha scriberetur, Athenis usurpabatur, ad diem duodecimum Kalendas Augusti [illegible, ~9 letters] Canicula oritur. Demus ex Hellesponto solvisse Apollodorum die undetimo post ortum Canicula, id est, Kalendis Augusti, antequam Athenas redeat, cum alio primum appellat, ut merces suas distrahat, & nonnisi viginti, postquam Athenas redierit, diebus fortem cum usuris accipere debeant Androcles & Naucrates, profecto elabentur dies quadraginta quatuor minimum, qui intercedunt à Kalendis Augusti ad decimum octavum Kalendas Octobris, à quo die incerta navigatio est & discrimini propior, quia post Idus Septembris oritur Arcturus vehementissimum sidus. Ergo cum Androcli & Naucrati reddita non sit pecunia, nisi eo tempore, quo periculose maria tentantur, atque ita non possint pecuniam suam maritimis usuris mutuam iterum in continenti dare sive ingenti periculo, nolunt quicquam de fenore nautico remittere, quemadmodum remittebant, si ex Hellesponto post Arcturi occasum solvissent, sed stant iis, quæ syngrapha cav entur, nempe volunt sibi dari in mille drachmas diesque usuras maritimas, scilicet drachmas centum vigintiquinque: atque id ita explicant: ΤΟΥΣ ΤΟΚΟΥΣ ΑΠΟΔΙΔΟΝΤΩΝ ΤΟΥΣ ΓΕΡΥΣΙ ΓΡΑΦΕΝΤΑΣ ΕΙΣ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ. Si post Arcturi occasum solvissent ex Hellesponto, cum alio atque alio appellerent mercatus causa, antequam Athenas redirent, & præterea nonnisi viginti post reditum diebus teneantur suum expungere nomen: ΣΩΘΕΝΤΩΝ ΑΕ
units.tr: But an error has crept into this passage. For a triobol was given each day on a tetradrachm. In a thousand drachmas there are two hundred and fifty tetradrachms, which yield seven hundred and fifty obols, or one hundred and twenty-five drachmas, each day. In my judgement the number read in the contract was this, but since it had been written with the numeral letter ρ, this letter was easily changed into the following σ, which is nearly the same shape as the preceding one, but drawn broad rather than long. It must therefore, on my authority, be restored to read [ΕΠΙ ΕΚΑΤΟΝ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΠΕΝΤΕ ΤΑΣ ΧΙΛΙΑΣ], at one hundred and twenty-five per thousand. These three thousand drachmas, then, yielded three hundred and seventy-five drachmas each day. Yet the same contract reads, in the words immediately following: "If they sail from the Pontus after the rising of Arcturus, to Hieron, at three hundred per thousand" [ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΕΤ' ΑΡΚΤΟΥΡΟΝ ΕΚΠΛΕΥΣΩΣΙΝ ΕΚ ΤΟΥ ΠΟΝΤΟΥ ΕΦ' ΙΕΡΟΝ ΕΠΙ ΤΡΙΑΚΟΣΙΑΙΣ ΤΑΣ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΑΣ]. Goods bought with the money lent on bottomry were carried at the risk of the creditor, as the Law I of the Digest on maritime interest also shows from this contract. The sea is tried dangerously from the sixth day before the Ides of March until the Ides of May, yet the diligence of the traders does not on that account cease. On the other hand, from the sixth day before the Kalends of June until the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October, the voyage is considered safe; that is, from the setting of Arcturus to its rising again. For, according to Euctemon's opinion, Arcturus rises on the eighth day before the Kalends of June [Ἀρκτοῦρος ἐὰς Νύκτα]. Therefore Androcles and Naucrates, who had lent this money on maritime interest, remit a little of the interest, namely twenty-five drachmas out of the one hundred and twenty-five which the thousand drachmas of bottomry yielded, in order that Artemon and Apollodorus, invited by this inducement, should not sail at the time when the voyage is uncertain and closer to danger, but after the setting of Arcturus [ΜΕΤ' ΑΡΚΤΟΥΡΟΝ], when the voyage is safe, so that they could return to Athens with neither their own nor the creditors' risk; for the voyage is then considered safe. And from this must also be explained what is found in the same contract: "If they do not put in, remaining at the Hellespont for ten days after the rising of the Dog Star, having sailed out, where the Athenians will not molest them [ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΕΙΣΒΑΛΛΩΣΙ ΜΕΙΝΑΝΤΕΣ ΕΠΙ ΚΥΝΙ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ ΔΕΚΑ ΕΝ ΕΛΛΗΣΠΟΝΤΩ, ΕΞΕΛΟΜΕΝΟΙ, ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΙΣ], and from there sail back to Athens and pay the interest, as written in the contract." The particle of this period is variously written: ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑ ΩΣΙΝ. For some manuscripts have ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΛΑΛΩΣΙΝ, others read ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑΙ ΩΣΙΝ. But I think it should be read as a single word, ΕΞΕΛΟΜΕΝΟΙ ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΥΣ, having put in at a place where the Athenians may not molest them, but rather be sacrosanct; this explains what he had said above: "If after the rising of Arcturus they sail from the Pontus to Hieron" [ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΕΤ' ΑΡΚΤΟΥΡΟΝ ΕΚΠΛΕΥΣΩΣΙΝ ΕΚ ΤΟΥ ΠΟΝΤΟΥ ΕΠ' ΙΕΡΟΝ]. For here ΕΠ' ΙΕΡΟΝ means the same as ΟΠΟΥ ΑΝ ΜΗ ΣΥΛΑΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΥΣ, where the Athenians may not be harmed but be held sacrosanct. He said "remaining at the Hellespont for ten days after the Dog Star" [ΜΕΙΝΑΝΤΕΣ ΕΠΙ ΚΥΝΙ ΗΜΕΡΑΣ ΔΕΚΑ ΕΝ ΕΛΛΗΣΠΟΝΤΩι], that is, if they did not pay off from the Hellespont within ten days. From the observation of Meton, whose nineteen-year cycle was in use at Athens when this contract was written, the Dog Star rises on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August [illegible]. Let us suppose that Apollodorus set sail from the Hellespont on the eleventh day after the rising of the Dog Star, that is, on the Kalends of August, before returning to Athens, and first put in at another port to sell his wares; and that Androcles and Naucrates were to receive their capital with interest only twenty days after his return to Athens; then at least forty-four days would pass between the Kalends of August and the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October, from which day the voyage is uncertain and closer to danger, because after the Ides of September Arcturus rises, a very violent star. Therefore, since the money was returned to Androcles and Naucrates only at the time when the seas are dangerously tried, and so they could not lend their money again on maritime interest immediately without great danger, they are unwilling to remit anything of the nautical interest, as they would have remitted had the ships sailed from the Hellespont after the setting of Arcturus; instead they hold to what the contract provides, namely that they wish to be given, on each thousand drachmas, maritime interest of one hundred and twenty-five drachmas; and they explain this thus: "Let them pay the interest written in the contract." If, after the setting of Arcturus, they sailed from the Hellespont, calling at one place and another for trade before returning to Athens, and moreover were held to pay off their debt only twenty days after their return... [ΣΩΘΕΝΤΩΝ ΔΕ ΤΩΝ ΧΡΗΜΑΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΑΠΟΔΩΣΟΥΣΙΝ].

units.la: ΤΩΝ ΧΡΗΜΑΤΩΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ ΑΠΟΔΩΣΟΥΣΙΝ ΟΙ ΔΑΝΕΙΖΑΜΕΝΟΙ ΤΟΙΣ ΔΑΝΕΙΣΑΣΙ ΤΟ ΓΙΓΝΟΜΕΝΟΝ ΑΡΓΥΡΙΟΝ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΗΝ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΝ ΗΜΕΡΩΝ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΝ, ΑΦ' ΗΣ ΑΝ ΕΛΘΩΣΙΝ ΑΘΗΝΑΖΕ: Androcles atque Naucrates vix ante nouum initum annum fortem suam cum vsuris acciperent, nam citima Neomenia Hecatombaeonis cadit in diem quartum Kalendas Iulias, remotissima vero Neomenia Hecatombaeonis in Enneadecaeteride Metonis adscribitur dici sexto Kalendas Augusti: Possemus certius pronunciare, si nobis constaret de anno, quo scripta est syngrapha, sed tamen, vti diximus, si post Arcturum soluerunt ex Hellesponto, nonnisi anno sequenti ineunte debitum expunxerunt: vult autem Androcles cum Naucrate vsuras accipere, perinde ac si eo, quo scripta erat syngrapha, anno reddidissent, quod accidisset, si ante Arcturi occasum soluissent ex Hellesponto, nempe ΕΠΙ ΕΚΑΤΟΝ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΓΕΝΤΕ ΤΑΣ ΧΙΛΙΑΣ. Pignori autem acceperunt in navi merces, videlicet termille cados vini Mendaei e Thracia. ΕΠΙ ΟΙΝΟΥ ΚΕΡΑΜΙΟΙΣ ΜΕΝΔΑΙΟΙΣ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣ ΠΛΕΥΣΕΙΤΑΙ ΕΚ ΜΕΝΔΗΣ Η ΣΚΙΩΝΗΣ ΕΝ ΤΗι ΕΙΚΟΣΟΡΩι ΜΗ ΥΒΑΗΣΙΟΣ ΝΑΥΚΑΗΡΕΙ. Huius meminit Stephanus: Μένδη, πόλις Θράκης, ἀπὸ Μένδης γυναικός· Ἀπολλόδωρος Μένδη αὐτῷ φησι. ὁ ἐθνικὸν, Μενδαῖος οἶνος. Habes item apud Hippocratem ἐν τῷ περὶ τῶν ἐντὸς παθῶν, vbi agit ἐπὶ τῆς τετάρτης νούσου νεφρῶν. καὶ οἶνον πίνειν λευκὸν Μενδαῖον μὴ χρῆσθαι. & paullo post. ἐπὶ τῆς τετάρτης νούσου νεφρῶν scribens, οἶνον πίνειν Μενδαῖον, λευκόν, εὐωδη[?].
units.tr: The debtors shall pay the money to the lenders within twenty days of arriving at Athens, the amount that becomes due under the contract. Androcles and Naucrates could scarcely receive their principal with interest before the new year began. For the nearest new moon of Hekatombaion falls on the fourth day before the Kalends of July, and the most distant new moon of Hekatombaion, in Meton's nineteen-year cycle, is assigned to the sixth day before the Kalends of August. We could state this more precisely if we knew the year in which the contract was written. But, as we said, if they sailed from the Hellespont after Arcturus, they paid off the debt only in the following year, early on. Androcles, however, wants to receive interest together with Naucrates as if they had paid in the year the contract was written. That would have happened if they had set sail from the Hellespont before Arcturus set, namely at 125 for the thousand [ΕΠΙ ΕΚΑΤΟΝ ΕΙΚΟΣΙΓΕΝΤΕ ΤΑΣ ΧΙΛΙΑΣ]. They took as a pledge the goods on the ship, namely three thousand jars of Mendaean wine from Thrace [ΕΠΙ ΟΙΝΟΥ ΚΕΡΑΜΙΟΙΣ ΜΕΝΔΑΙΟΙΣ ΤΡΙΣΧΙΛΙΟΙΣ, ΟΣ ΠΛΕΥΣΕΙΤΑΙ ΕΚ ΜΕΝΔΗΣ Η ΣΚΙΩΝΗΣ ΕΝ ΤΗι ΕΙΚΟΣΟΡΩι ΜΗ ΥΒΑΗΣΙΟΣ ΝΑΥΚΑΗΡΕΙ]. Stephanus mentions this: Mende, a city of Thrace, named after the woman Mende; Apollodorus says Mende for it, and the ethnic is Mendaean wine [Μένδη, πόλις Θράκης, ἀπὸ Μένδης γυναικός· Ἀπολλόδωρος Μένδη αὐτῷ φησι. ὁ ἐθνικὸν, Μενδαῖος οἶνος]. You also have it in Hippocrates, in the work on internal affairs, where he treats of the fourth disease of the kidneys, and says that white Mendaean wine should not be drunk [καὶ οἶνον πίνειν λευκὸν Μενδαῖον μὴ χρῆσθαι]. And a little later, writing on the fourth disease of the kidneys, he says to drink Mendaean wine, white, fragrant [οἶνον πίνειν Μενδαῖον, λευκόν, εὐωδη].

units.la: Non multum abeunt in diuersum Romani, vt constat exemplo syngraphae, quam è Scaeuolae Lib. XXVIII. Digestorum in Pandectas retulit Tribonianus Leg. CXXII. §. I. D. de verborum obligationibus. Scaeuolae verba sunt. Callimachus mutuam pecuniam nauticam accepit a Stichoferuo Seij in prouincia Syria, ciuitate Beruto vsque Brentesium, idque creditum esse in omnes nauigij dies ducentos sub pignoribus & hypothecu mercibus a Beruto comparatis, & Brentesium perferendis, & quas Brentesio emptura esset, & per nauem Beruto inuecturus; conuenisseque inter eos, vti CVM CALLIMACHVS BRENTESIVM PERVENISSET, INDE INTRA IDVS SEPTEMBRES, QVÆ TVNC PROXIMÆ FVTVRÆ ESSENT, ALIIS MERCIBVS EMPTIS, ET IN NAVEM MISSIS, IPSE IN SVRIAM PER NAVIGIVM PROFICISCATVR: AVT SI INTRA DIEM SVPRASCRIPTAM NON REPARASSET MERCES, NEC NAVIGASSET DE EA CIVITATE REDDERET VNIVERSAM CONTINVO PECVNIAM QVASI PERFECTO NAVIGIO, ET PRÆSTARET SVMPTVS OMNES PROSESQVENTIBVS EAM PECVNIAM, VT IN VRBEM ROMAM EAM DEPORTARENT, EAQVE SIC RECTE DARI FIERI FIDE ROGANTI STICHO SERVO LVCII TITII PROMISIT CALLIMACHVS, & cum ante Idus suprascriptas secundum conuentionem mercibus in nauem impositis, cum Herote conseruo Stichi, quasi in prouinciam Suriam peruenturus enauigauit: quaesitum est naue submersa, cum secundum cautionem Callimachus merces [debito] perferendas in nauem misisset eo tempore, quo iam pecuniam Brentesio reddere Romae perferendam deberet, &c.
units.tr: The Romans do not differ much from this, as the example of the contract shows, which Tribonian took from Scaevola, Book 28 of the Digest, into the Pandects (Law 122, §1, D. de verborum obligationibus). Scaevola's words are these: Callimachus received a maritime loan from Stichus, slave of Lucius Titius, in the province of Syria, in the city of Berytus, to Brentesium; and this was lent for all the days of the voyage, two hundred days, under pledges and a mortgage on the goods bought at Berytus and to be carried to Brentesium, and on those he was going to buy there, and which he would bring by ship to Berytus. And they agreed that when Callimachus reached Brentesium, then within the Ides of September, which would then be the nearest, after buying other goods and putting them on board ship, he himself would set out by sea for Syria. But if he did not repay the goods within the aforesaid day, nor sail from that city, he would at once return the whole money, as if the voyage had been completed, and would bear all the expenses of those carrying that money so that they might bring it to the city of Rome; and Callimachus promised that the money would be properly given and paid, on the faith of the request of Stichus, slave of Lucius Titius. And when, before the aforesaid Ides, according to the agreement, he had put the goods on board ship, he sailed with Herotes, fellow slave of Stichus, as if about to arrive in the province of Syria. The question is: the ship having sunk, since Callimachus had put the goods to be carried on board ship according to the agreement at the time when he ought already to have paid the money at Brentesium, to be carried to Rome, etc.

units.la: Sed quaedam hic sunt obseruanda, in quibus nobis non bene conuenit cum viris magnis: Existimant creditorem, quem initio nominauit Seium, postea vocari Titium: quod nobis non potest probari: quanquam enim Iurisconsulti promiscue his nominibus [Caius Seius, Lucius Titius] vtuntur: [illegible, ~12 letters] Plutarchus, [illegible, ~14 letters] οἱ Νομικοὶ Καίσαρ[?]ος Σηΐου, καὶ Λουκίου Τιτίου [illegible, ~10 letters], non tamen in eodem exemplo qui modo fuit C. Seius, dicitur L. Titius. Quare & LVCII TITII in syngrapha refero ad Callimachum, non autem ad Stichum: ὁ Λουκίου Τιτίου Καλλίμαχος.
units.tr: But certain things here must be observed, on which we do not agree well with great men. They think that the creditor, whom at first he named Seius, is afterwards called Titius. This we cannot prove. For although the jurists use these names interchangeably [Caius Seius, Lucius Titius], [illegible], Plutarch [illegible], the jurists speak of Caius Seius and Lucius Titius [illegible], yet in the same example the one who was Caius Seius is not called Lucius Titius. Therefore I refer LVCII TITII in the contract to Callimachus, not to Stichus: Callimachus of Lucius Titius.

units.la: Venit Brundusium Callimachus, ante Idus Septembris secundum conuentionem Brundusio soluit: quod postea negare videtur Scaeuola: nam scribit, eum soluisse eo tempore, quo iam pecuniam Brundusio reddere Romam perferendam deberet, quod est post Idus Septembris. Sed emendat vir summus, in nauem misisset, sed eo tempore, quo iam pecuniam, &c. vt est in quibusdam libris hoc sensu: Soluisse quidem nauem Callimachum ante Idus, sed eo tempore, quo iam pecuniam Eroti reddere deberet, id est, cum non longe abessent Idus, certumque esset iam intra Idus Berytum appellere eam non posse. Cum autem iam venissent Idus, necdum peregisset institutam nauigationem, post Idus naufragium fecit. Sed nihil est addendum, meo iudicio, nihil mutandum, in his quidem, sola quippe interpunctione adiuuandus est locus & exponendus. Ante Idus igitur Septembris merces in nauem imponit, tanquam in Suriam enauigat; neque recta Berytum versus nauigat, sed alio deflectit: inter haec naufragium facit postridie Idus Septembris: colligo ex his, sed ita distinguendis & interpungendis: Quaesitum est naue submersa (cum secundum cautionem Callimachus merces [debito] perferendas in nauem misisset.) eo tempore, quo iam pecuniam Brentesio reddere Romae perferendam deberet. Postridie Eidus Septembreis esse diximus, quia nisi intra Idus Septembreis, (id est, ipsis Idibus, quemadmodum intra Kalendas etiam ipsae Kalendae sunt Leg. 1. §. IX. D. de successorio edicto.) non reparasset merces, nec nauigasset de ea ciuitate, reddere debebat vniuersam continuo pecuniam: quae peti non poterat nisi postridie Idus Septembris, nam quod in diem debetur, ante soluti potest, peti non potest Leg. CXXXVII. §. II. de verbor. obligat. Atque ex his discimus non necesse fuisse, vt intra Idus Septembreis Berytum peruenirent, sed vt Brundusio soluerct: & omnes nauigij dies ducenti esse poterant: nam creditum est Callimacho in omnes nauigij dies ducentos a ciuitate Beruto vsque Brentesium, rursumque Brentesio Berytum. Neque puto initum fuisse horum ducentorum dierum numerum ante sextum Eiduum Martiarum, quo maria aperiuntur: itaque desinunt hi ducenti dies sexto Kalendas Octobreis: Non videbatur autem Callimachus Brundusio soluisse, quia enauigauerat, quod iam est expendendum: puto rescribendum: Cum ante Idus suprascriptas secundum conuentionem mercibus in nauem impositis, cum Herote conseruo Stichi, quasi in prouinciam Suriam, per Venetorum enauigauit. Non ille in Suriam nauigauit, sed ad Venetorum littora, cumque in ea esset ora, naufragium fecit postridie Idus Septembris, eo ipso tempore, quo Heroti pecuniam Brentesio reddere Romae perferendam debebat: Atqui non poterat censeri Brentesio soluisse, cùm enim esset in Venetorum ora: omnino necesse habuit Brentesium redire: facile autem mutauit per Venetorum in peruenturus.
units.tr: Callimachus came to Brundusium before the Ides of September and paid at Brundusium according to the agreement. Scaevola seems to deny this afterwards, for he writes that he paid at the time when he ought already to have carried the money from Brundusium to Rome, which is after the Ides of September. But the great man emends it: "put on board ship, but at the time when he was already to pay the money", etc., as is found in some books, with this meaning: Callimachus did indeed set sail before the Ides, but at the time when he ought already to pay the money to Herotes, that is, when the Ides were not far off, and it was certain that he could not reach Berytus within the Ides. When the Ides had actually arrived, and he had not yet finished the voyage he had begun, he was wrecked after the Ides. But nothing needs to be added, in my judgement, nothing changed here; the passage needs only punctuation to be helped and explained. Before the Ides of September, then, he puts the goods on board ship as if he were sailing for Syria; but he does not sail straight for Berytus, he turns aside elsewhere. Meanwhile he suffers shipwreck the day after the Ides of September. I infer this from these words, but they must be divided and punctuated thus: "The question is: the ship having sunk (since Callimachus had put the goods to be carried on board ship according to the agreement), at the time when he ought already to have carried the money to Brentesium to be carried to Rome." We have said that it was the day after the Ides of September, because unless within the Ides of September (that is, on the Ides themselves, just as "within the Kalends" includes the Kalends themselves, Law 1, §9, D. de successorio edicto) he had not repaid the goods nor sailed from that city, he ought to repay the whole money at once. That could not be demanded until the day after the Ides of September, for "what is owed on a day, before it is due, cannot be demanded" (Law 137, §2, de verborum obligationibus). From this we learn that it was not necessary for them to reach Berytus within the Ides of September, but to pay at Brundusium; and all the days of the voyage could be two hundred. For the loan to Callimachus was made for all the days of the voyage of two hundred, from the city of Berytus to Brentesium, and again from Brentesium to Berytus. Nor do I think the count of these two hundred days began before the sixth day before the Ides of March, when the seas are opened; so these two hundred days end on the sixth day before the Kalends of October. Callimachus did not seem to have paid at Brundusium, because he had sailed on, which must now be considered. I think it should be rewritten: "When before the aforesaid Ides, according to the agreement, he had put the goods on board ship with Herotes, fellow slave of Stichus, as if about to sail for the province of Syria, he sailed by way of the Venetian coast." He did not sail to Syria, but to the shores of the Veneti, and while he was on that coast he suffered shipwreck the day after the Ides of September, at the very time when he ought to have carried the money to Herotes at Brentesium to be carried to Rome. But it could not be counted as having paid at Brentesium, since he was on the Venetian coast; he was certainly bound to return to Brentesium. The change of "per Venetorum" into "peruenturus" is easy.

units.la: Sed nos reuocant Athenienses toculliones, qui referebant in sua diaria siue aduersaria & codices ea, quae faciebant nomina. Demosthenes ἐν τῷ κατὰ Τιμοθέου λόγῳ χρέως. οἱ γὰρ τραπεζῖται εἰώθασιν ὑπομνήματα γράφειν ὧν τε δίδασι χρημάτων, ἃ εἰς ὅ, τὶ, ἡ ὧν αὐτῆς τῆς τιθέσης, ἵν' ἡ αὐτοῖς γνώσιμα, τὰ τε ληφθέντα, καὶ τὰ τιθέντα καθ' ἕκαστα[?]. Atque horum ὑπομνημάτων in iudiciis frequens vsus, ad faciendam debiti fidem. Demosthenes ibidem: ὡσαύτως καλεσαμένου ἢ τοῦτον τὸν ἀνδρὸς τὴν διαθήκην, ἡ καὶ λόγον ἐκέλευσε[?] τὰ χρήματα ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης, ἡ αὐτὴ γὰρ ἀπωσάμενος, πέμψαντος Φορμίωνος[?] τὸν πρὸς αὐτὸν τραπεζίτην...[?] & infra. ἀνεῖς τοίνυν τὸν ἀμφισβητοῦντα ἀποκρίσεως μὴ τὰ χρέματα. Agri autem & possessiones omnes, vt & domicilia, quae aere alieno essent obstricta & oppignerata Danistis, ὅρους signari solebant à creditoribus. Qui ὅροι erant, vt plurimum, lapis, aut columna quaedam, indicans locum, in quo sita erat, signatum & creditori oppigneratum esse: ita Lib. III. cap. IX. Pollux. ὅροις ἐφεστὰναι χωρίων. λίθος δ' ὢν, ἢ στήλη ἢς δηλοῦσα, ὡς ἔστιν ὑπάρχοντος χωρίου. ὅτι ὁ τοῦτον ἔλεγεν ἡ ὃ ὅρος ὅμου ὅ χωρίον, ὡς ὁ σαιτίον ἀσκητὴν. Harpocration & Suidas docent ὅρους tabellas esse, quae affixae designabant aedes, aut praedia, aut alias possessiones hypothecae subiectas. ἀσκητὴν χωρίον, ὃ μὴ ὑποκείμενον δανείῳ· ὅταν γὰρ ὑποκέηται, εἰώθειν ὁ δανείσας αὐτὸ, τὴν δηλώσιν δὴ χρημάτων ἐπιτιμῶν ὡς χωρίον. Ὅ δ' αὐτὸ ἡ ἐπ' εἰκίας γῆς. Λυσίας δὲ ὡς τοῦ Αἰσχίνου τ' Σωκρατικῶν. & rursum in ὅρος. ὅρος, ὅτως σκάλλων οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι τὰ ἐπὶ τοῦ τῆς ὑποκειμένης οἰκίας ἢ χωρίοις χρήματα δηλῶσαι ὅτι ὑποκείμενα δανείῳ. Δημοσθένης δὲ ὡς Σπουδίας, καὶ Μένανδρος Παρασίτῳ.
