units.tr: "If anyone gives a foreign woman in marriage to an Athenian citizen as though she were his relative, let him be ignominious, and let his goods be confiscated. Let a third of the penalty go to the one who brings the charge, and let it be lodged before the Thesmothetae, to whom it belongs, just as with the cases of foreign status." [ΕΣΤΩ ΚΑΙ ΤΟΥ ΕΛΟΝΤΟΣ ΤΟ ΤΡΙΤΟΝ ΜΕΡΟΣ, ΓΡΑΦΕΣΤΩ ΔΕ ΠΡΟΣ ΤΟΥΣ ΘΕΣΜΟΘΕΤΑΣ, ΟΙΣ ΕΞΕΣΤΙ ΚΑΘΑΠΕΡ ΤΗΣ ΞΕΝΙΑΣ]

units.la: triens accusatori cedito: Accusanto, queis fas est, apud Thesmothetas, quemadmodum peregrinitatis.
units.tr: "A third is to go to the accuser. Let those who are entitled bring the charge before the Thesmothetae, just as in cases of foreign status."

units.la: Descripsit hanc Demosthenes Legem ἐν τῷ Νεαίρας. γεγράφηται ὁ Φερέφαν Σπέφανος ἐν τῷ γράφῳ, πρὸς τοὺς Θεσμοθέτας, Αθηναῖον ὅντα ξένης γυναῖκα ἀπὸ εἰσαγωγῆς ὡς αὐτῷ προσηκούσῃ, καὶ τὸν νόμον ἐν τῷ νόμῳ. καὶ μοι διάγνωσθι αὐτὸν νόμων.
units.tr: Demosthenes gives this law in his speech against Neaera. [In Greek, as garbled in the scan:] "Stephanus wrote the indictment before the Thesmothetae, charging that the woman, being a foreigner, had been introduced as an Athenian's kinswoman, and let the law be read to you." [γεγράφηται ὁ Φερέφαν Σπέφανος ἐν τῷ γράφῳ, πρὸς τοὺς Θεσμοθέτας, Αθηναῖον ὅντα ξένης γυναῖκα ἀπὸ εἰσαγωγῆς ὡς αὐτῷ προσηκούσῃ, καὶ τὸν νόμον ἐν τῷ νόμῳ. καὶ μοι διάγνωσθι αὐτὸν νόμων.]

units.la: NOMOS EAN DE TIS EKDIDO ΞΕΝΗΝ ΓΥΝΑΙΚΑ ΑΝΔΡΙ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩι, &c.
units.tr: Law: "If anyone gives a foreign woman in marriage to an Athenian man," etc.

units.la: Si quis, inquit, pro sua, aut sibi cognatione proxima peregrinam, vel è peregrina susceptam, elocarit: non elocabantur quippe susceptae filiae, nisi ἐκ τῶν νομίμων γάμων. Demosthenes hac ipsa Oratione. ἀλλ᾿ ἡ γυναῖκα αὐτῆς ἐν Αθηναίῳ ἐκδοθεῖσα, ἀξιοφανὴς αὐτῷ ἀποφαίνει γυναῖκα ἐχρῆτο. Poena sequitur. ATIMOS ESTO KAI H OUSIA AYTOY, ΔΗΜΟΣΙΑ ΕΣΤΩ. ignominiosus erat, & bona eius publicabantur, quod dixit Orator ἐξαίτειν δημίῳ in sequentibus. γοῦς ὃ ὅτι κινδυνεύοι ἐξελεγχθεὶς ξένης γυναῖκα εἰσαγαγεῖν, τὰ τῆς ἐξαιτήσεως δημίας ἀποτιμῆσαι. Sed triens bonorum accusatori cedebat. KAI TOY ELONTOS TO TRITON MEROS. Quemadmodum autem ξενίας δίκη, ita & haec apud Thesmothetas scribebatur. Seuerius quoque animaduertebantur peregrini, qui ciuem ducerent, aut ciui nuberent: in eos quippe haec scripta Lex est.
units.tr: "If anyone, he says, gives in marriage, as his own or as a near relative, a foreign woman, or one born of a foreign woman, (for adopted daughters were not given in marriage unless by lawful marriages)." Demosthenes, in the same speech: "But whoever gives in marriage to an Athenian a woman who is not his own, and then presents her as his wife..." [ἐκ τῶν νομίμων γάμων; ἀλλ᾿ ἡ γυναῖκα αὐτῆς ἐν Αθηναίῳ ἐκδοθεῖσα, ἀξιοφανὴς αὐτῷ ἀποφαίνει γυναῖκα ἐχρῆτο.] The penalty follows: "Let him be atimos, and let his property be public," so that he was ignominious and his goods were confiscated, as the orator says in what follows, that he should be handed over to the executioner: "since, if he were convicted of having introduced a foreign woman, the proceeds of the sale were to be paid to the public executioner." [ἐξαίτειν δημίῳ; γοῦς ὃ ὅτι κινδυνεύοι ἐξελεγχθεὶς ξένης γυναῖκα εἰσαγαγεῖν, τὰ τῆς ἐξαιτήσεως δημίας ἀποτιμῆσαι.] But a third of the goods went to the accuser. [καὶ τοῦ ἐλόντος τὸ τρίτον μέρος.] Just as there was a suit for foreign status (ξενίας δίκη), so this one was also brought before the Thesmothetae. Foreigners who took a citizen as a spouse, or who married a citizen, were punished more severely, since this law was written against them.

units.la: ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΞΕΝΟΣ ΑΣΤΗι ΣΥΝΟΙΚΗι ΤΕΧΝΗι, Η ΜΗΧΑΝΗι, ΗΙΤΙΝΙΟΥΝ ΓΡΑΦΕΣΘΩ ΠΡΟΣ ΤΟΥΣ ΘΕΣΜΟΘΕΤΑΣ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ, Ο ΒΟΥΛΟΜΕΝΟΣ ΟΙΣ ΕΞΕΣΤΙΝ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΑΛΛΩι ΓΡΑΦΕΣΘΩ ΚΑΙ ΑΥΤΟΣ ΚΑΙ Η ΟΥΣΙΑ ΑΥΤΟΥ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟ ΤΡΙΤΟΝ ΜΕΡΟΣ ΕΣΤΩ ΤΟΥ ΕΛΟΝΤΟΣ. ΩΣΑΥΤΩΣ ΔΕ ΚΑΙ ΕΑΝ Η ΞΕΝΗ ΤΩι ΑΣΤΩι ΣΥΝΟΙΚΗι ΚΑΤΑ ΤΑΥΤΑ ΚΑΙ Ο ΣΥΝΟΙΚΩΝ ΤΗι ΞΕΝΗι ΑΚΟΥΣΗι, ΟΦΕΙΛΕΤΩ ΧΙΛΙΑΣ ΔΡΑΧΜΑΣ.
units.tr: "If a foreigner lives together with an Athenian woman in cohabitation, by any art or device, let the accuser, whoever wishes and is entitled, lodge a charge before the Thesmothetae of the Athenians. If he is convicted on another charge, let him and his property be forfeit, and let a third of the penalty go to the accuser. Likewise, if a foreign woman cohabits with an Athenian man in these ways, and the man who lives with the foreign woman is convicted, let him pay a thousand drachmas." [ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΞΕΝΟΣ ΑΣΤΗι ΣΥΝΟΙΚΗι ΤΕΧΝΗι, Η ΜΗΧΑΝΗι, ΗΙΤΙΝΙΟΥΝ ΓΡΑΦΕΣΘΩ ΠΡΟΣ ΤΟΥΣ ΘΕΣΜΟΘΕΤΑΣ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΩΝ, Ο ΒΟΥΛΟΜΕΝΟΣ ΟΙΣ ΕΞΕΣΤΙΝ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΑΛΛΩι ΓΡΑΦΕΣΘΩ ΚΑΙ ΑΥΤΟΣ ΚΑΙ Η ΟΥΣΙΑ ΑΥΤΟΥ, ΚΑΙ ΤΟ ΤΡΙΤΟΝ ΜΕΡΟΣ ΕΣΤΩ ΤΟΥ ΕΛΟΝΤΟΣ. ΩΣΑΥΤΩΣ ΔΕ ΚΑΙ ΕΑΝ Η ΞΕΝΗ ΤΩι ΑΣΤΩι ΣΥΝΟΙΚΗι ΚΑΤΑ ΤΑΥΤΑ ΚΑΙ Ο ΣΥΝΟΙΚΩΝ ΤΗι ΞΕΝΗι ΑΚΟΥΣΗι, ΟΦΕΙΛΕΤΩ ΧΙΛΙΑΣ ΔΡΑΧΜΑΣ.]

units.la: Si quis peregrinus ciuem ducat, quocumque modo aut arte, accusato Atheniensium ciuicumque libuerit & licuerit apud Thesmothetas: si conuictus fuerit, ipse venditor, & bona eius, eorum triens accusatori cedito. Siremps [?] Lex dicta esto peregrinae, quae ciui nupserit: & si quis posthac rem habeas cum ea, quae peregrinitatis damnata est, mille drachmis multator.
units.tr: "If a foreigner takes an Athenian woman to live with him, by whatever means or art, let any Athenian citizen who wishes, and is permitted, bring the charge before the Thesmothetae. If he is convicted, he himself is to be sold, and his goods, with a third to the accuser. Let this be the law concerning a foreign woman who marries a citizen; and if anyone henceforth has relations with a woman condemned for foreign status, let him be fined a thousand drachmas."

units.la: Legem recitat Demosthenes ἐν τῷ χῷ Νεαίρας. ἐπειδὴ οὖν τὸν νόμον ὑμῶν διαγνώσεσθε, καὶ ὅτι τῷ γράφῳ ἔγραψατο Θεσμοῦντος ἐγράψατο, ἢ ὁ ἀγὼν ὅσα εἰσέρχεται εἰς ὑμᾶς. NOMOS. EAN DE XENOS ASTHI SYNOIKHI, &c. τῶν μὲν νόμων ἀκηκοᾶτε, ὦ ἄνδρες δικασταί, ὃς οὐκ ἐᾷ τῷ ξένῳ τὰ ἀγῶ οἰκοίκιαν, οὐδὲ τῷ ἀστῷ τὰ ξένῳ, οὐδὲ παιδοποιήσασθαι τέχνη, οὐδὲ μηχανὴ οὐδεμιᾷ. ἐὰν δὲ τὶς τῶν ἀστῶν ποιῇ, γράφῳ πεποίηκε κατ᾽ αὐτὸ ἐὶ) πρὸς τοὺς θεσμοθέτας, κατὰ τὴν ξένου καὶ τῆς ξένης. καὶ ἄλλῳ, πεφεύγεσθαι κελεύει. Tria sunt autem huius Legis Kapita, primo cauetur de peregrino, qui ciuem duxerit, quocumque tandem id sit factum modo: ei dica scribebatur apud Thesmothetas: conuictus vendebatur, atque eius fortunæ publicabantur: idem altero Kapite fancitum est in peregrinam, quæ ciui nupserit, vt etiam alibi legitur: νόμος κελεύει, ἐὰν ᾖ ἀστὸς τῇ Ἀθηναίῳ ξένη συνοικῇ, πεφεύγεσθαι ταῦτα. At si quis cum ea, quae peregrinitatis damnata est, rem habuerit, extremo huius Legis Kapite, mille drachmis multabatur: tam auerso scilicet à peregrinarum nuptiis erant animo. Quare etiam Lege vetitum erat, ne qua ciuis peregre nuberet.
units.tr: Demosthenes recites this law in the speech against Neaera: "Since, then, you will hear the law, and the indictment which was drawn up before the Thesmothetae, ..." [ἐν τῷ χῷ Νεαίρας. ἐπειδὴ οὖν τὸν νόμον ὑμῶν διαγνώσεσθε...] "You have heard the laws, gentlemen jurors, which do not permit a foreigner to live with a citizen woman, nor a citizen to live with a foreign woman, nor to make children by any art or device. If any citizen does so, the indictment is to be brought against him before the Thesmothetae, under the foreigner's name and that of the foreign woman; and the law orders that the other be sold." [τῶν μὲν νόμων ἀκηκοᾶτε, ὦ ἄνδρες δικασταί... πεφεύγεσθαι κελεύει.] There are three chapters in this law. First, it provides against a foreigner who lives with a citizen woman, by whatever means this is done: an indictment was written against him before the Thesmothetae; if convicted, he was sold, and his property was confiscated. The second chapter enacts the same against a foreign woman who marries a citizen, as is also read elsewhere: "The law orders that, if a citizen lives with an Athenian foreign woman, these things be prosecuted." [νόμος κελεύει, ἐὰν ᾖ ἀστὸς τῇ Ἀθηναίῳ ξένη συνοικῇ, πεφεύγεσθαι ταῦτα.] But if anyone had relations with a woman condemned for foreign status, by the last chapter of this law he was fined a thousand drachmas. So strongly were they set against marriages with foreign women. For this reason the law also forbade any citizen woman to marry abroad.

units.la: Ἐπὶ ξένης μὴ ἐκδιδόσθαι ἀ̓ξίῳ ἔσται.[?]
units.tr: "It will not be fitting to give [a woman] in marriage to a foreigner." [Ἐπὶ ξένης μὴ ἐκδιδόσθαι ἀξίῳ ἔσται.]

units.la: Laudat Vlpianus in Timocrateam, cuius verba paullo post reddemus. Negat hæc Lex licere ciui Athenienfi ἐπὶ ξένης peregre nubere: atque hinc est grauis illa Demosthenis expostulatio aduersus Timocratem. ἀλλὰ νὴ Δία τὰ ἀδελφῷ κακῶς διάχειν. ἀλλὰ εἰ γὰρ μηδὲν ἄλλο ἐδίκει, ἐξ τοῦ ἀξιῶς ἔδει ἀπολωλέναι.[?] πόσα ἐχρῶ ἐκ τοῦ ἡμετέρου ἐχρῶντο ἐπὶ Κερκυραίοις[?] ἀλλ' αὐτοὶ ἐδίκει. ἡ Κερκυρᾶς Κερκυραῖ. ὅς οὖν ἡ μὲν ἀδελφῷ ἐπ' ἐξαγωγῇ φησὶ μὲν ἐκδιδόναι, πάντα ἐκ τῆς ἐργῷ. Vlpianus ad hæc verba: ὡσαύτως ἀπελαύσαντος, ὅτι δὲ ξένης ἐκδίδοται ἀπὸ ὅσα, τῷ νόμου τῷ ἀπίρρητος. Itaque Ariltogitonis neptem viro maturam Athenienfis populus è Lemno insula euocauit, ne peregre nuberet. Refert Plutarchus in Aristide extremo. ἔχει οὖν ὅτι ζωμαςῶν ὅτω φερνίσαι τὴν ἐκ ἀρχὴν ὃν δῆμον, ὅπου ζυγατείδου Αεισογίπους ἐν Λήμνῳ πυθομένου[?] ἐπὶ ὁ Αἰχμάτ ἄλλος ἀλλά, ἀπὸ ἱστορεῖ ἀλλὰ σύμφωνος ἐκ ἀξιῶν Αἰσωπός[?] ἢ ὅτι ἀλλήλοις, ὁ Πομπεῖος χωρίον εἰς Φέρνειλ ἐπιδώκεν.
units.tr: Ulpian cites this in his commentary on Timocrates, and I will give his words shortly. He says this law did not allow an Athenian citizen to marry abroad [ἐπὶ ξένης], and hence comes Demosthenes' severe complaint against Timocrates: "But, by Zeus, he treated his brother badly! For if he had done nothing else wrong, it would have been enough to be ruined by this... How many things the Athenians did..., and he himself acted..." [ἀλλὰ νὴ Δία τὰ ἀδελφῷ κακῶς διάχειν...]. Ulpian on these words: the same benefit, but that she is given to a foreigner in marriage is forbidden by law. Thus the Athenian people recalled from the island of Lemnos the great-niece of Aristogiton, to be married to a man of her own city, so that she would not marry abroad. Plutarch reports this in the closing part of his Life of Aristides. [ἔχει οὖν ὅτι ...] Pompey granted land to ... (the text here is too garbled to be rendered with certainty).

units.la: Nuptiæ autem non tantum inter ciues constitutæ sunt, sed etiam licuit Solonis Lege eodem patre natas vxores ducere.
units.tr: Marriages were not only contracted between citizens; by Solon's law it was also permitted to marry wives born of the same father.

units.la: Ἐξεστι γαμεῖν τὰς ἐκ πατέρων ἀδελφάς.
units.tr: "It is permitted to marry sisters from the same father." [Ἐξεστι γαμεῖν τὰς ἐκ πατέρων ἀδελφάς.]

units.la: Laudant hanc Legem Græci Latinique scriptores. Cornelius Nepos in proœmio: Neque enim Cimoni fuit turpe, Athenienfium summo viro, sororem germanam habere in matrimonio, quippe cum ciues eius eodem vterentur instituto. & in Cimone. Habebat autem in matrimonio sororem germanam suam, nomine Elpinicen, non magis amore, quam more, ductus. Nam Athenienfibus licet eodem patre natas vxores ducere. Minutius Felix in Octauio. Athenis cum sororibus legitima coniugia Philo Iudæus ἀπαγορεύων ἐν εἰδὴ νόμῳ. ὁ μὲν οὖν Ἀθηναῖος Σόλων ὁμοπατρίους ἐφιέις ἀγαγεῖν, ὡς ὁμομητρίους ἐκώλυσεν. Licebat sororem eodem patre natam, non autem eadem matre, in matrimonio habere. Vnde Aristophanes Nebulis ad excitandum maius odium aduersus Euripidem, in cuius Æolo ἐκ ἀδελφὰς γαμοῦσι ἀδελφοί, addit de suo ἐκ ὁμομητείας.
units.tr: Greek and Latin writers both cite this law. Cornelius Nepos, in his preface: "For it was not disgraceful for Cimon, the greatest man among the Athenians, to have his full sister as his wife, since his fellow citizens followed the same custom." And in the Life of Cimon: "He had as his wife his full sister, named Elpinice, led not so much by love as by custom, for it is permitted to the Athenians to marry women born of the same father." Minucius Felix in the Octavius: "At Athens there are lawful marriages with sisters." Philo the Jew, forbidding this in the Special Laws: "Solon the Athenian allowed marriage with sisters from the same father, but forbade it with sisters from the same mother." It was permitted to have a sister of the same father, but not of the same mother as a wife. Hence Aristophanes, in the Clouds, to stir up greater hatred against Euripides, in whose Aeolus brothers marry sisters, adds on his own that they were from the same mother.

units.la: ὁ δ' ἀλλὰ ὅ ὅσ ἐξ ΕΥριπίδου ῥῆσιν τὴν ὡς ἐκ ἀδελφὸς, ὦ Ἀλξίκακε, τ' ὁμομητείας ἀδελφῷ.
units.tr: [Aristophanes' verse, as garbled in the scan:] "...the speech of Euripides in which brothers marry sisters, O Alexikakos, from the same mother." [ὁ δ' ἀλλὰ ὅ ὅσ ἐξ ΕΥριπίδου ῥῆσιν τὴν ὡς ἐκ ἀδελφὸς, ὦ Ἀλξίκακε, τ' ὁμομητείας ἀδελφῷ.]

units.la: Scholia: γίγαντ' ᾿Αλαῖος ὁ ἀδελφὸς ΕΥριπίδου Αἴολος λεξιλόγον. ἐν ᾧ πεποίηκε Μακαρέα τ' παῖδα Αἰόλου φιλέοντα Κανακῆ τ' ἀδελφῷ. διὰ ἡ πᾶ Αἴσχυλος ἔξεσι γαμεῖν τὰς ἐκ πατέρων ἀδελφάς, εἰς ἀξιῶσιν τῆς ἀδικήματος παρεσκευάσθη τ' ὁμομητείᾳ. Quare Archeptolis Themistoclis filius Mnesiptolemam germanam sororem duxit. Plutarchus in Themistocle: ζυγατέρας ὃ πλείους ἔχει, ὧν Μνησιπτολέμαν μὲν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιγαμητίσεως ζωοφύλιν Ἀρχέπτολις ὁ ἀδελφὸς ἐκ ὢν ὁμομητείος ἐγημεν. Atque hæc quidem Lex est; neque tamen sine nota Cimon, qui Elpinicem sororem vxorem duxit. Tzetzem, Suidam, aliosque minorum gentium mitto: Plutarchum habes in Cimonis vita. ἐπὶ ἡ ἡ ὡς ἀ ἀ ἡ πλη-
units.tr: Scholion: "Giant Aiolos, brother of Euripides' Aeolus, a speaker..., in which he made Makareus, son of Aiolos, love his sister Kanake. Because Aeschylus permitted marriage with sisters from the same father, he prepared for the charge of same-mother [marriage]." Hence Archeptolis, son of Themistocles, married his full sister Mnesiptolema. Plutarch in the Life of Themistocles: "Of his many daughters, Archeptolis, his son, married Mnesiptolema, the daughter of a different mother [?], not a full sister." [ζυγατέρας ὃ πλείους ἔχει, ὧν Μνησιπτολέμαν μὲν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιγαμητίσεως ζωοφύλιν Ἀρχέπτολις ὁ ἀδελφὸς ἐκ ὢν ὁμομητείος ἐγημεν.] This is indeed the law. Yet Cimon, who married his sister Elpinice, is not free of reproach. I pass over Tzetzes, Suidas, and other minor writers; you have Plutarch in the Life of Cimon. [ἐπὶ ἡ ἡ ὡς ἀ ἀ ἡ πλη-]

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters] ἀ[?]ξειν τῇ ἀδελφῇ. Sed hanc Cimonis cum Elpinice sorore damnatam & improbatam consuetudinem distinguit, idque optime, Plutarchus à legitimis illis cum sorore contractis nuptiis, liquet è sequentibus. εἰσὶ δ' οἱ τὸν Ἐλπινίκην, ὡς χρύφα τῆς Κίμωνι, φανερᾶς δὲ γαμηθῆναι συνοικῆσαι λέγουσιν, ἀξίου τῆς δικαιότητος νυμφίου [?] ἀφ' ὧν τῆς πίστεως [?] ἀποφεύγειν [?]. Athenæus Lib. XIII. καὶ Κίμωνος δὲ Ἐλπινίκη ἀδελφὴ συνοικίας [?] εἰς ὕστερον ἐκδοθῆναι Καλλίᾳ, καὶ Φυλάδη[?]-ης, μαθὼν ἔλαβε τῆς καλῆς ὁδοῦ αὐτὸς ὁ Περικλῆς ὁ τῆ Ἐλπινίκη μισθωσαι. Sed corruptus est hic locus; nam ut interpungitur, Elpinice Callię elocata non est, nisi postquam ab exilio rediit Cimo, quod falsum est: nam antequam ad Rempublicam accederet Cimo, huic Callię Elpinicem suam elocauit sororem. Colliges ex his Plutarchi: ἐπὶ δὲ Καλλίας τὴν Ἀθηναίων [?] ἐγκαλέσας ... τὸν μὲν ... ἀφ' ὧν ... Κίμωνα τῇ [?] ... Quare omnino interpungendum est apud Athenæum. καὶ Κίμωνος ἡ Ἐλπινίκη ἀδελφὴ συνοικίας εἰς ὕστερον ἐκδοθῆναι Καλλίᾳ, &c. Distinguit optime tempora, duo, quibus consuevit Cimo cum sorore: priori tempore, cum in uxorem eam haberet, quod per Leges licebat, non erat quod improbaretur Cimonis cum Elpinice consuetudo, ut quæ esset legitima: posteriori vero tempore, id est, postquam Callię eam locavit, consuetudinem non potuit nisi illegitimam habere: atque hæc posterior consuetudo illi vitio vertebatur, & recte id quidem: nam adulterium committebat. Quanquam non ea de causa in exilium pulsus est, ut illud afferat Andocides ἐν τῷ Ἀλκιβιάδου. Dicuntur ista, non ex vero, utiliter tamen à Rhetore ex artis legibus, quia scilicet Cimo, qui in exilium missus, consuevrat cum sorore, quæ Callię erat uxor, quanquam non ob hanc consuetudinem exulauit, nam ostracismus non erat pœna scelerum, sed quædam invidiosæ virtutis velut imminutio: unde Plato Comicus de Hyperbolo homine omnium bipedum vilissimo & nequissimo.
units.tr: [Fragment, illegible] ... to his sister. But Plutarch distinguishes this condemned and disapproved practice of Cimon with his sister Elpinice from the lawful marriages contracted with a sister, and does so very well, as is clear from what follows: "There are those who say that Elpinice, though secretly with Cimon, was openly married and lived with him, as a worthy bridegroom..." Athenaeus, Book XIII: "And Elpinice, sister of Cimon, was later given in marriage to Callias, and Periclès himself, who had learned of the beautiful... gave her in marriage." But this passage is corrupt; as it is punctuated, Elpinice was not given to Callias until after Cimon returned from exile, which is false, for Cimon gave his sister Elpinice to Callias before he entered public life. You will gather this from Plutarch: "But Callias, having accused the Athenians..., Cimon..." So Athenaeus should be punctuated differently: "And Elpinice, sister of Cimon, was later given in marriage to Callias," etc. This distinguishes well the two periods in which Cimon had relations with his sister. In the earlier period, when he had her as his wife, which the laws permitted, the relationship of Cimon with Elpinice was not open to censure, since it was lawful. In the later period, after he had given her to Callias, the relationship could only be unlawful, and this later relationship was held against him, and rightly so, for he was committing adultery. Yet he was not driven into exile for this reason, as Andocides claims in his speech against Alcibiades. These things are said not from the truth but for rhetorical effect, since Cimon, who was sent into exile, had lived with his sister, who was Callias' wife. Although he was not exiled because of this relationship, ostracism was not a punishment for crimes but a kind of diminishing of envied virtue; hence the comic poet Plato speaks of Hyperbolus, the most worthless and wicked of all bipeds.

units.la: χαῖρε πάντας ἐπὶ τὴν ἔξιν ... μὴ ... ἀξία, / ἀπὸ δὲ καὶ τὴν σιγμὴν ἀναξία, / οὐ γὰρ θιούσιν εἶναι ἐσθ' ... ἐκ... ἀφ' ὧν ... [?]
units.tr: Hail, all ... not worthy ... and also unworthy of the sigma ... for they do not ... from which ... [Obscura]

units.la: Præcipuè inter gentiles constitutæ sunt nuptiæ: quinimo Ἐπίκληρος virgo solis gentilibus & cognatis nuptum erat danda. Quæ sit Ἐπίκληρος, in superioribus diximus: hoc tantum addam Ἐπικλήρους dictas fuisse filias, etiamsi plures fuissent, dummodo nulli essent virilis sexus liberi. Scholiastes Comici ad hunc è Vespis versum:
units.tr: Marriages were established above all among the gentiles. Indeed, a maiden heiress (epikleros) was to be given in marriage only to a gentile and a kinsman. I have explained earlier what an epikleros is. I will add only that daughters were called epikleroi even when there were several of them, provided there was no male child. The scholiast on the comic poet, on this line from the Wasps:

units.la: καὶ ἀποθνήσκων ὁ πατὴρ τὰς δύο καταλίπῃ παῖδ' Ἐπίκληρον.
units.tr: "And when the father dies, he leaves two daughters, epikleroi" [καὶ ἀποθνήσκων ὁ πατὴρ τὰς δύο καταλίπῃ παῖδ' Ἐπίκληρον].

units.la: Καλοῦσι δὲ Ἐπικλήρους, καὶ δύο ὦσι θυγατέρες, καὶ πλείους. Eam puellam siue mulierem, extra cognationem enuberehon finit Solonis Lex ista.
units.tr: They call them epikleroi, whether there are two daughters or more. The law of Solon forbids this girl, or woman, to marry outside her kinship [ἐπίκληρος].

units.la: Μὴ ἐξεῖναι τῆς Ἐπικλήρου ἐξω τῆς ἀ-χιστείας γαμεῖν, ἀλλὰ πρῶτον τῷ ἐγγύτατα ... ἀ-τῆς μὴ τῇ χρυμῷ τοῦ ἐξ ... [?] συνοικεῖν.
units.tr: It is not permitted to marry the epikleros outside the next of kin, but first to the one nearest to her ... and to live with her [Μὴ ἐξεῖναι τῆς Ἐπικλήρου ἐξω τῆς ἀγχιστείας γαμεῖν, ἀλλὰ πρῶτον τῷ ἐγγύτατα ... συνοικεῖν].

units.la: Virgo dotalis extra cognationem ne enubito: sed agnato proximo nubito, & omnia sua bona in dotem adferto.
units.tr: A dowered virgin must not marry outside her kinship, but must marry the nearest agnate, and bring all her goods into the dowry.

units.la: Meminit Isæus ὅτι ὡς παῖς Ξεναίνετος ... τῆς κληρου τῆς Αεισάρχου. Τόπου δὲ παιδὸς ἀποθανόντος, καὶ τῆς ἑτέρας ἀδελφῆς, ἡ μήτηρ ἡ ἐμὴ ἐν πατρὶ ᾧ οἴκῳ Ἐπίκληρος ἐγίνετο. ἢ ὅταν μὲν ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἅπαντα τ᾽ ἡμῖν μένειν ἐγίνετο. ὥστε συνῆκεν δ᾽ αὐτῇ μὲν τὴν ἐπικλήρον τὰ ἐπὶ ὑπάτα ἤρως σῶσοικῶν[?]. Pollux Lib. III. cap. III. ὁ ἡ ἐπὶ τῇ Ἐπικληρῷ ὥσπερ σύνοικον ἢ ἥρως ἐχρήσατο[?]. Diodorus Siculus Bibliothecæ Lib. XII.
units.tr: Isaeus mentions ... the estate of Xenaenetus' child ... of the estate of Aristarchus. When the child died, and the other sister too, my mother became the epikleros in my father's house ... Pollux, Book III, chapter III, says that the epikleros was used like a ... Diodorus Siculus, Library, Book XII.

units.la: τέιτος δὲ νόμος διορθώσῃ ὁ αὐτὸς τὴν Ἐπικληρων, ὁ καὶ πρῶτος Σόλωνι κείμενος. ἐκέλευε γὰρ τὴν Ἐπικληρον ἐπιδικάζεσθαι τὸν εἰσιόντα γένους, ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ τὴν Ἐπικληρον ἐπιδικάζεσθαι τοὺς ἀγχιστεῖς. ὃ ὡς αὐτὸ ἀνάγκη σύνοικιν, ἡ πεντακοσίας σκτίσεις δραχμὰς εἰς προικῶν λόγον τῇ πενιχρᾷ Ἐπικληρῳ. Sed haec verba, ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ τὴν Ἐπικληρον ἐπιδικάζεσθαι τοὺς ἀγχιστεῖς, & quae sequuntur, spectant τὰς ἐπικλήρους ἰδίων πλουσίας, non autem dotales, de quibus Lex haec est, easque ambiebant cognati, & sibi vindicabant tanquam iure ciuili desponsatas sibi.
units.tr: The third law, correcting the epikleroi, is the same one that was first laid down by Solon. For it ordered that the epikleros be claimed by the nearest kinsman entering the family, and likewise that the epikleros be claimed by the close kin, who were necessarily to live with her, or else give five hundred drachmas as dowry on behalf of the poor epikleros. But these words, "and likewise the epikleros is to be claimed by the near kin", and what follows, refer to epikleroi rich in their own right, not to dowered women, to whom this law applies, and whom their kinsmen courted and claimed for themselves as if betrothed to them by civil law.

units.la: Ἰσαῖος δὲ τὸν τοῦ Ῥύρρου κλῆρον. δῆλον μὲν γὰρ ὅτι Ἐπικληρον μὲν καλοῦσιν, ἀκριβῶς δὲ ἠδὴ ὅτι δυοῖν θυγατέρα ἐμίμνον ἐπαρχίαν αὐτῆς. ἢ γὰρ ἡμῖν ἴνα τὴν ἐπικληρον ἡμῖν ἐπιδικασθῆναι, ἢ εἰ μηδεὶς ἡμῖν ἐβούλετο λαμβάνειν, τὴν ἀλλὰ τῶν[?] μαρτυρούντων· εἰ δὲ μή, τὴν ἄλλων τινὰ συνῴκισεν τὸν αὐτὸν ἔχοντα πεῖ πάσης τῆς οὐσίας ἐπιδικασάμενον, καὶ τοὺς νόμους ἐχὼν ταύτῳ γυναῖκα. Quare etiam dotales hae feminae ἐπίδικοι dicebantur, quarum nuptias petebant plures, vt iure ciuili ad se delatas. Pollux: ἐπίδικος ἡ ἡ Ἐπικληρος λέγεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἀμφισβητησίας τινὲς ἀλλὰ ὡς μᾶλλον εἰς αὐτὰς τῆς ἀρχείας καθήκουσης. Harpocration: ἐπίδικος ἡ ἡ ἀμφισβητουμένη Ἐπικληρος, ὅτε χρὴ αὐτὴν γαμηθῆναι. Omnes autem oportebat Ἐπικληρους sibi apud Praetorem vindicare, & iudicio experiri, quanquam nullus controuersiam faceret: id enim hac cautum est Solonis Lege.
units.tr: Isaeus, on the estate of Pyrrhus. It is clear that they are called epikleroi, and it is also clear that the estate was held for two daughters. Either the epikleros was to be claimed for us, or, if no one wanted to take her, the one ... of the witnesses; otherwise, another man, having the same claim over the whole property, married her, and held the woman by the law. Therefore these dowered women were also called epidikoi [ἐπίδικοι], whose marriages several men sought, as if brought to them by civil law. Pollux: an epikleros is called epidikos because of the dispute over her, but rather because the right of the magistrate falls upon her. Harpocration: an epidikos is an epikleros who is disputed, when she must be married. All epikleroi had to be claimed for themselves before the Praetor and tested in court, even if no one raised a dispute; for this was provided by the law of Solon.

units.la: ΚΛΗΡΟΥΝ ΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΚΛΗΡΟΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΠΙΚΛΗΡΩΝ, ΟΣΟΙ ΕΙΣΙ ΜΗΝΕΣ ΠΛΗΝ ΤΟΥ ΣΚΙΡΡΟΦΟΡΙΩΝΟΣ, ΕΠΙΔΙΚΟΝ ΔΕ ΚΛΗΡΟΝ ΜΗ ΕΧΕΙΝ.
units.tr: THE LOT AND THE EPIKLEROI, AS MANY AS THERE ARE MONTHS, EXCEPT SCIRROPHORION, ARE TO BE CLAIMED; AND NO ONE IS TO HOLD AN ESTATE WITHOUT A CLAIM [ΚΛΗΡΟΥΝ ΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΚΛΗΡΟΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΠΙΚΛΗΡΩΝ, ΟΣΟΙ ΕΙΣΙ ΜΗΝΕΣ ΠΛΗΝ ΤΟΥ ΣΚΙΡΡΟΦΟΡΙΩΝΟΣ, ΕΠΙΔΙΚΟΝ ΔΕ ΚΛΗΡΟΝ ΜΗ ΕΧΕΙΝ].

units.la: Haereditatem, dotalémque virginem in iure tibi vindicato: iudicia redduntor singulis menfibus, excepto Scirrhophorione: nullus haereditatem possideto, aut dotalem virginem in matrimonio habeto nisi iudicio expertus.
units.tr: Claim for yourself the estate and the dowered virgin in law: hearings are held each month, except Scirrophorion. No one shall possess an estate, or have a dowered virgin in marriage, unless he has been tested in court.

units.la: Legem descripsimus, vt mendose legitur apud Demosthenem ἐν τῷ πρὸς Σπουδίαν[?] ἀποδ. β. sed vertimus, vt legendam putamus hoc modo.
units.tr: We have copied out the law as it is read corruptly in Demosthenes, in the speech against Spudias. But we have translated it as we think it should be read, in this way.

units.la: ΚΛΗΡΟΥΝ ΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΚΛΗΡΟΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΠΙΚΛΗΡΟΝ, ΟΣΟΙ ΕΙΣΙ ΜΗΝΕΣ ΠΛΗΝ ΤΟΥ ΣΚΙΡΡΟΦΟΡΙΩΝΟΣ, ΑΝΕΠΙΔΙΚΟΝ ΔΕ ΚΛΗΡΟΝ, ΚΑΙ ΕΠΙΚΛΗΡΟΝ ΜΗ ΕΧΕΙΝ.
units.tr: THE LOT AND THE EPIKLEROS, AS MANY AS THERE ARE MONTHS, EXCEPT SCIRROPHORION, ARE TO BE CLAIMED; AND NO ONE IS TO HOLD AN UNCLAIMED ESTATE OR AN EPIKLEROS [ΚΛΗΡΟΥΝ ΔΕ ΤΟΝ ΚΛΗΡΟΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΠΙΚΛΗΡΟΝ, ΟΣΟΙ ΕΙΣΙ ΜΗΝΕΣ ΠΛΗΝ ΤΟΥ ΣΚΙΡΡΟΦΟΡΙΩΝΟΣ, ΑΝΕΠΙΔΙΚΟΝ ΔΕ ΚΛΗΡΟΝ, ΚΑΙ ΕΠΙΚΛΗΡΟΝ ΜΗ ΕΧΕΙΝ].

units.la: Emendationis fundus est ipse Demosthenes, cuius haec praecedunt: τὸν Ξίπω νόμον ὅτι τούτοις ἀφάγωσι, ὃς κελεύει ἐπιδικάσαι ἐπὶ τὴν Ἐπικληρων ἁπάντων, καὶ ξένων καὶ ἀστῶν. καὶ ἀνεπιδικον μὴ ἐξεῖναι ἔχειν, μήτε κληρον, μήτε Ἐπικληρον. Itaque Sositheus apud Demosthenem ἐν τῇ πρὸς Μακάρτατον dicit se iudicio fuisse expertum apud Praetorem de Philomaches nuptiis, etsi nullus ei negocium exhiberet, & de Philomache contenderet. οὐδὲ ἐκ τῆς οὔτ᾽ ἡμφισβήτησιν, οὔτε τὸν κληρον τὴν Αγίου, οὔτε τῆς γυναικὸς τῆς Ἐπικληρου, ὡ ἐγὼ ἔχω ἐπιδικασάμενος. & paullo ante, καὶ ἐγὼ Ζωτ᾽ ἐμαρτυρῆσαι αὐτοῖ, ὁ ἡ ΕΥΞΕ-λίδου θυγατέρα ἔχων ἐπιδικασάμενος ὡς ἡμὴ ὢν ἐπιτυχῶν. Haec ἐπιδικασία fiebat singulis anni mensibus, Scirrhophorione excepto: ΟΣΟΙ ΕΙΣΙ ΜΗΝΕΣ ΓΑΛΗΝ ΤΟΥ ΣΚΙΡΡΟΦΟΡΙΩΝΟΣ. Ratio est, quia mensis Scirrhophorion est vltimus anni, eoque obeunt plerique Magistratu, aut in referendis rationebus sunt occupati. Fiebat ἐπιδικασία apud Prætorem, qui signabat Fastos, si feminæ illæ ἐπικλήρφ essent ciues: sin inquilinæ apud Polemarchum. Demosthenes ea, ex qua Legem hanc describimus, Oratione. νόμος κελεύει ἐπιδικάζεσθαι τὰς ἐπικλήρους, εἰ τῶν πολιτῶν ἀπαιτῶν, καὶ ξένων, καὶ ἀστῶν. καὶ ταῖς μὲν τῶν πολιτῶν, τὸν Ἀρχοντα εἰσαγειν, καὶ ἐπιμελεῖσθαι, ταῖς δὲ τῶν μετοίκων τὸν Πολέμαρχον. Hinc Pollux Libro VIII. cap. IX. ταῖς Ἀρχοντα λαμβάνοντα κλήρων καὶ Ἐπικλήρων ἐπιδικάσαι. de Polemarcho Aristoteles. Πολέμαρχος εἰσαγει δικαστὰς (ꝫ. δικας ταῖς) τὰ τῶν κλήρων καὶ Ἐπικλήρων ταῖς μετοίκοις. Debebat itaque è Lege, qui ad sè declaratas iure credebat dotalis virginis nuptias, ceteros in ius vocare, vt sciret, an vellent controuersiam ei facere de dotali femina, alioquin iure ipso nulla erat hæc ἐπιδικασία. Neque tamen adhuc ἀντιδικιας erat ἡ Ἐπικληρος, quanquam μὴ τῷ νόμων καὶ τῆς ψήφου in mariti, qui eam sibi asseruerat, manum conuenisset: poterat enim qui sibi factam credebat iniuriam, in ius vocare illum, qui τῷ Ἐπικληρος vxorem habebat iudicio euictam & quæsitam.
units.tr: The basis of the emendation is Demosthenes himself, whose preceding words are: the law of Xipho, that they should eat ..., which orders that claim be made upon all epikleroi, both foreigners and citizens; and that no one may hold an unclaimed estate or epikleros [τὸν Ξίπω νόμον ... ἐπιδικάσαι ἐπὶ τὴν Ἐπικληρων ἁπάντων, καὶ ξένων καὶ ἀστῶν. καὶ ἀνεπιδικον μὴ ἐξεῖναι ἔχειν, μήτε κληρον, μήτε Ἐπικληρον]. So Sositheus, in Demosthenes' speech against Macartatus, says that he had been tested in court before the Praetor about Philomache's marriage, although no one brought a case against him and no one contested Philomache with him. And a little before, he says that he too gave evidence ... that he had claimed the daughter of Euxelides, having her as his own, and had succeeded. This claim was made in each month of the year except Scirrophorion: "all the months except Scirrophorion" [ΟΣΟΙ ΕΙΣΙ ΜΗΝΕΣ ΓΑΛΗΝ ΤΟΥ ΣΚΙΡΡΟΦΟΡΙΩΝΟΣ]. The reason is that Scirrophorion is the last month of the year, and in it most magistrates leave office or are busy with the rendering of accounts. The claim was made before the Praetor, who signed the registers, if the women were citizens by birth; but if they were resident aliens, before the Polemarch. Demosthenes, in the speech from which we take this law: the law orders that epikleroi be claimed, whether of citizens or foreigners and of residents; for citizens the Archon is to introduce and oversee, and for resident aliens the Polemarch. Hence Pollux, Book VIII, chapter IX: the Archon takes the estates and epikleroi and claims them. Aristotle on the Polemarch: the Polemarch brings in the judges for the estates and epikleroi of the resident aliens. Therefore, by the law, whoever believed that a dowered virgin's marriage had been declared to him by right was bound to summon the others to court, so that he might know whether they wished to contest with him over the dowered woman; otherwise this claim was void in law. Yet the epikleros was not yet a matter of contest, even though she had been placed under the hand of the husband who had claimed her, through the law and the vote; for anyone who believed he had been wronged could summon before the court the man who had an epikleros as his wife, to be won and sought by judgment.

units.la: ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΕΠΙΔΕΔΙΚΑΣΜΕΝΟΥ ΑΜ-ΦΙΣΒΗΤΗι ΤΟΥ ΚΛΗΡΟΥ Η ΤΗΣ Ε-ΠΙΚΛΗΡΟΥ ΠΡΟΚΑΛΕΙΣΘΩ ΤΟΝ Ε-ΠΙΔΕΔΙΚΑΣΜΕΝΟΝ ΠΡΟΣ ΤΟΝ ΑΡ-ΧΟΝΤΑ, ΚΑΘΑΠΕΡ ΕΠΙ ΤΩΝ ΑΛΛΩΝ ΔΙΚΩΝ. ΠΑΡΑΚΑΤΑΒΟΛΑΣ Δ' ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΩι ΑΜΦΙΣΒΗΤΟΥΝΤΙ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΠΡΟΚΑΛΕΣΑΜΕΝΟΣ ΕΠΙΔΙ-ΚΑΣΗΤΑΙ, ΑΤΕΛΗΣ ΕΣΤΑΙ Η ΕΠΙΔΙ-ΚΑΣΙΑ ΤΟΥ ΚΛΗΡΟΥ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΖΗι Ο ΕΠΙΔΙΚΑΣΑΜΕΝΟΣ ΤΟΥ ΚΛΗ-ΡΟΥ ΠΡΟΣΚΑΛΕΙΣΘΩ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΑΥΤΑ Ωι Η ΠΡΟΘΕΣΜΙΑ, ΜΗΠΩ ΕΞΗΚΕΙ ΤΗΝ Δ' ΑΜΦΙΣΒΗΤΗΣΙΝ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΩι ΑΡΧΟΝΤΙ, ΚΑΘΟΤΙ ΕΠΕΔΙΚΑΣΑΤΟ ΟΥ ΑΝ ΕΧΗι ΤΑ ΧΡΗΜΑΤΑ.
units.tr: IF THE CLAIM TO THE ESTATE OR THE EPIKLEROS IS DISPUTED, LET THE ONE WHO MADE THE CLAIM BE SUMMONED BEFORE THE ARCHON, AS IN OTHER SUITS, WITH A DEPOSIT, AND THE DEPOSIT IS TO BE THE CONTESTANT'S. IF THE ONE WHO MADE THE CLAIM IS NOT SUMMONED WITHIN THE TIME ALLOWED, THE CLAIM TO THE ESTATE IS VOID. IF THE ONE WHO MADE THE CLAIM IS NOT ALIVE, LET THE OTHER BE SUMMONED ACCORDING TO THE SAME TERMS, AS LONG AS THE TIME LIMIT HAS NOT EXPIRED; THE DISPUTE IS TO BE BEFORE THE ARCHON, WHO SHALL ASSESS THE PROPERTY [ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΕΠΙΔΕΔΙΚΑΣΜΕΝΟΥ ΑΜΦΙΣΒΗΤΗι ΤΟΥ ΚΛΗΡΟΥ Η ΤΗΣ ΕΠΙΚΛΗΡΟΥ ΠΡΟΚΑΛΕΙΣΘΩ ΤΟΝ ΕΠΙΔΕΔΙΚΑΣΜΕΝΟΝ ΠΡΟΣ ΤΟΝ ΑΡΧΟΝΤΑ, ΚΑΘΑΠΕΡ ΕΠΙ ΤΩΝ ΑΛΛΩΝ ΔΙΚΩΝ. ΠΑΡΑΚΑΤΑΒΟΛΑΣ Δ' ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΩι ΑΜΦΙΣΒΗΤΟΥΝΤΙ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΠΡΟΚΑΛΕΣΑΜΕΝΟΣ ΕΠΙΔΙΚΑΣΗΤΑΙ, ΑΤΕΛΗΣ ΕΣΤΑΙ Η ΕΠΙΔΙΚΑΣΙΑ ΤΟΥ ΚΛΗΡΟΥ. ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΖΗι Ο ΕΠΙΔΙΚΑΣΑΜΕΝΟΣ ΤΟΥ ΚΛΗΡΟΥ ΠΡΟΣΚΑΛΕΙΣΘΩ ΚΑΤΑ ΤΑΥΤΑ Ωι Η ΠΡΟΘΕΣΜΙΑ, ΜΗΠΩ ΕΞΗΚΕΙ ΤΗΝ Δ' ΑΜΦΙΣΒΗΤΗΣΙΝ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΩι ΑΡΧΟΝΤΙ, ΚΑΘΟΤΙ ΕΠΕΔΙΚΑΣΑΤΟ ΟΥ ΑΝ ΕΧΗι ΤΑ ΧΡΗΜΑΤΑ].

units.la: Si quis de hæreditate, aut dotali puella iudicio euicta controuersiam faciat, prouocato eum, qui eiicit iudicio, apud Prætorem, vt in aliis causis, cum sponsione. Si is qui iudicio eiicit, alios non prouocarit, nulla esto euictio illa hæreditatis. Si superstes iam non sit is, qui eiicit hæreditatem, prouocato si nondum definitum tempus abiit. Controuertito apud Prætorem, quemadmodum qui hæreditatem iudi-cio eiicit.
units.tr: If anyone brings a controversy about an estate, or about a dowered girl who has been won in court, let him summon the one who won her in court before the Praetor, as in other cases, with a sponsio. If the one who won in court has not summoned others, the winning of that estate shall be void. If the one who won the estate is no longer alive, let him be summoned, provided the time limit has not yet run out. Let the dispute be heard before the Praetor, in the same manner as for one who has won the estate in court.

units.la: Lex habetur apud Demosthenem ἐν τῷ κατὰ Μακάρτατον, cuius ista: ΕΑΝ ΔΕ ΜΗ ΖΗι Ο ΕΠΙΔΙΚΑΣΑΜΕΝΟΣ ΤΟΥ ΚΛΗΡΟΥ. ad finem vsque, feminas dotales non spectant, itaque suo loco infra, Deo dante, à nobis expendentur. Poterat igitur controuersia fieri de dotali femina ei, qui iam in iure sibi eam asseruerat: citabatur autem apud Prætorem: isque qui cum eo agebat, sacramentum deponebat, quod ἀντωμοσίαν [?] dicunt, nempe decimam eorum partem bonorum, quæ dotalis femina secum ferebat. ΠΑΡΑΚΑΤΑΒΟ-ΛΑΣ Δ' ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΩι ΑΜΦΙΣΒΗΤΟΥΝΤΙ. Sed hæc ἀμφισβήτησις [?] intra definitum aliquod tempus fieri debebat, intra quinque annos puto: nam hic est νόμως [?], vt è Demosthene docet Harpocration: certè in bonorum petitione id est definitum tempus. Isæus: ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ Πύῤῥου κλήρου. ὁ δὲ νόμος πιν-πε ἐπὶ τὴν κλῆρον δικάσασθαι τὸν κλῆρον, ἐπιδικῶ πλοῦτον ὁ κληρονόμος.
units.tr: This law is found in Demosthenes, in the speech against Macartatus, and runs as follows: "If the one who made the claim is not alive ..." up to the end. It does not concern dowered women, and so, as God grants, we shall consider it below in its proper place. It was therefore possible for a controversy to arise about a dowered woman against the one who had already claimed her in court. He was summoned before the Praetor, and the man who brought the case deposited a sacred pledge, which they call antomosia, namely a tenth part of the goods that the dowered woman brought with her. "The deposit is to be the contestant's." But this contest had to be made within a fixed period, I think within five years; for Harpocration, drawing on Demosthenes, shows that this is the legal period; at least, in the suit for an estate there is such a fixed time. Isaeus, in the case of the estate of Pyrrhus: the law gives five years for the claim to the estate, to the heir who claims the wealth.

units.la: Nec potior erat eorum conditio, qui dotales has virgines à patribus desponsatas, etiam supremis tabulis, vxores duxerant, poterant enim in ius vocari ex hac Lege:
units.tr: Nor was the position of those better who had taken to wife, even under the last testaments, the dowered maidens betrothed by their fathers, for they could be summoned to court under this law.

units.la: Τας μὲν τῶν πατρῴων ἐκδόσεις συνοικούσας ἀδρᾶσι γυναῖκας, αἱ δ' ὁ πατὴρ αὐτῶν τελευτήσας, μὴ καταλιπὼν αὐτὰς γνησίους ἀδελφοὺς, ὡς ἐγγύα τοῖς ἰδίοις ὁπαδίκους [?]
units.tr: Women given away by their fathers, who live with grown men as wives, when their father has died without leaving them legitimate brothers, ... [the rest of the Greek is too corrupt in the scan to render reliably].

units.la: Feminas à patribus elocatas, & à maritis domum deductas, si pater obeat nullis superstitibus liberis legitimis masculis, proximiores cognatione iure sibi vindicanto.
units.tr: Women given in marriage by their fathers and led home by their husbands: if the father dies and no legitimate male children survive, let the nearest kinsmen by blood claim them as their right.

units.la: Legem descripsimus, vt vulgo editur apud Isaeum ἐν τῷ τοῦ Πύρρου κλή-ρου. τὰς μὲν τῶν πατρώων ἐκδόσεις καὶ συνοικούσας ἀδρᾶσι γυναῖκας (ὡς ἐὰν τὶς ἀπ' ἀμείνον ἢ ὁ πατὴρ βουλεύσαιτο ;) καὶ ὡς ἂν ὅτι δῷ ἐκδόσεις, αἱ δ' πατὴρ αὐτῶν τελευτήσας, μὴ καταλιπὼν αὐτὰς γνησίους ἀδελφοὺς, ὡς ἐγγύατα ἡμοις ὁπαδίκους ὁ νόμος ἐὰν [?]. καὶ πολλοὶ συνοικοῦντες ἤδη ἀφηρημένας τῆς ἑαυτῶν γυναῖκας. εἶτα τὰς μὲν τῶν πατρώων ἐκδόσεις ἐκ τὸν νόμον ἐξ αἰσχῆς ὁπαδίκους ἐὰν [?] καθ' ἑαυτοῦ. Sed rescribendum est vbique ἐπὶ τῆς πατρῷων in locum horum ἐπὶ τῶν πατρώων. arguunt Isaeiista, ὡς ἂν τὶς ἀπ' ἀμείνον ἢ ὁ πατὴρ βουλεύσαιτο ; De desponsatis supremis patrum tabulis Demosthenes ἐν τῷ κατὰ Σπουδαίου ψευδομαρτυρίων β. Cꝛxoῑ̃ αὐτόν, εἰ̓σ ἐξ' ἐβούλετο ὀρθῶς ἀξιοῦσθαι, λαχεῖν ἐδὲ τὴς Ἐπικλήρου, εἶτα ἐκ δίδοιτο αὐτὴ γαμεῖσθαι, εἶτα ἐκ ἡμῖν ὁ ὁ ὁ ἐδ' ὡς ἐκ ἀπὸ ἀς, ἀπὸ τὸν Ἀρχοντα. εἰ δὲ ἐκ ξένης, ἀπὸ τὸν Πολέμαρχον. Hinc intelligendus Aristophanes Vespis.
units.tr: We have set out the law as it is commonly printed in Isaeus, in the speech On the estate of Pyrrhus: "Those who have given away and live with grown women (as if the father had planned something better?) ... and whoever gives in marriage, if their father dies and leaves them no legitimate brothers, the law ... as sureties ... and many who already live with their wives have taken them away from their own." Then: "Those who are given away by fathers, by this law, are liable ... against himself." But everywhere one must rewrite ἐπὶ τῆς πατρῷων in place of these words, to read ἐπὶ τῶν πατρῴων ("in the case of the paternal estates"). Isaeus's wording supports this, as in "if anyone had a better plan than the father's". On the epikleros and the father's last testament, Demosthenes in the second speech Against Spudias for false witness says: that a man who wished to be rightly thought worthy should claim the heiress, and then should not be given to her to marry, and then ... before the archon, and if from abroad, before the polemarch. From here Aristophanes in the Wasps should be understood.

units.la: καὶ ἀποθνήσκων ὁ πατὴρ τῆς δὲ κλῆρον καταλιπὼν παῖδας Ἐπικλήρου, λυπέουν ἡμᾶς μαχεῖ τῷ χεφαλῷ εἰπόντες τῇ δίκῃ, καὶ τὴ κλῆρῃ τῇ πάνυ σημεῖως τῆς σημείοιον ἐπαινοῖ, ἑδομένῳ τοῦτο ὡς τὶς δὲ ἡμᾶς ἀπιθολήσας λαμπίσμ.
units.tr: And when the father, dying, leaves an heiress daughter with the estate, ... [the rest of this Greek is too corrupt in the scan to render reliably].

units.la: Quod si quis τῆς Ἐπικληρου bonis inhians, eam Lege sibi vindicarit, neque tamen mariti res agat, vel quia frigidus, vel quia alio amore irretitus est, Solonis Lege conceditur τοῖς Ἐπικληρῆς, maritorum adgnatos sectari, qui illarum fundum incultum non deserant.
units.tr: If anyone, greedy for the goods of the epikleros, has claimed her by this law but does not carry on the husband's affairs, either because he is impotent or because he is caught up in another love, Solon's law allows the epikleros to seek out the husband's kinsmen, who will not leave her unworked field uncultivated.

units.la: Τῷ Ἐπικλήρου, αἱ ὁ κεκτημένος καὶ κύριος γαμηθῆς τὸν νόμον, αὐτὸς μὴ δυνατὸς ἢ πλησιάζειν, ἐπ' αὐτοῦ τὴν ἑαυτῆς ὀπήεσθαι.
units.tr: [The Greek here is too corrupt in the scan to render reliably; its sense is that the epikleros, if the husband who has acquired and holds her under the law is himself unable to lie with her, may summon another man for herself from his kin.]

units.la: Dotalis femina, si maritus, qui eam sibi iure vindicauit, coire non possit, cum mariti adgnatis concubito.
units.tr: A dowered woman, if the husband who has claimed her by right cannot lie with her, may have intercourse with the kinsmen of the husband.

units.la: Legem descripsit Plutarchus in Solone, νόμος τῇ Ἐπικλήρῳ δίδωσι, αἱ ὁ κεκτημένος καὶ κύριος γαμηθῆς τὸν νόμον, αὐτὸς μὴ δυνατὸς ἢ πλησιάζειν, ἐπ' αὐτοῦ τὴν ἑαυτῆς ὀπήεσθαι. Hac Lege obuiam iuisse Solonem scribit Plutarchus auaritiae: aut enim nuptias illius non expetent, aut certe si periit de rebus frons & pudor, non sine nota constitutas habebunt: bene tamen est, quod non quemuis admittit, sed illum tantum inter mariti adgnatos, quem voluerit, ὅπως οἰκίαν ἢ καὶ μητέρα τῆς ἡμῶν ὁ ἡ πιθανὸς. Quemadmodum autem infanti consultum voluit hac Lege Solon: ita & sequenti τῆς Ἐπικληρου pudori atque honori: ita enim sanxit.
units.tr: Plutarch describes the law in his Solon: the law gives the epikleros, if the husband who has acquired and holds her is unable to lie with her, the right to summon one of his kinsmen for herself. Plutarch writes that Solon by this law met the greed of those men: they would either not seek her marriage, or, if shame and modesty had been lost from their dealings, they would have it settled without disgrace. Still it is good that he did not admit just anyone, but only one of the husband's kinsmen whom she chose, so that the house might have ... Just as Solon wished to provide for the infant by this law, so he provided for the epikleros's modesty and honour, for this is what he enacted.

units.la: Τεῖς ἑκάστου μῆνος ὀπῶν [?] ὁ ἐπικληρῶν τὸν λεχόντα.
units.tr: Three times each month the husband shall lie with the epikleros [the Greek is in part corrupt in the scan].

units.la: Maritus dotalis feminae ter singulis mensibus cum ea pernoctato.
units.tr: The husband of a dowered woman shall spend the night with her three times each month.

units.la: Habes Plutarchus ibidem, qui hanc illius rationem explicat. καὶ γὰρ εἰ μὴ γίγνοιντο παῖδες, ἀλλὰ ἡμῖν τῆς αὐτῆς ὡς τῇ σῴφρονα γυναῖκα καὶ φιλοφρονοῦσῶν, πολλὰ τῆ συμλεγομένων ἐκεῖσε δυναμέων ἀφαιρεῖσθαι, καὶ τὰς ἀδελφοὺς δυσχερεῖς ἐκ ἐδίδον πολλαπλασίως ἀποσπᾶσθαι ὡς αὐτὸς. Quod si maritus τῷ Ἐπικληρου male tractaret, vel ipsa ἡ Ἐπίκληρος, vel quicumque vellet eius partes tutari, Lege agebat malae tractationis aduersus maritum. Grammatici: κακώσεως, δίκης εἰσαγωγὴ ὅτι τῆς ἐπικλήσεως. ὅτι δὲ ἔξεστι πρὸ τοῦ βαλλομένου τῆς ἐπικλήσεως βουλὴν [?] ἀνλὸν [?] τὴν ἐν τῇ Πυρφάνδρα κλήσεως λέγει Τεσίδιον, καὶ ἐν τῷ Λεωσθένη [?] Φιλωνίδου βιαίων, εἰ γήμησ. ὧν δὲ καὶ αὐτὴ ἀδικος. Postrema ista verba in superioribus sumus interpretati: Dica hæc scribebatur apud Prætorem. Pollux Libro VIII. cap. VIII. [?] ἀλλὰ δὲ ταῖς τὸν Ἀρχέλαον λαμβάνοντα κακώσεως. Ifæus ἐν τῷ Πυρφάνδρα κλήσεως. καὶ ὅσα αὐτὸν εἰσπράξεις ταῖς τὸν Ἀρχέλαον, κακωσθεῖσα τῷ Ἐπικλήσει. Licebat, cui lubebat, hanc dicam scribere: ἐξὸν καὶ πάντῃ τῆς βαλλομένης ταῖς Ἐπικλήσεως βουλὴν. idque sine vllo suo periculo, etsi causa caderet. Ifæus ἐν τῷ Πυρφάνδρα κλήσεω. διότι τε καὶ μόνων τούτων τῆν δίκην ἀκινδύνων τῶν διωκόντων ἄσων, καὶ ἔξον τῆς βαλλομένης βουλὴν ταῖς ἐπικλήσεως. ὅτε δὲ ἐπιτήμιον ταῖς τοῦς Ἀρχέλαον εἰσαγγελίας ἐστιν, ἀλλ' ἐαν σαφῶς ἐγκλήματος τῆς ψήφου οἱ εἰσαγγελλάντες μεγαλοβωνίαν, ὅτι ἀρυτημένα, ὅτι ταῖς δίκαιοι ἀρχέμηα τῆς εἰσαγγελίας. ἀλλὰ ταῖς μὴ διακόσιον ἀκινδύνως ἔξεστι τῆς βαλλομένῳ. Hanc dicam εἰσαγγελίαν vocat Ifæus, & paria faciunt Grammatici: ἐπεὶ δὲ εἰσαγγελία λέγεται, ὅτι ταῖς κακώσεων · αὕτη δὲ εἰσὶ ταῖς τὸν Ἀρχέλαον, καὶ τῆς Ἀρχέλαι ἀξιοῦσι, καὶ μὴ μεγαλοβωνίαν ἐπιφοῦσι μέσος τῆς ψήφου. Atque in his totum versabatur argumentum dramatis Cratini, cui titulus est Πυτίνη, quod lucem præferret his, quæ iam diximus. Interpres Comici ad Equites: τῶν Κωμωδίων Κρατῖνος ἐπλάσατο αὐτὴ ἵππ) γυναῖκα, καὶ ἀ-φίσταθαι τῆς σίωνοικοῦς τῆς σίῳ αὐτὴ θέλῃ, καὶ Κακώσεως αὐτὴ δίκην λαγχάνει. φίλοις δὲ ἐξιτυχούσας τῆς Κρατίνου δίαθαι μηδὲν ἐπεχρηστίαις, καὶ τῆς ἐχθρὰς αἰ-ρωταῖν τῶν αἰτίαν. τῶν δὲ μὲμφεσθαι αὐτὸ ὅτι μὴ χωμῳδεῖ, ἵ μηκέτι ἀγαλλέσαι τῇ μέσῃ. Effectus actionis Κακώσεως ταῖς ἐπικλήσεως concesse is est, vt possint à viris diuertere, ἀφίσταθαι τῆς σιωνοικοῦς τῆς σίῳ αὐτὴν ἀνδρέσιν, vt est in laudatis Scholiastæ verbis. Inter ceteras autem causas, cur Κακώσεως δίκη marito scriberetur, hæc præcipua videtur fuisse, si ad alias applicasset animum mulieres, & si vbi ad vxorem ventum esset, vt loquitur apud Terentium doralis Naufistrata, tum fieret senex. Diogenes Laërtius in Polemone ex Antigono Carystio ἐν τῇς βίοις. Φυγῆν δὲ τὸν Πολέμωνα καὶ δίκην Κακώσεως ὑπὸ τῆς γυναικὸς, ὡς μισηχοίοις σιωνοῦσα. Huc spectant Cratini è dramate laudato versus, quibus Cratini amicis causam aperit Comœdia, cur illi malæ tractationis dicam impegerit.
units.tr: Plutarch explains his reasoning in the same place: even if children are not born, the woman who is chaste and kind to her husband should not be deprived of many things from the property ... and the brothers should not be drawn away in the many ways that were not granted. But if the husband ill-treated the epikleros, either she herself or whoever wished to protect her interests could bring an action for ill-treatment against the husband. The grammarians: an action for ill-treatment, an indictment against the husband on account of the epiclerate. That it was possible, before the epiclerate was settled, to bring a suit... Isaeus, in the speech On the estate of Pyrrhus, and in the speech on the case of Archelaus and Philonides, if he married... Those are the things said. We have explained these last words in our earlier notes: this action was written down before the Praetor. Pollux, Book 8, chapter 8, speaks of the action brought against him who takes the heiress. Isaeus, in the speech On the estate of Pyrrhus: and whatever he exacts from the one who takes the heiress, when she has been ill-treated in her epiclerate. Anyone who wished could write this indictment, and it was allowed to anyone to bring a suit on behalf of the epikleros, and this without any danger to himself, even if the case were lost. Isaeus, in the speech On the estate of Pyrrhus: for this reason the prosecutors of these suits alone were free from danger, and it was open to any who sued to bring the suit on behalf of the epikleros. This indictment is not a public impeachment, but if the accusers plainly prove the charge of ... the case of the impeachment. But those who have not been accepted may bring the suit without danger. Isaeus calls this suit an impeachment, and the grammarians agree: since it is called an impeachment, it is an action for ill-treatment; these concern Archelaus, and they claim the estate of Archelaus, and they do not impose a penalty of great magnitude in the vote. And in these matters the whole argument of Cratinus's play, entitled Pytine, turned, which brought light to what we have already said. The commentator on the Comic poet, on the Knights: Cratinus invented in his comedies a woman, a mare, who wishes to withdraw from her husband's household, and she brings an action for ill-treatment against him. And when she had been unhappy, she was unable to use the Cratinus's comedy in these matters, and she brought the cause against her enemies. Some complained that it was not comic, so that they no longer rejoiced in the middle. The effect of the action for ill-treatment on behalf of the epikleros was granted in this form: that they could separate from their husbands, withdrawing from the household of the men, as is in the words of the Scholiast quoted above. Among the other causes why an action for ill-treatment was written against the husband, this seems to have been the chief one: if the husband had turned his mind to other women, and if, when he came to his wife, as Terence's dowered Nausistrata says, he had become an old man. Diogenes Laertius in his Life of Polemo, from Antigonus of Carystus in his Lives: Polemo was exiled and sued by his wife for ill-treatment, because he was hostile to his wife. To this refer the verses of Cratinus from the play cited, in which the Comedy reveals to Cratinus's friends the cause why she brought the action of ill-treatment against him.

units.la: ἀλλ' ἐπιμαχρέλαι βάλλομεν εἰς τὸν λόγον παρέστεργον. ἐκσῆσας ἀρὸς ἐπέραν γυναῖκα ἔχων τὸν νοῦν, κακῶς εἶπει πρὸς ἑτέραν, ἀλλ' ἅμα μὴ ὁ γλῆσ. ἅμα δὲ μὴ δίκαι Θεοῖ ποτ' αὐτὴ παρόντεργον.
units.tr: But we have put in the argument for the sake of ... [the Greek here is too corrupt in the scan to render reliably; its sense is that a man who has kept his mind on another woman speaks ill of his wife to another, and that this is not, at the same time, just before the gods].

units.la: Multauerat Solon cum qui virginem deflorasset, drachmis cencum:
units.tr: Solon fined the man who had deflowered a virgin one hundred drachmas.

units.la: Εαὶ ἁρπάσῃ ὡς ἐλθεῖαι γυναῖκα, ἐ βιά-σηται, ζημίαν ἑκατὸν δραχμὰς ἀδίναι.
units.tr: If he carries off a woman who is free and does not use violence, let him pay a fine of one hundred drachmas.

units.la: Qui virgini ingenuæ vim intulerit, drachmis centum multator.
units.tr: Whoever has used violence against a free-born virgin shall be fined one hundred drachmas.

units.la: Refert Plutarchus in Solone, etsi autem multa iocularior, quam par fuit, videatur, tamen μὴ ἀσυμίζοντος πότε τῆς νομίσματος ἐν τῇ πόλει, μεγάλης ἐπὶ ἐι τῆς Φαγνευκῆς ζημίας ὃ δυναστείαν, vt inquit ibidem Plutarchus. Virginem imminucre dixerat Solon βίαν. Hesychius, βίαν, ὁ Σόλων ὁ βία μιγνύσθαι. ὁ ἡ χ[ῶ]ρ[αν] ὀπτεῖν. [?]
units.tr: Plutarch relates this in his Solon. Though many things seem rather more jocular than fitting, yet, since the coinage in the city was not ... a great penalty in the Phagnevic ... as Plutarch says in the same place. Solon had used the word bia for forcing a virgin. Hesychius: bian, "Solon: to mix by force"; ... [the rest is corrupt in the scan].

units.la: Sed id postea mutauit, cautumque est, vt is qui virginem imminueret, mille penderet drachmas.
units.tr: But later he changed this, and it was provided that whoever forced a virgin should pay a thousand drachmas.

units.la: Τὸν βιασάμενον κόρῳ χιλίας δίδοναι.
units.tr: Whoever ravishes a maiden shall give a thousand. [Τὸν βιασάμενον κόρῳ χιλίας δίδοναι.]

units.la: Laudat Marcellinus in Hermogenem: νόμος τὸν βιασάμενον κόρῳ Ἀθηναῖ χιλίας δίδοναι. Hinc intelligendus Syrianus in eundem Hermogenem: νόμος τὸν ἐξιόντα Σπαρτηνὸν εἰς πόλεμον, εἰ ἔχοι γυναῖκα, παραθέσθαι τῷ συμπατρὶ, πλὴν γυναικὸς λαβὼν ἐκ ἔτους ἐπαίσαν ἐπὶ ὁ Σπαρτηνὸς, χρὴ εἰ αὐτὸν ὡς δημόσιον ἀδικημάτων ἀδικῶν [illegible, ~6 letters] δίδοναι. [?]
units.tr: Marcellinus cites Hermogenes: a law of Athens that whoever ravishes a maiden shall give a thousand [νόμος τὸν βιασάμενον κόρῳ Ἀθηναῖ χιλίας δίδοναι]. From this one should understand Syrianus on the same Hermogenes: a law that a Spartan setting out for war, if he had a wife, should entrust her to a fellow citizen, but if he took a wife without the consent of ... the Spartan, he should be treated as a public wrongdoer ... [illegible] ... to give [νόμος τὸν ἐξιόντα Σπαρτηνὸν εἰς πόλεμον, εἰ ἔχοι γυναῖκα, παραθέσθαι τῷ συμπατρὶ, πλὴν γυναικὸς λαβὼν ἐκ ἔτους ἐπαίσαν ἐπὶ ὁ Σπαρτηνὸς, χρὴ εἰ αὐτὸν ὡς δημόσιον ἀδικημάτων ἀδικῶν [illegible] δίδοναι]. [?]

units.la: Sed neque satis seuere animaduerti raptores virginum, visum est iis qui secuti sunt. Quare Lege sancitum est, vt is qui virginem imminuerat, eam in vxorem duceret.
units.tr: But neither did the ravishers of maidens seem to be punished severely enough by those who came after. Therefore it was enacted by law that whoever had ravished a maiden should marry her.

units.la: Τὸν βιασάμενον κόρῳ, αὐτὴν γαμεῖν.
units.tr: Whoever ravishes a maiden shall marry her. [Τὸν βιασάμενον κόρῳ, αὐτὴν γαμεῖν.]

units.la: Laudant Syrianus & Marcellinus in Hermogenem. Plautus Aulularia:
units.tr: Syrianus and Marcellinus on Hermogenes cite this. Plautus, in the Aulularia:

units.la: Si quid ego erga te imprudens peccaui, aut gnatam tuam, Vt mihi ignoscas, eamque vxorem mihi des, vt Leges iubent.
units.tr: If I have unwittingly wronged you in any way, or your daughter, forgive me, and give her to me as wife, as the laws command.

units.la: Terentius in Adelphis Act.IV. Sc.VII.
units.tr: Terence, in the Adelphi, Act 4, Scene 7.

units.la: D. O stulte, tu de psaltria me somniasAgere, hoc peccatum in virginem est ciuem. M. Scio.
units.tr: D. You fool, do you dream that I am going to deal with a harp-girl? This sin is against a citizen maiden. M. I know.

units.la: D. Oho, scis, & patere? M. Quidni patiar? D. Dic mihi,Non clamas? non insanis? M. Non. D. Malim quidem. Puer natus est. M. DI bene vortant. D. Virgo nihil habet.
units.tr: D. What, do you know, and still you bear it? M. Why should I not bear it? D. Tell me, do you not cry out? Are you not mad? M. No. D. I would rather you were. The boy is born. M. May the gods bring it well. D. The girl has no dowry.

units.la: M. Audiui. D. Et ducenda indotata 'est? M. Scilicet.
units.tr: M. I have heard. D. And is she to be married without a dowry? M. Of course.

units.la: Quibus e verbis colligere est, non ἁπλῶς ducendam esse ab eo virginem, qui ei vitium obtulerit: sed si virgo ciuis sit: itaque in Lege scribendum est, τὸν βιασάμενον κόρῳ ἀξίωσ, αὐτὴν γαμεῖν. Quod autem addunt Rhetores ἀπαξιῶσι indotatam, non colliges e Terentij verbis indotatani esse ducendam, quamuis pater possit ei dotem dicere dare: sed tantum virginem ciuem, siue ea nihil habeat, ac proinde indotata sit, siue in re lauta sit, ducendam esse ab eo, qui vim illi intulit: Leges enim id iubent: vnde Donatus ad hunc Terentij locum. Ducenda scilicet, nisi damnandus sit Æschinus. & hoc verbum necessitatis vim habet. Vt autem duceret, qui rapuerat, exorare necesse habebat patrem virginis, vt sibi desponderet daretque: hinc apud Plautum Lyconides adolescens de nuptiis Phædriae Euclionem illius patrem appellat, verbis, quae iterum adscribemus:
units.tr: From these words one may gather that the maiden must not be married simply by the man who has done her violence, but only if she is a citizen maiden. So in the law it should be written: whoever ravishes a maiden must, if she is worthy, marry her [τὸν βιασάμενον κόρῳ ἀξίωσ, αὐτὴν γαμεῖν]. As for what the rhetoricians add, that she is to be married even if she is indotatam, you will not infer from Terence's words that a maiden without a dowry must be married, although her father may say he gives her a dowry; rather, a citizen maiden, whether she has nothing and is therefore without a dowry, or is in comfortable circumstances, must be married by the man who used force against her, for the laws require this. Hence Donatus on this passage of Terence: She must be married, of course, unless Aeschinus is to be condemned; and this word carries the force of necessity. That the ravisher might marry her, he had to beg the girl's father to betroth her to him and give her: hence in Plautus the young man Lyconides addresses Euclio, the girl's father, about the marriage of Phaedria, in the words we shall quote again:

units.la: Si quid ego erga te imprudens peccaui, aut gnatam tuam, Vt mihi ignoscas, eamque vxorem mihi des, vt Leges iubent.
units.tr: If I have unwittingly wronged you in any way, or your daughter, forgive me, and give her to me as wife, as the laws command.

units.la: Exorandus quoque a raptore pater, qui nuptiis auctor esset. Quare Micio ex hoc more apud Terentium, ne Æschinum metu amittendae puellae excruciet diutius, non appellatus ab eo de nuptiis, vltro exoratum se oftendit:
units.tr: The father, too, had to be entreated by the ravisher, since he was to be the giver in the marriage. Hence Micio in Terence, so that he does not torment Aeschinus any longer with fear of losing the girl, does not wait to be asked about the marriage but shows himself ready to be persuaded of his own accord:

units.la: In qua ciuitate tandem te arbitrare viuere? Virginem vitiasti, quam te ius non fuerat tangere. At postquam id euenit, cedo, Numquid circumspexti? aut numquid tute prospexti tibi Quid fieret? si te ipsum mihi puduit dicere. Bono animo es, duces vxorem hanc.
units.tr: In what state, then, do you think you are living? You have violated a maiden whom you had no right to touch. But since this has happened, tell me, have you looked around you? Or have you yourself considered what should be done? I am ashamed to say it of you. Be of good cheer; you shall take this woman as wife.

units.la: Verum si pretium accepisset siue virgo, siue mater illius, ab adolescente, qui compresserat, Leges non cogebant eam in vxorem ducere. Colligo ex his Terentianæ Softratæ verbis, Eunucho:
units.tr: But if the maiden, or her mother, had received payment from the young man who had ravished her, the laws did not compel him to take her as wife. I gather this from the words of Terence's Softrata in the Eunuchus:

units.la: Peiore res loco non potis est esse, quam in hoc, quo nunc sita est, Primum indotata est: tum præter ea, quæ secunda ei dos erat, Perijt: pro virgine dari nuptum non potest. hoc reliquum est, Si inficias ibit, testis mecum est annulus, quem amiserat. Postremo, quando ego conscia mi sum, à me culpam hanc procul esse, nec Precium, neque rem vllam intercesse illa aut me indignam: experiar Geta.
units.tr: Her position cannot be worse than it is now. First, she has no dowry; then, besides, the dowry that was a second hope for her has been lost. She cannot be given in marriage as a maiden. This is the remaining hope: if he denies it, I have as witness the ring which he had lost. Finally, since I am conscious that this fault is far from me, and that there was no payment or anything else between her and me, nor am I unworthy of her, I shall try it, Geta.

units.la: Lege Solonis non licebat tutori in vxorem ducere matrem pupillorum suorum.
units.tr: By the law of Solon it was not lawful for a guardian to marry the mother of his wards.

units.la: Τὸν ἐπίτροπον τῇ τῆς ὀρφανῆς μητρὶ μὴ οἰκοῖσιν[?] Tutor pupillorum suorum matrem in vxorem ne ducito.
units.tr: A guardian shall not marry the mother of his orphan ward. [Τὸν ἐπίτροπον τῇ τῆς ὀρφανῆς μητρὶ μὴ οἰκοῖσιν[?]] Latin: a guardian of his wards shall not marry their mother.

units.la: Legem refert Diogenes Laertius in Solonis vita: καλλίστην[?] δὲ κάλλιστην[?], τὸν ἐπί-τροπον τῇ τῆς ὀρφανῆς μητρὶ μὴ οἰκοῖσιν[?]. Qua Lege voluit pupillorum bonis consulere, ne qua fraus illis ob matris nuptias fieret. Sed videtur, aut antiquata fuisse hæc Solonis Lex, aut concessum fuisse tutoribus, qui testamento dabantur, matres pupillorum suorum in vxores ducere, siquidem moriens pater supremis testamenti sui tabulis id cauisset. En tibi exemplum à Demosthene, vbi de parentibus suis, patrisque tabulis supremis agit εἰς τὰ[?] κατὰ Ἀφόβου ψευδομαρτυριῶν α'. Δημοσθένης γὰρ ὁ ἐμὸς πατὴρ, ὦ ἄνδρες δικασταί, καταλιπὼν οὐσίαν ἀξιόλογον[?], πεπαρὼν τε τὴν δίκαια ταλάντων[?]. ἐμοὶ δὲ ἐπὶ πᾶσιν[?] ὅτι, καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν[?] πέντε[?]. ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν ἡμετέρων μητέρων, πεντήκοντα μνᾶς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν εἰσενεγκόντα[?]. Βυλδισάμενος δὲ ἀφ᾽ ἡμῶν[?], ὅτ᾽ ἐμοῦ τελευτῶν[?], ἀπέμπε Ταῦτα ἐπεχείρησεν Ἀφόβῳ τε Τούτῳ, καὶ Δημοφῶντι τοῦ Δημοσθένους υἱῷ[?]. Δημοφῶν δὲ τὸν ἐμὸν ἀδελφόν, καὶ δύο ταλάντα βύβλια ἐδωκεν ἐχθρὸν αὐτῷ τοῦτο τὴν μητέρα, ἣ πεζῇ οὐδὲν ἀπεγίνετο μνᾶς, ἡ τὴν οἰκίαν, καὶ σκεύη χρήσαθαι τοῖς ἐμοῖς[?]. Ita Pasio vxorem suam nuptum dat Phormioni, eumque tutorem dicit Paficlis filij sui natu minoris testamento. Demosthenes εἰς τῇ ὑπὸ Φορμίωνος παραγραφῇ[?]. Ὅτι[?] τοῦτο[?] ὁ Πασίων ἐπιτροπικὸς[?] Ταῦτα ἀξιόλογος, Φορμίων ἔφη[?], τὴν μὲν γυναῖκα λαμβάνει καὶ κατὰ τὸν ἀδελφὸν[?], τὸ ἡ ἴδιος ἐπιτρέψαι[?]. Apud Romanos tutor factam pupillam suam, vt scribit Modestinus, nec ipse vxorem ducere, nec filio suo in matrimonio adiungere potest. Lege XV.D. de sponsalibus. quinetiam Senatusconsulto, inquit Paulus, quo cautum est, ne tutor pupillam vel filio suo, vel sibi nuptum collocet, etiam nepos significatur. Lege LIX.D. de ritu nuptiarum: itemque hares extraneos. Lege LXIV.D.eod. Prohibentur autem huiusmodi nuptiæ, ne pupilla in re familiari circumscribantur ab his, qui rationes eis gestæ tutelæ reddere compelluntur. d. Lege LXIV.D.eod. Tres tamen sunt exceptiones: Prima est, si id beneficium à Principe impetratum sit vt habes Lege VII.C.de interdicto matrimonio.
units.tr: Diogenes Laertius, in the Life of Solon, relates the law: [καλλίστην[?] δὲ κάλλιστην[?], τὸν ἐπί-τροπον τῇ τῆς ὀρφανῆς μητρὶ μὴ οἰκοῖσιν[?]]. By this law he wished to provide for the goods of the wards, so that no fraud should be done to them through the mother's marriage. But either this law of Solon seems to have become obsolete, or it was allowed for guardians who were appointed by will to marry the mothers of their wards, provided the dying father had provided for this in the final provisions of his will. Here is an example from Demosthenes, where he speaks of his own parents and his father's last will, in the speech Against Aphobus, on false witness (1): "For my father Demosthenes, gentlemen of the jury, left a considerable estate, and gave to me and my brother ... and to my mother fifty minae ... and when he was dying he tried to hand over these things to Aphobus and to Demophon, the son of Demosthenes ... and Demophon gave my brother two talents, and this to my mother, who received nothing ... the house and the furnishings for my use." Thus Pasio gives his wife in marriage to Phormio, and by his will names him guardian of his younger son Paficles. Demosthenes, in the speech against Phormio's paragraphe: "Pasio, as guardian, is said to have ... Phormio takes the wife, and according to the brother's ... she was entrusted to him." Among the Romans, a guardian who has made his ward his own, as Modestinus writes, can neither marry her himself nor join her in marriage to his son. See the fifteenth law of the Digest, on betrothals. Moreover, Paulus says that by the senatus consultum, by which it was provided that a guardian may not match his ward with his son or with himself, a grandson is also understood. See the fifty-ninth law of the Digest, on the rite of marriages, and likewise heirs are to be treated as strangers: see the sixty-fourth law of the same title. Such marriages are forbidden so that the ward may not be cheated in her family property by those who are compelled to render accounts of their guardianship to her. See the same sixty-fourth law. There are, however, three exceptions. The first is, if this privilege has been obtained from the Emperor, as you have in the seventh law of the Code, on the interdiction of marriage.

units.la: Jmpp. Diocletianus & Maximianus AA. & CC. Paragonio.
units.tr: The Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, Augusti and Caesars, to Paragonius.

units.la: Si tutor vel curator pupillam vel adultam quondam suam sibi, vel filio suo, nullo diuino impetrato beneficio, in matrimonio collocauerit, manet infamia contra eum. Ergo si diuinum impetrasset beneficium, nulla cum manebat infamia. Altera exceptio est, si post vicesimum sextum annum aetatis puellae nuptiae contractae sunt: nam anno vicesimo quinto aetatis puellae finitur tutela, superest praeterea annus utilis ad agendum cum tutore actione tutelae. Colliges ex his Pauli verbis Libro II. Sententiarum: Non est matrimonium, si tutor, vel curator pupillam suam intra vicesimum & sextum annum non desponsam a patre, nec testamento destinatam, ducat uxorem, vel eam filio suo iungat. Lege LXVI. D. de ritu nuptiarum. itemque è Rescripto Imperatorum Valeriani & Gallieni AA. ad Lucium: Si patris tui pupillam nondum reddita tutelae ratione, vel post redditam, nondum exacto quinto & vicesimo anno, nec non utili anno, uxorem duxisti, nemmatrimonium cum ea habuisse, nec filium ex huiusmodi coniunctione procreasse videri potes. Lege VI.C. de interdicto matrimonio. Si igitur puellam, post annum aetatis eius vicesimum quintum exactum, itemque utilem annum, id est, post exactos viginti sex eius aetatis annos, uxorem duxisset, erat matrimonium.
units.tr: If a guardian or curator has married his ward, or a former ward, to himself or to his son without having obtained a divine favour, the infamy remains upon him. Therefore, if he had obtained a divine favour, no infamy remained. The second exception is if the marriage was contracted after the girl had passed her twenty-sixth year of age. For the guardianship ends in the girl's twenty-fifth year, and in addition there remains a useful year for bringing the action of guardianship against the guardian. You may gather this from the words of Paulus in Book II of the Sentences: "It is not a marriage if a guardian or curator takes his ward, not betrothed by her father nor destined by his will, as his wife before she is twenty-six, or joins her to his son." See Law 66 of the Digest, On the Rite of Marriages; and likewise from the rescript of the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus, Augusti, to Lucius: "If you took as your wife your father's ward, before the account of the guardianship had been rendered, or after it had been rendered but before the twenty-fifth year had been completed, and also before the useful year, you may be said not to have had a marriage with her, nor to have begotten a son from such a union." See Law 6 of the Code, On the Prohibition of Marriage. Therefore, if he had married the girl after her twenty-fifth year was completed, and likewise after the useful year, that is, after her twenty-six years of age were completed, it was a valid marriage.

units.la: Tertia denique exceptio indicatur his verbis, non desponsam a patre, nec testamento destinatam, ducat uxorem, Lege d. LXVI. D. de ritu nuptiarum, quam etiā habes in laudato Valeriani & Gallieni AA. Rescripto ad Lucium: Sane si hoc pater puella, cum decederet, postulauit, & nuptiae rite contractae, & filius videtur iure susceptus. Paulus Libro V. Quaestionum: Tutor vel curator adultam uxorem ducere non potest, nisi a patre desponsa, destinatave, testamentove nominata condicione nuptiis, secuta fuerit. Lege XXXVI. D. de ritu nuptiarum. Vir summus in Observationibus, quidam forte legeret: Tutor vel curator adultam uxorem ducere non potest, nisi a patre desponsa, destinatave testamento, nominata condicione, nuptias secuta fuerit. nominata condicione, id est, viro nominato, cui filiam destinat pater, demonstrata persona viri, cui filiam nubere cupit post mortem suam. At potius legendum ex l. qui pupillam. D. ad leg. Iul. de adult. Nisi a patre desponsa destinatave testamentove nominata condicionem nuptiarum secuta fuerit. In l pater. D. de cond. & dem. testamento designata. Verum ego nihil hic mutandum censeo, sed sola interpunctione & interpretatione opus est: Nisi a patre desponsa, destinatave, testamentove nominata condicione nuptiis, secutus fuerit. Pater antequam decederet poterat filiam suam desponsare tutori eiusdem, vel etiam si non desponderet, cum sibi destinare generum expressis verbis, vel etiam, adscripta testamento condicione nuptiis, designare, nempe hoc modo, Caiae filiae meae ducenta lege, si L. Titio nupserit. Designatur enim his verbis, adscripta testamento condicione hac, Lucius Titius, cui Caius Seius velit filiam suam nubere. ita intelligo verba Papiniani è Libro VIII. Responsorum: Pater Seuerianam Proculam Aelio Philippo cognato nuptiis testamento designauit. eidem filiae praedium, si Aelio Philippo nupsisset, verbis fideicommissi reliquit, quod si non nupsisset, idem praedium Philippo dari voluit. Lege C I. D. de condicionibus & demonstrationibus. Aelius Philippus designatur nuptiis Seueriana Proculae ab eius patre, hac testamenti condicione, Seueriana Proculae filiæ meæ prædium do lego, si Ælio Philippo nupserit. Nemo enim dubitare poterit in hac testamenti huius condicione, patrem Seuerianæ Proculæ voluisse eâ nuptum dari Ælio Philippo, eumque daturum fuisse, si superfuisset. Ergo quando pater filiam suam tutori vel eius filio desponderat, aut destinauerat, aut adscripta testamento condicione nuptiis designauerat, & filia patris voluntatem sequeretur, nuptiæ rite erant contractæ: alioquin adulterium erat, non matrimonium. Marcianus Libro X. Institutionum: Qui pupillam suam duxit uxorem contra Senatusconsultum, nec matrimonium est hoc, & potest adulterij accusari qui tutor & curator fuit, & infra vicesimum sextum annum duxit uxorem, non à patre desponsam, vel destinatam, vel testamento denominatam. Lege VII. ad Legem Iuliam de adulteriis.
units.tr: Finally, the third exception is indicated by these words, "not betrothed by her father nor destined by his will, takes as his wife," in the aforementioned Law 66 of the Digest, On the Rite of Marriages, which you also have in the rescript of the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus to Lucius cited above: "Indeed, if the girl's father, when he was dying, made this request, and the marriage was duly contracted, the son is also regarded as lawfully acknowledged." Paulus in Book V of the Questions: "A guardian or curator cannot take an adult woman as his wife, unless the marriage has followed upon a condition named by her father in a betrothal, a destination, or a naming in his will." See Law 36 of the Digest, On the Rite of Marriages. A distinguished man in his Observations, perhaps reading it differently, wrote: "A guardian or curator cannot take an adult woman as his wife, unless the marriage has followed upon a condition named by her father in a betrothal, a destination, or a naming in his will." Here "a condition named" would mean a man named, to whom the father designates his daughter, the person of the husband being specified, whom he wishes his daughter to marry after his death. But it is rather to be read from the law Qui pupillam, D. ad legem Iuliam de adulteriis: "Unless the marriage has followed upon a betrothal or destination by her father, or a condition of marriage named in his will." In the law Pater, D. de conditionibus et demonstrationibus, it reads "designated in his will." But I think nothing here needs changing; what is needed is only a different punctuation and interpretation: "Unless the marriage has followed upon a betrothal by her father, or a destination, or a condition of marriage named in his will." Before he died, a father could betroth his daughter to his guardian or to the guardian's son, or even if he did not betroth her, he could expressly destine a son-in-law for himself, or even, by adding a condition of marriage to his will, designate one, namely in this way: "I bequeath two hundred to my daughter Caia, if she marries Lucius Titius." For she is designated by these words, the condition being added to the will, "Lucius Titius," whom Gaius Seius wishes his daughter to marry. I understand in this way the words of Papinian in Book VIII of the Responsa: "A father by will designated Aelius Philippus, his cousin, as husband for Severiana Procula. He left to the same daughter an estate, in the form of a fideicommissum, if she married Aelius Philippus; but if she did not marry, he wished the same estate to be given to Philippus." See Law 101 of the Digest, On Conditions and Demonstrations. Aelius Philippus was designated by Procula's father as husband for Severiana Procula, under this condition of the will: "I give and bequeath an estate to my daughter Severiana Procula, if she marries Aelius Philippus." For no one can doubt, in this condition of the will, that the father wished Severiana Procula to be given in marriage to Aelius Philippus, and would have done so had he survived. Therefore, when a father had betrothed his daughter to a guardian or to his son, or had destined her, or had designated a marriage by a condition added to his will, and the daughter followed her father's wish, the marriage was duly contracted; otherwise it was adultery, not marriage. Marcianus in Book X of the Institutes: "He who took his ward as wife contrary to the Senatus consultum, this is not a marriage, and he who was guardian or curator and took a wife below the age of twenty-six, not betrothed by her father, or destined, or named in his will, can be accused of adultery." See Law 7 on the Julian Law concerning adulteries.

units.la: Inter Seruos autem proprie non erant Nuptiæ, sed συνοικίαι[?], neque illæ, quibuscum consuevuerunt, Uxores, sed potius coniuncta conserua, è quibus habebant filios, vt eleganter vocat M. Varro de R.R. Libro I. cap. XVII. Earum verò vsum Seruis concessit Solon hac Lege:
units.tr: Among slaves, properly speaking, there were no marriages, but cohabitations [συνοικίαι]; nor were those women with whom they lived called wives, but rather "fellow-slaves living together," from whom they had children, as M. Varro elegantly calls them in De re rustica, Book I, chapter XVII. Solon granted slaves the use of these women by this law:

units.la: Χρῆσθαι δὲ δούλαις συνοικίαις γυναιξίν. Serui feminis vtuntur.
units.tr: Slaves may make use of female cohabitants. [Χρῆσθαι δὲ δούλαις συνοικίαις γυναιξίν]

units.la: Legem laudat Plutarchus in Amatorio: ὡς γὰρ Σόλων κατέδειξε, δούλαις μὲν ἐξὸν [illegible, ~40 letters]. Sed, vt dixi, hæ συνοικίαι non possunt dici Nuptiæ: Quare is, cui Orationem scripsit Demosthenes [illegible, ~30 letters] vt probet nutricem suam liberam esse, non seruam, hoc argumento vtitur, quod nuptias cum viro constituerit. Verba eius sunt: [illegible, ~60 letters].
units.tr: Plutarch cites the law in the Amatorius: "For as Solon laid down, it is permitted to slaves [...]" But, as I said, these cohabitations cannot be called marriages. Therefore he for whom Demosthenes wrote an oration [...] to prove that his nurse was free, not a slave, uses this argument, that she had contracted a marriage with a man. His words are: [...]

units.la: Solonis Lege Sponsæ, cum ad nuptias irent, iubebantur phrygetrum ferre, quo possent agnosci:
units.tr: By Solon's law, brides, when they went to the wedding, were ordered to carry a phrygetrum, by which they might be recognized:

units.la: Τὰς Νύμφας ἰσάσας ὅτι τὸ γάμων, φρύγετρον φέρειν σημεῖον.
units.tr: The brides, having been made equal in the matter of marriage, are to carry a phrygetrum as a sign. [Τὰς Νύμφας ἰσάσας ὅτι τὸ γάμων, φρύγετρον φέρειν σημεῖον]

units.la: Sponsæ, cum domum mariti deducuntur, phrygetrum in signum ferunto.
units.tr: Brides, when they are led to their husband's house, shall carry a phrygetrum as a sign.

units.la: Laudat Legem Pollux Libro I. cap. XII. Σόλων δὲ, καὶ τὰς Νύμφας ἰσάσας ὅτι τὸν γάμων, ἐκέλευσε φρύγετρον φέρειν σημεῖον. Quid sit φρύγετρον varie exponunt. Pollux quidem dicit esse, ὃ τὰς κόσμους ἐφρύγειν. Hesychius verò interpretatur ξυλάφιον, ὃ κινοῦσι τὰ πεφρυγμένας κριθάς. Eo autem officij sui admonebantur Sponsæ, nempe curæ sibi esse debere rem familiarem.
units.tr: Pollux cites the law in Book I, chapter XII: "Solon also ordered that brides, made equal in the matter of marriage, carry a phrygetrum as a sign." [Σόλων δὲ, καὶ τὰς Νύμφας ἰσάσας ὅτι τὸν γάμων, ἐκέλευσε φρύγετρον φέρειν σημεῖον] Scholars explain variously what the phrygetrum is. Pollux indeed says it is that which roasted the ornaments [ὃ τὰς κόσμους ἐφρύγειν]. Hesychius, however, interprets it as a wooden utensil [ξυλάφιον] with which they stir parched barley. By it the brides were reminded of their duty, namely that the care of the household ought to be theirs.

units.la: Lege quoque cauerat Solon, vt sponsa in thalamum mariti deducta, cydonium malum gustaret.
units.tr: Solon had also provided by law that the bride, once led into the husband's bedchamber, should taste a quince.

units.la: Τῷ νυμφίῳ τῷ νυμφίῳ συνκαθείργνυσθαι μῆλον κυδωνίης συνγευσάμενην.
units.tr: [Τῷ νυμφίῳ τῷ νυμφίῳ συνκαθείργνυσθαι μῆλον κυδωνίης συνγευσάμενην.] The bride, having tasted a quince, was to be shut up with the bridegroom.

units.la: Sponsa in thalamum deducta, malum cydonium gustato.
units.tr: The bride, led into the bedchamber, having tasted a quince.

units.la: Habet Plutarchus in Solone: εἰς τὴν πρώτην ... [illegible, ~50 letters]. Idem ἐν τοῖς γαμικοῖς ... [illegible, ~20 letters] huius rei causam aperit: ὁ Σόλων ἐκέλευε τῷ νυμφίῳ τῷ νυμφίῳ συνκαλύπτεσθαι μῆλον κυδωνίης καταφαγόντα, ἀπὸ πόλεμος (ὡς ἔοικεν) ὅτι δὴ τῷ ... [illegible, ~30 letters].
units.tr: Plutarch in Solon has: "into the first [...]". The same author, in his Conjugalia [...], explains the reason for this thing: "Solon ordered the bridegroom to ... after eating a quince, from war (as it seems), because ... [...]"

units.la: DE DOTIBUS.
units.tr: ON DOWRIES.

units.la: TITULUS II.
units.tr: TITLE II.

units.la: Xorem Dotis datio divortio à concubinis secernebat, ut in palliato Plauti Trinummo: Sed ut inops, Infamis ne sim, ne mihi hanc famam differant, me Germanam meam sororem in concubinatum tibi Sic sine dote dedisse magis, quam in matrimonium.
units.tr: The giving of a dowry distinguished a wife from concubines, as in Plautus' Trinummus, a comedy in Greek dress: But so that I, being poor, am not infamous, lest they spread this rumour about me, that I gave my own sister in concubinage to you, thus without a dowry rather than in marriage.

units.la: Nuptiarum enim legitimarum certissimum argumentum erat Dos, cum dotatas esse feminas ad subolem procreandam, replendamque liberis ciuitatem, maxime sit necessarium, inquit Pomponius. Quare eleganter Artemidorus filiam cum creditore comparat, quae grandis dotem poscit: Δημήτρις ... τὸν αὐτὸν ἔχοντα λόγον ἐπιδικάσῃ καὶ ἡ γυνὴ τὴν γυναῖκα μὴ ἀνάγκης ἀπαιτῇ, καὶ ὅταν μὴ πολλὰς αἰτήσα-φῇ φερτίδων, ἀπαλλαγῆς λαβοῦσα ... ὡς Δημήτρις. Itaque legitimam fuisse Pyrrhi uxorem, Nicodemi sororem negat Ilaeus ἐν τῇ [?] τῆς Πύῤῥα κλήρου, quia sorori Nicodemus dotem non dixit, non dedit: unde quaerit ὡ πνα πο-τί γυναῖκα φησὶν Θίδις ἐκδοῦναι τὴν ἀδελφὴν Νικόδημος. quasi dotem nullus dixerit, nullus dederit. Quare etiam qui [illegible, ~9 letters] uxorem ducebat, γυναικονόμος, id est, instrumentis dotalibus acceptam tamen dotem ferebat, & cauebat, ut ex eadem Oratione liquet. Neque tamen concubinae & pellices omnino ἀγαμοῦσι erant: legitimas enim uxores imitantur: unde in hac Isaei Oratione: ἐπὶ καὶ οἱ ... πανμαχὶ διδόντες ... ἐκ τῶν ... πρὸς ... ὁμολογοῦσι ita αἱ ... ἰδίας quae legitimae uxores Atheniensium ciuium esse non poterant, sed concubinae tantum, [?], mille illas drachmas, quas è bonis paternis auferebant, ad eum, cui iungebantur, virum adferebant; hinc Isaeanae illi Philae, quam Xenocli Cyprio elocauit Endius, dedit in quasi dotem χλίας δραχμάς. De Dote autem Leges aliquot scripsit Solon, & hanc quidem primo:
units.tr: For the surest proof of a lawful marriage was the dowry, since it is especially necessary that women be endowed for the bearing of children and for filling the state with offspring, says Pomponius. So Artemidorus neatly compares a daughter who demands a large dowry to a creditor: [Δημήτρις ... τὸν αὐτὸν ἔχοντα λόγον ἐπιδικάσῃ καὶ ἡ γυνὴ τὴν γυναῖκα μὴ ἀνάγκης ἀπαιτῇ, καὶ ὅταν μὴ πολλὰς αἰτήσαφῇ φερτίδων, ἀπαλλαγῆς λαβοῦσα ... ὡς Δημήτρις.] Thus Ilaeus, in his speech on the estate of Pyrrhus, denies that Pyrrhus' wife was a lawful one, the sister of Nicodemus, because Nicodemus did not call it a dowry nor give it as one. Hence he asks [ὡ πνα πο-τί γυναῖκα φησὶν Θίδις ἐκδοῦναι τὴν ἀδελφὴν Νικόδημος], as if no one had called it a dowry or given one. Therefore also the man who [illegible] took a wife, the gynaikonomos, that is, received a dowry by means of dotal instruments and took care of it, as is clear from the same speech. Yet concubines and mistresses were not altogether unmarried, for they imitate lawful wives. Hence in this speech of Isaeus [ἐπὶ καὶ οἱ ... πανμαχὶ διδόντες ... ἐκ τῶν ... πρὸς ... ὁμολογοῦσι], so that the women who could not be lawful wives of Athenian citizens, but only concubines, brought those thousand drachmas, which they took from their fathers' goods, to the man to whom they were joined. Hence Isaeus' Philae, whom Endius let out to Xenocles the Cypriot, gave a thousand drachmas as a sort of dowry [χλίας δραχμάς]. Solon wrote several laws on dowry, and this one first:

units.la: Ἰμάτια τρία, καὶ σκεῦη μικρὰ νομίσματος ἀξία, ἐπεσθαι δ᾽ μηδὲν ἐπιφέρεσθαι τὴν γαμουμένην φερνάς.
units.tr: [Ἰμάτια τρία, καὶ σκεῦη μικρὰ νομίσματος ἀξία, ἐπεσθαι δ᾽ μηδὲν ἐπιφέρεσθαι τὴν γαμουμένην φερνάς.] Three garments, and small vessels of modest value; let the bride bring nothing further with her as dowry.

units.la: Tres tantum vestes, & vasa aliquot non magno constantia sponsa ad maritum deferto in dotem.
units.tr: Only three garments, and some vessels not costing much, let the bride take to her husband as dowry.

units.la: Refert hanc Legem Plutarchus in Solone: Τὰ δ᾽ ἄλλων γάμων ἀφῆκε τὰς φερνάς, ἱμάτια τρία, καὶ σκεῦη μικρὰ νομίσματος ἀξία καλῶς, ἐπεσθαι δ᾽ μηδὲν ἐπιφέρεσθαι τὴν γαμουμένην. Opponit Solon virginibus dotalibus, quae totam hereditatem in dotem adferunt, ceteras omnes, siue ἐπιγαμίας, siue ἄνευ sint, quas tres tantum vestes, & quaedam modici pretij vasa non elaborata artis, secum ad maritum deferre matrimonij ergo iussit: ἢ δὲ ... ἐλλέπει μαθφοεγυκὴ ὤνιον εἰς τὸ γάμων, ἀλλ' ὅτι πενιχρὸς καὶ χαρίεις, καὶ φιλότιμος ἡγεῖσθαι τὸν ἀνδρὸς τὴν γυναικὸς σωφρονισμόν[?].
